### T129 (shared::tree's ASSIGN pattern keeps its `(?<!\$)\{` lookbehind, so each of its scans runs on fancy-regex's backtracking machine at every position, found by T83 2026-11-21: over T79's ux corpus the walk is 59.31 G instructions with T83, env_from's ASSIGN scan 16.41 G of it (66,294 calls) and read_where_it_stands' 3.75 G (121,284 calls), 34% together, measured 2026-11-21 (callgrind, `/tmp/t83/out/cg.inl.ux.out`, env_from kept out of line in a throwaway copy))

- **Approach**: five of the walk's patterns run in the regex crate's automaton, the one-character look that held each on
  fancy-regex's backtracking machine read by hand at the match it judges, as T83 read REDIRECT's:
  - THE PREMISE, RESTATED: fancy-regex 0.14 takes a word boundary as it takes a lookaround - `Assertion::is_hard` marks `\b` and
    `\B` hard and its analysis compiles a pattern holding one to its own machine (read 2026-11-21, `fancy-regex-0.14.0/src/lib.rs`
    and `src/analyze.rs`) - so ASSIGN's `\b(?:do|then|else)\s` held it there as its `(?<!\$)\{` did; dropping the lookbehind alone
    would have moved nothing. Both are read by hand.
  - THE READING (`tree.rs`'s `assignments` and `look_refuses`): at a start past the text's first character, an ASSIGN match's first
    character says which opening it took - one of `;&|(` or a newline, a `{`, or the `d`, `t` or `e` of `do`, `then` or `else` - and
    the openings are disjoint there, so the look is that opening's alone and depends on the start only, never on the rest of the
    match: a `$` before the `{` refuses (`(?<!\$)`), a word character before the word refuses (`\b`; past ASCII, Unicode's `\w`
    through a `^\w$` pattern, `is_word`, as fancy-regex's own boundary reads it). At the text's first character nothing stands
    before, so no look refuses. A refused match is tried again a character on (its first is one byte), a taken one goes on from its
    end, as fancy-regex's scan did; so each start's match is the fancy pattern's at that start or none, and the scan finds the same
    leftmost matches.
  - THE OTHER FOUR, each the walk's pattern whose one hard part is a one-character look at a fixed place: CONTINUED's
    `(?<!\\)` (`joined`, which also writes out the replacement); bind's SOURCED's `\b` before `do`, `then` or `else` (`sourced`,
    `look_refuses` without the brace's look); bind's PRINTF_V's `\b` before `printf` (`printf_v_names`); MKTEMP's `\b` after
    `mktemp` (`mktemp_call`: the pattern opens with `^`, so the word stands at one place and a word character after it leaves no
    match).
  - THE CALLERS: env_from, read_where_it_stands and bind's `bindings` through `assignments` (`bindings` scanned ASSIGN twice, once
    for the names and once for the chains after them, and now once); `bindings`' SOURCED and PRINTF_V; sanitize's and env_from's
    `joined`; env_from's `mktemp_call`. Each pattern keeps its gate, so what a command builds is unchanged (`tree/tests/builds.rs`)
    but for `WORD`, the one-character `^\w$` pattern, built only when a character past ASCII stands before a look.
  - NOT TAKEN, each a look the automaton cannot hold or another builder's file: LOOP's `in\b` stands inside an optional group, so
    refusing it changes which reading the group takes, not only whether the match stands; HEREDOC (`tree/python.rs`) and shape's
    `strip_heredocs` hold a backreference; `py_c::reads`' 11.74 G of `is_match` is T89's module (left as T89's builder works there).
  - PINNED (`tree/tests/looks.rs`): each scan against the fancy pattern it replaced, on every text of up to N pieces of its
    alphabet - ASSIGN every group's span (0 to 4) on 9 pieces to 5 (`$`, `{`, `do `, a letter, `é`, `²`, `;`, `A=`, `export `)
    and on 9 to 4 for the other openings and the quoted values (`then `, `else `, a letter, `é`, `²`, `;`, `A=`, `"`, `'`: groups 2
    and 3 read), CONTINUED's joined text on 4 to 7, SOURCED's answer on 8 to 5 and on 7 to 4 for `then` and `else`, PRINTF_V's
    names and offsets on 7 to 5, MKTEMP's spans on 9 to 5;
    and each pattern built with a backtracking limit of one step reads a long text with no error where the fancy pattern it
    replaced, built so, errs - the regex crate's automaton has no steps to count. Each look turned off in a scratch copy fails its
    differential and the copy as written passes, measured 2026-11-21 (`cargo test tree::tests::looks` on `/tmp/t129/mut` and
    `/tmp/t129/fix3`, `/tmp/t129/fix4`, `/tmp/t129/out/mutate2.log`, `check3.log`, `check4.log`, `check5.log`: the brace, the
    word, the word past ASCII read as `char::is_alphanumeric`, CONTINUED's, SOURCED's, MKTEMP's and PRINTF_V's, and the word's look
    kept for `do` alone, which fails ASSIGN's and SOURCED's `then`/`else` texts). Every line of the five scans, `look_refuses` and
    both arms of `is_word` is run by the tree tests, measured 2026-11-21 (`cargo llvm-cov` on `/tmp/t129/fix4`,
    `/tmp/t129/out/cov-fix4.txt`; its one red test, py_c's `window_307_runs_as_typed`, reads a file the copy lacks).
  - THE COUNTS, measured 2026-11-21 (callgrind over T79's ux corpus, 2,311 rows, `walk_judged` inclusive through T83's timer
    `/tmp/t83/scripts/walker/time.rs`, each copy `git archive 2653b8931a`'s `rust/guard/shared` (the same as HEAD 9bd338e244's)
    with this task's files over it and T89's `py_c::argv_places` hunk in tree.rs taken out (`/tmp/t129/scripts/mkcopy.py`),
    `/tmp/t129/out/cg.{head,fix,fix2,fix4}.ux.out`): HEAD 59.31 G (59,306,394,627, T83's figure reproduced), fancy-regex's machine
    51.32 G of it; ASSIGN and CONTINUED 30.90 G; with SOURCED 28.05 G. With PRINTF_V and MKTEMP 26.66 G (26,662,310,660, 45.0%
    of HEAD's), fancy-regex's machine 17.60 G of it, measured 2026-11-21 (callgrind, `cg.fix4.ux.out`, its callers read by
    `callgrind_annotate --tree=caller`): 11.78 G through `is_match`, nearly all `py_c::reads`' (T89's module), and 5.66 G through
    `captures_from_pos`; that the five patterns no longer reach it is the one-step pin's. The walk of every row of the probes and the three corpora (q 6, bx 59,116, ux 2,311, tx 995 rows; each row
    walked judged with the mirror, plain and with no main) is byte-identical to HEAD's, measured 2026-11-21 (T83's walker
    `/tmp/t83/scripts/walker/main.rs`, `/tmp/t129/out/{q,bx,ux,tx}.{head,fix,fix2,fix4}.jsonl`, `cmp`).

   (every pattern built through `crate::regex`, a scan ending on its first error or never erring).

### T129 Performance checklist (docs/performance-checklist.md - prompts, never a gate; time is the goal, calls the measure)

1. **Where does the time go?** Not a hamlet or Mode A stage: the guards' walk (`shared::tree::walk_judged`). At HEAD,
   fancy-regex's backtracking machine is 51.32 G of the walk's 59.31 G over the ux corpus, measured 2026-11-21 (callgrind,
   `/tmp/t129/out/cg.head.ux.out`, T83's `cg.inl.ux.out` for env_from's share): ASSIGN's scans 16.41 G in env_from, 3.75 G in
   read_where_it_stands and 7.29 G in `bindings`' two (its `bound_texts` 12.17 G at HEAD, 4.87 G with ASSIGN read by hand,
   `cg.fix.ux.out`); SOURCED's search 2.87 G (`bound_texts` 4.87 G to 2.01 G, `cg.fix2.ux.out`); MKTEMP's and PRINTF_V's 1.39 G
   together (the walk's 28.05 G to 26.66 G, `cg.fix4.ux.out`, PRINTF_V's 0.19 G of it from `bound_texts` 2.01 G to 1.81 G);
   `py_c::reads`' searches 11.74 G (T89's).
2. **Removes work, or only moves it?** Removes it, a better algorithm: the automaton reads each text once where the backtracking
   machine tried every opening at every position, and `bindings`' second ASSIGN scan is gone.
3. **What do you expect it to save, and why?** About half the walk: ASSIGN's 16.41 + 3.75 + 7.29 G, SOURCED's 2.87 G, MKTEMP's
   and PRINTF_V's 1.39 G and CONTINUED's share, each scan's cost falling to the automaton's linear pass (the figures of item 1).
4. **How does the work grow with the settlement?** No settlement: the walk grows with the command. The machine's cost grew with the
   text's length times the openings tried at each position, an assignment's `\s*` and the rest retried from each; the automaton's is
   linear in the text, so the longest commands gain most.
5. **What did the before and after show, and under what conditions?** Callgrind, measured 2026-11-21: 59.31 G before, 26.66 G
   after (ASSIGN and CONTINUED 30.90 G, SOURCED 28.05 G). Wall time of the walker over the corpora, HEAD's and this task's built
   walkers run in turn under the same load (three walks a row; host load 33 to 41, measured 2026-11-21, `/usr/bin/time`,
   `/tmp/t129/scripts/pair.sh`, `/tmp/t129/out/pair.log`): ux 25.83 s to 12.38 s (the median of three each), tx 2.81 s to
   1.53 s (median of three), bx 158.78 s to 107.48 s (one each) - evidence under load, not a pass.
6. **Did any map move, and does it still keep the research?** No map: the walk is a guard's, and its every output over the corpora
   is byte-identical to HEAD's.

### T89 (shared::tree judged a `python3 -c` program that writes a place it computes from `sys.argv` as writing where the shell stands, found by T79 on 2026-11-21: `cd <mirror>/research/questions; python3 -I -c "import sys; open(sys.argv[2],'w').write('x')" a /tmp/q/txt/a.txt` and its two loop forms were rewritten (sid t) or refused (sid nobody) through HEAD's main-tree while `cp` and `echo >` to the same scratch place passed, measured 2026-11-21 (`/tmp/t79b/judge/probe-mt.jsonl` #2-#8 through HEAD 2653b8931a's binary `/tmp/t89/bin-head`, `/tmp/t89/out/head.probe.{t,nobody}.mt.tsv`); of the corpus's 852 commands running a `-c` program that indexes `sys.argv`, 11 write through `open(sys.argv[N], <mode>)` and HEAD's main-tree refuses 4 of them, each writing scratch standing in the mirror (bx#29969, bx#54240, bx#58694, ux#2209), measured 2026-11-21 (item 4))

- **Approach**: the program's `sys.argv[N]` in a write is the command's N-th word after the program, placed as the walk places a
  word; everything the binding cannot read keeps HEAD's reading (feature 204's D5, a write where the shell stands).
  - the binding, `py_c::argv_word(n, after, env, home)` - the one small function `tree::program`'s reader can call for T125: the
    words after the program as the walk holds them (each name it binds already in the text, `bind`, or in `env`), a redirect and its
    target no word, a name unset dropped from the text by `bind` as bash drops its unquoted expansion; `sys.argv[0]` (the `-c`) and
    an index past the words are None, and so is any index at or past a word that may be other than one word (`one_word`: a glob,
    a brace, `$@`, a substitution of either kind, a name the walk does not know, a value holding a blank or empty - a plain quoted
    word reaches the walk without its quotes, so `"$X"` and `$X` cannot be told apart - and a held word quoted only in part);
    a word bash may split (`may_split`, the session's ruling 2026-11-21, option A) - `$__unread__` (`bind`'s mark for a loop's value
    cut at a glob, or a name read) or a `_` (`bind`'s mark for a loop value's blank, a typed `_` told from it by nothing) - is the
    word where it is the one asked for (its first piece lies where its start does) and ends the count past it: an unquoted `$f`
    over a glob matching `Seeing from Above.pdf` makes `sys.argv[2]` `from`, written where the shell stands (item 4), so every
    index past such a word keeps HEAD's reading. The cost: a quoted `"$f"`, one word in bash, reaches the walk without its quotes
    and keeps HEAD's reading too (ux#2209, bx#54240), and so does a bare `$f` whose glob matches no blank name (bx#58694); the
    alternatives priced were the walk carrying the quote state (`tree/bind.rs`, T129's) and expanding the glob where the shell
    stands, both filed as T140; the session chose A, no verdict worse than HEAD's.
  - the write, `py_c::argv_writes`: the program Python receives (`received`, the shell's expansions undone; `reads` is that and
    `only_reads`, unchanged in what it judges) with each write through `sys.argv[N]` read past (`argv_masked`) - an `open` of it whose
    arguments are not all a read's (its name and path masked, its mode and keywords left for the writers to be sought in, so an
    `opener=` that writes stays a write), its chained `.write(` or `.writelines(`, and a `json.dump(x, <that open>)` (bx#29969) - must
    then pass `only_reads`; every `argv` the program names must be a `sys.argv[N]` read (none sliced, aliased, assigned, deleted
    from or imported by name) and `sys` the module it imports (`import sys`, not rebound).
  - a name bound to it, `py_c::argv_inlined` (the review's ruling, 2026-11-21: bx#58999's `p=sys.argv[1]; t=open(p).read(); ...;
    open(p,'w').write(t)` is T89's "program that writes a place it computes from `sys.argv`"): a name bound by a statement of its
    own, `NAME = sys.argv[N]`, whose every other mention is an `open`'s path (`open(NAME` then `,` or `)`), is read as `sys.argv[N]`
    there before `argv_masked` reads the program; a name mentioned any other way - used, bound again by any Python form, opened by
    another module, named in a literal - leaves the program as it is, so its write through the name keeps HEAD's reading. Every
    rebinding form (an assignment, a loop, `as`, a parameter, `del`) is a mention that is no `open`'s path, so none can make the

   other way, a word count it cannot know, a loop's or a read's value before the word, which bash may split - is judged as before.

   lands where the shell was last known); T31's and T42's read judgment (`reads`, unchanged, still the stdin route's); T79's walk,
   its `bind` and its one rule for an unresolved place (`path_write`, `known_place`, `settled`), read, not changed; T125 (the same
   binding for `tree::program`, so `argv_word` stands alone); the brief's files (`py_c` and its tests; one `tree.rs` hunk outside
   them, named in the Approach); T129's (`tree.rs` ASSIGN) and T118's (`tree/program.rs`, gate-write) files left alone;

   (T79's found-and-left, its line in tasks.md); R: none - a guard's rule, no research question.

### T115 (fixed sleeps in four hook suites waited 0.3 to 1.0 s for an event the next check reads, and `test-finished-run-hooks.sh`'s `settle` ran its check unready at a 1 or 2 s deadline, so a slow host could fail good work as the stall-watchdog suite's fixed 1 s did at T92's landing, observed 2026-11-21 (T111's sweep, as T115's line records it))

- **Approach**: each fixed sleep before a check that needs an event becomes a wait for that event to a deadline, in case 3's form
  (`for _ in $(seq "$WAIT_TRIES"); do <the state the check reads> && break; sleep 0.1; done`), and the check after it is unchanged, so a
  state that never comes still fails it. One knob per suite, `WAIT_TRIES=300` (30 s) and `SETTLE_S=30` in the finished-run suite, a GUESS
  only a red run pays, labeled at each, not derived from the shapes waited on, which measured a median of 0.008 and 0.012 s and at
  most 0.071 s, measured 2026-11-21 (T111's `/tmp/t111-measure/shapes.sh`, n=200, a load of 16 to 17).
  - THE FIX, `test-clone-sync-hooks.sh` (HEAD's 186, 273, 287) and `test-land-tooling.sh` (184), where HEAD's text slept 0.3 s
    (observed 2026-11-22, method: `git show HEAD:tests/hooks/<suite>`): an `exec -a make` fixture is waited for until its
    `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` argv0 reads `make` (`argv_make` in the clone-sync suite, the same loop inline in land-tooling's). Before its
    exec the process is a copy of the suite, which the gate's `own-make` (argv0 and cwd) and the gate lock's `running_gate` (argv0 and a
    word `done`) both read as no make, observed 2026-11-22, method: reading `rust/gate/crates/tree/src/lock.rs`, and the `cd` runs
    before the `exec`, so an argv0 of `make` means its cwd is set. Land-tooling's case also ends the `sleep 120` child (`pkill -P`, as
    clone-sync's case does), where a kill of the shell alone left it running for two minutes, observed 2026-11-22, method: reading the
    case beside clone-sync's.

### T115 Approach (checklist part A)

1. **The goal, in the world.** No map changes. `make hooks-test`'s clone-sync, land-tooling, idle-tests, closing-checks and
   finished-run suites pass on good work under load, and still fail an `exec -a make` that never execs, a timer that never exits or
   never removes its arming file, a check that outlives its TERM, and a fixture's state that never comes.
2. **The constraints.** T115's line; FR-012 (red first); constitution XIII (no known regression: each suite's checks the same, case 8's
   made able to fail) and XIV (a check that fails good work is a defect, and so is one that cannot fail, fixed here); the launcher's
   ground rules: the five suites and this section alone, nothing of T118's (`tree/program.rs`, `gate_write_hooks`), T89's (`tree`'s
   `py_c`) or T129's (`tree.rs`), nothing committed.

### T91 (T79's bind rule refuses two kinds of scratch write HEAD allowed, found by T79's second plan review, 2026-11-21: a name assigned twice in straight-line code is judged at each value, and past the 64-binding cap a lone loop falls back to T79's unknown reading, the mirror)

- **Approach**: two changes in `rust/guard/shared/src/tree/bind.rs`, red first, on HEAD `30e95ca94b`.
  - the shapes at HEAD: a name judged at each assigned value in tx 8 of 995 rows, ux 62 of 2,311, bx 281 of 59,116; past the 64 cap ux 8, bx 14, tx 0 - every one a product of several names (largest single loop 31 values, 21 distinct; products 70 to 680), no lone loop past 64, measured 2026-11-22 (an instrumented copy of the walk, `/tmp/t91/scripts/probe/main.rs`, one process a corpus, `/tmp/t91/out/probe.*.tsv`).
  - (a) a straight reassignment reads its last value: `Bound::Straight`, a name assigned more than once in straight-line code, is one binding - each bare assignment renamed `__s<k>_NAME` and each read bound to the assignment last before it (by the assignment's end, so `D=$D/b` reads the one before), a read before any assignment the environment's value or empty. `straight()` takes it only where no function, `source`, `readonly`/`declare`/`typeset`/`local`/`unset` stands in the command, each read's assignment is bare and alone in its command, the stretch from it to the read holds no compound word, brace group, comment, backtick, `$(`, `${...}` beyond a name and op, or `)` underflow, and no read of the name assigns or takes a word on its value (`${D:=W}`, `${D:-W}`, `${D-W}`; the last two added on T91's first plan review, below); else `Bound::Assigned`, judged at each value as before (decision D-a). Only bare assignments are renamed: a first cut renamed an `a=` inside a `python3 -c "..."` (bx#50157), measured 2026-11-22 (T83's walker, `/tmp/t91/scripts/walkall.sh`).
  - (b) a lone loop past the cap is judged value by value: `bound_texts` collects the many-valued names in read order; the one many-valued name of a command gets `MAX_VALUES = 128`, else `MAX_BINDINGS = 64` as before, so a product of names past 64 keeps T79's unknown reading, unchanged; loop values deduplicated by text; `bindings` skips a name already bound (decision D-b).
  - where the final rule takes: Straight names bx 5 rows (5 names), tx 0, ux 0; still Assigned tx 8 rows (10 names), ux 62 (65), bx 276 (441); past the cap ux 8, bx 12 (deduplication took 2 bx rows under 64), measured 2026-11-22 (`/tmp/t91/target-probe2`, `/tmp/t91/out/probe4.*.tsv`).
  - red first: HEAD's `bind.rs` with T91's tests and a stub `MAX_VALUES` (both changes off), `cargo test --lib tree::tests::` 52 passed, 2 failed - `a_straight_reassignment_reads_its_last_value` at its first case and `a_loop_past_the_cap_is_judged_value_by_value` at 65 values; `a_mirror_value_at_either_end_is_still_read` (30 cases, a mirror value first, last or between) passes at HEAD and pins that (a) keeps every refusal, measured 2026-11-22 (`/tmp/t91/red`, `/tmp/t91/out/red-T91.log`). T91's first plan review asked after `D=<mirror>/x; D=; touch ${D:-<mirror>/z}/f`: the fix read it `/f` elsewhere, where bash writes `<mirror>/z/f` and HEAD refused it (at `<mirror>/x/f`) - a regression of (a), fixed here: the case and `${D-W}`'s added to the either-end pin, red with the first fix (`a_mirror_value_at_either_end_is_still_read` at that case) and green with the op excluded, `cargo test --lib tree::tests::` 54 passed, measured 2026-11-22 (`/tmp/t91/fix`, `/tmp/t91/out/red2.log`, `/tmp/t91/out/green5.log`); the exclusion only moves a name back to HEAD's reading at each value. Green: `make rust-test CRATE=rust/guard/shared` 427 passed, 0 failed (the two million-step tests and `window_307_runs_as_typed`, red in the /tmp copy, green in the clone), measured 2026-11-22 (`/tmp/t91/out/rtest.log`).
  - a moved pin: `a_name_assigned_from_pwd_is_where_the_shell_stands_then`'s `cd C && WT=$PWD; echo; WT=/tmp/q/wt; touch $WT/x.py` now reads `["elsewhere"]`, as bash writes it; its `;` variant keeps `["clone","elsewhere"]` (the `cd C &&` before the first assignment is not straight-line under (a)'s rule).
  - the replay, HEAD against the fix (main-tree, gm-tree and make-only with session `nobody`, gate-write in gate mode, every row's verdict and message hash): fx 1,134, tx 995 and ux 2,311 rows each 0 changed on all four guards; bx 59,116 rows 0 changed on main-tree, gm-tree and make-only (gate-write over bx, the slowest, still running at this writing; its first 13,587 rows 0 changed), measured 2026-11-22 (`/tmp/t91/scripts/runall.sh head|fix`, `/tmp/t91/rp/{head,fix}.<c>.*.tsv`, `diff` of the sorted rows). T83's walker over q, tx and ux byte-identical; bx 3 rows differ: bx#21184 (`F=A; F=B; cat >> $F`: HEAD read both targets, the fix B alone, as bash) and bx#23083, #27145 (the same target set, duplicate targets fewer), measured 2026-11-22 (`/tmp/t91/scripts/walkall.sh`, `/tmp/t91/out/w.<c>.{head,fix}.jsonl`). The 22 over-cap rows at HEAD: main-tree, gm-tree and make-only allow all; gate-write refuses 7 (ux#508, #940, #941, bx#25781, #28198, #28365, #28370), unchanged from HEAD (each a product of names, which T91 leaves as it was).
  - the cost: ux's `walk_judged`, inclusive, HEAD 26,849,671,432 instructions (T129's halved walk in the base), the fix 26,834,553,158 (0.06% fewer, no rise), 11.62 M a row at HEAD and 11.61 M with the fix over 2,311 rows, measured 2026-11-22 (`valgrind --tool=callgrind`, T83's release `time` binary over `/tmp/t79/ux-all.jsonl`, `/tmp/t91/out/cg.{head,fix}.ux.out`; the fix's binary was built with `MAX_VALUES = 256`, code identical on ux, no lone ux loop past 64).   - decisions: D-a - the straight-line rule is narrow on purpose: a name read after any branch, loop, substitution or function keeps HEAD's reading at each value, which over-refuses but never under-refuses (the either-end pin); widening it to `&&` and `$(` was priced from the probe (`probe2.*.tsv`: most Assigned names stand after one) and left, since an assignment after `&&` or `||` may not run, so its read may see the value before it. - `D=; echo x > ${D:-/diagram/x}/f` run from /tmp is read as a write to `/f` (elsewhere) at HEAD and with the fix, but bash writes the mirror `/diagram/x/f`: `bind.rs`'s `replaced()` drops the `:-` default when the name is assigned, measured 2026-11-22 (T91's probe, HEAD and the fix). Not fixed here: an empty or unset value must take the default, which needs the walk's own expansion (`expand` in `tree.rs`) to judge the op, outside this task's bind rule, and it predates T91 (T79). The same drop reads `${D:+<mirror>/z}` as an unknown target elsewhere from /tmp at HEAD, where bash writes the mirror for a set `D`, measured 2026-11-22 (HEAD's walker, `/tmp/t91/q2/ph.jsonl`). Filed as T144; lands before T140.
- `D=<mirror>/x; D=/s/y; X=`date`; touch $D/f` (or `X="$(date)"`, a brace group, a comment line, `${X:-$(pwd)}` in the stretch from the last assignment to the read), run standing in the mirror, is refused though bash writes `/s/y/f`: each costs the session an escape or a rewrite; the either-end pin holds these cases as refusals today, measured 2026-11-22 (`/tmp/t91/q2`, the pin). Not fixed here: `flat` would have to skip a substitution's body and a comment and scan a brace group for an assignment to the name, a parse the walk does not make in `bind.rs`; T91 keeps HEAD's reading at each value for them (D-a), so no refusal is lost. Filed as T145; lands before T140.

**Performance work?** No.

### T142 (the tool's incremental build linked a stale codegen unit, so every gate command failed until a source of that crate moved: rust-lld `undefined hidden symbol: anon.0482a95c....1.llvm.17705557342783902695` referenced from `l7r_gate_task-faf2a19073b9305a.ads6op1mfn3gc3gvm7k1udw55.rcgu.o`, 8 failed builds 2026-11-22 04:23-04:47Z, measured 2026-11-22 (session transcripts, `/tmp/t142/scan.py`))

- **Approach**: measured first, then the launcher heals the one crate the linker names:
  - HOW OFTEN, measured 2026-11-22 (`/tmp/t142/scan.py` and `scan2.py` over `~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl`, tool results holding a
    `rust-lld: error: undefined hidden symbol`, deduplicated by timestamp and symbol): the tool profile failed to link 10 times in one
    night - `l7r-rust` twice (02:47Z and 04:20Z, `l7r_shared`'s units 1lmunt73iiew8o59oo8g4kasl and 2n3yaxv6qj1cgib5jtzvnsyqu) and
    `l7r-gate` about 8 times (04:23-04:47Z, the one unit above, across the main session and five builders); before that only a test
    build, `l7r_gate_archive`'s lib test on 2026-11-19 01:18-01:25Z (four builds, the dev profile, also incremental). The guard log
    records no build (0 hits for `not built|build failed`, its newest 3,000 entries, measured 2026-11-22 (grep over `~/.claude/guard-log`)) and the launcher kept no build log; the guard's
    `build.log` holds only its last build (00:17, a 45 s timeout, measured 2026-11-22 (reading `build.log`)).
  - WHICH SESSION, measured 2026-11-22 (`llvm-nm -A` over every workspace rlib in `tool/deps`, `/tmp/t142/rlibcheck.sh`: an
    undefined `.llvm.<n>` symbol no member of the same rlib defines): one rlib of 148 crates' sets, `libl7r_gate_task-faf2a19073b9305a`,
    still broken at 00:15 local; its unit `ads6op1mfn3gc3gvm7k1udw55.o` is in session `incremental/l7r_gate_task-0y4ovoj4hibk7`
    (of the crate's 5, one per build variant), the object dated 2026-11-21 12:01 and reused into the rebuilds of 23:53, 00:14 and
    00:15. The CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 build that "cleared it" made a separate set (`l7r_gate_task-295557feace9901b`, its fingerprint's
    profile hash 7235404091355536516 against 5813646903328134276), so the bad incremental rlib kept a fresh fingerprint and came back
    at the next incremental build. The cause is rustc 1.87's incremental release with local ThinLTO reusing a unit's post-LTO object
    while the unit defining a symbol it imports is rebuilt under a new `.llvm.` suffix; nothing in this tree's code.
  - CONCURRENCY ruled out, measured 2026-11-22 (`flock -n tool/.cargo-lock` while a scratch build ran: rc 1, held): cargo holds that
    lock for each build, so two clones' landings, a builder and the main session serialize on one target dir; the guard's `timeout 45`
    kills the build's whole process group, and rustc finalizes an incremental session only on success.
  - REPRODUCED in a scratch copy of the cache (`/tmp/t142/target`, copied 2026-11-22 00:14, the real cache untouched): the copy's
    `faf2a19073b9305a` rlib held the same undefined symbol; a rebuild after a neighbor's `l7r_shared` edit recompiled the crate and
    cleared it (3 m 42 s, the whole chain, load 48, measured 2026-11-22 (`time cargo build`, `/tmp/t142/b1.log`)); the planted old rlib could not be relinked (`crate required to be available in
    rlib format`: its SVH no longer matches), so the retry is pinned on a stub cargo, which prints rust-lld's text.
  - THE FIX (`scripts/gates/l7r-gate.sh`): a build whose error holds `undefined hidden symbol` takes each `<crate>-<meta>.<unit>.rcgu.o`
    the linker names, drops the incremental session holding that unit (`incremental/<crate>-*/s-*/<unit>.o`'s crate directory) and
    `.fingerprint/<crate>-<meta>`, under cargo's own `tool/.cargo-lock`, prints what it dropped, and rebuilds once incrementally; a
    link error that names no unit rebuilds once with CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0; a second failure is refused as before with the cargo text.
    The rust-lld lines are shown, not the thousands-of-words link line. The drop is the task line's own "dropping that crate's
    incremental session": only the directories the linker names, never `incremental/` or the target wholesale.
  - REBUILD TIMES, measured 2026-11-22 (`/tmp/t142/time.sh`: a scratch copy of `rust/` at `/tmp/t142/clone` built into
    `/tmp/t142/target2`, one real function appended to the crate, the launcher timed, load 15-22): the task crate 7.1-8.8 s through
    HEAD's launcher, 6.2-8.2 s through T142's (unchanged: the new code runs only on a failed link); `l7r_gate_core` 5.3-8.3 s and
    4.5-4.9 s, measured 2026-11-22 (`/tmp/t142/time.sh`); the heal itself, dropping `l7r_gate_task`'s session and fingerprint and rebuilding, 4.8 s (the real cache's copy, load
    32), measured 2026-11-22 (`time cargo build`, `/tmp/t142/b3.log`). Always non-incremental, rejected on this measurement (T95's own call kept), measured 2026-11-22 (`/tmp/t142/time.sh` with CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0): the task crate, a leaf, 6.7-8.1 s, about the
    same, but `l7r_gate_core` 83.0-106.8 s and `l7r_shared` 98.2-115.9 s against 4.9 s and 4.3 s incremental, and the first
    CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 build of a set 107.8 s. A test-file edit costs the tool build nothing (0.1 s, measured 2026-11-22 (`/tmp/t142/time.sh` on `set_down/tests.rs`): `#[cfg(test)]` modules are
    not in its dep-info), so "only test files changed" was the neighbors' non-test edits recompiling the crate.
  - WHY CLEARING THE CACHES DID NOT HELP 449 T244 (its builder's note, 449 T245 folded here), measured 2026-11-22 (its transcript's
    commands, 04:20-04:21Z): it removed `incremental/l7r_shared-*`, `l7r_rust-*`, `l7r_gate_core-*` and the rest, but not their
    fingerprints, so cargo kept the broken rlib as fresh, never recompiled it, and relinked the same undefined symbol; only a
    separate CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 set linked. The stale state is the rlib behind a fresh fingerprint, not the session alone: in the
    scratch copy the broken `faf2a19073b9305a` rlib, restored with its stale session and an out-of-date fingerprint, was recompiled
    incrementally and linked clean (8.3 s, `rlibcheck.sh` then empty), measured 2026-11-22 (`/tmp/t142/e2e.log`). No codegen or LTO
    flag differs between builds of one crate: the two task-crate sets' fingerprints differ only in their profile hash (incremental
    on or off), with the same rustflags, features and target, measured 2026-11-22 (`.fingerprint/*/lib-l7r_gate_task.json`); the
    profile's `lto` default (local ThinLTO across 256 units) is what makes the `.llvm.` names, and `lto = "off"` stays rejected by
    T95's measurement (15-40% slower to run, observed 2026-11-11, method: scratchpad/t95/bench.py, as `rust/Cargo.toml` records).

### T147 (a landing refused on another task's open plan-review passes, which only that task's landing writes; the first pass took no escape)

- **Approach**: measured first, then the rule moved into the one owed set every refusal reads (`reviews`' `ledger_passes/left.rs`),
  and `make land`'s first pass asks it with the tasks it lands:
  - HOW THE PASSES WERE CHOSEN, measured 2026-11-22 (reading `cheap.rs`, `ledger_passes.rs`, `rows.rs`, `trace.rs`): never by the
    landing's tasks. The first pass writes (`write_ledger`) every owed MODE 4 pass whose reply quotes a recorded verdict or whose
    feature's `plan-review.json` holds its task's verdict dated that day (`--write-plan-reviews`, any feature, any task), then every
    pass `trace::belongs` ties to the landing's feature (`--write specs/<n>-.../`, any task of it); then it refused on any `| ? |`
    left, with no escape. The push's `ledger-owed --refuse` row and `make land-tooling` refuse on the same set, `LEDGER_ROWS_OK` their
    escape. By hand, `make ledger-owed WRITE=` refuses a recorded plan review as the landing's own (451 T105).
  - THE CROSS-FEATURE CASE, reproduced: 4 of 449's plan reviews (T158, T241, T250, T197) stayed owed after a 451 landing's two
    writes, measured 2026-11-22 (a worktree at the clone's HEAD bdb111b827, the two writes run on its ledger): their verdicts are
    uncommitted in the clone, so not in the landing worktree's record, their replies quote none, and 451's write traces none of them.
  - THE WITHIN-FEATURE CASE, not reproduced as a plan-review refusal: the 449 T244 landing attempts' ledger commits wrote T158's,
    T203's, T241's and T243's plan-review rows themselves (6 + 2 rows in 70a2773d0c, 4 + 1 in 4d2e56a7e9, 3 + 1 in a8b34d9e44,
    3 + 1 in e73cf5fded), measured 2026-11-22 (`git show` of the landing worktree's reflog commits); a 449 landing at HEAD left 0
    plan reviews owed and 86 other passes, measured 2026-11-22 (the same worktree, 449's two writes). Those 86 (impl-drift
    `DECIDE_OK` dispatches, workflow units, modal and record checks no subject ties to a feature) are what refused - no landing
    writes them; `make ledger-owed WRITE=` from the session that ran them does, and its rows must be committed before a landing
    alone sees them (70 still owed with the clone's 46 uncommitted rows added, measured 2026-11-22, the same worktree).
  - THE RULE (`left.rs`): a refusal (`--refuse`, or `--landing`) leaves out a MODE 4 pass whose subject names its feature and task
    where that feature's specs directory is here, the task is ticked in neither `tasks.md` nor `tasks-done.md` (absence counts as
    open: land-alone commits a task's own lines only, de7ecc7de4) and is not one the landing lands (`--landing <feature dir>
    --tasks "<ids>"`); it says which open tasks it left, on stdout, refusing nothing for them. A block review (no task), a ticked
    task's, a feature absent here, and every other pass still refuse, with `make ledger-owed WRITE=` named. The listing by hand
    (no `--refuse`) names every pass. At the push the landing's tasks are ticked, so its own passes refuse there too.

    writer appends it with `append_row_with`, the hooks' writer. The run's make target is `shared::make::outermost_goal`, the landing's
    `/proc` walk moved there so every writer reads it one way (its test moved with it).
  - THE WRITERS (decision: in process where a Rust tool already runs the step, a recipe's span through the shell's one door
    `l7r-gate measure event-log phase` otherwise):

      write theirs too, both running `make hooks-test`;

      `generate`, `render` and `page` cut at each staged artifact's mtime (svg, png, html), a deliberate reading labeled at the point
      of change: an edit of the engines to report their own timings moves every map's engine id for a measurement;
    - the gate's phases (`src: gate`, the phase its step - `seeds`, `counters-inert`, `preflight`, `static`, `format`, `reference`,
      `hooks-test`): `measure runstats phase|phase-pre`, which `make done` already called per phase, write the line in process given the
      tree (`$(CURDIR)`), no process added;
    - `make record`, `make quick`, `make preflight`, `make cohort` (`src` the target): the Makefile's `TIMED` macro (quick's checks moved
      to `_quick`, timed whole);
    - page sessions (`src: page-session`, `step: write|check`, `name` the session id): `pages/src/runner/work.rs`, filed by the
      runner's own environment.
  - THE READERS (`where_time/columns.rs`): `category` books each line - compile (`build`, `cover-build`), hook suites, map generation
    (a map's steps, a cohort, the gate's seeds and reference), tests (the checks' `test` and `cover-run`, quick, preflight, counters),
    gate (a landing's), docs (record, a page session's write) and review (its check); a container (a landing's `end`, `static`,
    `hooks-test`, a lint) none. `lint` and `format` (the checks' `rust` lines, the gate's `format`) are booked to no category,
    a decision: a lint's clippy is compile and check in one process with no seam a line can mark, and rustfmt is neither, so booking
    either to compile or tests would misstate one of them; their seconds stay in the holding run's own bucket, as before T153 (a
    lint's own `build` line, where kept.rs builds first, is still booked to compile). `Split` is a run's phases by category, carved first first (`PHASE_COLUMNS`: compile, hook suites, map
    generation, tests, gate, docs, review) so parallel suites count once and no second twice; the runs table, the critical path and the
    flight book through it, and both tables gain `hook suites` and `map generation` columns (`feature-report` reads the same columns
    through `where_time::columns_text`). A page session, detached, is held by no Bash run: booked under its task directly, never loose.

### T153 Performance checklist (docs/performance-checklist.md - prompts, never a gate; time is the goal, calls the measure)

`caller-files` mtime to its `hooks-test.exit` mtime, the jobs counted from `hooks-test.log`'s `ran` line) pays about 0.16 s, 0.2%, and a map step pays one in-process line (about 2 ms, the same measurement) on a draw of hundreds of ms (measured 2026-11-22, the county-magistracy-example lines above), a CACHED map one line.

### T156 (the Stop hook's free-slot count misread five live builder descriptions on 2026-11-22, the session's note)

- **Approach**: the Stop hook's free-slot check (`set_down_hooks.rs` `free_slot`, its builders read by `set_down_hooks/builders.rs`) reads a builder's brief as the session writes it, and a landing in flight holds the slots. (a) `builder_brief` takes the feature number and every task id before the description's first colon, words between allowed (449 T268 already took `449 bundle T259, T277:`; pinned here), and a range `T289-T300` is each of its members, its first id's width kept (`T02-T04`); a range written backwards, with a letter, or wider than `SPAN` (200, a CONVENTION past the widest bundle seen, twelve) is its two ends, as before. (b) A running agent whose description names a landing before its colon (`449 batch landing: ...`), or whose prompt's first line runs `make land` (never `land-tooling` or `land-stop`), is a LANDER: `builders` returns it beside the builders, and `free_slot` names no task-start while one runs. A landing brief naming neither reads as no lander, by rule: it fails toward a start the session sees named, never a hidden hold. (c) A landing PROCESS in this clone holds the slots too: `landing_process` walks `/proc` (`L7R_PROC_ROOT` in tests) for a process whose working directory is the clone or its landing worktree (`<clone>-land`) running `l7r-gate land` (not `--stop`) or `land-alone.sh` - the land crate's `stop::landing_pids` shape; the land crate is not the shared crate's to import, so the few lines are read here. (d) Found while testing: a running builder's own tasks, a bundle member never task-started among them (T289-T300's ten between), could be named the next start; `next_independent` skips them now (fixed here).

### T158 Performance checklist (docs/performance-checklist.md - prompts, never a gate; time is the goal, calls the measure)

### T155 (a TRIAL, measured 2026-11-22: the task line said a landing recompiles what the clone already built - 117 min of make land phases over 6 landings, 28 of them coverage builds - because cargo's fingerprints carry each tree's absolute path, so the landing worktree's own target directory cannot use the clone's builds)

- **Approach**: a measurement, no code changed. The question: how much of a landing's build recompiles what the clone's closing checks already built for the same content, and does a content-keyed compilation cache (sccache) or building the landing at the clone's own path remove it? **Verdict: build neither.** (a) sccache removes nothing: it hit 0 times across the two paths, and the coverage build, which is most of a landing's compile, is uncacheable under it. (b) Building at the clone's path saves little: every file the landing's checkout writes is newer than the clone's build, so it is rebuilt anyway. And it is unsound: a file the checkout did not write, older than the clone's build of a different copy, is reused silently - a tree holding a failing test passed coverage clean. Every figure below is machine minutes summed over rustc calls, which overlap. The host was at load 44-50 on 22 cores, so per-unit times run 2-5x an idle host's, measured 2026-11-22 (`uptime` during the runs, and the same units' times across the pairs' logs).
  - **Why a landing compiles at all** (measured 2026-11-22). Method: the clone's event logs, every `Phase` line with `t0` from 2026-11-22T05:00Z. For each `land gate` (17), each `rust` lint, cover-build or build line inside it was matched against the clone's own green (code 0) lint or cover-build lines that ran between the previous landing's end and this one's start and named any of the same crates. The landings' Rust build steps came to 90.6 min, measured 2026-11-22 (the clone's land Phase lines from 05:00Z, matched to its own green lint and cover-build lines between landings). 49.3 min were on crates the clone had checked green in that window, measured 2026-11-22 (the clone's land Phase lines from 05:00Z, matched to its own green lint and cover-build lines between landings). 30.9 min were on crates it never checked green there, measured 2026-11-22 (the clone's land Phase lines from 05:00Z, matched to its own green lint and cover-build lines between landings). 10.4 min were the counting build (`test-counters`), which no closing check runs, measured 2026-11-22 (the clone's land Phase lines from 05:00Z, matched to its own green lint and cover-build lines between landings). Only the 49.3 is reachable by sharing the clone's builds, about 2.9 min a gate, measured 2026-11-22 (the clone's land Phase lines from 05:00Z, matched to its own green lint and cover-build lines between landings). Even that is not all duplicate, because a kept result is keyed by contents (`rustc/kept.rs`) and `land-alone.sh` step 5 seeds the clone's kept results: a crate the clone checked green with the landing's contents is not run or compiled at the landing at all. A landing compiles a crate for one of three reasons: the clone's tree held other tasks' uncommitted edits in it or a crate it builds on; the clone's run of it was red; or a crate the landing must run builds on it. The 17 gates' wall time was 103.9 min, of which the union of their Rust phases was 85.8, measured 2026-11-22 (the gate lines against the union of the phase spans inside them). The other 18 min is unbooked: the gate tool builds and the non-Rust phases, measured 2026-11-22 (the gate lines against the union of the phase spans inside them).
  - **The controlled pairs** (measured 2026-11-22 19:20-20:10 EST). The clone itself was dirty: 10 uncommitted files in `rust/gate/crates/registry` and `rust/mode_a`, observed 2026-11-22 (`git status --short -- rust/`). So two scratch worktrees stood in for the two sides: `/tmp/t155/t155clone` played the clone and `/tmp/t155/t155land` played the landing, each with its own target directory (`~/.cache/l7r-cargo-target/<basename>`). Both were warmed at 61e8b7b20f (the landing before HEAD: lint, cover, dead, and test-counters on the landing side) and then moved to 1dffe4d5af (HEAD, the last landing). Each step ran as `scripts/gates/l7r-gate.sh rust <step>`, not `make done`, because `make done` commits its run record. The clone side ran closing checks' Rust steps (lint, cover, dead). The landing side was seeded from the clone side's kept results as `land-alone.sh` step 5 does (`cp -a -u`), then ran lint, cover, dead and test-counters. Every rustc call was logged by a `RUSTC_WRAPPER` in front of the gate's own wrappers (`/tmp/t155/bin/logrustc`), with crate, kind, `--test`, wrapper, features and span, and from pair 2 on the profile (pair 1's tool and debug units were told apart by hand from the crates and the step). A landing unit counts as a DUPLICATE when the clone side compiled the same crate, kind, mode, features and profile and neither the crate nor any workspace crate it builds on differed between the two trees (`/tmp/t155/bin/dup2.py`). The two ignored magistracy sheets 451 T159 names were copied in from the clone. `mode_a`'s pool sweep was still red in both trees at both commits on those copies (`county-magistracy-example.svg`, left `(Some(0), Some(1))`), so its result was never kept. That is T159's family (an ignored generated sheet a test reads), not filed again.
    - Pair 1, a clean clone at the landing's commit: the landing compiled 4.2 min, and the duplicate was 0.66 - the `l7r-rust` tool binary, rebuilt in each target directory (shared, core, tree and rustc crates in the tool profile), measured 2026-11-22 (pair 1's rustc logs, `rustc-C1-*.tsv`). Another 1.70 was `mode_a`'s coverage build again, because the clone side's run was red on the copied sheets; a crate red in the clone does not land, so that is not counted as a duplicate, measured 2026-11-22 (pair 1's rustc logs, `rustc-C1-*.tsv`). The other 1.5 was its own: the counting build. Lint and every green crate's cover compiled nothing: each was reused from the seeded results. Wall: landing lint 34 s and cover 64 s, against the clone side's 110 s and 169 s, measured 2026-11-22 (`rustc-C1-*.tsv`, `times.txt`).
    - Pair 2, a dirty clone. Both trees took the same task edit, a comment appended to `gate/crates/core/src/lib.rs`. The clone side also took the clone's real uncommitted `registry` and `mode_a` diff of 19:20, and the landing a red probe in a registry test. The landing compiled 82 units, 14.2 min, in lint and cover: 5.15 duplicate (30 rlibs of crates the dirty pair does not reach), 7.82 on crates built against the other registry (same names, different inputs), 1.24 its own, measured 2026-11-22 (pair 2's rustc logs, `rustc-C2-*.tsv`, through `dup2.py`). The core comment was appended by hand to both trees before the clone side built, where a real landing gets the task's edit by checkout, newer than the clone's build; that part of the duplicate is the setup's, measured 2026-11-22 (pair 2's rustc logs, `rustc-C2-*.tsv`, through `dup2.py`). Wall: lint 8 s and cover 169 s, measured 2026-11-22 (`rustc-C2-*.tsv`, `times.txt`).
  - **(a) sccache** (measured 2026-11-22). sccache 0.13.0+ds-3build1, not in the container before: Ubuntu's archive package, installed for this trial (`apt-get install sccache`), with nothing else downloaded, `SCCACHE_DIR` under `/tmp/t155`. A toy workspace of two path crates, built at two paths: incremental builds are never cached ("incremental": 4 of 4), test binaries never ("crate-type"), and a second path missed every unit that a second build at the first path hit (2 of 2). The real gate, `rust cover --crate rust/gate/crates/tree` with `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0` and sccache inside the logging wrapper, at the clone side's path and then the landing side's: 4 cacheable misses at each path (the tool profile's four rlibs) and 0 hits at the second, measured 2026-11-22 (`scc-stats.txt`, sccache's own stats per run). Every coverage unit was "multiple input files", not cached: cargo hands sccache the gate's `RUSTC_WORKSPACE_WRAPPER` script (`cover.rs`'s `workspace_only`, 449 T100) as the compiler and rustc as an input. The run's verdicts were unchanged. Lint under sccache was not measured. The red probe (`assert_eq!(1 + 1, 3, "T155 red probe")` in tree's `a_rust_only_change_starts_none_of_the_python_checks`) failed cover, exit 1. Restored, it was clean, and both paths' runs were clean, measured 2026-11-22 (`scc-stats.txt`, `scc-*.out`). sccache 0.13 has no base-directory option (`strings` of the binary: no `BASEDIR`). The landing tree then sat at the clone's path, and `l7r-gate.sh` keyed it the clone's target directory. The clone's next run then recompiled 0.8 min that its own tree had built before (registry's test binary, research), measured 2026-11-22 (`rustc-C2-same.tsv`, `rustc-C2-clone-after.tsv`). **It is unsound.** Cargo judges a path crate fresh when no source file is newer than its last build, and the two trees' files at one path break that. The landing's tests would run the clone builders' code, not the commit's. On pair 2 the registry probe was caught because `l7r_shared`, which registry builds on, was rebuilt from the newer checkout, not because cargo saw the probe; the tree test shows the case with nothing upstream to rescue it. Stable cargo 1.87 has no content-keyed freshness (`-Zchecksum-freshness` is nightly). **Saves at most the units built only from files the checkout did not write - a third of pair 2's, an upper bound with the setup's hand edit in it - and exactly those are the units it can reuse wrongly. Weakens the gate: a red tree lands green.** Not proposed.

It runs the mirror's `l7r-guard.sh` if that file is executable, else the copy beside itself. `setup` runs the mirror's `setup-dev-env.sh --ensure` by bash if that file exists, else the tree's. Its header holds the reasons the commands carried: the timeout above the wrapper's 45 s build limit (449 T005, `L7R_GUARD_BUILD_SECS`'s default in `l7r-guard.sh`, a knob), and the setup hook's 2026-10-04 ruling. `CLONE_MAIN` is its test seam for the mirror, as in `sync-with-main.sh`.

  - **The launcher is held as a guard file** on both routes, because it now decides what the settings' commands decided. `guard_file_hooks.rs` holds it through `GUARD_SOURCE`, beside `l7r-guard.sh`. `make_only_hooks.rs` holds it through `GUARD_FILE` and the `SOURCE_NAMES` screen. Its name is `l7r-hook`, not `run`: make-only screens a command by substring before walking it, and `run` would have sent most commands through the walk.
  - **The wave replay** (`workflow_hooks.rs`) now runs a tree's settings commands with `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` set to that tree. The new command reads that variable. The old one read it only when the mirror had no dispatcher. Without the change, a session whose project directory lacked the launcher would replay every command as exit 127, and the unit would go through unguarded.

### T171 (observed 2026-11-23: the coordinator's Stops were refused again and again in the same words - 268 make-run refusals ("A MAKE RUN THIS SESSION STARTED IS STILL GOING") in its session, each stored twice in its transcript, which the task line counted as about 550, and 134 set-down refusals since 2026-11-20, measured 2026-11-23 (the session transcript's `stop_hook_summary` records of `l7r-guard`, `/tmp/t171/stops.py`); most named a builder's own gate or a builder the slot count did not see)

- **Approach**: three fixes, each in the guard that said the block.
  - A RUN A BUILDER STARTED IS THE BUILDER'S (`rust/guard/src/guards/finished_run_hooks.rs`, `finished_run_hooks/runs.rs`, `set_down_hooks.rs`'s `alive`). `launch_of` reads the launch line's agent and its session id. A launch line of another session is `Starter::Session`, a `Status::Session` run: this session's turn closes, and the context line names that session. `set_down_hooks::still_running` follows an agent the session's transcript never names up its meta's `parentAgentId` (`alive`, at most `HOPS` 4, a CONVENTION), so a run a builder's own sub-agent started is waited on while that sub-agent runs, and judged as a detached run once it has stopped. `Procs::gone` drops a pid whose `stat` is gone or a zombie's, asked after its status: a run that ended while `/proc` was read is no run.
  - A BUILDER NO BRIEF NAMES HOLDS A SLOT (`rust/guard/shared/src/guards/set_down_hooks/builders.rs`). `builders()` returns `Running { named, unnamed, landing }`. `unnamed_builder` is an agent the session dispatched (`spawnDepth` 1) of the type `general-purpose` whose brief `builder_brief` does not read as a builder's. The free-slot count adds them, each its own slot, and lists each as "a builder (no task named)".
  - AN UNCHANGED REFUSAL IS SAID ONCE (`rust/guard/shared/src/once.rs`, NEW, `pub mod once;` in `shared/src/lib.rs`; wired in `set_down_hooks::judge` under the key `set-down` and `finished_run_hooks::judge` under `finished-run`). A guard's refusal is said in full the first time. A repeat whose text is unchanged (its SHA-256 kept in `<git dir>/l7r-said/<session id>.json`) is one line, `still: <its first 8 words> - unchanged since HH:MM` (UTC), and is still a refusal (exit 2). A changed text, or a block back after a Stop that passed without it, is said in full again. A payload with no session id, or a record that cannot be read or written, says it in full: the summary saves words, never a refusal.
  - A COMPACTION FORGETS WHAT WAS SAID (`once::forget`). A SessionStart whose `source` is `compact`, `clear` or `resume` removes `<git dir>/l7r-said/<session id>.json`, so the next Stop says each block in full, its fix command with it. Both guards now take SessionStart (`set_down_hooks` and `finished_run_hooks`), each forgetting the record under the root it says its own blocks from, and refusing or reporting nothing on it. A `startup`, or a SessionStart naming no source, forgets nothing: a new session id has no record. `.claude/settings.json`'s SessionStart entry has no matcher, so every source reaches the guard and the settings are unchanged, observed 2026-11-23, method: `jq '.hooks.SessionStart'` of the settings.
- **Decisions**:
  - D1. NO TIME-WINDOW MATCHER FOR DETACHED RUNS. A detached run (no harness ancestor, no launch line) cannot be tied to a builder by its pid. Matching it to the builder whose launch came shortly before it would be a guess, and a wrong match lets a turn close over a run nothing watches, the 2026-09-12 incident the guard exists for. The class is also gone. Since T164 landed (2026-11-23 03:15 UTC), a builder's verify gate runs in `<clone>-review`, which `live_runs(clone)` does not own (the nearest enclosing working tree), and 451 T15's `no_poll` refuses any other detached make or cargo run. So the 8 detached verify-gate refusals since 2026-11-22, 6 of them a builder's, cannot recur in the clone. Since T164 there was 1 make-run refusal, the vanished-pid race fixed here, measured 2026-11-23 (each refusal's pids against the event log's launch lines, `/tmp/t171/launch.py`, `/tmp/t171/who.py`).
  - D2. A TYPED CHECK AGENT TAKES NO SLOT. This is an exception to the task line's literal words, "an agent whose description names no task still counts as a builder": the rule is narrowed to the `general-purpose` type at `spawnDepth` 1. The type is the narrowest rule that counts the first and not the second. Counting a round arbiter would read three builders running with a builder slot truly free and let the turn end, the empty slot T88 was filed to fill.

### T171 Approach (checklist part A)

1. **The goal, in the world.** A Stop refusal says something the session needs. A run a builder or another session started is left to its starter, a run already ended is no run, a builder whose brief names no task holds its slot, and an unchanged refusal is said in one line until something changes, in full again after a compaction.
2. **The constraints.** FR-013 (the builders' loop faster). The GM on hook output, 2026-11-23: "That amount of output consumes tokens, so could we accomplish the same thing with no loss of fidelity and fewer tokens?" So the one-line repeat is still a refusal, and a block back after a passing Stop carries its command again, as does a block after a compaction, whose context may have lost the full text (constitution XIII: no known regression). The GM 2026-09-12 (docs/guards.md, the finished-run row): a run nothing watches is never abandoned, hence no matcher (D1). T88's rule on what a builder is (D2). T85's reading of a builder's run (its launch line's `by`) is kept and extended, not replaced.
3. **Where each comes from.** G: the GM's words above (2026-11-23 and 2026-09-12). O: the table above (the coordinator's Stops replayed, 2026-11-23). O: T88's and T164's plan sections.
4. **Do they describe the world here?** Yes. They were measured on the coordinator's own Stops in this clone, its transcript against the event log.
5. **The order.** After T164 (the review tree, which D1 rests on) and T169 (the hook launcher the suites run through). Nothing waits on it.
6. **The exits.** Green: the guard crates' tests, the set-down and finished-run suites, the closing checks, MODE 4 CLEAR. Red: what failed recorded and the task set down, a claim that it cannot be done ruled through `make arbiter-ask`.

### T171 Performance checklist (docs/performance-checklist.md - prompts, never a gate; time is the goal, calls the measure)

1. **Where does the time go?** Into the coordinator's turns and context. Each Stop refusal is read and answered by the model, and its whole text stays in the transcript: 35,829 characters of Stop blocks since 2026-11-22, measured 2026-11-23 (`/tmp/t171/fix3.py`). A refusal that should never have been said also costs a turn, and there were 17 of 79 since 2026-11-22: 10 make-run refusals (the 8 verify gates T164 removed, the 2 races fix 1 removes) and 7 slot refusals (the table above).
2. **Removes work, or only moves it?** It removes work. The 2 race refusals and the 7 slot refusals are not said at all (T164 already removed the 8 verify-gate ones), and 28 unchanged repeats are one line instead of the full block.
3. **What do you expect it to save, and why?** About a third of the Stop blocks' characters (32% on the replay) and a turn for each refusal removed, measured 2026-11-23 (the table above). The cost is one small JSON file read and written per refusing Stop. The replay did not model compactions: each one has its next refusal said in full again, so the cut is that much smaller.
4. **How does the work grow with the settlement?** It does not. This is tooling, and it grows with a session's Stops, not with the size of a settlement.
5. **What did the before and after show, and under what conditions?** The replay above, on the coordinator's own Stops from the event log and the transcript. It counts refusals and characters, not time, so the host's load does not enter. This is evidence, not a pass.
6. **Did any map move, and does it still keep the research?** No map moved: guard code only.

### T175 (observed 2026-11-23: 451 T170's builder was refused every `rust/` edit in the clone by 449's building-reviews, which read the review tree `<clone>-review` since 451 T164; the guard log holds 20 engine-freeze refusals that day, all edits in the clone, 18 of them while every live review read the review tree, measured 2026-11-23 by `make guard-log GUARD=engine-freeze SINCE=2026-11-23` against each review transcript's first and last record and its prompt's `Review tree:` line, `/tmp/t175/firings.log`)

- **Approach**: `engine_freeze_hooks` held an engine edit in any tree the session owns while any map review it launched ran. Since T164 a review reads its own review tree, a worktree at a commit, which an edit in the clone cannot change. The guard now reads the tree each live review reads from its dispatch prompt, the first record of its transcript: the text between `Review tree: ` and `, a worktree at ` (`review_tree`). `live_reviews` returns each review's line with that tree, and `judge` keeps a review only when it names no tree or the edit's path (realpath, compared by components, so `<clone>` is not a prefix of `<clone>-review`) is inside its tree. A tree that is not absolute or has no `.git` now counts as no tree, so a malformed or removed tree keeps today's rule: refuse. The filter runs before the engine-edit question, so a clone edit under reviews that read their own tree starts no `l7r-gate` process. The rolls are unchanged: they run in the clone and keep freezing it. The refusal's words are unchanged (only the reviews and rolls holding the edit are listed), so no message-check is owed. The 105 map-review transcripts on disk all open on a `user` record with a string prompt; the 22 that name a review tree all parse to `/diagram/.clones/diagram-backlog-review`, which exists. `docs/guards.md`'s row is the session's to apply once 451 T170 lands; its text is in the handoff `.git/l7r-handoffs/T175-ad1f9ea1ecdfee6b8.md`.

| step | figure | what it says |
|---|---|---|
| before | 20 refusals on 2026-11-23, all clone edits; 18 under reviews that all read the review tree, 2 (01:26, 01:30) under reviews with no tree, measured 2026-11-23 (the method above) | 18 refusals held edits the reviews could not see |
| after | the same shapes in the suites: a clone edit under a tree-reading review passes; an edit in the review tree, a clone edit under a review naming no tree, and a clone edit under a roll are refused, measured 2026-11-23 (`tests/hooks/test-engine-freeze-hooks.sh` 41/41, the guard crate's 488 tests) | the 18 pass, the 2 are still refused |

### T177 (observed 2026-11-23, 451 T170's census: 255 guard wordings stood BASELINE, unreviewed, in `dev/guard-messages.tsv`; ranked by measured cost a session, `/tmp/t177/scripts/rank3.py`, the run of 2026-11-23T11:06:39Z)

- **Approach**: rank the BASELINE wordings by what a session pays for them, review them in that order through the typed `message-check` agent, one wording an agent (at most three at once), cut what fails, and stop where a review buys too little. The ranking, the cuts and the stop are below; the stop is a decision for MODE 4. No Makefile change: a round's units are `make guard-messages BUNDLE=1`'s MANIFEST split at `## KEY`, each with the full text it replaced appended (`/tmp/t177/scripts/units.sh`, `oldtext.py`, `oldtext3.py`).

**THE RANKING, measured 2026-11-23** (`/tmp/t177/scripts/rank3.py` over the coordinator's transcript `c6fd72d1-....jsonl`, 174,714,017 bytes, 2026-11-17 to 23, and its 1,658 subagent transcripts - "a session" below is that whole session; the full ranking `/tmp/t177/baseline-ranking.tsv`). Method: both sides masked as the record masks a wording, then relative paths and feature slugs; each wording found by its first 8 such words, the longest common prefix ruling a tie; a Stop text split at its blank lines. An occurrence is priced at its length before T177 - its span, capped at the suites' rendering, or for a family T170 capped as a list at its worst case - and a Stop block said again unchanged at T171's one-line repeat (70 characters; 28 of set-down's 94 builder-slot blocks). Rows sharing their first 8 words are one FAMILY, summed, since one cut re-keys every member. Of the hook texts read, 875,725 of the coordinator's 920,070 characters and 1,974,133 of its builders' 2,306,255 matched a recorded wording (the residue is mostly wordings T170 cut, user-level hooks and guards no suite renders); the 255 BASELINE wordings fall in 168 families, 879,048 characters a session, 55 of them seen.

| # | family (guard, kind) | shown | priced characters a session | BASELINE keys |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | make-only's guard-file refusal (`make_only_hooks`, refuse) | 178 | 139,141 | 1 |
| 2 | finished-run's detached-run Stop block (`finished_run_hooks`, refuse) | 269 | 126,997 | 4 |
| 3 | builder-stop's not-decided block (`builder_stop_hooks`, block) | 210 | 107,940 | 1 |
| 4 | context-cap's builder refusal (`context_cap_hooks`, refuse) | 130 | 90,785 | 1 |
| 5 | no-poll's busy-wait refusal (`no_poll_hooks`, refuse) | 110 | 54,560 | 1 |
| 6 | static-runs' closing-order notice (`static_runs_hooks`, notice) | 97 | 46,711 | 2 |
| 7 | blocked-fetch's attempts notice (`blocked_fetch_hooks`, notice) | 368 | 38,272 | 1 |
| 8 | set-down's builder-slot block (`set_down_hooks`, refuse) | 94 (28 repeats) | 28,690 | 2 |
| 9 | guard-file's root-Makefile notice (`guard_file_hooks`, notice) | 64 | 27,904 | 1 |
| 10 | make-only's cargo refusal (`make_only_hooks`, refuse) | 66 | 27,812 | 1 |

**THE PRICE OF A REVIEW, measured 2026-11-23.** A review costs R = 14.4k tokens: every `message-check` dispatch of the three rounds read 14k tokens in (6k to 10k of it cached) and wrote 0.3k to 0.7k out (`make review-cost`, e.g. ab9b70f54e3ec0099, a92df90484ef842d4, a91ac500286d36459). A token is rho = 2.2 characters of a guard message: the median over 703 guard refusals the builders read, each the rise in the next model call's context (input, cache read and cache creation) less the call's own output, the quartiles 2.12 and 2.20 (`/tmp/t177/scripts/rho.py`, `GUARD=1`, over the 1,658 subagent transcripts). So one review is R x rho = 31,680 characters, and a family of k BASELINE keys, one review a key, costs k x 31,680 a round. THE CONVENTIONS: both sides count a token once as it enters a context (T170's measure); the review's cached input counts in full; a session's re-reads of a message still in its context are not counted, which would raise every saving; the reviews run on Sonnet and the sessions on Opus, priced alike here.

**THE ROUNDS - every first review failed, so every cut cost at least two.** Round 1 (6 reviews, the families 1 to 5 and 7): 6 of 6 FAILED. Round 2 (14 reviews: those cuts at their suites' renderings and worst cases, plus the two list messages T177 holds at their worst case): 8 PASS, 6 FAIL - four the second FAIL on their subject, two the first. Each second FAIL is the tripwire, so the round arbiter ruled first, twice: `ask:guard-wordings-third-round` (afeb4afdca86f6f88, continue: two of the four reversed round 1's own fixes and siblings passed the forms faulted; blocked-fetch's one-attempt notice stands, three cut once more, each its LAST review) and `ask:guard-wordings-sleep-and-slot` (aad643ace8004667b, continue: the disguised sleep takes its original first line, the builder-slot block's three wordings stand). Round 3 (7 reviews): 4 PASS, 3 FAIL - all brevity alone, settled by the second ruling. Every verdict is recorded in `dev/guard-messages.tsv`, the replies in `/tmp/t177/r2replies/`, the rounds in `/tmp/t177/round-map.txt`. The second ruling ordered a tool, its `tooling_fix` in `arbiter.jsonl` verbatim: "In the message-check round logic, make the earlier ruling's cap (ask:guard-wordings-third-round) the standing rule: when a unit's second review FAILs on BREVITY alone and FIDELITY passes, the text as reviewed stands and its PASS is recorded automatically, with no arbiter ask." It is made here: `make guard-messages KEY=<key> VERDICT=BREVITY:<the key of the failed wording this text replaced>` records such a review as PASS, the text standing (`suite_tools/messages.rs` `second_review`, its test `a_second_review_failing_on_brevity_alone_passes_and_a_first_is_refused`; the FAILED tip names the form with its own key). What the tool checks and what its caller says: that the review is a SECOND is checked against the key it names - that key's row must be a FAIL of the same guard and kind, its wording rendered by nothing now, and named by no other second review, so one FAIL is the first of one second; or the verdict is refused as a first review's. The key is named because guard and kind alone hold several wordings (make-only's refusals, finished-run's four keys), so a FAIL of the kind would have passed a sibling's first review (MODE 4's second round, D6c). That the new text replaced that wording, and failed on brevity alone with FIDELITY passing, is the caller's reading of the reply, as with every verdict recorded. Its row is no reviewer's PASS: its `by` cell reads "<agent> (a second review failing on BREVITY alone - the text stands, the round arbiter's standing rule, ask:guard-wordings-sleep-and-slot; the first: <agent>, key <failed key>)", naming the ruling as the rows it ruled by hand name theirs (MODE 4's first round, D6b, read a bundle that left the `tooling_fix` out: see Found and left).

**THE CUTS, before and after, in characters a session** (after = before less each occurrence's measured change, old suite length less new, times shown - the paths and ids are the same on both sides):

| # | family | reviews | before | after | saved a session | reviews' cost | repaid in |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | make-only's guard-file refusal | 2 | 139,141 | 90,903 | 48,238 (821 -> 550, x 178) | 63,360 | 1.3 sessions |
| 2 | finished-run's Stop block | 7 | 126,997 | 96,869 | about 30,128 (x 269, about 112 a block: the header 12, and a run's output path, named once now, about 86 characters, with its 14) | 221,760 | 7.4 |
| 3 | builder-stop's not-decided block | 3 | 107,940 | 94,500 | 13,440 (514 -> 450, x 210) | 95,040 | 7.1 |
| 4 | context-cap's builder refusal | 2 | 90,785 | 75,965 | 14,820 (743 -> 629, x 130) | 63,360 | 4.3 |
| 5 | no-poll's busy-wait (and the disguised sleep, seen 0 times) | 3 + 2 | 54,560 | 36,410 | 18,150 (496 -> 331, x 110) | 158,400 | 8.7 |
| 7 | blocked-fetch's attempts notice | 3 | 38,272 | 54,832 | -16,560 (104 -> 149, x 368: round 1 failed its FIDELITY, a bare `Q unknown: unknown` line, and the legend that fixed it adds 45 characters) | 95,040 | never - a fidelity fix |
| 8 | set-down's builder-slot block | 4 | 28,690 | 26,380 | 2,310 (35, x 66 full blocks; its 28 repeats unchanged) | 126,720 | 55 |
| - | the pop-ups' batch refusal, at its worst case | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 (seen 0 times) | 31,680 | never |
| | **total** | **27** | **586,385** | **475,859** | **110,526 (18.8%)** | **855,360**, and the two rulings 282k tokens (620k characters) | 7.7 sessions, 13.3 with the rulings, measured 2026-11-23 (make review-cost and the ranking) |

The session's BASELINE wordings: 879,048 characters before, 768,522 after.

**THE STOP, a decision for MODE 4: a chosen horizon, not a break-even.** The draft line reviewed a family while its whole cost a session was at least k x 31,680 (one review a key), so that its review repaid in one session - a CHOICE of horizon, which neither the GM's words nor the rulings set: families 1 to 5 and 7 cleared it, 6 did not (46,711 < 2 x 31,680 = 63,360), nor any after. The line is worse than it assumed, measured 2026-11-23 (the rounds and cuts above): every cut cost at least TWO reviews a key, since every first review failed, and a cut returned 18.8% of its family's cost, not all of it. At a longer horizon the line moves: the cuts made repay in 1.3 to 55 sessions, two never, measured 2026-11-23 (the cuts table), and family 6 would in about 14, measured 2026-11-23 (0.188 x its 46,711 a session against four reviews' 126,720), within that range. So T177 STOPS at the families reviewed (and the two worst cases its text names) not on a repayment line but on what is left: of the other 161 families, 292,663 characters a session, measured 2026-11-23 (the ranking less the 7 families cut), 113 were never shown in the session, so a review of them returns nothing, and the 48 shown are wordings that work - a long message is no defect, and the GM's words of 2026-11-23 ask a question (fewer tokens with no loss of fidelity), not for every wording to be reviewed. They stay BASELINE as T170 recorded them. MODE 4 rules on this stop in place of the task's literal "the 255". The superseded rows (each cut's replaced wordings and their FAIL rows, rendered by nothing now) are deleted from the record by key.

| step | figure | what it says |
|---|---|---|
| before | 586,385 characters a session over the 7 families cut (879,048 over all 255 BASELINE wordings) | the ranking above, measured 2026-11-23 |
| after | 475,859 (768,522) | the same occurrences at the new suite lengths, measured 2026-11-23 by `make hooks-test`'s renderings |

### T177 Approach (checklist part A)

1. **The goal, in the world.** The guard messages a session pays for most say what their reader needs in fewer characters, each wording reviewed; the list-growing two T170 left are held at their worst case.
2. **The constraints.** FR-013 (the builders' loop faster). T170's record and budget check (`make guard-messages`, `dev/guard-messages.tsv`). `message-check`'s rubric: FIDELITY first - a fix command or escape is never cut. The tripwire on a check's third round, ruled by the round arbiter.
3. **Where each comes from.** G: the GM 2026-11-23 on hook output ("could we accomplish the same thing with no loss of fidelity and fewer tokens?"). O: the ranking, the review prices and the before and after above. O: the two rulings, `specs/451-time-retro-and-efficiency/arbiter.jsonl`.
4. **Do they describe the world here?** Yes: measured 2026-11-23 (the ranking over the coordinator's own session and builders of 2026-11-17 to 23, the cuts at the suites' renderings and worst cases of today's code).
5. **The order.** After T170 (the record and the check it fills). Before T174, which brings guard-file's Read notice and the bypassing Stop modes to the check (the notice appended to its line here).
6. **The exits.** Green: `make guard-messages` says every wording reviewed or baselined; the guard crates and `make hooks-test`'s suites green. Red: what failed recorded and the task set down, a claim that it cannot be done ruled through `make arbiter-ask`.
7. **The search smell.** none.
8. **The budget.** One landing.
9. **Done, measured.** 2026-11-23: `make guard-messages`: "292 wordings, each reviewed or baselined and within its budget". `make crate-checks` (test, lint, format): `rust/guard` 491 passed, `rust/guard/shared` 461 passed, `rust/gate/crates/plan` 173 passed (`/tmp/t177/crate-checks3.log`). `make hooks-test`: every T177 suite green; its one other red, l7r-gate.sh.1's "mode-a building-programs --check: the real page", is 449's open bundles', not T177's (observed 2026-11-23, method: its output, "docs/building-programs.md is STALE - run `make building-programs`", a page built from what those bundles edit - `rust/mode_a`, `pool/magistracies`, `docs/build*.md` - none of them a T177 file, by `make closing-checks`' split of the clone's files by task, `/tmp/t177/closing4.log`). RED FIRST: the cuts' crate tests changed before the guards (477 passed, 13 failed, `/tmp/t177/red1.log`), and the BREVITY tool's named key and ruling before its code (490 passed, 1 failed, `/tmp/t177/red3-guard.log`).
10. **Before moving a constant.** n/a.
11. **Before fitting things into room.** n/a.
12. **Before any fix.** A message's length is no defect; the cuts are performance work. Two defects found and fixed: finished-run's run with no output file was told to grep `(no file)`, a wait that never ends (now waited on by its pid, `while kill -0`, held in the worst case); builder-stop's crate-test gate fixture's quoting ate `make decide` (fixed with the suite's).

**THE CHANGES.** `make_only_hooks.rs` guard-write arm: no "ungated-sibling" clause, no "hour:383@4" example, no "If this fired" trailer. `finished_run_hooks.rs`: the header "IS STILL RUNNING; NOTHING WILL WAKE THIS SESSION FOR IT:"; a run's output named once, in its wait; a run with no output file waited on by its pid. `builder_stop_hooks.rs`: the gate's no-CLEAR why carries one sentence - the decide, the MODE 4 review it prints (its type, in the background, its notification waking the builder), the fix and the deferrals (the round arbiter's first ruling); "(feature 451 T84)" and "(recorded)" cut. `context_cap_hooks.rs`: the why one clause, no FR-006 or latency figures. `no_poll_hooks.rs`: the fix names `run_in_background: true` and `POLL_OK="<what you are waiting for, two words or more>"`; the busy-wait and the disguised sleep take no why. `blocked_fetch_hooks.rs`: the attempts head says what a line holds. `shared/checks/handle.rs` `batch_said` and `shared/guards/set_down_hooks.rs` `slot_said` (no "(feature 451 T88, L7R_BUILDERS=N)") and `builder_said` (a bundle past `listed::SHOWN` tasks said as its first and the `cat` of a kept file, where that is shorter), both held at their worst case in `suite_tools/messages/worst.rs` with the no-output-file run. `suite_tools/messages.rs`: `VERDICT=BREVITY:<failed key>`, the second ruling's tooling fix, its row naming the ruling and the failed key. `rust/gate/crates/plan/src/plan/bundle/rulings.rs`: a plan review's `rulings.md` carries a cited ruling's `tooling_fix` beside its ruling, why and what, the MANIFEST saying so (`bundle.rs`). Each cut's history is kept in a code comment.

**Found and left?**
- guard-file's notice on a Read of a guard file ("This is a GUARD file. An edit to it is refused unless..."), about 375 characters read 153 times, 57,375 characters a session over the builders, is rendered by no suite, so no review or budget reaches it (observed 2026-11-23, method: the ranking's residue and a grep of the suites' corpus). Not fixed here: it is T174's class (a guard's messages reaching the check). Filed as T174 (its line names it); lands before T22.
- a plan review's bundle carried each cited ruling's utc, ruling, why and what, but not the `tooling_fix` a block may decide under, so MODE 4's first round on this section ruled the BREVITY tool unordered though the second ruling ordered it (observed 2026-11-23, method: the round-1 bundle's `rulings.md` beside `arbiter.jsonl`). Fixed here: `bundle/rulings.rs` `FIELDS` carries `tooling_fix`, red first (`rulings/tests.rs`, `bundle/tests.rs`: 171 passed, 2 failed, `/tmp/t177/red2-plan.log`).
- builder-stop's block for a deferral alone (the gate's why with no review clause) is said as the gate gave it; no suite renders that variant (observed 2026-11-23, method: `tests/hooks/test-builder-stop-hooks.sh`'s two `gate` fixtures). Not a defect: its why names its own `make task-add`.

**Performance work?** yes. It makes the builders' loop faster: 110,526 characters a session fewer in the guard messages the coordinator and its builders read (586,385 -> 475,859 over the families cut).

### T177 Performance checklist (docs/performance-checklist.md - prompts, never a gate; time is the goal, calls the measure)

1. **Where does the time go?** In the context the guard messages add: 879,048 characters a session in the 255 BASELINE wordings, 586,385 of it in the seven families cut, each read as input by the next model call.
2. **Removes work, or only moves it?** Removes it: the characters cut are never sent; the history they carried is in code comments. One cut adds (blocked-fetch's legend, 16,560 a session) for fidelity.
3. **What do you expect it to save, and why?** 110,526 characters a session, about 50k tokens; the reviews and the two rulings cost about 671k tokens once, repaid in about 13 sessions like the one measured (7.7 without the rulings).
4. **How does the work grow with the settlement?** It does not: it grows with the guards fired, not with a map.
5. **What did the before and after show, and under what conditions?** The ranking's occurrences priced at the old and the new suite lengths, the same paths both sides, measured 2026-11-23 on one coordinator session; the finished-run figure is an estimate (one run a block, an 86-character output path). This is evidence, not a pass.
6. **Did any map move, and does it still keep the research?** No map moved: the tooling only.

### T174 (observed 2026-11-23, 451 T170's census: 17 of the 58 corpus files of `make hooks-test HOOKS_ALL=1` empty, repo-safety's, shell-check's and source-block's among them; 451 T177's ranking: guard-file's notice on a Read of a guard file rendered by no suite)

- **Approach**: bring each guard message no suite rendered to the budget check, price each by what a session pays for it, review the one family whose review repays (T177's break-even, one review 31,680 characters a key, measured 2026-11-23) and record the rest BASELINE with its figure.

**WHAT REACHES THE RECORD NOW, measured 2026-11-23** (each changed suite run into a private corpus, `L7R_MESSAGE_CORPUS=/tmp/t174/c<n>`, then `l7r-guard messages check` over it and the record - the same check `make hooks-test` runs - so the clone's shared corpus held no unrecorded key while builders land from it):
