### T263 (449/451's landing gate, 2026-11-26: `an_unchanged_mid_task_notice_is_said_once_then_in_one_line` failed once on its first assertion and passed 4 of 4 repeats)

- **Approach**: the cause is the test fixture's copy, and the fix is in the fixture (`rust/guard/src/guards/clone_sync_hooks/tests.rs`); no code of the guard changes.
  - **Not 451 T258's state restore.** The fixture clone's `scripts/sync-with-main.sh` is a three-line `sh` fake (`template()`, the `script(&clone.join("scripts/sync-with-main.sh"), ...)` call): the real sync-in and its detached `state-sync.sh restore` never run in a clone-sync test. Observed 2026-11-26, method: the fixture read.
  - **The cause.** `World::new` copied the template with `copy()`, `std::fs::copy` a file, so THIS process held each world's script open for writing while it wrote it. A thread forking in another test copies every open descriptor until its child execs - the hazard `write_executable` (`rust/guard/src/guards.rs`) already names and avoids for the scripts a test writes; the fixture's copy of them was outside it. A child forked during the copy of the fake and slow to its exec (the gate's load) still holds the script open for writing when the hook runs it: the kernel refuses the exec ("Text file busy"), `ask` returns code -1 with no output, and `refresh_mirror` takes its failed branch.
  - **The notice in the failing case** is `clone-sync: <clone> has uncommitted work (mid-task) - clone merge skipped; mirror refresh FAILED: ` with nothing after the colon. This is RECONSTRUCTED by forcing (below), not recovered: the red gate's record (`fc74a396a0`) keeps the result, not the test's output, and the assertion printed no text. Any failure to start the script (the descriptor race, or a fork refused under load) gives this same notice; the descriptor race is the one this fixture makes possible that its neighbors do not, and the one forced.
  - **The fix.** `copy()` is one `cp -a <template>/. <world>`: `cp`, a child, holds the only descriptors that write a world's files and has exited when `copy` returns, so no fork of this process can inherit one. All four fakes (the clone's sync, the tree's `l7r-gate.sh` and `layout_carry.sh`) are covered at once, where a fix a script would leave the next one added exposed. The why is at `copy` with "do not copy a world's scripts in-process again"; the module's header no longer says "copied in-process".
  - **The first assertion prints the notice** (`"{full}"`), so a failure of it shows what was said.
  - **No kept test forces the race.** `std::fs::copy` has no point between its open and its close a test can stop at, and the fixed copy holds no descriptor to hand a child; the forcing below was a stub in the unfixed copy, kept as a diff in the builder's scratch and described here. A kept test that hands the script to a child and reads `FAILED: ` would pin the kernel's "Text file busy", not this code.
  - **The guard is not changed.** In a real clone the script is a tracked file git wrote, never one this process holds open, so the notice cannot differ there for this reason. That a refresh which cannot START its script says `FAILED: ` with nothing after it is left as it is: it is the same branch a failing script takes, and it is said in full every time.
  - **Time**: measured 2026-11-26 (`<test binary> clone_sync_hooks`, the 27 clone-sync tests in one process, the harness's own `finished in`, on a machine other sessions were loading), 0.20 s on one run before and 0.15 to 0.51 s over five runs after, the copy now one child a world where it was a copy a file in-process. No figure here is a target.
  - **Siblings: every way a test of `rust/guard` could run a file its own process wrote**, observed 2026-11-26, method: `grep -rn` over `rust/guard/**/*.rs` for each form, every hit read. The kernel refuses only a file run DIRECTLY (the program a `Command` names, or a `#!` script) while it is open for writing; a file handed to `bash` as an argument is only read. So an instance needs a file made executable or copied executable in-process, or an executable one rewritten in-process:
    - made executable in-process (`from_mode(`, `set_permissions`, any `0o` mode literal, `.mode(0o`, a `chmod` child): `finished_run_hooks/runs/tests.rs` marks its files `0o755` and only parses their names, never runs them; the scratch-sweep tests restore a directory's mode; `tool.rs` opens a lock file `0o644`; every `chmod` hit is a command line under test as text. No instance.
    - copied in-process (`fs::copy`): the fixture's `copy`, fixed here; `review_round_hooks.rs` copies plan files it never runs. No other instance.
    - an executable rewritten in-process (`fs::write`, `File::create`, `OpenOptions` on a path ending `.sh` or under a `scripts/`, `bin/` or `hooks/` directory): the clone-sync tests write none of the template's fakes (they change one only through `script`, which is `write_executable`); `ledger_hooks/tests.rs`, `finished_run_hooks/tests.rs` and `runs/tests.rs`, `record_edit_gate/tests.rs` and `wait/tests.rs` write plain files with no mode and no `#!`, which their guards run as `bash <file>` or only read. No instance.
    - the fakes a test does run directly are written by `write_executable` (`install`, a child), `script` here and `exe` in `suite_tools/bench/tests.rs` among them.
    The crates outside `rust/guard` were not searched: the task is this guard's test.

| step | alone off: fixed and pinned | fresh block vs HEAD | pool manifests moved | the last resort |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| the clone-sync fixture's worlds are copied by no descriptor of the test process | forced red on the unfixed copy by the stub of item 9 (2026-11-26); fixed at `copy`, its why and "do not" beside it; no kept pin, for the reason above | n/a: tooling | none | n/a |
| a failed first assertion shows the notice | the assertion's `"{full}"`, seen in the forced red's output (2026-11-26) | n/a: tooling | none | n/a |

One probe did not reproduce it unforced, measured 2026-11-26 (a 110 s loop over the unfixed test binary, `clone_sync_hooks --test-threads 64`, beside 66 busy loops on 22 cores): 0 failures in 37 runs of the 27 clone-sync tests. ### T267 (`make claims-checked` failed with "File exists (os error 17)" in a linked worktree whenever a reply line was held, observed 2026-11-26 in a builder's worktree)

- **Approach**: The held searches are kept in the tree's own git directory, found from `root/.git` itself.
  - **The cause, confirmed.** `silent::SEARCHED` was the path `.git/claims-searched.json`, joined onto the root at `commands.rs:384`. In a linked worktree `.git` is a file (`gitdir: <clone>/.git/worktrees/<name>`), so the write under it failed creating the directory. Reproduced 2026-11-26 by a new test on the old path (`make rust-test CRATE=rust/gate/crates/claims`): `l7r-gate claims record` exited 1 with "File exists (os error 17)" where 3 (a held line) was due.
  - **The fix** (`rust/gate/crates/claims/src/claims/silent.rs`). `SEARCHED` is now the file's name alone, and `silent::kept_at(root)` gives its place: where `root/.git` is a file naming a `gitdir:`, that directory (a relative name read against the root); otherwise `root/.git`. No git process is run. `record_cmd` asks it; `hold`'s signature is unchanged. A plain clone's file stays where it was, so nothing is migrated.
  - **Per tree, not the clone's common directory - the choice and its reason.** A search is kept under its claim's key, and every worktree of a clone has the same keys. `hold` also forgets every kept search whose pages its bundle holds, and overwrites a key it holds again. In one shared file a second tree's round on the same claim would answer, overwrite or forget the first tree's search, and the first tree's line would be held a second time or passed unread - against 451 T218's "read the nearest three, then file". The crate's other state under git, the in-flight marks (`flight.rs`), stays in the common directory: each mark is named by its bundle's own path, so two trees never meet there, and it already asks git for the directory (its `root.join(".git")` is only the fallback when git answers nothing).
  - **The census** (observed 2026-11-26, method: `grep -rnE 'join\("\.git"\)|"\.git/[a-zA-Z]'` over `rust/gate` and `rust/guard`, tests and fixtures left out, each hit read). In the claims crate the one direct path was `silent.rs`, fixed here; `flight.rs:49` is the fallback named above. In other crates the hits fall in three classes: probes of a root (`.join(".git").exists()`), which a `.git` file satisfies; fallbacks after a git call; and state paths joined straight onto `.git`, the same shape as this one. The third class is listed for the coordinating session as candidates, none of them run in a worktree here: the gate's `reviews` (`prereq.rs` 68, 72, 227, 665; `prereq/scoped.rs:48`; `prereq/tree.rs` 49, 84; `snapshot.rs:238`), `record` (`stale_terms.rs:508`, `merge_answers.rs` 132, 140), `owed` (`owed/answers.rs:422`), `arbiter` (`bundle/sections.rs:430`), `cohort` (`speckit_todo/report.rs:179`), `ci` (`switches.rs:312`), `trials` (`model_trial/case.rs` 237, 463); the guard's `idle_tests_hooks.rs`, `finished_run_hooks.rs` (156, 333), `review_round_hooks.rs` (712, 765, 851), `escalation_hooks.rs:333`, `pair_hooks/state.rs` and `pair_hooks/review.rs`, `stall_watchdog_hooks/pass.rs` (280, 457); and the `.is_dir()` probes that pass a worktree over in silence (`clone_sync_hooks.rs` 335, 354, 552; `archive/store.rs:161`).

### T272 (the Stop hook's QUESTION UNFILTERED was refused three times on 2026-11-25 for a table row of session c6fd72d1's final message that lists a handoff file's contents, `what's waiting on you` among them: 451 T235's remaining false positive, observed 2026-11-26, method: every `QUESTION UNFILTERED` refusal in that session's transcript, counted by its quoted line)

- **Approach**: `escalation_hooks::stated_ask` gains one more statement form, and keeps every ask it read before.
  - **The cases, read from the transcript.** (1) The row is `| Where things stand and what's next | this conversation | a morning handoff file in the repo: what landed, what's open, what was measured, what's waiting on you. Enough for a session with no memory of today. |`. It is not a status cell saying an item waits on the GM, which the task's brief took it for: `what's waiting on you` is the last of the row's `what` clauses naming the kinds of content a file holds, and names no decision. A false positive. (2) `- **The two-builders rule is marked provisional, for you to confirm.** I'd recorded it as closed under your pre-approval. ...` (2026-11-26) asks the GM for a confirmation: `for you to confirm` is `STATED`'s own phrase, T235's record rules the like form (`a candidate fix for you to decide on`) as putting something to him, and escalation-check kept it, reworded as an offer, where it cuts information. A true positive: the rule is unchanged for it, and it is pinned as an ask.
  - **The rule.** A `waiting (on|for) you` is `listed`, and no ask, when the text before it ends a `what's` / `what is` / `what was` / `what were` clause (an optional `still`) that follows a list's `,` `;` `:` or `and`/`or` (`LISTED`), and the text after it ends the clause (`.`, a table's `|`, the line's end) or goes on to a sibling `what` clause (`LIST_GOES_ON`). Both sides bound it, as T235's exemptions are bounded: with no list before it (`Here is what's waiting on you.`, `The budget answer is what's waiting on you.`), or with the thing that waits named after it (`: the budget's words`, `is the split`, `, the budget answer`, `(the budget answer)`, `waiting on your budget answer`), it is still an ask. T235's table rule is untouched: `| T26 | Waiting on your budget answer |` and `| T22 | yours to decide |`, a cell that says an item waits on him, still fire, so no status-cell exemption is built (it would undo those pinned asks).
  - **How wide the form is.** In session c6fd72d1's transcript `what ... waiting (on|for) you` occurs only as this row, measured 2026-11-26 (`grep -oiE "what.{1,12}waiting (on|for) you.{0,60}"` over the transcript: the row and its three refusals). The rule is written for the form, an enumeration of contents, not for the one line.
  - **Measured on T235's corpus** (112 labeled firings, 2026-10-26 to 2026-11-25, in the session scratchpad): through the fixed guard 82 fire, all 74 T and all 8 B, and none of the 30 F, the same figures as T235's after, measured 2026-11-26 (`measure.py` over `labeled.json`, each message through `tests/hooks/escalation-hooks.sh stop`). The corpus predates the row, so it shows only that no ask is lost.

### T268 (451 T263's forced red, 2026-11-26: a sync script that cannot START left the clone-sync notice ending `mirror refresh FAILED: ` with nothing after the colon)

- **Approach**: the guard's runs of the clone's `scripts/sync-with-main.sh` (the mid-task mirror refresh and the clean clone's sync-in) go through one helper that tells a script that could not be started from one that ran and failed, and says the system's reason for the first.
  - **The cause.** `ask` (`rust/guard/shared/src/tool.rs`) answers a program that cannot be spawned with code -1 and no output, dropping the spawn's error; `refresh_mirror` and the clean clone's sync-in (`rust/guard/src/guards/clone_sync_hooks.rs`) print the tail of that empty output after `FAILED: `. Observed 2026-11-26, method: both call sites read, and the red run below.
  - **`ask_started`**, new in `tool.rs`: `ask`'s body returning `std::io::Result<Said>`, the error the spawn's own. `ask` is `ask_started(...)` with an error answered -1 with nothing, so its contract and its every other caller are unchanged (the module's header says so and names the new function). `Said` gains no field: `layout_carry.sh`'s caller prints a non-empty `err`, so an error carried there would add a line to the sync notice.
  - **Not inferred from the code.** "-1 and no output" is also what a script a signal killed answers, so the notice says "could not be started" only when the spawn itself failed.
  - **`sync_script`**, new in `clone_sync_hooks.rs`: runs the script with the caller's arguments and returns its output, or for a failure the words after the notice's colon - the output's last lines as before (two for the sync-in, one for the refresh), or `scripts/sync-with-main.sh could not be started (<the system's reason>)`. The script is named because a bare "No such file or directory" does not say which file. Its why is beside it.
  - **The two notices, in the unstartable case**, as the test reads them: `... - clone merge skipped; mirror refresh FAILED: scripts/sync-with-main.sh could not be started (Permission denied (os error 13))` and `clone-sync: auto sync-in FAILED in <clone> - resolve before modifying the repo: scripts/sync-with-main.sh could not be started (No such file or directory (os error 2))`. A script that ran and failed says what it said before (the existing tests' `FAILED: said`).
  - **A script that ran, failed and said nothing** (the plan review's block, 2026-11-26: the same empty tail by another road, in the helper being written) says its exit: `scripts/sync-with-main.sh exited 7 and said nothing`, or, with no exit code, `scripts/sync-with-main.sh said nothing and gave no exit code (a signal ended it?)` - a question because `ask` answers -1 both for a signal and for a wait that failed. A failure with output says its output, unchanged. After this no failure of the script leaves the colon bare.
  - **The sync-in notice is fixed too**: the brief names the mirror refresh; the clean clone's sync-in runs the same script through the same `ask` and had the same empty tail (constitution XIV, fixed where found).
  - **Scope.** Only this guard's runs of the sync script changed. The other callers of `ask` across the guards were not surveyed for a notice with an empty tail.

### T271 (the 2026-11-25 parallel trials, `specs/449-rust-codebase/port-talk-agenda.md` item 1: builders in worktrees of one feature write their plan review bundles under one directory, `/tmp/l7r-check`, and their scratch files into one session scratchpad)

- **Approach**: the changed-blocks bundle's directory is keyed by its tree; the builder brief tells a builder to prefix its scratch files with its task id.
  - **Which bundles two trees collide on, measured 2026-11-26.** The plan tool writes two bundles (`rust/gate/crates/plan/src/plan/bundle.rs`). A task's own, `plan-<feature>-<task>` (`make decide`), is named by its task: two trees share it only when both decide the same task, and a task has one builder, so two builders never do. The changed-blocks one, `plan-<feature>-blocks-<tasks>-<8 hex>` (`make plan-delta`), took its 8 hex from the owed blocks' keys and digests alone: two trees whose plans owe the same blocks at the same text got one directory. Method: the new test, on HEAD's code, built both bundles from two fixture trees holding the same plan into one bundles directory - both changed-blocks prompts named `plan-999-x-blocks-plan-e3172c58`, the second build having removed and rewritten the first, its MANIFEST's `Built from the tree` line and its `make -C <tree> plan-verdict` command the second tree's. In the real trees the same day, `l7r-gate plan owed specs/451-time-retro-and-efficiency` listed the same 34 owed blocks in the session's clone and in this task's worktree (both at 38a5d147f5; the T269 and T270 worktrees stand at the same commit), so a `make plan-delta` in each would have named one directory. Two trees that owe different blocks, or the same blocks at different text, already differed by the 8 hex and by the task ids in the name.
  - **The fix.** `delta_prompt` hashes the tree's path (`tree_of`, 451 T257's, the path the MANIFEST names) with the blocks' digests. The name keeps its shape, `blocks-<tasks>-<8 hex>`, so every reader of it follows unchanged: the plan hold's pattern (`rust/guard/shared/src/checks/planhold.rs`), the plan-round cap's subject (`rust/guard/src/guards/review_round_hooks.rs`, which reads the feature and the task ids, never the hex), the ledger's subject (`ledger_passes/rows.rs`, the directory's whole name) and the Agent guards' bundle patterns (`check_bundle_hooks.rs`, `pair_hooks`), found 2026-11-26 by `grep -rn "blocks-\|l7r-check" --include=*.rs rust`. `plan-verdict` reads no bundle path: it takes the reviewer's JSON and the tree it runs in. One tree's rebuild of the same blocks is the same directory, as before.
  - **The task's own bundle is left as it is**: a decision narrower than the task line's words ("key the plan review bundle by tree"), taken on the measurement above. Its directory ends `-T<n>`, which the plan hold's pattern reads the task from; keying it by tree would change that shape for a collision two builders cannot have.
  - **The brief.** `scripts/container/builder-brief.md`'s pasted block gains one line: prefix every scratch file with the task id. The coordinating session added it by hand to each brief since the trials.

### T270 (451 T261's builder, measured 2026-11-26 (12 escape records replayed at their commits, against the reading by reason in T261's line): escapes read by their reason gave a false finding, 60% counted as unstarted tasks' stubs and none of the 12 records replayed holding one, and 451 T262 gave the record a `held` list nothing yet counts)

- **Approach**: `make audit`'s Bypasses section ends with a count of the plan gate's escapes by what each record's `held` list says, never by its reason.
  - **Where.** A new module, `rust/gate/crates/measure/src/measure/audit/held.rs` (`class`, `lines`), called by `runs()` in `audit.rs` after the listing of the last 15 bypasses. The count is over every record in `dev/bypass-log/` whose `target` is `plan-gate push` or opens `plan-gate tick `; it prints nothing where there is none.
  - **What `make audit` did before.** It classified nothing: the listing prints each record's reason (`why`), and a reader grouped the reasons. The task's line calls that classifying by reason text; the listing is unchanged, and the count is added under it.
  - **The classes, named from the record's shape** (read 2026-11-26: `bypass_record`, `held_row`, `tick_gate` and the door's `bypass-record` in `rust/gate/crates/plan/src/plan.rs`):
    1. `held not recorded (a record before 451 T262)` - no `held` key, or one that is no list. A push recorded with no range has none either; `plan-gate.sh` always passes the range.
    2. `nothing held` - `held` is an empty list: the gate listed no feature.
    3. `a plan or its review record missing, no block listed` - rows, none with a block (`plan-missing`, `plan-review-missing`).
    4. `at a push: blocks held, of ticked tasks or outside every task` - a row with a block, target `plan-gate push`.
    5. `at a tick: blocks held, of the asked task, of tasks ticked before it or outside every task` - a row with a block, target `plan-gate tick <feature>`.
  - **Why the classes are by place and not "ticked tasks' blocks" against "asked tasks' blocks".** The record names the place and the feature, not the task asked for, and a block key is a heading, not an owner. What it does carry is where the gate judged, and 451 T84 fixes what is judged there: at a push the ticked tasks' sections, at a tick the asked task's and those ticked before it, at both the blocks outside every task's section. So classes 4 and 5 say exactly that and no more. A count by owning task needs the tick's record to carry the task id: a title in the builder's report, not built here.
  - **`plan-gate decide-defer`** records (`DEFER_FORM_OK`, the decide lint's escape) are not counted: another escape, with no `held`.
  - **The real log, measured 2026-11-26** (method: `scripts/gates/l7r-gate.sh measure audit runs` in the worktree at 38a5d147f5): 1281 plan-gate escape records (642 at the push, 639 at the tick, by `jq` over `target`), all 1281 `held not recorded`, 0 in each other class. The newest is dated 2026-11-26T03:41:00Z, before T262 landed; no escape has been honored since, so no record carries `held` yet (`grep -rl '"held"' dev/bypass-log` lists none). Those 1281 are not classed by their reasons: the count says the record does not say.
  - **The audit-register entry** `dev/audits/plan-gate-escape.md` said the count by `held` was a reader's query; it now names this count and its classes.

### T269 (451 T258, 2026-11-25: `scripts/state-sync.sh`, newly called from `make land`'s and `make land-tooling`'s recipes, landed with the audit register's check asking no entry - `dev/audits/tooling-state.md` says so in its own words)

- **Approach**: the audit register's delta check (`rust/gate/crates/checks/src/checks/audit_register/detect.rs`) reads one more form of LANDING STEP: a script newly called from a landing recipe. The kinds stay five; an item is `landing script scripts/<path>`, the name an entry's `covers:` line gives it, as the other landing steps are named (`push check <name>`, `landing gate <name>`).
  - **The cause.** `detect::items` read a Makefile only for its `$(MAKE) <target>` edges (`make_graph`), and the landing only where `STEPS` and `REFUSALS` name it in the Rust; a recipe line that runs a script was read by nothing. Observed 2026-11-26, method: the function as written, and the red run of item 9.
  - **What is read** (`landing_scripts`): the recipe lines of `land`, `land-batch` and `land-tooling` (`LANDING_TARGETS`) in the Makefile, the value of each Makefile variable those lines expand and of each that one expands in turn (`landing_recipes`: `$(LAND_RUN)` IS the landing, `$(DISK_FLOOR)` and `$(SCRATCH_TREES)` hold a script each), and the push's own two scripts whole, `scripts/land-tooling.sh` and `scripts/sync-with-main.sh` (`LANDING_SCRIPTS`) - the three the brief names, make land, make land-tooling and the push script. NOT the whole gate chain's recipes: the Makefile's hook roster (its `for h in ... scripts/state-sync.sh ...` lines of `make hooks-test`) names scripts it does not call, and a reader over every chain recipe would fire on a roster line.
  - **What a script's name is** (`script_names`): each `scripts/<path>` over the characters of a path that ends in a file's extension, a trailing sentence stop cut, a `#` line not read. So `scripts/*`, `scripts/gates/` and `scripts/gates/$g.sh` name no script.
  - **New is by name over all of them together**, the base against the head (the shape of T259-D3 for constants): a call moved from a recipe into the push script, or a script the landing already calls somewhere, adds nothing.
  - **The Makefile's rule-line reading is one function now** (`rule`), which `make_graph` and `landing_recipes` both ask, so a target-specific variable line (`land: export LAND_NOTE = ...`) is no rule to either. `make_graph`'s behavior is unchanged (its tests as they were).
  - **`dev/audits/tooling-state.md` gains `covers: landing script scripts/state-sync.sh`**, and its prose no longer says the check cannot see it; `docs/guards.md`'s row, `docs/process-decisions.md`'s register paragraph and `dev/audits/audit-register.md`'s measurement say the new reading and its replay.

### T285 (2026-11-26: the coordinating session made each builder a fresh worktree by hand and deleted it and its build cache after the landing, against the reused-worktrees rule of `docs/process-decisions.md`, "Two code builders at once" - a cold tree's first closing checks took 14-30 minutes against about a minute warm, measured 2026-11-26 (the day's closing-checks runs, that entry's figures))

- **Approach**: a clone's builder worktrees are a standing POOL that one tool hands out and frees, and a guard refuses the hand forms. Three pieces: the registry (`rust/guard/shared/src/builder_pool.rs`), the tool (`rust/gate/crates/task/src/builder_tree.rs`, `l7r-gate builder-tree`, five make targets and `make land`'s release) and the guard (`rust/guard/src/guards/builder_pool_hooks.rs`).
  - **The registry** is `<clone>/.git/builder-pool.json` (the clone's common git directory): each tree's path, the feature and tasks holding it, since when. Membership is the registry, never a name's shape; a new tree is `<clones>/<clone>-b<N>`, N from 1. Its log is `builder-pool.log` beside it, a JSON line an event (make, take, release, discard, adopt, drop).
  - **`make builder-tree T=<task> [F=<feature>]`** (`take`): the tree the task already holds, else the first FREE tree brought to the clone's HEAD (`git checkout -f --detach`) and marked held, its path alone on stdout and what happened on stderr; with none free, ONE more made (`git worktree add --detach`) while the pool is under its cap, said to be COLD, its guard binary built before it is handed out by the tree's own `scripts/hooks/l7r-guard.sh` with `L7R_GUARD_PRINT_FRESH=1` and a limit of 1800 s, a GUESS knob (`L7R_BUILDER_GUARD_SECS`), where the wrapper's own limit of 45 s, its knob `L7R_GUARD_BUILD_SECS`, was 451 T286's failure under load; at the cap, refused, each tree with its holder.
  - **What holds a free tree (the dirty refusal).** A builder never commits; its work is carried to the clone and landed there, so a released tree still holds those edits uncommitted. An uncommitted path - modified, deleted or untracked - whose content IS the clone's HEAD's (`git hash-object` against `HEAD:<path>`) is landed work and no hold: the tree is brought to HEAD over it. Any other path holds the tree: the handout is refused, each path named. `DISCARD="<two words or more>"` takes the tree over them (`git checkout -f`, `git clean -fd`, ignored files kept), the reason on the pool's log. A free tree so held is never passed over for a new cold one: the cold tree is the failure the task exists to end, so the tool refuses rather than hide it. Decided by this builder; the builder's brief from the coordinating session asked for a refusal on a dirty tree that says what holds it, and neither the GM's words nor T285's line settles it; the cost is one more step for the coordinator when a builder left a probe behind.
  - **`make builder-tree-release T=<task>`** and **`make land`**: the tree freed, it and its build cache left in place, brought to HEAD where nothing holds it (else left as it is, the paths named). A task holding no tree is a quiet exit 0. `make land`'s recipe calls `l7r-gate builder-tree landed <F> <T...>` after a landing (exit 0 or 3), which exits 0 whatever happens and says `the release failed - the landing stands` where it did; the recipe's own `||` covers a tool that could not start. `make land-batch`'s recipe makes the same call. AND BY ANY OTHER ROUTE (the plan review of 2026-11-26, D4b): at every handout a tree whose every holding task is ticked in its feature's `tasks.md`, or archived in `tasks-done.md`, in the clone is freed first (`landed`), so a tick by hand or a landing whose release did not run leaves no tree held, and no hand step is owed. EVERY HOLD NAMES ITS FEATURE (the plan review of 2026-11-26, round 2): a handout or an adoption with a task and no feature (`F=`, else `SPECIFY_FEATURE`, which both make targets pass) is refused with that said, so no hold exists that the freeing step cannot read; pinned in `what_cannot_be_done_says_so_and_a_landing_s_release_never_fails`.
  - **`make builder-trees`**: each tree, its holder, since when, its cache's size (`du -sh`), `GONE from disk` where it is. **`make builder-tree-drop TREE=<path> REASON="<two words or more>"`**: the one removal - `git worktree remove --force`, the cache directory, the registry line; a held tree refused. **`make builder-tree-adopt TREE=<path> [T=] [F=]`**: a worktree of the clone made before the pool joins it under its own name (the landing's, tooling landing's and review's trees refused).
  - **The three trees of 2026-11-26 are adopted under their own names, not renamed.** Measured 2026-11-26 in `diagram-backlog-t271` (idle, its cache 8.1 GB), method `/usr/bin/time` on `cargo build --profile tool -p l7r_gate -p l7r_guard` and `cargo test --no-run -p l7r_guard` against its cache: warm 0.11 s and 0.08 s, after `git worktree move` to `diagram-backlog-b3` with the cache directory moved too 66.5 s and 41.7 s (every workspace crate rebuilt, the registry crates kept), and moved back 68.3 s and 41.7 s again. Cargo's fingerprints hold the workspace's absolute path, and a pool tree has six more profiles to rebuild (observed 2026-11-26, method: `ls ~/.cache/l7r-cargo-target/diagram-backlog-t271` - `tool` and `debug`, the two timed, and `cover-browser`, `cover-embed`, `cover-gate`, `cover-guard`, `cover-mode_a`, `cover-phases`), so a rename is not warm. The tree is back under its name and warm in those two profiles.
  - **The cap** is `builder_pool::CAP` = 4 (`L7R_BUILDER_POOL`), a GUESS knob: the largest count the sizing rule allows at once, read from `scripts/container/builder-brief.md` ("three or four at once only for batches that compile nothing") and `docs/process-decisions.md`, "Two code builders at once", not a count this builder measured; the count worth running is T284's to measure.
  - **The guard** reads a Bash command through the shared walk (`shared::tree::walk`: each write with where it lands, variables and `cd`s followed) and refuses (a) `git worktree add` of a path under `<mirror>/.clones/`, (b) `git worktree remove` or `move` of a registered pool tree, (c) an `rm` whose operand is a pool tree, its build cache (`~/.cache/l7r-cargo-target/<tree's name>`, `L7R_BUILDER_CACHE`) or a directory holding either; each refusal prints the pool's command. `BUILDER_TREE_OK` with a reason escapes, checked first. THE TOOLING'S OWN TREES ARE EXEMPT BY WHERE THE CALL IS MADE: `scripts/land-alone.sh:554`, `scripts/land-tooling.sh:119`, `scripts/gates/review-tree.sh:142` and the pool tool call git inside a program, and a hook reads only the tool call (`make land ...`); a hand `git worktree add .../<clone>-land` is refused like any other, pinned both ways in the suite. `move` is refused beside `remove` because it chills the cache as a removal does (the measurement above).
  - **Limits accepted** (this builder, 2026-11-26). A path-qualified `git` is NOT one of them: it is a defect, carried under "Found and left?" below. ### T281 (the store of rendered guard messages lay in the git common directory, one for every worktree of a clone: on 2026-11-26 a builder's `make guard-messages BUNDLE=1` said "nothing owed" for wordings its own red hooks-test had just named, and 451 T292's last hooks-test went red on the wordings of a guard only T285's tree held)

- **Approach**: the renderings are kept a tree at a time, and a keyed copy sits beside the shared stamps so the stamps can stay shared.
  - **Both effects reproduced first**, 2026-11-26, with two worktree fixtures (a fixture repository of stub guards, a linked worktree beside its main one) through the real `make hooks-test` and `make guard-messages` recipes on HEAD's code, method: `tests/hooks/test-parts.3.sh` before the fix, 11 passed, 4 failed. (a) Tree B changes a wording and its run names it unreviewed; tree A, at the old wording, runs; B's `make guard-messages` then names nothing. (b) B gains a guard A does not hold; A's `make guard-messages` and A's `make hooks-test` name that guard's wording unreviewed. The fourth red is the same reader fault in one tree: a rendering left in the store by a guard the tree no longer holds is judged for good.
  - **The cause, two faults.** `tests/hooks/hookrun.sh` wrote `<common dir>/hooks-test/messages/<job>.jsonl`, one file a job for every tree; and `messages::corpus` reads every `.jsonl` of the directory, never the run's roster.
  - **The tree's store.** `<the tree's own git dir>/hooks-test/messages/`, found by `l7r-guard messages store <dir>` (`git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir`, since a linked worktree's `.git` is a file, as T254 and T267 did), the one resolver the hooks-test recipe (which hands it to `hookrun.sh` as `HOOKS_MESSAGES`) and the `guard-messages` recipe (its check, `BUNDLE=1`, `KEY=`, `REHEAD=1`) both ask. `dev/guard-messages.tsv`, the reviewed record, stays one tracked file.
  - **Why a store by tree alone is not enough.** The suites' stamps are shared on purpose: a fresh worktree off main reran 5 suites of 46 where it had rerun all, 83 s against 151 s (measured 2026-10-12, commit d7456c4c8d's message). The skip trusts a stamp plus "its messages are kept". With the stamps shared and the store per tree, a fresh tree holds no messages, so it would rerun every suite, the saving undone, and a tree whose content moves to a key another tree has stamped would skip holding its own stale rendering. Stamps per tree was priced and not taken, since it undoes the same saving.
  - **The keyed rendering.** A green job also leaves `<common dir>/hooks-test/rendered/<job>@<key>.jsonl`, the key the one its stamp will hold, written before the stamp and moved into place whole, one a job (`hookrun.sh`). A suite is skipped only where a rendering at the stamp's key exists. After the fan-out one call, `l7r-guard messages gather <rendered> <tree store> <list>`, makes the tree's store this run's: a skipped suite's files are replaced by the renderings at its stamp's key (what this tree's own run would render, the key being the suite's inputs), a suite that ran keeps what its job wrote, and a file of no suite on the run's roster is removed. A skipped suite whose keyed rendering is gone by then (another tree's run replaced it in between) fails the run by name with the fix, `make hooks-test` again, which reruns it.
  - **What it costs.** Each clone's first `make hooks-test` after this lands reruns every suite once, since no keyed rendering exists yet (one full run of the suites, 160 s inside this task's first closing checks beside two other builders, measured 2026-11-26 (`make closing-checks T=T281`, its hooks-test line)). One more launcher call a run (`messages store`), and one fewer `ls` a suite in the loop.
  - **The landing's and the review tree's seed.** `scripts/land-alone.sh` and `scripts/gates/review-tree.sh` copied the common `hooks-test/` into their tree's own git directory beside the crates' kept results. Nothing read that copy (the recipe reads the stamps from the common directory since commit d7456c4c8d; observed 2026-11-26, method: `grep -rn hooks-test rust scripts tests` for a reader of a tree's own `hooks-test/`, none but the two copies), and with the tree's store now at `hooks-test/messages` it would fill that store with the clone's renderings before the tree's own run. Both copies no longer take `hooks-test`; fixed here (MODE 4's finding on this section's first round).

### T284 (2026-11-26: nothing kept two trees' compiles apart, so the builder count was capped by the chance that they coincide - three builders' anonymous memory peaked at 6.4 GiB of the container's 10 and load at 94 on 22 cores, measured 2026-11-26, `docs/process-decisions.md`, "Two code builders at once")

- **Approach**: each cargo call of the checks that compiles holds one of a counted set of machine-wide slots for its length (`rust/gate/crates/rustc/src/rustc/slot.rs`), and the wait is a category of its own in the time readers (`rust/gate/crates/measure/src/measure/where_time/columns.rs`). T284's line also asks for the re-measurement at three and four builders; that half is the coordinating session's next step, run with this in, and is not done here.
  - **What was measured first** (2026-11-26, read-only, method: `python3 dev/measurements/2026-11-26/builder-count/slot-coincide.py`, the three-builder run's 292 samples of 13:37-14:27 UTC joined by time with the 380 `Phase` lines the checks wrote in that window, the clone's `.git/l7r-events/`). All 12 of the highest memory samples (5.9-6.4 GiB anonymous) and 7 of the 8 highest counts of rustc (39-46) fall where all three trees were in a `cover-build` at once (measured 2026-11-26, method: that script). Of the window's phase minutes, coverage builds were 57.9, lint 33.2, coverage runs 19.8, test builds 6.2, `cargo fmt` 1.1 and test runs 0.2. The machine ran three compiling steps (`cover-build`, `lint`, `build`) at once for 1,396 s of 2,602, two for 509 s, one for 631 s (measured 2026-11-26, method: that script). One tree's own closing checks never ran two compiling steps at once: the five steps it runs at once are coverage RUNS (test binaries), so a slot a cargo call is in effect a slot a tree. Where no check's phase ran the samples reach 2.6 GiB and 13 rustc (measured 2026-11-26, method: that script): the wrapper's tool build and the hook suites' guard build, which write no `Phase` line.
  - **What takes a slot.** Every cargo call through `cargo_in` but `cargo fmt` - clippy, a test build (`--no-run`, `kept.rs`'s and `stepped`'s), `cargo test`, `cargo test --doc`, `test-times`' build, the `hamlet` stage's `cargo run` (a release compile) - and the coverage build in `cover.rs`, which starts cargo itself. Not `cargo fmt`, `llvm-cov show-env` or `report`, `cargo --version`, or a test binary run directly: none compiles. Decided by this builder from the measurement; the brief left which calls are heavy to it.
  - **The slot** is the `flock` of a file `slot-<i>` under `~/.cache/l7r-build-slots/` (`L7R_BUILD_SLOT_DIR`), taken with `flock -n` on the open file through the `flock` program as `l7r_shared::tool::flock` does, tried in order, looked at again every half second (`POLL`, a GUESS). It is signed with the holder (tree, pid, make target, the cargo words) for a waiter's line. The lock is the open file's, so a holder that dies frees it; no daemon, nothing to clear.
  - **The count** is `L7R_BUILD_SLOTS`, default 2 (`DEFAULT`), a GUESS knob labeled so beside it: it is a cap on compiling cargo calls at once, not on builders - a third, fourth or fifth builder edits, tests and runs its coverage runs freely and queues only for the seconds its compile would have coincided with two others. Three compiles at once is the peak the samples show, at load median 42 on 22 cores (measured 2026-11-26, `docs/process-decisions.md`, "Two code builders at once", the three-builder run's samples), and each of the three ran about 15 rustc at the peaks, 46 over 3 (measured 2026-11-26, method: that script), so two fill the cores; cargo's own `-j` stays a job a core. One slot is unmeasured. `0` is no slot: nothing is made or asked.
  - **Never a deadlock, never a refusal.** A call holds one slot and waits for no second (the coverage build lets its slot go before a failed group is asked again a crate at a time). The cargo a holder starts carries `L7R_BUILD_SLOT_HELD`, and a gate run started under it has no slots, so a crate's tests that run the checks do not wait on the slot their own `cargo test` holds. A slot directory that cannot be made, a slot file that cannot be opened, a `flock` that cannot start, and a wait past the ceiling (`L7R_BUILD_SLOT_CEILING`, 900 s, a GUESS: over the longest coverage build of the three-builder run, 589 s (measured 2026-11-26, method: that script's `max` of `cover-build`, in cold trees under three-way load), and half the run lock's 1,800 s, which a waiter holds its target directory under) each let the call run without a slot, said on stderr. The run lock is taken first, the slot inside it; nothing holding a slot waits on a run lock. WHAT THE CEILING COSTS: it is there for a holder that hangs, which would otherwise stop every tree's checks for good. But it is not confined to that case. Waiters are not served in arrival order: each looks every half second, and a tree that lets a slot go takes one again the instant its next compile starts, so under sustained load from several builders one waiter can be kept out to the ceiling (the knob `L7R_BUILD_SLOT_CEILING`) with no holder hung - not measured; the plan review of 2026-11-26 raised it. A pass is then one more compile at once, three, which is the peak already measured. Each pass is said on stderr and written as a `slot-wait` line of `code` 1, and `dev/audits/build-slot.md` reopens the count on one such line in a week. Decided by this builder; the alternative priced was to wait without end (a hung cargo in one tree then holds every tree's landing until someone kills it) and to refuse past the ceiling as the run lock does (a red gate for a throughput control).
  - **The wait is booked.** A call that waited writes one `Phase` line, `src` `rust`, `step` `slot-wait`, its span the wait, `code` 1 where it ran without a slot; a call that did not wait writes none. `columns::category` reads it as `waiting on a build slot` (`SLOT_WAIT`), first of `PHASE_COLUMNS`, so a wait inside a lint's or a test build's span is taken out before the compile; `make task-time` shows it as a category and `make where-time` as a column. A waiter says it waits each minute (`NOTICE`), naming the holders. A coverage build's slot is taken before its phase's clock starts; a lint's, test build's or test run's phase line spans its wait - accepted by this builder: the readers subtract it, and moving those clocks means threading the slot through `stepped` and `kept.rs`; the cost is that a script reading raw `Phase` lines must subtract `slot-wait` lines itself (said in `dev/audits/build-slot.md`).
  - **Not covered, and why.** Two compiles take no slot: the wrapper's own tool build (`scripts/gates/l7r-gate.sh`'s `build`, before any gate program exists to take one) and the hook suites' guard build. Both are shell, write no `Phase` line a wait could be booked by, and were not at the peaks: where no check's phase ran the samples top out at 2.6 GiB and 13 rustc (measured 2026-11-26, method: that script), against 5.9-6.4 GiB where three coverage builds coincide. A limit accepted by this builder, not a defect: its cost is that such a build can run beside two slotted compiles, and what would reopen it is the re-measurement showing one at a peak. It is named as a candidate in the builder's report for the coordinating session to file or not.
  - **The re-measurement is the rest of T284's own line** ("then re-measure three and four code builders with it"): no other task carries it. This builder's brief names it as what this work blocks, and the coordinating session runs it with the slot landed and records the count in `docs/process-decisions.md`, "Two code builders at once", whose paragraph on the slot says it is owed.
  - **A test's world has no slots** (`Slots::off()`), so no test of the crate touches `~/.cache`; the slot's own tests name a scratch directory.
  - **A landing's gate takes the same slot as a builder's**: both run `l7r-gate rust`, and the directory is under the home, outside every tree.
  - **The record**: `dev/audits/build-slot.md` (measurement, falsifier, cost, the alternatives weighed), a paragraph in `docs/process-decisions.md`, "Two code builders at once", and the `rustc` row of `rust/gate/CLAUDE.md`. - **Approach**: a check pass is tied to the task that held the pool tree it was dispatched from, when it was dispatched, and a landing's write of ledger rows asks the same split its refusal asks; the reading is `ledger_passes/left/pool.rs`, a new rung of `left/whose.rs`.
  - **The cause, replayed on the real pass**, measured 2026-11-26 (the clone's `check-passes.jsonl`, the agents' meta files and transcripts, `task-starts.jsonl` and `builder-pool.log`, read rung by rung against `whose.rs`): the message-check pass `aacfece6ce5ac4886` (16:19Z; its second round `a258d8d9d92cfd749`, 16:23Z) was dispatched by T295's builder `a4bee62b55c262244` from the pool tree `diagram-backlog-t270`. Its subject (`Judge the guard message unit(s) in the bundle: read /tmp/l7r-check/guard-messages/MANIFEST.md and th`) and description (`Message check static-runs`) name no task. Its builder's description is `Build 451 T295 wrong-tree guards`, which `builder_brief` does not read as a builder's (its pattern wants the feature's number first). And had it been read, T295 had no start row: its first in feature 451 is 16:46:14Z, made in the clone by the landing's session, and `whose.rs` leaves a pass only to a STARTED task - the pool handed T295 its tree at 15:42:54Z and nothing started it there. So the pass was nobody's and refused the T281 and T284 landing (their starts 16:15Z and 16:23Z, their trees released 16:27Z). The event log's own booking failed the same way: the two dispatches' lines carry no `task`. T272's refusal was the same shape before the pool existed, by the task line; its time is not in the event log, and the one builder-dispatched message-check of that hour is T268's builder's (13:16:27Z, from a worktree made by hand), which the landing's refusal was not replayed against.
  - **Escalation-check passes are not this case**, measured 2026-11-26 (the day's three in `check-passes.jsonl`, each one's subject and its meta file's `spawnDepth` and `parentAgentId`): each is the coordinating session's own dispatch (`spawnDepth` 1, no parent) naming the clone or the landing tree (`Tree: /diagram/.clones/diagram-backlog (origin`), tied to no task, and holds the push as before.
  - **The rule as built.** After a pass's own words (its subject, its description) and before its builder and page session, `whose.rs` asks the pool: the tree the pass's subject names, else the one the first line of its dispatching agent's brief names, and who held that tree at the time of the pass's transcript's first record, by the pool's log (`<git common dir>/builder-pool.log`). The log and not the registry: `builder-pool.json` says who holds a tree now, and `diagram-backlog-t270` was T295's until 16:54:35Z and T303's from 17:13:14Z, so the registry read at a later landing would hand T295's pass to T303. A hold stands for the task's start for this rung alone; T157's and T167's started rule is unchanged for every other source. The pass is then left to that task's landing while the task is not ticked, owed by a landing that lands it, and - its task ticked, its tree free at the time, its hold naming no feature, its transcript carrying no time - owed by every push as before.
  - **The write side.** `make land`'s write (`cheap.rs`'s `--write specs/<feature>/`) wrote every owed pass the feature's trace reached, another open task's of the same feature among them, and did not write its own tasks' pass where the trace did not reach it (a message-check's subject names no feature), so the landing was refused on a row only a hand write could add. The write now carries `--landing <feature> --tasks <its tasks>` and asks `left.rs`: another open task's pass is not written, its own tasks' is written, any other is the trace's as before. A write no landing asks (`make ledger-owed WRITE=`, a page session's) is unchanged.
  - **A pass tied to no task still holds the push.** Of the 806 check dispatches of 2026-11-24 to 2026-11-26, 272 carry no task in the event log (134, 79 and 59 a day), measured 2026-11-26 (method: the `PreToolUse` `Agent` lines of `/diagram/.clones/diagram-backlog/.git/l7r-events/*.jsonl` whose `agent` is a defined check, counted by day and by a missing `task`). It counts dispatches, not the passes left unrowed at any one push, and it is a floor for what `whose.rs` ties to nothing: the event log books the main session's own line to the last start mark where its words name no task (D2), which `whose.rs` never does. 199 of them are the coordinating session's own dispatches (no `by`), which no tree or builder ties and which hold as before; 73 were dispatched by a subagent (56, 14 and 3 a day). The pool's log begins 2026-11-26T14:57Z, so the new rung reaches only that day's: of its 3, two are the passes above, now T295's, and the third is T268's builder's of 13:16Z from a hand-made tree, which no log names - hand-made trees are refused since 451 T285.
  - **Replayed on the real passes with the built tool**, measured 2026-11-26 (the two log lines above as `--log`, an empty scratch ledger in the builder's tree, `L7R_CACHE_OFF=1`, so nothing of the clone's was written): `--write specs/451-time-retro-and-efficiency/ --landing 451-time-retro-and-efficiency --tasks T295` wrote 2 rows, and the same with `--tasks T303`, the tree's holder now, wrote 0 (`2 pass(es) not traced to it stay owed`).
  - **Red first**, measured 2026-11-26 (`scripts/gates/l7r-gate.sh rust test --crate rust/gate/crates/reviews`, the new `left/pool/tests.rs` against HEAD's `whose.rs`, `left.rs` and `ledger_passes.rs`): the landing of T281 was refused on all nine fixture passes, T295's builder's and T303's among them (`left: (1, [true, true, true, true, true, true, true, true, true])`, want the six untied alone); and with HEAD's `ledger_passes.rs` under the new `left.rs`, the write test fails at T281's write, which wrote T295's traced pass. After the fix the crate passes 209 of 209 and the land crate 123 of 123, its write asserted to carry `--landing 449-x --tasks T1`.

5. **The order.** No dependency. T303, built beside it in its own pool tree, touches no file of this task.
6. **The exits.** Green: `make builder-checks CRATE="rust/gate/crates/reviews rust/gate/crates/land"` green in the builder's tree (the first tier, the trial of 2026-11-26), every new line met by the new tests; the full gate and the coverage run are the landing's. Red: what failed recorded and the task set down, a claim that it cannot be done ruled through `make arbiter-ask`.
7. **The search smell.** none.
8. **The budget.** One landing.
9. **Done, measured.** The new test red on HEAD's code and green after, and the land test's write arguments, measured 2026-11-26 (above).
10. **Before moving a constant.** n/a.
11. **Before fitting things into room.** n/a.
12. **Before any fix.** The finding: a landing refused four times on 2026-11-26 on passes another task's builder ran, observed 2026-11-26, method: the replay above. No map changes.

**Found and left?**
- The event log books a pool builder's check dispatch to no task, for the two causes above: `builder_brief` (`rust/guard/shared/src/guards/set_down_hooks/builders.rs`, its pattern `^\s*(\d{3})\b`) does not read a description that opens `Build 451 T295 ...` as a builder's, and the booking wants a start row the pool builder's task does not have. Its visible effect: the two message-check dispatches of 16:19Z and 16:23Z carry no `task` in the 451 event log, so `make task-time` and `make feature-report` book their time to no task; the same reader is the Stop hook's count of running builders (`stalls.rs`), `builder_stop_hooks.rs` and `check_bundle_hooks/own.rs`, none of which was replayed here. Not fixed here: it is the guard's shared reader with four callers (observed 2026-11-26, method: a search of `rust/guard` for `builder_brief(` outside its tests) and their hook suites, a job of its own beside this task's one (the builder brief's sizing), and this builder was briefed to file no task. Filed as T310; lands before T302.

**Performance work?** no: it changes which landing owes and writes a ledger row; nothing runs faster.

### T309 (2026-11-26: the landing gate of 451 T295 went red on `rust/gate/crates/arbiter/src/arbiter/bundle/reviews.rs` line 221, "no test reaches", and green on the re-run minutes later; the same red was listed apart at T272's closing checks that morning)

- **Approach**: the tie-break is given a fixture whose transcripts' modified times are set, and the crate's tests are closed to the machine's state: the transcripts, the check state of the tree they run in, and the live guard log.
  - **The cause is the clock, not the live transcripts**, measured 2026-11-26. The task line supposed the tie was reached through `~/.claude/projects`. Method 1, measured 2026-11-26 (a probe, reverted: the unset test seam and a dispatch with an `aid` made to panic, then `scripts/gates/l7r-gate.sh rust test --crate rust/gate/crates/arbiter`): 41 of 41 tests passed, so no test of the crate read the live transcripts - 449 T99's thread-local seam already covered the two tests that reach `spec_rounds`, and no fixture dispatch carries an `aid`. Method 2 (`scripts/gates/l7r-gate.sh rust cover --crate rust/gate/crates/arbiter` with `HOME` an empty directory holding only a link to the build cache, `L7R_RUST_FRESH=1` set directly): clean on HEAD, line 221 reached. What reached it was `plans_specs_reviews_and_the_feature`, whose three matching fixture transcripts are written back to back and sorted on their modified times as the clock left them. Method 3, measured 2026-11-26 (three files written back to back in a shell loop, their `stat` times compared, 300 rounds, on the container's overlay filesystem): two or more tied in 300 of 300, all three carrying one stamp - the kernel stamps a write from a coarse clock, one tick's. So the line is reached while two of the three writes fall in one tick and missed when a loaded machine parts all three, which is what a gate beside other builders' coverage builds does by turns.
  - **Red first**, measured 2026-11-26 (the same cover command on the live `HOME`, after setting the three fixture transcripts' times to 100, 200 and 300 seconds and nothing else): `reviews.rs - lines no test reaches: 221`, every run.
  - **The fix.** `reviews/tests.rs`: `aged` sets a fixture transcript's modified time (`File::set_modified`); the old test's three rounds are 100, 200 and 300; the new `spec_rounds_of_one_time_keep_their_paths_order` gives two dispatches one time and a third an earlier one, and asserts the rounds' order. The transcripts reach the sort already sorted by path and the sort is stable, so the tie-break restates an order it cannot change: the test pins that order and reaches the line, and claims no more.
  - **The tests read a fixture's transcripts or none.** `reviews.rs`'s `transcripts_base`: in a test build the directory the test gave (`TRANSCRIPTS`) and, where it gave none, the empty path, which holds nothing - before, the machine's. `bundle.rs`'s two reads of a round's reply take the same base (`marks::reply_in`), where `marks::reply_of` read the machine's for any dispatch with an `aid`. The binary's build reads `~/.claude/projects` as before.
  - **The checks door's test read and wrote the machine**, observed 2026-11-26, method: what the empty `HOME` held after the cover run, two files under `.claude/guard-log`. `close_answers_its_usage_and_its_verdict` called `close_cli`, which reads the check state of the tree the tests run in and, at each accepted reason, writes a `CHECK_CLOSED` escape to the guard log: 2,229 entries holding `nothing to close here` stood in `~/.claude/guard-log`, observed 2026-11-26, method: `grep -l` over the directory. `close_in(root, args)` now carries the work, the test runs it on a scratch tree, and the process's `GUARD_LOG_DIR` is the test binary's own directory, as the land, plan and task crates' `quiet_census`.
  - **The proof**, measured 2026-11-26 (the cover command twice after the fix, on the live `HOME` and on the empty one with `L7R_RUST_FRESH=1`; the crate's lines of `lcov-arbiter.info` reduced to reached or not and compared): clean both times, the same 4,382 lines reached and none missed in each; the empty `HOME` held nothing but its cache link afterwards. Before the fix the empty-`HOME` run reached 4,316 lines and wrote the two guard-log entries, measured 2026-11-26 (the same reduction of that run's `lcov-arbiter.info`, and `find` over the empty `HOME`).
  - **Not changed**: `arbiter::cli(&["bogus"])` and `arbiter::cli(&["bundle", "--check-ask", "x"])` run on the process's directory and environment to reach the two `cli` wrappers; both answer before reading a file.

### T289 (2026-11-26: a builder listed what it found as candidates and the coordinating session filed them from memory - four went unfiled until the GM asked, and six plan reviews BLOCKED in round 1 on a found-and-left item with no filed task id: T250, T265, T295, T305, T309 and T285's limit, counted by the coordinating session from that day's reviews and given in this task's brief)

- **Approach**: a builder files what it found itself, from its pool tree, with the `make task-add` that already exists; `make carry` is made to keep both trees' filed boxes and plan stubs; the brief and the report format say so. No new command.
  - **Decision 1: no command that reads a report; the builder runs `make task-add`.** The task line asked for "a command that takes a builder's report (or its candidates file) and files each listed title". The coordinating session's brief of 2026-11-26 replaced that design with this one, on the second cost the task line does not name: a filed id is needed BEFORE the report, in the builder's own plan section (`make decide` refuses a deferral without `Filed as T<n>; lands before T<m>.`, `rust/gate/crates/plan/src/plan/lint/deferral.rs`, 451 T17), so a command run on the finished report comes too late for the six blocked rounds. Filing at the find closes both costs: no candidate is left for anyone to file, and the section carries its id in round 1.
  - **Decision 2: nothing changed in `make task-add`; the allotment already holds across trees.** Measured 2026-11-26, method: a new test, `two_worktrees_filing_at_once_take_two_ids_each_in_its_own_tree` (`rust/gate/crates/task/src/task_add/tests.rs`), run on the code as it stood (`make rust-test CRATE=rust/gate/crates/task`): two linked worktrees of one fixture clone, the second filing started while the first held the lock through a quick of 0.3 s, took T10 and T11, each box and section in its own tree only. It passed unchanged. Why: 451 T255 put the id's read under the feature's `flock` in the git COMMON directory and made it read, besides the tree's own four files and `main`/`origin/main`, the reservations in `<common git dir>/task-ids.txt`, which every worktree of the clone shares; a pool tree is a linked worktree of the clone (observed 2026-11-26, method: `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` in this tree prints the clone's `.git`, whose `task-ids.txt` holds 451's ids to T312). So of the brief's two options - a shared counter, or reading every tree's tasks.md under the lock - the shared counter is the one already built, and the simpler: it needs no list of trees. The test is kept as the measurement's record.
  - **Decision 3: `make carry` keeps both sides of two trees' filed tasks** (`rust/gate/crates/land/src/land/carry.rs`). Reproduced 2026-11-26, method: the new test `two_trees_filed_tasks_are_carried_with_both_boxes_and_both_stubs` - two worktrees of a fixture clone each file a task with the real `task_add::cli` and commit, both are carried into the clone - against the old behavior, each of its two faults put back in turn (`make rust-test CRATE=rust/gate/crates/land`): (i) plan.md was no file the carry resolves, so the second carry STOPPED on `specs/451-x/plan.md`; (ii) with plan.md let through, tasks.md was kept LINE by line - theirs' line dropped where ours held the same line - so the second box lost its `      research: rendering` line, the same words as the first box's. In feature 451's files both the box and the stub are appended at the file's end (its tasks.md has no GM-review box and its plan.md no `## T<n> - the close` heading), so every pair of filing trees conflicts in both.
    - The rule built: a conflicting hunk both sides only added to is kept both, ours first, then theirs BY BLOCK. In tasks.md a block is a list line with its continuation lines (a blank its own block), dropped where ours has it whole or theirs is the bare list line of a block ours has; one list line with different lines under it on each side stops, as a choice between them - the Occasions case of 451 T292 is unchanged, its tests pass as written. In plan.md each side's addition must open with a `### T<n>` heading (whole sections, the stub `make task-add` writes); a block (a `### ` heading and the lines under it) of theirs is dropped only where ours has it whole, because every stub's template lines are the same; one task's section written differently by both sides stops, since that is a choice between them. Anything else stops as before, nothing resolved.
  - **Decision 4: the words.** `scripts/container/builder-brief.md`: the pasted block gains the line `FILE what you find and leave, yourself, from your tree: ...`, and the sizing list a bullet with the measurement and "do not write 'do not file tasks' into a brief". `scripts/container/builder-report-format.md`: CANDIDATES is each found item as `filed: T<n>` with its title, or `NOT filed: <the command's refusal>`; "ids to file before the tick" leaves FOR THE SESSION's examples. The "do not file" instruction stood in no file of the repository (observed 2026-11-26, method: `grep -rni "not file"` over `scripts/`, `docs/`, `.claude/agents/` and `rust/guard`): it was written into each brief by the session, so the brief file's new bullet is where it is withdrawn. No guard refuses a builder's `make task-add` (the same grep over `rust/guard` for `task-add`: the event log's timing and the plan hold's attribution only). The `carry` line of the Makefile, the `land` row of `rust/gate/CLAUDE.md` and the module's own text name plan.md.

| step | alone off: fixed and pinned | fresh block vs HEAD | pool manifests moved | the last resort |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| two trees filing at once take two ids | `two_worktrees_filing_at_once_take_two_ids_each_in_its_own_tree`; green on the old code (451 T255 built it) | n/a: tooling | none | n/a |
| a carry of two trees' filed tasks keeps both boxes and both stubs | `two_trees_filed_tasks_are_carried_with_both_boxes_and_both_stubs`; red on each old fault | n/a: tooling | none | n/a |
| a box's continuation line stays with its box; a plan section kept whole, a clash stopped | `keep_both_takes_only_list_lines_both_sides_added`, `keep_both_takes_whole_plan_sections_both_sides_added` | n/a: tooling | none | n/a |

### T289 Approach (checklist part A)

1. **The goal, in the world.** A thing a builder finds and leaves is a filed task before its report is written, its id in the builder's own plan section, and reaches the clone with the builder's commit; nobody files from memory.
2. **The constraints.** 451 T17 (a deferral names its filed task and its order); 451 T255 (one writer of ids across the clone's trees); 451 T292 (`make carry` resolves only what keeping both sides provably answers, and stops on the rest); 451 T84 (one filing at a time); the builder brief's sizing (a new command is a builder of its own); 100% line coverage of new Rust.
3. **Where each comes from.** G: the task line. O: the coordinating session's brief with its counts of the unfiled candidates and the blocked rounds, observed 2026-11-26, method: the session's own count of that day's reports and reviews, given in the brief; and the tests' measurements above.
4. **Do they describe the world here?** In part, measured 2026-11-26 (the allotment test and the carry test above, each run on the old behavior): the cost is as described, the task line's remedy - a command over the report - would not have met the blocked rounds, the allotment the brief asked to be measured was already safe, and what was broken is the carry.
5. **The order.** No dependency. Until it lands, a builder still lists candidates and the session files them.
6. **The exits.** Green: `make builder-checks CRATE="rust/gate/crates/task rust/gate/crates/land"` green in the builder's tree, the carry test red on each old fault and green after. Red: what failed recorded and the task set down, a claim that it cannot be done ruled through `make arbiter-ask`.
7. **The search smell.** none.
8. **The budget.** One landing.
9. **Done, measured.** Measured 2026-11-26, method: `make rust-test CRATE=rust/gate/crates/land` three times - 125 passed with the change; with the tasks.md blocks cut line by line, 2 failed (the two tests of decision 3's fault ii); with plan.md also refused, the same 2 failed, the carry test on the STOPPED line naming `specs/451-x/plan.md`.
10. **Before moving a constant.** n/a.
11. **Before fitting things into room.** n/a.
12. **Before any fix.** The finding: a carry of a second tree's filed task stops on plan.md, and where it did not stop would write a task box without its research line, which the research-boxes rule and `make tick` read. No map changes.

**Found and left?** none. The carry's line-by-line keeping (decision 3, fault ii) was found in this task and is fixed here.

**Performance work?** yes, `[perf]`: it makes the builders' loop faster by removing a plan review's second round and a filing by hand for each found-and-left item, the kind of saving the GM approved on 2026-11-19 as "Fewer plan re-rounds". It is not an engine-speed task, so it carries no checklist, and no before-and-after timing is owed: no tool runs faster, a round is not run.

### T104 (the idle-tests suite failed a landing gate on good work, 2026-11-26 16:19Z, `make land` for T281 with two builders' checks beside it: `HOOK TESTS FAILED: idle-tests-hooks.sh`, green on the rerun unchanged; T99 had found two of its cases able to do that, case 6 red in 1 of 64 copies at a load of 133.7 and case 4b red 3 of 34 once, measured 2026-11-21 (T99's `many.sh`); the GM, 2026-11-26: "I agree with prioritizing the test that fails under load being fixed.")

- **Approach**: three causes, each reproduced first, in `tests/hooks/test-idle-tests-hooks.sh` and, for one, in the guard (`rust/guard/src/guards/idle_tests_hooks.rs`). So the gate's case is not named here; reproduction shows the ways below that the suite goes red on good work.

Reproduced: 8 of 8 copies red, "the losers deferred (0)", with each arming's return 1.0 s late, measured 2026-11-26 (`t104-shadow.sh`, 8 copies at a load of 242). The first cut read the run log at the second deferral, before the winner's start was written, and was red in 7 of 192 copies, measured 2026-11-26 (`t104-many.sh`, three batches of 64 at loads of 247 to 329); the wait now includes the start.

That is case 4b's shape on 2026-11-21: its three checks red (no second record, so no "skipped" in the newest record and no skip surfaced) and "changed content rolls again" green after them.     The fix is in `write_json`, the one writer of the state file and of every record: the document is written beside the file under the process's own name and renamed over it. The records gain the same: the suite reads a record as soon as its name appears.

Case 9 was red in 1 of 64 beside burners, measured 2026-11-26 (`t104-many.sh`). - **Approach**: the tests of `rust/mode_a` that read a pool sheet read it as the pool sweep does - a hand sheet as tracked, a declared generated exception composed in process from its tracked `<map>.compound.json` - so none reads a file git ignores.     - Every Rust source that names the tree outside its crate, by the rust checks' own definition (`rustc/kept.rs`: `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`, `top()`, `toplevel()`), observed 2026-11-26, method: `grep -rn` over `rust/**/*.rs`, each hit read for the path it joins: 69 `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` hits and 8 files naming `top()` or `toplevel()`.
    - Every crate's declared reads (`[package.metadata.l7r] reads`), observed 2026-11-26, method: `grep` over each `Cargo.toml` under `rust/`, each declared path set against the ignored listing above: three crates' reads cover the pool's generated output, `rust/mode_a` and `rust/gate/crates/pool` (`pool/`, `legacy-hand-authored-pool/`) and `rust/gate/crates/checks` (`.`). The other crates' declared paths hold, of that listing, only caches (`__pycache__/` under `scripts/`, `tests/`, `specs/` and `l7r/diagram/`) and the fixture crate's `Cargo.lock`, whose reader (`rust/gate/crates/rustc`) copies three named tracked files; `rust/gate` declares `development-secrets.ini`, which git ignores and a tree may lack.
    - A test can also reach the tree by a relative path or the working directory, observed 2026-11-26, method: `grep -rnE` for a `"../../` literal and `current_dir()` over `rust/**/*.rs`: no hit joins a path under `pool/`.
    - The tests of those three crates and of `rust/gate` in a scratch clone of this tree's HEAD that holds no ignored file, measured 2026-11-26 (`git clone` into the scratchpad, the clone's own launcher `scripts/gates/l7r-gate.sh rust test --crate ...` with `L7R_RUST_FRESH=1`): `rust/mode_a` 360 passed, 1 failed - the armory's pool test, `Os { code: 2, kind: NotFound }` at its `read_to_string` - and `rust/gate/crates/pool` 54 passed, `rust/gate/crates/checks` 196 passed, `rust/gate` 8 passed. No other crate was run there: that no other reads generated output rests on the reading above.

    | test | the ignored file | a fresh tree has it | before | now |
    |---|---|---|---|---|
    | `rust/mode_a` `audit::armory::tests::every_pool_magistracy_draws_its_armory_where_its_seed_rolls_it` | the two generated sheets' `.svg` | no | red, NotFound | composes both from their specs |

    No other test reads one: the rest of `rust/mode_a`'s real-tree tests read tracked files (the three hand magistracy sheets and the shrine's, every `.notes.md`, the hamlets' and the legacy pool's manifests, the specs, `tests/fixtures/`), and the pool sweep and the one-sheet sweep already composed (449 T211, T252); `rust/gate/crates/checks` and `rust/gate` passed in the scratch clone.

### T298 (the task line's count, observed 2026-11-26, method: the day's report as the coordinating session read it: a day's task time report was 2,294 lines in 38 per-task tables with no table of the window, the GM had to remember the period to ask for, and a batch landing's gate was booked to whichever of its tasks the mark or the command line named)

- **Approach**: `make task-time` opens with one table of the window and one line a landed task, books every `make land` to a batch that is no task's, drops four booking faults, and takes `SINCE=last`. The code is `rust/gate/crates/measure/src/measure/task_time/`: `top.rs` (the opening), `tiers.rs` (the batches and carries read from the logs), `book/tier.rs` (the second tier's rule), `book/cats.rs` (the category names, split out of `book.rs`, which had passed the file-scale bar) and `asked.rs` (the marker).
  - **How a batch landing was booked before** (the task's first question), measured 2026-11-26 (method: the report of HEAD's build over 2026-11-26T17:00:00Z to 18:58:30Z on the clone's logs, 364 lines, its per-task make-target tables read for `make land`): to ONE task, and not the same way twice. The T303 T305 batch's run was T303's (`make land | landing | 1 | 3.9` min) and its blocking T305's (`make land | landing | 0 | 0.0 | 2.9` blocking); the T309 T289 batch's first run, red, was T309's and its re-run T289's, 8.2 and 7.8 min, measured 2026-11-26 (the same report's two tables). The run went to the first task its command line started and its blocking to the task the session's mark named. Nothing was split and nothing counted twice.
  - **The window table and the task lines** (decision, labeled `map drawing convention`: a report's layout, no claim states it). The report opens with `## The window, every category` (minutes, blocking, each as a percentage of the working time) and `## The landed tasks, one line each` (landed, builders, builder minutes, minutes, blocking, where its own table ends). Builder minutes are the builder's span in the event log, start to stop, never its report's account; a resumed builder's later spans are not in it yet (found and left, below).
  - **The second tier, booked apart** (decision, the GM's second message in `request.md`'s T298 section). Every `make land` is a batch, of one task or several: its key is `(feature, "second tier: <tasks>")`, a task of no one's. In the window table it is ONE category, `the second tier (a batch's gate, repairs and push)`; it has its own section, one line a batch (tasks, landed, gate runs, re-runs, gate minutes, each failure and what its repair cost, minutes, blocking) and its time by what it was. A batch is read from the landing's `Phase` lines; a `make land` run with no end line is an attempt still in flight or stopped, its tasks read from the command's `T=`.
  - **A task's own table ends at its carry** (the task line's words). The carry is the `make carry FROM=<tree>` whose tree the pool's log (`<git common dir>/builder-pool.log`) says the task held. With no carry found (a task built in the clone, a carry no transcript holds) the table ends where the batch's first attempt starts, and the task's line says which: a GUESS, a knob (`Batch::from` in `book/tier.rs`), labeled so in the module's doc. After its landing a main session's line that names the task only because the mark never moved is the session's own (`-`).

### T298 Approach (checklist part A)

1. **The goal, in the world.** The GM asks for the time since he last asked without naming a period, reads where the window's time went in one table and one line a task, and sees the second tier's time and blocking on lines of their own, against no task.

3. **Where each comes from.** G: his three messages of 2026-11-26 in `request.md`'s T298 section; the task line's other words are the coordinating session's. O: the before and after reports and the trace above.
4. **Do they describe the world here?** Yes: the clone's event log, pool log and transcripts for the window from 17:00Z, read 2026-11-26 with both builds (above).
5. **The order.** Before the before-and-after comparison of two-tier checking, which reads its second tier line. 451 T316 (`prewarm`) lands after it and extends `columns::category` itself.
6. **The exits.** Green: `make builder-checks CRATE="rust/gate/crates/measure"` green in the builder's tree (the first tier, the trial of 2026-11-26); the full gate and the coverage run are the landing's. Red: what failed recorded and the task set down, a claim that it cannot be done ruled through `make arbiter-ask`.
7. **The search smell.** none.
8. **The budget.** One landing.
9. **Done, measured.** The five tests red before and green after, and the real window's minutes conserved (735.4 and 735.3), measured 2026-11-26 (above).
10. **Before moving a constant.** n/a: no claim's number moves; the second tier's blocking defaults are new GUESS knobs, stated above.
11. **Before fitting things into room.** n/a.
12. **Before any fix.** The findings: a batch's gate booked to one of its tasks, a 80.9 min sampler in T305's table, four make targets in `Makefile targets the guard's table does not book`, and 12.1 min of a batch's gate waits read as a wait loop, each observed 2026-11-26 in the reports above. No map changes.

**Found and left?**
- A `make carry` held or refused while a gate runs, and another run's build-slot wait while the gate holds a slot, are not attributed to the gate, and a carried task that no `make land` has yet named has no batch: two of the three signals the task line names for the second tier's blocking read as zero whatever happened. Not fixed here: each needs a signal the logs do not yet carry (the carry's refusal, the slot's holder), a build of its own. Filed as T319; lands before T302.
- The event-log reader keeps one start and one stop an agent, so a resumed builder's later spans are dropped: the task lines' builder minutes read 7.6 of T303's 7.9 min, 13.9 of T309's 15.2 and 8.8 of T289's 13.7 (measured 2026-11-26, method: the 451 log's start and stop lines for each builder against the report's column). Not fixed here: the reader (`events.rs`, `load_all`) is shared with `make where-time` and `make feature-report`, and keying its lines by their second as well broke a test that pins two stops a second apart as one and moved other reports' figures, so it was reverted and is a task of its own. Filed as T324; lands before T302.
- `wait loops (held open, no work)` is still 25.6 min of the window's 128.7 min of blocking, its largest category, in tasks' own tables (measured 2026-11-26, the after report above); the defect fixed here shows one way such a minute is not a wait the task was held by - a builder's leftover background loop named in the session's `inflight`, blocking the waiter's task by 451 T243's default for a run with no clue. Not fixed here: outside a batch there is no landing run to prefer, and which of those loops held a task up has to be measured loop by loop first. Filed as T328; lands before T302.

**Performance work?** no: it changes what a report shows and where time is booked; nothing runs faster.

The first ran with both of the machine's slots free throughout and warmed all 34 crates in 61.3 s with none cut short, measured 2026-11-26 (its own log, a line a crate, and the wall time). The handout keeps that commit in the tree's own git directory (`prewarm-base`) and the next one starts the pre-warm from it; a tree with none on record is measured from where it stood before the handout brought it on. A cold tree's first handout writes it and starts nothing: its whole cache is cold, which the handout already says. Decided by this builder from reading `release`; the brief's sketch named the commits since the tree's previous HEAD.
