The pre-warm then takes each crate whose build reads a changed file - its own files, a crate's it builds from by path, the workspace's manifests - through the kept keys' own reader (`Kept::reads_any` over `Reads::Source`), fewest dependencies first, so a crate is built before those that build on it.
  - **The same build as a real run's.** One `cargo test --no-run --quiet --manifest-path <crate>` a crate, the words `stepped` asks first (449 T93's "builds the test binary first"), through `cargo_call`, the one builder of a cargo call's words and environment that `cargo_in` now uses too, from the tree's root with the tree's own target directory. Nothing is run and no result is kept: a kept result is a real run's alone. `builder-tree` starts the tree's own wrapper from the tree, with the handout's `L7R_GATE_TREE`, `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` and make variables taken out of its environment.
  - **It holds a slot only while another is spare** (the brief: "never hold a slot while the tree's own builder (or anyone) waits on one more than briefly"). It never goes through `slot::around`: it takes a slot only where one is free at that instant (`slot::free_now`) and a second is free beside it (`slot::spare`, which looks at each slot's lock and holds none), else looks again a poll later, and so writes no `slot-wait` line. While its cargo runs it looks every half second (`POLL`, a GUESS, the slot's own) for a real run in its tree - a live member of the run lock's record of the tree's target directory (`runlock::busy`; the pre-warm joins no run) - which ends it, and for the machine's slots: once none is spare, a compile of some tree having taken the last, it kills its cargo, with what cargo started, as one process group, gives its slot back, and builds the crate again when two are free. So the next compile to start, of any tree, finds a slot free. The rule reads the slots' own locks, which every tree's holders take whatever slot code that tree runs, so it holds from the first pre-warm, with no tree left unseen. With one slot on the machine (`L7R_BUILD_SLOTS=1`) it builds nothing; with none (`0`) it builds freely, as every compile does.
  - **A waiter's mark was built first and replaced** (plan review round 1). The first form let the pre-warm build beside a real compile and yield when a waiting call left a file beside the slot files. Run live it held a slot while two real runs of other trees waited 39.3 s and 25.2 s, measured 2026-11-26 (their `slot-wait` `Phase` lines beside the pre-warm's): those trees ran the slot code from before this task and left no mark. A rule that needs every tree's code to be new fails for as long as one is not, so the mark was taken out and the spare rule above built in its place.
  - **It fails nothing.** The handout does not wait for it: the process is started in its own process group with its input closed and its output to `prewarm.log` in the tree's git directory, and a pre-warm that cannot start is one line of the handout's notes. It exits 0 whatever cargo said (a crate that does not build is the builder's own run's to report), runs one a tree (`prewarm.lock` in the target directory), and stops at a ceiling of 900 s (`CEILING_S`, a GUESS knob, `L7R_PREWARM_CEILING`). `L7R_PREWARM=0` starts none, and stops one that was started by hand.
  - **Booked apart.** Each cargo call of a pre-warm writes one `Phase` line, step `prewarm`, make target `prewarm`, code 130 where it was cut short. `columns::category` names that step and books it to no call, so a pre-warm whose span falls inside a builder's own Bash call is not that call's compile. `make task-time` does not yet show its seconds as a category: the lines are in the event log, and T317 books them by the task that held the tree.
  - **The record**: `dev/audits/builder-prewarm.md` (measurement, falsifier, cost), the `rustc` and `task` rows of `rust/gate/CLAUDE.md`, `make builder-tree`'s help line.

### T316 Approach (checklist part A)

1. **The goal, in the world.** A builder handed a warm pool tree finds, at its first test run, the crates others moved already built, so that run compiles its own edit alone; and no compile of any tree finds every slot held because a pre-warm holds one, for more than a poll.
2. **The constraints.** T316's line in tasks.md. The brief: measured first; started detached at the handout, after the tree is at HEAD and held; the test builds through the gate's own path (the slot, the target directory, the words of a real run); a slot only where one is free, never held while anyone waits on one more than briefly, the pre-warm ended by a real run in its tree; logged to the tree's git directory; never failing the handout; off at `L7R_PREWARM=0`; a `prewarm` `Phase` line; red-first tests; 100% line coverage of new Rust; an audit-register entry.
3. **Where each comes from.** G: T316's line of `tasks.md`, which carries his question of 2026-11-26. O: the measurements in the Approach.
4. **Do they describe the world here?** Yes for the mechanism, measured 2026-11-26 (the Approach's first two bullets): a handout's moved crates are compiled by the first run. The size of the gain is what moved: the test build's 7.2 s on the handout, measured 2026-11-26 (its `build` `Phase` line), more where a crate many build on moved.
5. **The order.** After T284 (the slot) and T285 (the pool); before T302.
6. **The exits.** Green: `make builder-checks CRATE="rust/gate/crates/rustc rust/gate/crates/task rust/gate/crates/measure"` here (the first tier; the full gate runs once in the clone over the batch). Red: what failed recorded and the task set down, a claim that it cannot be done ruled through `make arbiter-ask`.
7. **The search smell.** none.
8. **The budget.** One landing.
9. **Done, measured.** RED FIRST, 2026-11-26, method: the handout's call of `prewarm` taken out of `take`, `make rust-test CRATE=rust/gate/crates/task`: `98 passed; 1 failed`, the new test; `moved` made to return no crate, `make rust-test CRATE=rust/gate/crates/rustc`: `97 passed; 5 failed`, the five of `rustc::tests::prewarm` as they then stood (one since rewritten for the spare rule, round 1); both restored, `99 passed` and `102 passed`, and `rust/gate/crates/measure` `235 passed`. THE FIRST TEST BUILD after the core crate moved: 7.7 s without the pre-warm and 0.1 s after it had finished, measured 2026-11-26 (the Approach's second bullet). `make builder-checks` over the crates changed, green.
10. **Before moving a constant.** n/a: new knobs, `CEILING_S` = 900 s and `POLL` = 0.5 s, each labeled GUESS beside it and in `dev/audits/builder-prewarm.md`.

Visible effect: a pre-warm's cost is read from the raw `Phase` lines of `.git/l7r-events/`, not from the report. Not fixed here: it is the readers' work in the `measure` crate (`columns.rs`'s `tie`, `task_time/book.rs`), a job of its own beside this one. Filed as T317; lands before T302.
- The lint's build is not warmed: clippy's artifacts are another build than `cargo test --no-run`'s, and the first `make builder-checks` after a handout compiles them (4.8 s for `land` on the handout measured 2026-11-26, method: the `lint` `Phase` line of `make builder-checks CRATE=rust/gate/crates/land` in `diagram-backlog-t269`). Visible effect: a builder's first lint still compiles what others moved. Not fixed here: the task's line asks for the test builds, and a second build a crate doubles what a pre-warm holds a slot for, so it is measured on a deep crate first. Filed as T318; lands before T302.

- One real test run of nine that ended a pre-warm failed in its tests and passed when run again (the Approach, "The end by a real run, run live"). Visible effect: a builder's first run after a handout could go red on good work, once in nine here. Whether the killed cargo, the guard's rebuild under the suite (the recipe touched `rust/guard/shared`, which the guard's wrapper rebuilds on) or the `land` suite itself caused it is not known: the output was not kept and eight further tries, three by the same recipe, passed. Not fixed here: there is nothing yet to fix, only a failure to reproduce with its output kept. Filed as T329; lands before T302.
- A pre-warm that a real run ends early leaves crates unbuilt, and the next handout no longer counts them as moved, because the handout's commit is recorded when the pre-warm starts. Visible effect: where the builder's own runs never built those crates, a later builder's first run compiles them with no pre-warm, as before this task. Not fixed here: it is no worse than no pre-warm, and the fix (the base written when a pre-warm finishes) changes who writes the record. Filed as T330; lands before T302.

**Performance work?** yes (a `[perf]` task, 451 FR-013: it makes the builders' loop faster); not an engine-speed task, so `docs/performance-checklist.md` does not apply.

The 6: a report describing an ask's wording (`"For you to confirm" does ask you for a confirmation, so the hook was right`), a check described by its question (`It asks: is a pool tree free, and does the queue hold a task ...?`), a checklist's own questions listed (`3. What do you expect to save?`), two figures of a time breakdown (`485 minutes of blocking were waiting on you, 27% of the window's blocking.`, `Blocking minutes, with waiting on you kept separate:`), and an offer the escalation-check had kept that morning, restated, each read from the 18 firings, observed 2026-11-26, method: the quoted line of each refusal.
  - **The rules**, each the narrowest that passes its line:
    - (a) DESCRIBED: a quoted or backticked phrase that is the subject of `does ask you` / `did ask you` is blanked with its verb before the spans are, since the span is what tells it from the session's own `I do ask you`. A question inside a span was already blanked.
    - (b) REPORTED: the `?` rule does not read a line whose last sentence runs from `asks:` / `asks whether` / `asks if` to its `?` with no `you` or `your` in it and no other `?` on the line. `The review asks: are the wider banks acceptable to you?`, `... asks whether a tree is free. Can I hand it to T300?` `It asks: is a tree free? And may I hand it to T300?` and `What do you make of the check? It asks: is a tree free?` still fire.
    - (c) CHECKLIST: the `?` rule does not read an item of a numbered or bulleted list of two or more whose every item ends `?`, under a lead-in ending `:` that names a checklist, or questions something `has`, `asks`, `holds`, `lists`, `poses`, `carries` or `answers`, and names neither the GM nor the session (`you`, `your`, `I`, `my`, `me`, `we`, `our`). No exemption for lists: `Two questions for you:`, `Open questions:`, `I have two questions on the checklist:`, a list with an item that is no question, a single item and a list with no lead-in all fire, and an item in a question's own words (`Should I ...`, `ASK` and `STATED`) fires wherever it stands, as suite case 9 (the 2026-10-25 message) does.
    - (d) FIGURE: `waiting (on|for) you` is a measurement where a count of minutes, hours, seconds, days or a share (`%`, `percent`), with an optional `of ...`, is the subject of `was`/`were` before it (the past tense of a measurement, never `is`/`are`), and the clause ends after it (`.`, `;`, `|`, `)`, the line's end) or goes on to another figure (`, 27%`). `3 questions were waiting on you.` (a count of things), `Two hours of review are waiting on you.` (work put to him), `... were waiting on you: the budget's words.`, `..., the budget answer.`, `... waiting on your budget answer.` and `The sheet has been 40 minutes waiting on you.` still fire, each a line of the Rust test, observed 2026-11-26, method: the test's asks.

### T299, T282 Approach (checklist part A)

1. **The goal, in the world.** A final message that reports an ask's wording, a check's question, a checklist's questions or a figure of the time spent waiting on the GM ends its turn with no refusal; where a refusal is still false, the session goes on and the GM reads nothing about it. A message that puts a question, a confirmation, a decision or an offer to him is still refused until the filter has read it.
2. **The constraints.** Feature 429 FR-002 and amendment 1 (a question or an offer with no review behind it owes the filter); feature 432 (a kept question named by its id is no new ask); T235's and T272's pinned asks and statements, every one as it was; 451 T170 (a changed guard message is reviewed).
3. **Where each comes from.** G: the GM's words of 2026-11-26 in this section's heading, as the coordinating session's brief relays them. O: the two corpora measured above.
4. **Do they describe the world here?** Yes: the 28 real firings and T235's 112 ran through the real guard before and after, measured 2026-11-26 (each message through `tests/hooks/escalation-hooks.sh stop` in a fixture clone).
5. **The order.** No dependency. T282 is this bundle's rule (a) and its key item, one landing with T299.
6. **The exits.** Green: `make builder-checks CRATE="rust/guard"` and `tests/hooks/test-escalation-hooks.sh` in the builder's tree, the full gate at the landing. Red: what failed recorded and the task set down, a claim that it cannot be done ruled through `make arbiter-ask`.
7. **The search smell.** none.
8. **The budget.** One landing.
9. **Done, measured.** RED FIRST, measured 2026-11-26. On HEAD's guard the new Rust test failed (`make rust-test CRATE=rust/guard`: 539 passed, 1 failed, on the described ask), and the five statements of suite case 13 were each refused (the same lines through `tests/hooks/escalation-hooks.sh stop`). After, measured 2026-11-26 (`make rust-test CRATE=rust/guard` and `tests/hooks/test-escalation-hooks.sh`): 540 passed, and with the key's test, red with the mask off (540 passed, 1 failed: 7 keys for 5), 541 passed, the suite 67 passed, 0 failed. The corpus's false rate fell from 33% (6 of 18) to 8% (1 of 13) with no T lost, measured 2026-11-26 (the 28 through the guard, before and after).
10. **Before moving a constant.** n/a.
11. **Before fitting things into room.** n/a.
12. **Before any fix.** The finding: the hook refused turns that asked the GM nothing, six on these two days through HEAD's guard, each a filter run or the session's own account of a false positive in a message to him. No map changes.

**Found and left?**

- The restated kept offer still fires (one of the 13): an ad-hoc escalation-check's verdict is recorded nowhere the guard reads. Not fixed here: it needs a record of what an ad-hoc check kept, a new mechanism and not a detector rule. Filed as T335; lands before T302.
- This tree's first test build after its pre-warm failed to link twice (`rust-lld: undefined hidden symbol` in `l7r_guard`'s lib test), and built once the newest incremental session directory of that build was removed, observed 2026-11-26 (`make rust-test CRATE=rust/guard`). The pre-warm ended mid-build is the suspected cause, not shown: the directory's time was after the two failed builds. Not fixed here: it is the gate's `rustc` crate and T316's pre-warm, to be reproduced first. Filed as T336; lands before T302.

**Performance work?** no: it removes false refusals of a Stop hook; nothing runs faster.

### T293 (the GM asked on 2026-11-26 whether the tooling shows where a task's time is going while it is in progress, his words in `request.md` under "2026-11-26: a live view of the tasks in flight (451 T293)"; it did not: `make task-time` books a task's categories when it lands)

- **Approach**: a new read-only command, `make task-progress [BACK=<N>h] [AT=<ISO UTC>]`, which runs `l7r-gate measure task-progress`. The code is `rust/gate/crates/measure/src/measure/task_time/progress.rs` (the view), `progress/scene.rs` (who is running) and `progress/render.rs` (the text), with the audit entry `dev/audits/task-progress.md`. It prints one block for each held pool tree's builders, one for each landing in flight, a line for each page session and each review agent of the session's own, the pool's free trees, and the tasks carried into the clone that no landing has placed. No booking rule changed and `make task-time`'s output is untouched: three one-line visibility edits (`pub mod progress;`, and `pub(super)` on `book::actor` and `tiers::dir_name`) are all the existing code gives up.
  - **T293-D1, a submodule of `task_time` with its own subcommand** (CONVENTION: where code lives, no claim states it). A child module reads `task_time`'s private `sums`, `load`, `all_logs`, `bases` and `iso_of`, so nothing is copied and nothing is made public beyond the two `pub(super)`.
  - **T293-D2, a builder's minutes are the landed report's booking over its family alone** (CONVENTION). `book::book` runs over a world holding only the builder's own lines, the agents it dispatched and theirs, and their runs, and the result is summed over every key by category. Reason: the categories and rules are the landed report's with no second booking to drift from it, and summing over every key makes a wrong task name on a line harmless.
  - **T293-D3, one block for each HELD POOL TREE, then one for any running builder no tree is held for** (CONVENTION). A tree's builders are found by its task, its feature number and a start at or after the tree's take, read from the registry `builder-pool.json`. Reason: a builder waiting on its plan review has STOPPED, so a rule of "a start and no stop" would drop exactly the builders a reader most wants to see; builders made 41 background Agent dispatches that day, each returning in under 2 s (observed 2026-11-26, method: the build half's count over the 451 event log's builder Agent calls).
  - **T293-D4, RUNNING is two tests** (CONVENTION). An agent is running when it has no stop, or own lines after its stop, AND its session's latest `Stop` line names it `inflight` or its last line is after that `Stop`. Reason: a start with no stop is also an agent cut off; three agents had a start and no stop, two running builders and a `spec-fidelity` cut off four minutes after it started, and the latest `Stop` named exactly the two (observed 2026-11-26, method: a Python pass at 20:27Z over the 451 log's start, stop and `Stop` lines since 08:00Z). A `Stop` written before the `inflight` field cannot say, and the agent is then taken as running.
  - **T293-D5, the step now is the open make run with its LAST FINISHED phase: a DEVIATION from the task line**, which asks for "the open make span". No `Phase` line is ever open: the writer takes a span as `<step>:<t0>:<t1>:<code>` (`event_log/phase.rs`) and has no start form, so each line is written when its step ends. The phase running at this moment sits in the run's own category until its line lands, and the output's header says so. Reason for not adding a start marker: it changes the event log's writer and every reader of it, a task of its own, and the open run with its last finished phase already names where a builder is.
  - **T293-D6, a call open now is closed at the moment of the view by a line made in memory, never written** (CONVENTION). An open call is a `PreToolUse` with no end, begun no earlier than its actor's last call that ended and after its last stop; an older one with no end was refused by a guard and never ran. The session's own open calls are closed the same way, which is how a foreground `make land` is seen. Reason: `columns::runs` and the booking read closed spans only, and a made line lets both run unchanged.
  - **T293-D7, the model turn open now is a row of its own**, `builders: the turn open now (its tool not yet known)` (CONVENTION). Reason: the booking names a turn by the call that ends it, which has not happened yet.
  - **T293-D8, context is read live from the builder's transcript** (CONVENTION), by `l7r_shared::context::context`, the context-cap guard's own reader, against `CAP_TOKENS`; where no transcript is found, from its stop line's `ctx`; else it is said to be not known. Each figure printed names its source. Reason: the log carries `ctx` only on a `SubagentStop` line, so a running builder has none there.
  - **T293-D9, a pool tree's `Phase` lines are re-tasked from the pool's log** (CONVENTION, around the open T332). Each such line takes the task that `builder-pool.log` says held its tree when the phase began, and a block's runs are tied only to `Phase` lines whose `clone` is its own tree: two builders share the session's id and both run `make builder-checks`. A builder no tree is held for takes the phases that no pool tree wrote and that name its task.
  - **T293-D10, a resumed builder is shown RUNNING on the in-flight test alone and its block's minutes are headed AT LEAST** (CONVENTION, around the open T324). Its line says it may have stopped again since its last line. Reason: the reader keeps one start and one stop for an agent, so the later spans cannot be read until T324 lands, and a floor that says it is a floor is true.
  - **T293-D11, a landing in flight is a session `make land` run open at the moment of the view that passes the in-flight test** (CONVENTION): a call closed by T293-D6, or a background run with no end or an end at or after that moment. Its tasks come from the open attempt `tiers::batches` finds, its phase is the last finished `make: land` `Phase` line, and its minutes are the same booking over its one run. Where no open attempt matches the run - its end line is written and its call has not yet returned - it is named by its call's task alone.
  - **T293-D12, staged is each task's latest carry with no landed batch naming the task after it and no landing in flight** (CONVENTION), from `tiers::carries`. A red attempt since the carry is said on the line, and a held tree's block says when its task was carried.
  - **T293-D13, a page session is ONE LINE: a DEVIATION from the task line**, which lists a page session beside a builder with its task, tree, context and categories. The line is a run log `page-sessions/run-*.log` written since the read-back that has not said `ALL DONE`, with the brief it is in and how many of its briefs have ended. Reason: a page session is a detached runner of fresh sessions, not an agent of the session's, so no start line, pool tree or family ties its sessions' lines to a block, and booking them is left to its own task (Found and left, below) rather than guessed here. The bound on the file's time is needed because a killed runner's log never says `ALL DONE`: 73 of the directory's 299 entries held the line, and the entries are not all run logs (observed 2026-11-26, method: `grep -l 'ALL DONE'` over the clone's `page-sessions` directory against `ls | wc -l`).
  - **T293-D14, the read-back is the earliest held tree's take or `BACK_H` hours, whichever is earlier** (`BACK_H` is 2.0, a GUESS and a knob: unmeasured, set to hold a builder's whole run; `BACK=` overrides it). Only logs modified since the read-back are parsed. `AT=` gives the view as of a past moment: the set-aside lines are cut there too, though a transcript read today can still name a later end.
  - **T293-D15, the minutes shown are machine minutes, and blocking minutes are not shown** (CONVENTION). A run and the turn beside it both count, so a block's minutes can pass its clock, which the header says. Reason: blocking is found by walking the main session's waits, and a family's world has no main session in it.
  - **A defect of the build half found by this half's test and fixed here**: a task carried twice showed its EARLIEST carry on its held tree's block, against the rule beside the loop that the latest carry is the one a landing waits on. `landings()` walks the carries latest first and wrote each one over the last; it now keeps the first it writes. Pinned by `a_cut_off_builder_a_carried_tree_and_a_landing_gone_red`, red before the fix.
  - **A second, in the Makefile, fixed here**: the build half's `.PHONY` line ran `task-progress` and `land-batch` together, so neither was declared phony.
  - **The figures.** The command took 19.2 s of wall time on the session clone's real logs with the tool built, four builders in flight and a read-back near two hours (observed 2026-11-26, method: `time scripts/gates/l7r-gate.sh measure task-progress --root /diagram/.clones/diagram-backlog`, one run at about 20:45Z, the two runs that rebuilt the tool first taking 44.3 s and 41.5 s). `make task-time SINCE=24h` is recorded at 55 s (observed 2026-11-26, method: the figure T298's builder recorded for the same clone, not re-run here). Its output on those logs, whole, is in the build half's handoff, `.git/l7r-handoffs/T293-build.md` of the session clone.

### T293 Approach (checklist part A)

1. **The goal, in the world.** While builders, a landing or a page session are running, one command says which are running, what each is doing at this moment and where each builder's minutes have gone so far, in the same categories the landed report will use.
2. **The constraints.** FR-013 (performance work first); the task time breakdown's booking (451 T243, T298) is reused and not copied; the command reads only and joins no gate; the builders' context cap is read with the guard's own reader; the open T324 and T332 are worked around in the open, never hidden.
3. **Where each comes from.** G: the GM's words of 2026-11-26 in `request.md` under "2026-11-26: a live view of the tasks in flight (451 T293)". O: the measurements of T293-D3, T293-D4 and T293-D13 above. The rest of the task's line is the coordinating session's.
4. **Do they describe the world here?** Yes: the command was run on the session clone's real logs with builders in flight, its blocks named the held trees' tasks, and the one thing it missed on a real run, a landing in flight, was fixed and pinned.
5. **The order.** After T298 (the booking it reuses) and T285 (the pool it reads); before T324 and T332, whose gaps it names and whose landing removes its two workarounds.
6. **The exits.** Green: every test of the table green and `make builder-checks CRATE="rust/gate/crates/measure"` green. Red: what failed recorded and the task set down, a claim that it cannot be done ruled through `make arbiter-ask`.
7. **The search smell.** None: each rule came from a real run's output read against what was in flight at that moment.
8. **The budget.** One landing.
9. **Done, measured.** The tests were written AFTER the code, so there is no red-first run of the whole to claim. What was seen red: on the build half's first test run 3 of its 5 tests failed, one on a real defect (a child agent met at its launch before its own start got no kind and no start time, fixed in `scene.rs`) and two on wrong expectations (observed 2026-11-26, method: the build half's `make rust-test CRATE=rust/gate/crates/measure`, as its handoff records). On this half's first run of its four new tests 2 failed, one on the carry defect above and one on an expectation of mine that the loader refuses a line whose time it cannot read, which it drops; that part of the test was removed (observed 2026-11-26, method: `make rust-test CRATE=rust/gate/crates/measure`, `248 passed; 2 failed`). After, `make builder-checks CRATE="rust/gate/crates/measure"` is green with `250 passed` (observed 2026-11-26, method: that command, its log `t293-checks-8.log` in the session scratchpad). No coverage run was made in this tree: the first tier forbids it, and the batch gate's is the one that counts.
10. **Before moving a constant.** n/a: `BACK_H` is a new GUESS knob, no claim's.
11. **Before fitting things into room.** n/a.
12. **Before any fix.** No map changes. The carry fix changes what a reader of the command's own output sees: a held tree's block named a carry that a later one had replaced.

**Found and left?**
- A resumed builder's later start and stop lines are not read, so its block's minutes are a floor and it may be shown RUNNING after it has stopped again; the output says both. Not fixed here: it is the event-log reader's rule, which every report shares. Filed as T324; lands before T22.
- A `Phase` line written from a pool tree can name another task; this view re-tasks each from the pool's log, and `make task-time` does not. Not fixed here: the line's writer is the build tools', outside this command. Filed as T332; lands before T22.
- `make task-time` books the gap between a builder's stop and its resumed next line as that builder's model turn. Not fixed here: it moves the landed report's numbers and sits on T324's lines. Filed as T345; lands before T22.
- A carry is booked to the task that took the tree in the carry's last second, so the staged list can name the wrong task: on the real logs T308 was listed as carried at a moment that was T301's carry. Not fixed here: it changes `make task-time`'s batch tables. Filed as T346; lands before T22.
- A compound command is named by its first make target alone, so a builder in `make docs; make builder-checks` reads as in `make docs` throughout. Not fixed here: the name is `book::run_cat`'s, which the landed report shares. Filed as T348; lands before T22.
- A page session has one line and no minutes by category, where the task's line asks them as a builder's (T293-D13). Not fixed here: its sessions' ids must first be read from the runner's log and their lines booked as a family's, a build with its own measurement. Filed as T350; lands before T22.
- A builder's background run whose shell died with no notice stays listed as in the background, and one that ends in the seconds the view is being read is dropped from its builder's line. Not fixed here: a subagent's shells have no in-flight list to test against, a design of its own. Filed as T349; lands before T22.

**Performance work?** yes (a `[perf]` task, 451 FR-013: it shows where the builders' loop spends its time while it runs); not an engine-speed task, so the performance checklist's engine items do not apply.

### T274 (the number of builders at once is certified against the container's memory limit from samples, and on 2026-11-26 those samples were a shell loop the coordinating session started by hand, so the three- and four-at-once comment batches ran unsampled (`docs/process-decisions.md`, "Two code builders at once"))

- **Approach**: a detached sampler, one a clone, writes the machine's memory and load as a JSON line every ten seconds, `make builder-tree` asks for it at every handout, and `make sampler-report` reads a window as one table (`rust/gate/crates/measure/src/measure/sampler.rs`, its report `sampler/report.rs`; the handout's call in `rust/gate/crates/task/src/builder_tree.rs`; `make sampler`, `sampler-start`, `sampler-stop`, `sampler-report`). Built by a first builder and closed by a second (the brief's two halves); each decision below is the first builder's unless it says otherwise, with its label and its reason.
  - **D1. The samples live in `<git common dir>/l7r-events/samples/mem-samples.jsonl`. Label: DEVIATION from the brief's path** (`<git common dir>/l7r-events/mem-samples.jsonl`); the task line's "into the tree's l7r-events" still holds. Reason, read from the code and not measured: every reader of that directory takes a `.jsonl` there for a feature's event log, and none descends into a folder. The hook's launch lookup scans the most recently written `.jsonl` first (`rust/guard/shared/src/guards/event_log_hooks.rs`, `launch_line`), which would always be the samples; `measure/events.rs` (`lines_of`, `all_logs`), `tool_yield.rs` and `stepback_bundle.rs` read every one; `cohort/speckit_todo/report.rs` (`active`) calls a clone active by the newest entry's time, so a file written every ten seconds would keep an idle clone "active" for as long as the sampler ran. Observed 2026-11-26, method: those five call sites read, and `scripts/`, `tests/hooks/` and the Makefile searched for a walker of the directory - the one found, `scripts/state-sync.sh`'s `commit`, skips what is not a file, so the folder does not break `make state-push`, and the samples are therefore not kept off the container with the event logs. The readers were not run against a file at the brief's path. Were the brief's path held literal, the change is the constant `DIR` and a filter in each of those readers.
  - **D2. A module of the `measure` crate; the `task` crate gains no dependency. Label: design decision.** `measure` already builds on the pool registry (`l7r_shared::builder_pool`) and holds `task-time`; `builder_tree` runs the gate binary as a program, as the pre-warm of 451 T316 does.
  - **D3. The sampler names itself. Label: design decision.** The pid file (`l7r-sampler.pid` in the git common directory) is written by the sampler, its own pid and start time, and it reads the file before every sample. So two starts at once leave one sampler (the other ends at its next sample), a stop is a file removal that works where the signal does not, and a sampler whose clone was deleted ends by itself. The pid file is not claimed with `create_new`: the self-check gives the guarantee with fewer states. Cost: for at most one interval two samplers can both write, a duplicated line.
  - **D4. Alive is the pid AND its start time, and a zombie is dead. Label: design decision.** A pid the kernel gave to another process does not read as the sampler.
  - **D5. Started through `setsid` with its three streams on `/dev/null` and every other inherited descriptor marked close-on-exec. Label: design decision** (the pattern of `rust/gate/crates/pages/src/runner.rs`, `close_inherited`). Without it a handout read through a pipe would wait on the pipe for the sampler's hours, and an inherited build slot's `flock` would be held as long. A start read through a pipe returned in 0.39 s, measured 2026-11-26 (`time` of `scripts/gates/l7r-gate.sh measure sampler start 2>&1 | cat` in the clone, one run, the build half's).
  - **D6. A second start exits 0. Label: design decision.** "One is running" is the wanted state, and `make builder-tree` asks at every handout.
  - **D7. The sampler ends at its size bound (`MAX_BYTES`), and the next start moves the file aside. Label: derived from a measured line size; no knob.** A line was 277 bytes with four trees held, measured 2026-11-26 (18,036 bytes over 65 lines, `wc -c` and `wc -l` of the real run's file, the build half's). A twelve-hour run at ten seconds is 4,320 lines, about 1.2 MB by that line size, so 4 MiB holds about 42 sampled hours (arithmetic from the measured line, 2026-11-26). The sampler ENDS at the bound, as the brief says; a start that finds the file past it moves it to `mem-samples.1.jsonl`, replacing the one before, and begins a new one - without that the next handout's sampler would end at once and sampling would stop for good, silently. A clone keeps at most two files; the report reads both.
  - **D8. Each line carries `max`, `cores` and `peak`. Label: design decision.** The report is then a function of the file, and the audit entry's falsifier - a report that disagrees with the cgroup's `memory.peak` - is checked on every report: `memory.peak` tracks `memory.current`, page cache included, so the report sets the sampled `cur` peak beside it (over it, the line says DISAGREE) and prints how far `memory.peak` rose in the window, which is what a spike between two samples leaves.
  - **D9. The median is the middle sample (the mean of the middle two), the 95th percentile the nearest rank. Label: CONVENTION**, chosen because the two reproduce the figures `docs/process-decisions.md` records for the kept hand logs (the baseline below).
  - **D10. Stall and OOM kills are the sums of the rises between one sample and the next, booked to the later sample's row, and a pair more than 120 s apart (`GAP_S`, a GUESS knob), or whose counter fell, is booked to no row and counted on the report's "gaps" line. Label: design decision with one GUESS knob**, `GAP_S`, which is twelve of the default interval, so a late sample under load is no gap and a stopped sampler is.
  - **D11. A row is the count of pool trees HELD by the registry, and the report prints the caveat. Label: design decision, with its limit filed** (Found and left). A hand log's `builders=` is its count; a hand log with none is the row `?` - no count was invented for those logs.
  - **D12. CPU stall is read from `/proc/pressure/cpu`, the brief's file. Label: design decision.** In this container that file may be the host's and not the cgroup's `cpu.pressure`; the two were not compared.
  - **D13. The knobs. Label: GUESS knobs, each said so beside its constant, in the make help and in the audit entry.** `L7R_MEM_MARGIN_GIB`, 7: the anonymous memory a sample is counted over, 3 GiB under the limit, the figure the 2026-11-26 runs were read against; the report's head line names it a GUESS knob. `L7R_SAMPLE_MAX_H`, 12: longer than any batch run so far, so a sampler nobody stops still ends. `L7R_SAMPLE_S`, 10, is not a guess: it is the hand loop's interval, kept so the kept logs and the sampler's compare sample for sample.
  - **D14. `make builder-tree` asks after ANY handout that exits 0, the "already holds it" one too, and waits for the start so its line is shown. Label: design decision.** What the start said is appended to the handout's standard error; a start that fails or cannot be run is a line, never the handout's exit code; `L7R_SAMPLER=0` asks for none. On a cold handout it asks only after the new tree's guard build, so where that is the clone's first handout the guard's compile goes unsampled.
  - **D15. The sampler writes no `Phase` line and no event-log line. Label: design decision.** It is in no task's time. `make task-time SINCE=1h` ran with the samples folder present and printed no line naming the sampler or the samples, observed 2026-11-26, method: the command's output read (the build half's; it shows the reader did not break, and there is no timing of it without the folder to say it did not slow).
  - **D16. The samples' folder is made once, at the loop's start, and a line's append never makes it. Label: design decision.** A sampler whose clone was deleted must not make the clone's directories again on its way out.
  - **D17 (the closing builder's). The words `make builder-tree` asks with are a function of their own, `sampler_words`. Label: design decision.** In `Env::live` they were a closure that ran only where `L7R_SAMPLER` was not `0` in the environment of the test run itself, so whether its lines were reached depended on who ran the tests; apart, each case is a test's.
  - **The real run** (2026-11-26, the build half's, in the clone `diagram-backlog`, four pool trees held throughout; method: `make sampler-report SINCE=2026-11-26T20:52:00Z` after `make sampler-stop`). 65 samples from 20:52:11 to 21:02:51 UTC, 10.7 minutes, with anonymous memory median 1.27 GiB, 95th percentile 1.82 GiB and peak 2.13 GiB, which is 21% of the 10.00 GiB limit, no sample over the margin, 0.2 s of memory stall and 14.9 s of CPU stall, load median 11.6 and peak 15.2 on 22 cores, at most 4 `rustc` at once, no OOM kill, no gap, and the sampled `memory.current` peak 9.49 GiB under the cgroup's `memory.peak` of 9.99 GiB, the line reading "agree", measured 2026-11-26 (that report's table and the lines under it). Read it as four trees held by a batch that was mostly reading: it certifies nothing about four builders compiling. A second start, through a real `make builder-tree T=T274 F=451` with the sampler stopped, returned within the second and said `sampler: started`, and three samples followed at ten seconds, observed 2026-11-26, method: the handout's output and the file's last lines read (the build half's).
  - **The sampler's cost** (2026-11-26, the same run, the build half's). 0.06 s of CPU over the 65 samples, measured 2026-11-26 (6 clock ticks, `awk '{print $14+$15}' /proc/<pid>/stat` at 100 ticks a second), which is 0.9 ms a sample; 7.2 MiB resident, measured 2026-11-26 (field 24 of the same file, 1,848 pages). The directory holds three kept hand logs, where the brief said four. Two builders: 236 samples, anonymous median 1.91 GiB, 95th percentile 5.66 GiB, peak 6.34 GiB, 4.4 s of memory stall, measured 2026-11-26 (the report's `all` row for `mem-samples-two-builders.log`). The first two agree with what `docs/process-decisions.md` records for those runs. `echo`, not `ls`, in that command: `ls` puts newlines into the make variable and the recipe prints nothing.

### T274 Approach (checklist part A)

1. **The goal, in the world.** Whenever builders hold pool trees, the machine's memory and load are being sampled without anyone having started it, and one command reads a batch's window as the figures the builder count is certified from.
2. **The constraints.** T274's line in tasks.md. The brief: a sample every ten seconds of the cgroup's anonymous memory, `memory.current`, memory pressure and load, read without starting a program a sample; one sampler a clone, detached, bounded in hours and in size; started by `make builder-tree`, never failing a handout; a report by the count of builders; an audit-register entry; tests with 100% line coverage of new Rust. `docs/process-decisions.md`, "Two code builders at once", whose re-measurement at three and four builders the sampler is the tool for.
3. **Where each comes from.** G: none quoted - T274's line in `tasks.md` carries no words of the GM's and rests on the decision record. O: the measurements in the Approach, and that record's own (the kept hand logs).
4. **Do they describe the world here?** Yes, measured 2026-11-26 (the Approach, "The real run"): the sampler ran on the live machine beside four held trees, its spacing exact and its report in agreement with the cgroup's own peak; and the report over the kept hand logs gives the figures the decision record holds for them (the Approach, "The baseline").
5. **The order.** After T285 (the pool, whose registry a sample reads and whose handout starts it) and T316 (the handout's other detached start); before T351.
6. **The exits.** Green: `make builder-checks CRATE="rust/gate/crates/measure rust/gate/crates/task"` here (the first tier; the full gate runs once in the clone over the batch), and for this task the crates' cover step, `make crate-checks` over the same two. Red: what failed recorded and the task set down, a claim that it cannot be done ruled through `make arbiter-ask`.
7. **The search smell.** none.
8. **The budget.** One landing.
9. **Done, measured.** The tests were written after the code, so red was shown by breaking one behavior at a time (2026-11-26, method: the behavior taken out of the source, `make rust-test` over its crate, the `test result` line read, the source restored and compared with its copy). By the build half, observed 2026-11-26, method: each run's `test result` line, in a crate of 251 tests: a second start not seeing the running one, 250 passed and 1 failed; a pid file's process alive whatever its start time, 250 passed and 1 failed; the 95th percentile taking the rank below, 249 passed and 2 failed; a rise across a gap booked, 250 passed and 1 failed. By the closing half, observed 2026-11-26, method: each run's `test result` line: the fallen counter not a gap, 251 passed and 1 failed, the new test; the loop with no size bound, 250 passed and 2 failed, both ending; the handout's call of the sampler never reached, `rust/gate/crates/task` 99 passed and 1 failed, the new test. All restored, observed 2026-11-26, method: the `test result` lines of `make builder-checks` over the two crates, green: `measure` 252 passed, `task` 100 passed. COVERAGE: `make crate-checks CRATE="rust/gate/crates/measure rust/gate/crates/task"` said `cover clean on 2 crate(s)` on its first run, measured 2026-11-26 (its own output: 111 s of wall time, 104.3 s of it the cover build, and no `slot-wait` `Phase` line, so no wait for a build slot).
10. **Before moving a constant.** n/a: new knobs only (D10, D13), each labeled beside it and in `dev/audits/memory-sampler.md`.
11. **Before fitting things into room.** n/a.
12. **Before any fix.** Not a defect of a map: no map changes. The measurement it answers: the three- and four-at-once batches of 2026-11-26 ran with no samples, because the samples waited on a session starting a loop.

**Found and left?**

- `make sampler-report`'s rows are the pool trees HELD, not the builders at work: the real run's 65 samples at 4 held showed at most 4 `rustc` and an anonymous peak of 2.13 GiB, a batch mostly reading, measured 2026-11-26 (the Approach, "The real run"). Visible effect: a row for N trees held cannot certify N builders compiling, so a builder count read from it is read too low on memory. Not fixed here: the report's rows by trees at work need a join with the event log's Phase lines, a second reader and its own tests. Filed as T351; lands before T302.

**Performance work?** yes: a measurement task, counted as performance work by the GM's words of 2026-11-20; it makes nothing faster itself. Not an engine-speed task, so `docs/performance-checklist.md` does not apply.

### T339 (451 T315's measurement of 2026-11-26: most of every run of `rust/guard/shared`'s suite is one test of the idle check waiting real seconds, and two more wait a second each)

- **Approach**: the idle check's clock is asked of its `Procs` (`rust/guard/shared/src/guards/set_down_hooks/idle.rs`), the tests' table steps a stand-in clock in place of waiting, and the spelling test's text is cut to the shortest round length past the old limit.
  - **Where the 8 s went**, observed 2026-11-26, method: the test and `idle.rs`'s `watched` read side by side: two rechecks of 1 s (`L7R_IDLE_RECHECK_SECS=1`), then two waits of about 3 s each, a builder's 2 s bound (`L7R_STALL_SECS=2`) and the second `watched` adds past a crossing. All four are `std::thread::sleep`.
  - **Why not a knob in fractions.** The brief gave two routes: (a) the knobs taking fractions or milliseconds, (b) a clock the test drives. (a) cannot reach tens of milliseconds with production unchanged: the second added past a crossing is a constant, not a knob, so each crossing wait stays over 1 s; the bound is a whole number printed in the notice (`silent >{bound} s`), so a fraction there is a message change, which this task makes none of; and waits that stay real stay open to load. Chosen by this builder under the brief's instruction ("choose by what keeps the production path identical and the test still proving looks again until its budget").
  - **The rule as built.** `Procs` gains two methods with bodies of their own: `now()`, `Instant::now()`, and `sleep(time)`, `std::thread::sleep(time)`. The check's four uses of the clock go through them: its first wait (`L7R_IDLE_CHECK_SECS`), the budget's deadline, the comparison of the next look against it, and the wait before that look. The two tables that answer for production - `Blind`, and the guard crate's `Ctx` in `finished_run_hooks.rs` - define neither method, so both run the bodies above: the production path makes the same calls it made, and no file outside `rust/guard/shared` changes. `stalls::stalled` still reads the machine's `SystemTime` against a transcript's modified time; it is not changed.
  - **The stand-in clock.** The tests' `Table` (`tests/stalls.rs`) notes each wait asked, tells a time moved on by their sum, waits none, and runs a `meanwhile` given the time waited so far: the crossing case backdates the builder's transcript by it (so `stalled`'s real clock reads the builder as that much quieter), the turn cases append the session's turn. Past 50 waits it fails its test, so a check that never stops looking is red, not a hang.
  - **What the test pins now.** `the_idle_check_looks_again_until_its_budget`: three looks and two waits of exactly one second each for a watch that ends at the third; for a watch that never ends under a budget of three seconds, four looks, three waits of one second each and then the hand-on, twice (stronger than before: the old case, a budget of one second against a recheck of one, proved only that a check with no room for one recheck hands on at once, kept here as a budget of zero: one look, no wait); a builder crossing its bound named after one wait of what was left of the bound and a second, the bound here the shipped ten minutes where the old test's was two seconds (the builder's silence is still read off the machine's clock, so a bound of seconds would let a slow first look find it already past: the old test, asserting only that two seconds of wall time had passed, bore that, and an exact count of waits would not); a turn during that wait silent after one wait. `the_idle_check_waits_its_seconds`: one wait of exactly the knob's seven seconds before the block is said, and `Blind`'s own clock is the machine's (a sleep of twenty milliseconds takes that long by `Instant` and by `Blind.now()`), which is what meets the two new bodies. `a_reply_during_the_idle_check_s_wait_silences_it`: the reply written as the stand-in wait passes, no thread and no timing.
  - **Red first**, measured 2026-11-26 (`make rust-test CRATE=rust/guard/shared`, one change to `idle.rs` at a time, each restored from a copy): the recheck dropped - 504 passed, 1 failed, the budget test's "three looks" reading 1 for 3; the budget stop one second late - 504 and 1, "a look each second of its three" reading 5 for 4; the crossing look dropped - 504 and 1, the set-down block said where the stalled builder's notice was wanted; the turn's read after the wait dropped - 504 and 1, "a turn while it waits" given the stalled builder's notice for nothing; the first wait slept on the machine's clock in place of the table's - 503 and 2, both idle tests. With the code as landed, 505 of 505. The old tests against the new code do not build (a `Table` literal without its clock's fields), so there is no run of them.

### T336 (a pool tree's first test build after its pre-warm failed to link, `rust-lld: undefined hidden symbol`, twice on code that was right (2026-11-26, `diagram-backlog-t270`, found by 451 T299's builder); the cause is proved by the measurement under `dev/measurements/2026-11-26/prewarm-link/`: a test build killed past rustc's front end, as the pre-warm's cut killed it)

- **Approach**: two fixes the measurement supports. The pre-warm never cuts a build in flight (`rust/gate/crates/rustc/src/rustc/prewarm.rs`), and the gate's test build heals this one linker error once (`rust/gate/crates/rustc/src/rustc/stale.rs`, called from `stepped` in `rustc.rs`).
  - **The cause, as measured** (the measuring builder, 2026-11-26, method: in the pool tree `diagram-backlog-t270`, `cargo test --no-run --quiet --manifest-path rust/guard/Cargo.toml`, the pre-warm's own words, one cargo at a time under a build slot, eight guard source files changed before each try, the build left to finish or killed at a drawn moment, then built once more; `t336-harness.py`, its rows in `t336-results.jsonl` and `t336-results-late.jsonl`, tabulated by `t336-tabulate.py`). Of 54 tries in which a build was cut, 29 then failed to link; of 20 tries left to finish, 0 did. By signal: SIGTERM 16 of 31, SIGKILL 7 of 10, SIGINT 6 of 13. Every failure followed a cut that had written into the crate's FINISHED incremental session (same inode, new size or time), and none of the 11 tries whose cuts wrote nothing failed, and cuts in the first 3 s of an 11 s build never failed, measured 2026-11-26 (the same rows). Shown: a cut build changes files of the finished session in place. Inferred, not read in rustc: that the working session's files are hard links of the finished one's. The day's own record shows the sequence with no reproduction: `rust/guard` cut by the pre-warm at 16.2 s and again at 2.5 s, then built by the pre-warm itself, exit 101 with the link error, before any real run, observed 2026-11-26, method: the tree's `prewarm.log` of that day, kept as `t336-prewarm-2026-11-26.log`.
  - **Fix 1: the pre-warm yields between crates only.** `build`'s loop no longer kills its cargo: a real run starting in the tree, the last slot taken or the ceiling passing while a crate builds is noted with its time and the build runs to its end, its slot held until then. `run`'s loop head, before the next crate, ends the pre-warm on a real run or the ceiling and starts nothing while no slot is spare, as before. `End::Cut` and the 130 code go; the crate's line in `prewarm.log` says the seconds it ran on past the moment the first form would have cut it. Why no narrower rule: any kill past the front end can break the session, by any of the three signals, and no safe moment is visible from outside the rustc.
  - **A reading of the brief, said.** The brief's sentence has the pre-warm END before the next crate on "a real run in its tree or no spare slot". It ends on a real run; on no spare slot it WAITS at the loop's head, as T316 built it and as the handoff recommends, because ending there would leave every later crate cold whenever two trees compile for a moment. Nothing waits behind a pre-warm that holds no slot.
  - **What never cutting costs, accepted.** A real run started in the tree waits on cargo's lock of the build directory, and a compile of another tree can wait in the slots' queue, for the REST OF ONE CRATE, where T316's promise was a poll. Of the 160 crates pre-warmed on 2026-11-26 the median took 2.0 s, nine in ten under 13.0 s, and the longest 82.7 s (`rust/mode_a`), measured 2026-11-26 (method: every `prewarm` `Phase` line of that day with code 0, the measuring builder's count). Chosen by this task's builders on the measurement, at the brief's direction. The alternatives priced, measured 2026-11-26 (the measuring builder's table in the handoff and `t336-inc0-fresh.log`): cut, then drop the crate's incremental directories (a 22 to 44 s rebuild of `rust/guard` from nothing against its 11 s incremental build: more than the pre-warm buys), give the slot back and keep compiling (a third compile at once, the memory peak the slots exist to stop), heal only (every cut still risks a from-nothing rebuild: 29 of 54), `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0` for the pre-warm (0 of 20 broke a session, but it is another artifact set: 36.2 s to build, and the real build after it still compiled 12.2 s against 0.08 s for a fresh one).
  - **Fix 2: the test build heals this link error once.** `stepped`'s `--no-run` build is now one call, `stale::built`: where cargo fails and its words carry `undefined hidden symbol`, it reads the units the linker names (`<crate>-<hash>.<unit>.rcgu.o`, as a path under `<profile>/deps/` or as a member of an rlib), and under cargo's own `.cargo-lock` of that build directory drops EVERY incremental directory of each named crate (`<profile>/incremental/<crate>-*`) and each named build's fingerprint, then asks the build once more. It never asks a third: the second build's answer is the crate's, under a line saying what was dropped (a heal that linked says its line on the gate's own stderr, since `stepped` goes on to the run and keeps nothing a green build said). Where the linker names nothing under the tree's target directory, names a crate with no incremental directory, or another cargo holds the lock past 120 s (GUESS, the knob `LOCK_S`), nothing is dropped and the failure comes back with the repair named.
  - **The scope of the drop, and its evidence.** The whole crate's incremental directories, not the one holding the named unit: all 29 failing tries built green once the guard's incremental directories were moved away, measured 2026-11-26 (the harness's repair step, 22 to 44 s a rebuild), while the one-directory removal healed once on the day (T299's builder) and was not measured. The launcher's retry (T142) drops the one directory holding the unit; this one is wider on purpose and says so in `stale.rs`. A fingerprint is dropped only beside an incremental directory: alone it would rebuild from the same session.
  - **Counted.** A heal writes one `Phase` line, step `link-heal`, with the second build's code, spanning the drop and that build, inside the `build` line's span, so its seconds stay booked as compile and its lines can be counted in `.git/l7r-events/`. `columns::category` names no category for it.
  - **What of T146 remains.** This is T146's `make rust-test` half. Left to T146: the guard launcher's own incremental build (`scripts/hooks/l7r-guard.sh`). The coverage build's link is T206's.
  - **Red first, and the fix run live**: item 9.
  - **The record**: `dev/audits/builder-prewarm.md` (the cut's removal, the accepted cost, the falsifier and threshold restated), the `rustc` row of `rust/gate/CLAUDE.md`, `make builder-tree`'s help line, the headers of `prewarm.rs`, `stale.rs`, `phase.rs`, `slot.rs` and `task/src/builder_tree.rs`, one line of `scripts/container/builder-brief.md`.

### T340 (451 T315's measurement of 2026-11-26: the guard crate's test run goes on waiting after its tests end, on processes the tests leave behind)

- **Approach**: the stand-in sessions of `rust/guard/src/guards/clone_sync_hooks/tests.rs` wait in the shell itself on a pipe the test holds, in place of a `sleep 5` the shell started; no file outside that test file changes, and no guard's code or message.
  - **The cause, as found**, observed 2026-11-26, method: every `Command` and `spawn` of the crate's sources read (`grep` over `rust/guard/src`), and the count checked against a process listing one second after the binary's exit. Three tests of the clone check need a LIVE process whose command line names `claude`: the check reads `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` of the pid a sessions record is named for (`args_of`, asked by `sid_is_live` and `forked_from` in `clone_sync_hooks.rs`; `parked_by` reads the records alone, and its claimant's liveness is `sid_is_live`'s), so only a real process with those arguments can stand in for another session, observed 2026-11-26, method: the three tests and those functions read. They started `sh -c 'sleep 5; :' claude ...`: the `; :` keeps the shell from exec'ing the `sleep`, so the command line keeps the arguments - and so the `sleep` is the shell's CHILD. Each test ended its stand-ins with `kill` and `wait`, which end the shell alone; its `sleep 5` lived on under pid 1 with the test binary's stdout and stderr. One in `a_clone_another_live_session_claims_is_refused`, three in `a_forked_background_session_shares_its_launchers_clone`, five in `a_parked_background_job_shares_its_parkers_clone`: the nine the task line counts.
  - **The candidates the task line names, read and cleared**, observed 2026-11-26, method: each file read. `finished_run_hooks/runs/tests.rs` and `finished_run_hooks/tests.rs` start nothing: their `sleep` lines are text in a stand-in `/proc`. `scratch_sweep_hooks/tests.rs` starts two `sleep 60`, their own processes (no shell between), and kills and waits both. `idle_tests_hooks/tests.rs` starts one `sleep 5`, which the check under test kills and the test waits for. `passes_in_time` (`guards.rs`) kills and waits its child. After the fix the pipe ends with the binary's exit, so nothing holds the run's output, and no `sleep 5` is alive a second later (below).
  - **The rule as built.** `fake(args)` runs `sh -c 'read _' <args...>` with its stdin a pipe the test holds: `read` is the shell's own builtin, so nothing is forked and the command line still carries the arguments; the stand-in ends at the test's `kill`, or with the pipe if a test panics before it. An inherited stdin would not do: the gate gives the tests none to read, and the stand-in would end at once. The one stand-in written out in `a_clone_another_live_session_claims_is_refused` is now `fake(&["claude"])`, the same process. What each test proves is unchanged: a live process with those arguments, for as long as the test wants it. Chosen over closing the `sleep`'s output (the processes would still outlive the run, nine a run) and over killing the shell's process group (more to get wrong than a stand-in with nothing to leave).
  - **Red first**, measured 2026-11-26 (`make rust-test CRATE=rust/guard FRESH=1`, then the built binary with `--exact` on the new test, 20 times): `a_stand_in_session_starts_no_process_of_its_own` reads the kernel's list of the stand-in's children (`/proc/<pid>/task/<pid>/children`) before it ends it. On the old stand-in: 548 passed, 1 failed, the list holding one pid where none was wanted, and 20 of 20 alone red. On the new: 549 of 549, and 20 of 20 alone green.
  - **Before and after, the gate's test phase**, measured 2026-11-26 (`make rust-test CRATE=rust/guard FRESH=1`, the `test` step's `Phase` line in the event log, in the pool tree `diagram-backlog-t270`, another builder at work on the machine throughout): before 5.28, 5.27 and 5.27 s at load 10.5, 9.7 and 8.4, the binary's own `finished in` 2.08, 2.02 and 2.06 s, and after 2.54, 2.54 and 2.68 s at load 11.5, 11.5 and 10.9, `finished in` 2.07, 2.08 and 2.21 s. A first batch of after runs, taken while the load climbed from 8.6 to 14, read 3.24, 3.72 and 6.54 s with `finished in` 2.72, 2.71 and 5.28 s, measured 2026-11-26 (the same command and lines): the tests themselves slowed, and the phase ended 0.5 to 1.3 s after them. The wait after the tests' end was 3.2 s and is 0.5 s in the three steady runs, cargo's own start and report, measured 2026-11-26 (each phase less its `finished in`).
  - **Before and after, the binary by hand**, measured 2026-11-26 (`t340-measure.sh`: the binary run into a pipe under a new empty `TMPDIR`, as the gate's leak pin gives it, its exit and the pipe's end timed, then run again into a file and `ps` read one second after its exit, the `sleep 5` processes counted less the count before): before, at load 11.4, 9.7 and 10.2, exit at 2.00, 2.04 and 2.04 s, the pipe's end at 5.16, 5.17 and 5.18 s, 9 alive each time, and after, at load 10.1, 8.9 and 9.7, exit at 2.14, 2.39 and 2.28 s, the pipe's end at 2.14, 2.39 and 2.29 s, 0 alive each time.
  - **The gate's side.** Part of the wait is the gate's: `run_in` (`rust/gate/crates/rustc/src/rustc.rs`) takes cargo's output with `Command::output`, which returns when the pipe ends, not when the binary exits, observed 2026-11-26, method: the function read. The key: the content id of every file of the crates this one builds from by path, the files those compile in, the workspace's manifests, lockfile and `.cargo/config.toml`, the crate's own `Cargo.toml`, the compiler, the build's words and the `RUSTFLAGS` and `CARGO_ENCODED_RUSTFLAGS` it inherits; NOT the crate's own sources, which are what a build of the crate alone compiles.

### T359 Approach (checklist part A)

1. **The goal, in the world.** A filed task that turns out a duplicate or no defect is closed in one command, with its reason on its line and in the event log; a task started by mistake is unstarted in one command, after which it holds no landing, owes no closing order and reads as not started to every reader of the start log - while the `make static` runs it made since its last landing stay counted, an unstart resetting none.
2. **The constraints.** The task's line; one mark a task in its own tree (451 T254) and a bundle's one mark (451 T141); the filing lock of 451 T84; the plan gate's scope (451 T84); the pool's registry (451 T285); the tick's archive (449 T142); every escape and refusal names the compliant command (root `CLAUDE.md`, "What is enforced").
3. **Where each comes from.** O: the landing of 2026-11-26 that refused T322, T323, T356 and T358 for their stubs, and the mark moved by hand that day (the task's line and T343's). The GM's words name neither command; what to build is the coordinating session's, from those two observations. O: the measurements of the table above.
4. **Do they describe the world here?** Yes: the four tasks are withdrawn by the command and a landing asks nothing of them (the table above); `make task-unstart` was run for real only on its refusal (`T=T999`: no mark), its success path in the crate's tests.
5. **The order.** After T254 (the marks), T285 (the pool) and T289 (a builder files what it finds). Before T369.
6. **The exits.** Green: the eight changed crates' tests, lint, format and coverage clean, and the suites of the guards whose files changed. Red: what failed recorded and the task set down, a claim that it cannot be done ruled through `make arbiter-ask`.
7. **The search smell.** None: each refusal was written from a state a reader would mishandle, and the readers were found by one search for the log's name over `rust/`, `scripts/` and the Makefile.
8. **The budget.** One landing.

### T332, T344 (bundle) (two filings of one defect: a pool tree's `Phase` lines carried the task of the tree's last `make task-start`, which no handout moves - all 179 `Phase` lines of T315's check runs in `diagram-backlog-t269` carried T285 through five handouts, observed 2026-11-26 (T344's line; method: the 451 event log's `Phase` lines of that tree from 20:07 UTC counted by their task field, against `.git/builder-pool.log`))

- **Approach**: a tool's own line written from a held pool tree takes its task from the pool's registry at the moment it is written.
  - **Where the task is read (the finding).** A check's `Phase` line (`rust/gate/crates/rustc/src/rustc/phase.rs`, `wrote`) is appended with no payload and no task, so `filed` (`rust/guard/shared/src/guards/event_log_hooks/filed.rs`) reaches its last link: `in_force`, the last row of the START LOG (`<git common dir>/task-starts.jsonl`) that names the line's tree and feature. It is not the mark files (`task-marks/`): both features' mark directories in this clone were empty when read, 2026-11-27 (`ls` of the clone's `.git/task-marks/*/`), while this tree's lines still carried T271, the task of its last start row (2026-11-26T13:42:28Z).
  - **The rule.** `pool_task` in `filed.rs`, asked just before `in_force` and only where `in_force` was asked (the main session's own line: no agent, no page session, no task named by the line): the first task of the registry's entry for the line's tree (`l7r_shared::builder_pool::read`, `builder-pool.json`), where the entry's feature - the pool's key, the feature's number, or its directory name - is the line's feature. A tree the pool does not list, a free one, and one held for another feature or for none are answered by `in_force` as before.
  - **A start after the handout stands.** A `make task-start` the tree's builder ran after the entry's `since` is the builder's own later word and names the task: a bundle's builder in a tree held for `a,b` that starts `b` has its lines booked to `b`. A start with no time is not one; a handout whose time does not read is older than every timed start.
  - **Why the registry is read and no start is written at the handout (the task lines' two routes).** T344's line asks that `make builder-tree T=` set the tree's mark; T332's that the task be read from the pool. A mark file written at the handout (`marks::write`) would move no `Phase` line, since the writer does not read marks. What would move it is a start ROW at the take and an undo row at the release, and the start log has readers a start nobody made would tell wrong: the landing's "was each task started in this clone" (`rust/gate/crates/land/src/land/ready.rs`), the stall check's start-since-the-last-landing (`rust/guard/shared/src/guards/set_down_hooks/stalls.rs`), the time breakdown's first start of a task (`rust/gate/crates/measure/src/measure/task_time.rs`), and the static-runs count, which reads the raw log on purpose (451 T359-D9b); and the undo at release would erase the builder's own earlier starts of that task (`marks::live_starts` drops every earlier start of the task in the tree). Reading the registry in the one link changes what one reader sees and nothing else.
  - **Why in `filed.rs` and not in `phase.rs`.** The rustc crate's writer is one of several tools that append a row from a tree (`append_row_with`); the link in `filed` answers for every one of them, and a row that carries its own task (a landing's) never reaches it.
  - **The re-file.** `make events-refile` (`rust/gate/crates/measure/src/measure/event_log/refile.rs`) moves a line between FEATURES and leaves a line whose task its feature has where it is, so it does not undo this; its one use of the start in force is for a line a brief moves to another feature, which a tool's own line has none of.
  - **Cost.** One read of `builder-pool.json` for each line that reaches the last link - a tool's own rows and the main session's hook lines that name no task - a file of 39 lines in this clone, measured 2026-11-27 (`wc -l` of its `.git/builder-pool.json`); the read was not timed.
  - **On the real machine.** In this tree, held for T332,T344 since 2026-11-27T00:23:54Z: the 1,060 `Phase` lines of 2026-11-26 and the 19 of this handout written before the change (its pre-warm's and the red run's) carry T271; every line after the rebuilt gate ran - `make builder-checks CRATE=rust/guard/shared` (6 lines) and `make rust-test CRATE=rust/gate/crates/plan` (3 lines: `slot-tell`, `build`, `test`) - carries T332, measured 2026-11-27 (the clone's `.git/l7r-events/451-time-retro-and-efficiency.jsonl`, its `Phase` lines whose clone is this tree, read by task and time).
  - **The lines already written.** Not rewritten. 3,255 of the 451 log's 3,883 `Phase` lines from a pool tree name a task other than the first task of the tree's holder at their start, 385 minutes of spans (t269 1,197 lines, t270 1,107, t271 881, b1 70), measured 2026-11-27 (each such line's task against the detail of the tree's last take at or before its `t0` in `.git/builder-pool.log`; an upper figure: a bundle's second member and a builder's own later start count as differing). `make task-progress` re-tasks them at read time (`retask`, `task_time/progress.rs`, since T293); `make task-time` does not.

### T394 (the GM's question of 2026-11-27 on the blocking minutes `make task-time` booked to the second tier, and the measurement it led to, `dev/measurements/2026-11-27/tree-idle/results.md`: the three warm pool trees stood idle 336 of 1,440 tree-minutes (23%) from 2026-11-26T17:00Z to 2026-11-27T01:00Z with the queue never short, measured 2026-11-27 (`tree-idle.py`), because the session worked a builder's end as commit, carry, resolve, check, land and only then briefed the next builder)

- **Approach**: one command at a builder's end, `make builder-done T=<task(s)> MSG="<subject>" [F=<feature>] [GUARD="<guard-edit reason>"]` (`l7r-gate builder-done`, `rust/gate/crates/task/src/builder_done.rs`, new; wired in `rust/gate/crates/task/src/lib.rs` and `rust/gate/src/lib.rs`; the Makefile's `builder-done` target), which commits the builder's pool tree, keeps the commit where the tree's next handout cannot lose it, releases the tree and prints the next dispatch AHEAD of the carry. The idle figures are the measurement's, measured 2026-11-27 (`tree-idle.py`, read-only over the session's transcript and the 451 event log; the record is `dev/measurements/2026-11-27/tree-idle/results.md`, which the clone holds and this builder's tree, handed out before it was committed, does not). The command's effect on those figures is NOT measured here (Found and left, T401).
  - **What it does, in order**, in the pool tree the registry says the tasks hold (the tree is never passed): refuses with nothing done (below); removes the stray `default_*.profraw` files an instrumented binary dropped; `git add -A`; `git commit -F` a message file in the tree's own git directory (the subject, a `GUARD_EDIT_OK:` line when `GUARD=` is given, the co-author trailer); writes the commit under `refs/l7r/done/<feature>-<task>`, one ref a task; appends a `done` line (the tree, the holder, the commit, the time) to the pool's log; releases the tree through `builder_tree::release`, which brings it to the clone's HEAD; prints the commit, the release, then `1. make builder-brief ...` and `2. make carry FROM=<tree> COMMIT=<sha>`. It never carries, lands or pushes.
  - **What it refuses, nothing done and the tree still held** (exit 2): no task, no feature, a subject that is empty or more than one line, a `GUARD=` of one word; a tree the tasks do not hold, or hold only as part of a bundle (the exact `T=` printed); a tree gone from disk; an operation git left unfinished in the tree (a cherry-pick, merge, revert, pick of several commits, rebase); an unmerged path; nothing to commit; a conflict's markers in a changed file (the guard's own `conflict_marker_hooks::has_conflict`); a guard file changed with no `GUARD=` (the exact re-run printed, the subject shell-quoted); a done commit of one of the tasks not yet carried. A `git commit` that fails (a hook) is exit 1 with git's words, nothing left staged, the tree still held.
  - **DECISION, the commit is kept by a ref** (label: tooling convention). The release detaches the tree at the clone's HEAD, so nothing but the tree's reflog would name the builder's commit, and an unreferenced commit is git's to prune. `refs/l7r/done/<feature>-<task>` keeps it until it is carried; a ref whose commit is carried is deleted at the next `make builder-done`. A bundle's tree is done only by the whole bundle and gets one ref a task on the one commit.
  - **DECISION, "carried" is told by the author's time and the subject** (label: tooling convention). A carry is a cherry-pick, so the carried commit has another id: `git branch --contains` never names it, and `git cherry` (a patch-id) misses a carry that kept both sides of a `tasks.md` conflict. A cherry-pick keeps the author's time and the subject, so a done commit is carried where the clone's HEAD holds a commit of the same two, read in ONE `git log --since` from the oldest done commit. A pick the carry skips as empty leaves no such commit in HEAD, so that test alone would list it forever: the carry itself now deletes the done ref at its verified end (below), and this test is what remains for a commit that reached HEAD without the carry's end (a carry stopped on a conflict and finished by hand). One known miss, not reached by a real subject: a done commit made in the same second and with the same subject as a commit already in HEAD would read as carried, which the fixture's commits (all named `c`) showed in this builder's first version of one test and no `make builder-done` subject, which names its task, repeats.
  - **DEVIATION from the task line's sketch: the guard-file rule is asked in process** (label: deliberate deviation). The line says the command "commits the builder's tree with the message given"; the session's hand commit was held to the guard-file rule by the Bash hook that reads a `git commit` command, and a commit this binary runs passes no hook. So the command asks the rule itself: a changed guard file with no `GUARD=` is refused. `guard_file()` is a COPY of the guard's list (`rust/guard/src/guards/guard_file_hooks.rs`, `named`), because a gate crate may not read the guard's binary crate (`check guard-deps`); the copy is named as one in the code. Not fixed here: one list in `l7r_shared` is an edit of the guard's own sources and suites. Filed as T396; lands before T313.
  - **DEVIATION from the task line: the queue's next task is not named** (label: deliberate deviation). The line says the command "prints the queue's next task and its make builder-brief command". `specs/451-time-retro-and-efficiency/queue.md` is prose the session edits (numbered items naming several tasks, "after T316", "LANDED"), which code could only guess at, so the command prints `make builder-brief T=<the first task of specs/<feature>/queue.md no tree holds> F=<n> KIND=<...>` with the placeholder left for the session. Not fixed here: a queue code reads is 451 T313's design. Filed as T395; lands before T313.
  - **DECISION, the printed carry keeps `FROM=`** (label: tooling convention). The pool's log supplies the tree for `FROM=` (the clone where the log names none). `make carry` only resolves the commit there, and any worktree of the clone resolves it, released or handed out again; the land crate's test below runs exactly that.
