### T394 Approach (checklist part A)

1. **The goal, in the world.** A pool tree goes to its next task as soon as its builder's work is committed: the session's first act at a builder's end is one command and the next dispatch, and the carry, its conflicts, the gate and the landing run while the next builder works. No builder's commit is lost by its tree moving on.
2. **The constraints.** The pool's registry and its release are 451 T285's (`builder_tree.rs`), reused, not copied. A builder's commit reaches the clone only by `make carry` (451 T292), never a hand cherry-pick. A guard file's commit owes its `GUARD_EDIT_OK:` reason (feature 170). The second tier stays the session's (the GM's ruling of 2026-11-26, `docs/process-decisions.md`, "Two tiers of checking"): this command runs no check. A gate crate reads nothing of the guard's binary crate (451 T66, `check guard-deps`). No history is rewritten: the command commits and writes refs, nothing else.
3. **Where each comes from.** G: the GM's words of 2026-11-27 on T394's line, copied to `request.md` ("a pool tree is handed on as soon as its builder's work is committed (451 T394)"); they ask that the blocking be got to the bottom of, and the command is the coordinating session's answer to what the measurement found. O: the tree-idle measurement. The constraints are earlier tasks' and are named with them above.
4. **Do they describe the world here?** Yes for the cause: 170 of the 336 idle tree-minutes fell while the session was in its own turn and 105 while a landing ran, measured 2026-11-27 (`tree-idle.py`, each idle 10 seconds classed by what the session was doing). Whether the command removes them is not known until it has been used over a like window (T401).
5. **The order.** After 451 T285 (the pool) and T292 (`make carry`), both landed. Before T313 (the pool kept full, which reads the queue and adds the Stop hook's refusal), T395, T396 and T397. T398 and T397's first and second parts are built here.
6. **The exits.** Green: `make builder-checks CRATE="rust/gate/crates/task rust/gate rust/gate/crates/land"` and `tests/hooks/test-make-only-hooks.sh` in the builder's tree, the full gate with its coverage at the batch's landing. Red: what failed recorded and the task set down, a claim that it cannot be done ruled through `make arbiter-ask`.
7. **The search smell.** none.
8. **The budget.** One landing.
9. **Done, measured.** RED FIRST, the build half, measured 2026-11-27 (`make rust-test CRATE=rust/gate/crates/task` against a stub whose `run` refused and whose `listed` was empty): 111 passed, 7 failed, the seven `builder_done` tests. The closing half, measured 2026-11-27 (the same command with `take`'s check switched off): 117 passed, 2 failed, the handout test and the written-over test as it then stood; and measured 2026-11-27 (`make rust-test CRATE=rust/gate/crates/land`): 128 passed, 1 failed with the done ref deleted before the prune (`holds no commit`), 128 passed, 1 failed on the old argument check (`COMMIT=` alone), and 128 passed, 1 failed with the carry's end deleting no ref (the plan review's first round). After, measured 2026-11-27 (`make builder-checks` over the three crates): the task crate 119 passed, 0 failed, the land crate 129 passed, 0 failed, lint and format clean on the three; `tests/hooks/test-make-only-hooks.sh` 144 passed, 0 failed; `make docs` 217 targets, 0 undocumented. The task crate's tests run fresh six times in a row, 119 passed each, measured 2026-11-27 (`FRESH=1 make rust-test CRATE=rust/gate/crates/task`), after one test of this half failed once on the fixture's shared subject (the Approach's second known miss). Live, read-only, observed 2026-11-27, method: `make carry` with neither argument printed the recipe's refusal, and `make carry COMMIT=no-such-commit` reached the binary and was refused "holds no commit". NOT run: coverage (the second tier's, by the GM's ruling), `make static`, `make hooks-test`, `make quick`; the command on the live pool - this task's own builder's end is its first use.
10. **Before moving a constant.** n/a: no constant moves. The audit entry's 10% is new, a GUESS knob no verdict depends on.
11. **Before fitting things into room.** n/a.
12. **Before any fix.** Not a defect of a map: no map, sheet, verdict or guard message changes. What a session sees differently: a builder's end is one command, `make builder-trees` lists the commits that wait, `make builder-tree` refuses a task its next tree while its own commit waits, `make carry` takes `COMMIT=` alone, and its last line names the done ref it cleared.

### T391 (T332's review made it a condition, and T332's own measurement files it: 3,255 of the 3,883 `Phase` lines pool trees wrote into the 451 log name a task other than the first task of the tree's holder at their start, 385 minutes of spans, measured 2026-11-27 (T332's plan section: each line's task against the detail of the tree's last take at or before its `t0` in `.git/builder-pool.log`); `make task-progress` re-tasked them at read time and `make task-time` did not. T393 - a bundle's carry is no task's - is built here too, in the same file family)

- **Approach**: the reports read a pool tree's `Phase` line by the task the pool's log says held the tree when the phase began; the log is left as written. T393 is built here: a holder's detail is split by one function.
  - **What a `Phase` line's task decides (the finding).** One thing: which Bash run the line is tied to (`tie`, `rust/gate/crates/measure/src/measure/where_time/columns.rs`). Among the runs of the line's session whose span holds it, a run with the line's make target and the line's task comes before one with the target alone, the latest started breaking a tie; a line that fits no run is counted loose. A tied phase splits ITS RUN's minutes into compile, tests and the rest and adds none, so a wrong task can move a task's compile and tests minutes and can never move its total. A session's builders share its id, so two builders each inside a `make builder-checks` are told apart by the task alone.
  - **The rule** (`rust/gate/crates/measure/src/measure/task_time/held.rs`, new; `retask`). A `Phase` line whose `clone` is a tree the pool's log names, begun while a holder held that tree for the line's feature, takes the holder's first task. A line from a tree the log does not know, from a time nobody held it, or filed under a feature the holder was not held for keeps its own.
  - **One function, four readers.** `make task-time` (`task_time.rs`, `run`), `make task-progress` (`task_time/progress.rs`, `view`, whose own `retask` is deleted) and `make where-time` (`where_time.rs`, `booked`) call `held::retask` before their runs are read; `make feature-report` reads its timing columns through `where_time::columns_text`, which calls `booked`, so it is the fourth with no edit of its own.
  - **DECISION, a hold ends at its release.** The function `make task-progress` had took the tree's last `take` at or before the line, whatever followed, so a line written after the release still took the last holder. The log's rows are now read as HOLDS (`holds`): one opens at a `take`, at a tree's `make` for a task, or at an `adopt` of a held tree, and ends at the tree's `release` or its next handout. The task line asks for the holder at the line's start; after a release there is none. `make task-progress` reads through the same function and so takes this too; a builder's block there reads its tree's lines by the tree, whatever task they name, and its tests pass unchanged.
  - **DECISION, a `make` row and an `adopt` row open a hold.** A tree made for a task is written `make`, never `take`: `diagram-backlog-b1` was made for T274 at 2026-11-26T20:38:58Z and released at 21:38:22Z with no `take` between, observed 2026-11-27 (method: the clone's `.git/builder-pool.log` read row by row). Read as takes alone its lines would keep the stale task; with the row counted T274's tests minutes go from 5.8 to 9.9, measured 2026-11-27 (the two binaries' reports of that window, read row by row). `tiers::takes`, which names the holder a `make carry` ran under, kept `take` rows alone for the same reason and found T274 no carry; it now keeps every row that opens a hold (`held::opens`, the one test both readers use), so T274's own table ends at its carry, 21:34. That is the plan review's first-round ruling: the section had deferred it, and it is fixed here.
  - **DECISION, a line naming one of the holder's tasks keeps it.** A bundle's holder is its first task (the brief's words). But since T332 the writer books a bundle's line to the second member where the builder started it (T332's section, "A start after the handout stands"); overwriting that with the first would undo T332 at read time. So the first task replaces only a task that is none of the holder's.
  - **DECISION, the holder's feature is checked.** A line is re-tasked only where its feature - its log's, which the readers tag, or for `make where-time`, which reads one feature's logs untagged, that feature's name - is the holder's number or opens with it and a hyphen. T332's writer-side rule checks the same; without it a line filed in another feature's log would be given a task of this one's.
  - **T393, built here.** `held::holder` reads a detail (`451 T324,T345`) as its feature number and its tasks, split on spaces and commas; `tiers::batches` (which split on spaces alone), `make task-progress`'s staged list and `retask` read it, and `held::first` gives the carry's run its clue (`451 T324`) in `book/tier.rs`'s `run_booking`, which keyed the run to a task named `T324,T345`. T393's own section, where the clone's tasks.md has its box (its filing commit was not in this tree), is this one.
  - **On the real logs**, measured 2026-11-27 (the old binary kept as a copy and this tree's, run back to back, `l7r-gate measure task-time --root /diagram/.clones/diagram-backlog --since 2026-11-26T17:00:00Z --until 2026-11-27T01:00:00Z`; each task's compile and tests rows read from its own section, since the one-line table has no such columns):
    - The window's totals do not move: 2670.9 minutes and 501.2 blocking before and after, measured 2026-11-27 (the two binaries' reports of that window, read row by row). Phases tied to no run fall from 5,937 (308.6 min) to 5,513 (253.2 min), and the window's compile row goes from 60.5 to 74.1 minutes, tests from 137.6 to 146.3, waiting on a build slot from 3.4 to 5.6, each taken out of its own runs' other minutes, measured 2026-11-27 (the two binaries' reports of that window, read row by row).
    - The three largest moves: T347's compile 0.0 to 5.2 minutes, T274's tests 5.8 to 9.9, T315's tests 1.0 to 4.8 (and its compile 0.1 to 2.8), measured 2026-11-27 (the two binaries' reports of that window, read row by row). T316's tests fall 26.2 to 24.8 as its compile rises 0.6 to 2.3, measured 2026-11-27 (the two binaries' reports of that window, read row by row). Nine tasks' compile or tests rows change (T289, T298, T316, T293, T315, T274, T336, T340, T347), and no task's minutes or blocking change by T391.
    - T336's 163.3 minutes do not move, and cannot by this task: they are its builders' own runs, booked by each call's own line (58.0 wait loops, 42.3 shell reads and file edits, 25.9 the model's turns running a command), while its compile goes 1.2 to 1.4 and its tests 10.0 to 10.1, measured 2026-11-27 (the two binaries' reports of that window, read row by row).

### T139 (`tests/hooks/test-no-poll-hooks.sh`'s case "two waiters on one quiet file and no run: still gone" failed good work under load - "expected dead, rc=0" at T118's closing run, observed 2026-11-22, and again in a batch gate, observed 2026-11-27 - and passes alone: the T71 case before it ended its call sleep first, and the shell that ran on forked a `tee` that wrote or held `fresh.log` after the case's touch)

- **Approach**: the T71 case of section 6b ("a live call whose command opens with its assignment and tees into it: alive") ends its
  call SHELL FIRST. One line of `tests/hooks/test-no-poll-hooks.sh` changes, with its comment, and the comment over the later
  case's touch is restated; no guard, no guard message and no crate changes.
  - THE CAUSE, as proved. The call is `bash -c "... eval 'B=<dir>; sleep 30; echo ... | tee -a $B/fresh.log'"`. The case ended it
    with `pkill -P "$WA_RUN"` (its sleep), then `kill "$WA_RUN"` (its shell), then `wait "$WA_RUN"`. A shell whose sleep has died
    goes on to its next command: where it ran between the two kills it forked `echo | tee -a fresh.log`, and that tee, no child of
    the suite, outlived the `wait`. The next case touches `fresh.log` two hours old and expects "gone"; a tee that writes it after
    the touch (the staleness belt), holds it open for writing, or is read as a live process that writes it, answers alive.
  - **T139-D1, built: the shell is killed first.** `WA_KIDS=$(pgrep -P "$WA_RUN"); kill "$WA_RUN"; wait "$WA_RUN"; kill $WA_KIDS`.
    A shell killed while its `sleep 30` still runs forks nothing more, so no tee exists in any interleaving: the shell dead before
    it forked the sleep, or the sleep forked after the `pgrep`, each ends with no pipeline (in the second, a `sleep 30` is left to
    end by itself, as the cases above this one already leave theirs: they end `kill "$WA_RUN"; wait "$WA_RUN"`, shell first).
    The sleep's pid is read before the kill because `pkill -P` finds no child of a dead shell. What the T71 case proves is its
    `alive` assertion, made before the teardown and unchanged; the later case keeps `fresh.log`, its two waiters and its touch.
  - **T139-D2, NOT built: the call in a process group of its own, ended in one signal** (`setsid bash -c ...`, `kill -- -<pgid>`).
    Priced, not measured: it changes how the T71 case's call is STARTED, which is what that case proves (the walk reads the
    call's command line, which would open `setsid bash -c` until the exec, and `wa_settle` would accept that line), and one
    signal to a group still reaches its members one after another. D1 changes only the end, and is ordered by a `wait`.
  - **T139-D3, NOT built: the later case on a file of its own.** It would pass, and would leave the stray tee running into the
    cases after it (the "a process holding it open: alive" check at the section's end reads `fresh.log` too) and past the
    section's `rm -rf`. It moves the reader away from the leak rather than ending it.
  - **T139-D4, NOT built: the later case waiting on a condition** (no process naming `fresh.log` but its waiters). The stray tee
    may not be forked yet when such a wait looks, so the condition is met a moment before it is false; only an end that forks
    nothing is certain.
  - THE SAME SHAPE ELSEWHERE, left as it is: the two reader cases later in 6b end `pkill -P` then `kill` too (`WA_R1`, and `WA_R3`
    with `WA_R4`). What their shells run on to is a `grep`, a file test or a `tail -1` of `quiet.log` - reads, which the helper
    counts as no producer (451 T61) - so no outcome is wrong there (observed 2026-11-27, method: each of the section's `pkill -P`
    lines read with the command its shell runs next).
- **Red first**, observed 2026-11-27, method: a scratch copy of the suite at HEAD (`t139-red/old.sh` in the session's scratchpad,
  `HERE` pinned to this tree's `tests/hooks`) with `sleep 0.5` between the `pkill -P` and the `kill`, run as `PARTS_CASES=case_6b`
  with a `tee` first on `PATH` that sleeps 2 s before the real one - a deliberate delay, no load: 3 of 3 runs red, each
  `27 passed, 1 failed`, the one failure this case's "expected dead, rc=0". The same copy with the 0.5 s delay and the real
  `tee`, observed 2026-11-27, method: that copy run without the slowed `tee` on `PATH`: 2 of 2 green (`28 passed, 0 failed`), the tee done before the touch - the race needs both. The fixed order under the
  same slowed `tee`, with 0.5 s after the `pgrep`, after the `kill` and after the `wait`, observed 2026-11-27, method: `t139-red/new.sh` run as the red copy was: 3 of 3 green,
  `28 passed, 0 failed`, the sleep's pid gone after each.

### T314 (the batch gate of 2026-11-26 18:27 UTC: `tests/hooks/test-state-sync.sh` red beside three builders, 41 of 41 alone a minute later)

- **Approach**: the suite's three waits on a background run (`tests/hooks/test-state-sync.sh`, cases 11 and 13) wait on their condition to a deadline of 120 s (a GUESS knob, `STATE_SYNC_WAIT`) and a wait that runs out is itself a FAIL saying what it waited for; the lock is probed last; `scripts/state-sync.sh` is not changed.
  - **Which case failed: no record names it.** Searched 2026-11-26 (method: the clone's event log `.git/l7r-events/451-time-retro-and-efficiency.jsonl` for the suite's `Phase` lines; every file of `/home/agent/.claude/jobs/c6fd72d1/` modified in the gate's window, 18:20 to 18:36 UTC; the `land-b*.log` files, of which none is that run's - `land-b2.log` is the green run after it; the session's transcript and its subagents' for the suite's `FAIL` lines). What is kept: one event line, observed 2026-11-26, method: that log read - the suite run from 18:25:14.963 to 18:26:49.641 UTC, 94.7 s, exit 1, in `make land` for T289. Alone it takes 4 to 6 s (measured 2026-11-26: 28 of the 30 runs below) so that run was 16 to 24 times slow.
  - **The timing it assumes, by reading.** Every case but two is synchronous: it runs `state-sync.sh` in the foreground and reads the result. No case compares times of day or seconds (the answers' `utc` values are fixed strings), and every path is under the suite's own `mktemp -d` or the fixture clones' `.git`; the tool's own scratch files are `mktemp`'s. The three timing assumptions are the three waits on a run that `--detach` or `--if-fresh` leaves in the background, each a loop of 100 rounds of `sleep 0.1` that ran out SILENTLY and went on: (a) case 11, for the failed detached push to log its failure and free the lock, before the next detached push; (b) case 11, for that next push to put its answer on the branch; (c) case 13, for a fresh clone's background restore. Where (a) runs out, the next push meets the lock (`flock -n`), is skipped as the tool is built to skip it, and (b) can never come, so the case reddens whatever (b)'s bound.
  - **Each made certain**, measured 2026-11-26 (`t314-make-slow.sh` and `t314-slow-runs.sh` in the session scratchpad: a copy of `state-sync.sh` in which the nth background launch sleeps 30 s while it holds the lock, and a copy of the suite pointed at it; 3 runs for each of the three launches, one at a time): on the old suite 9 of 9 red, each `40 passed, 1 failed` - launch 1 and launch 2 red on "the next detached push carries it", launch 3 on "a clone with no mirror restores", each the line predicted before the run. The old loops ran out at about 11 s each, measured 2026-11-26 (those runs' wall time: 14 to 21 s where one loop ran out, 26 to 27 s where two did, the suite itself about 4 s). On the fixed suite, measured 2026-11-26 (the same copies made again from it, run the same way): 9 of 9 green, `43 passed, 0 failed`, 34 to 36 s a run.
  - **The fix.** `await <what it waits for> <condition...>` polls the condition and returns the moment it holds; past `WAIT` seconds (120, `STATE_SYNC_WAIT`) it is a FAIL of its own that says what never came, and returns 1, so a wait that ran out never ends green. The three conditions are named functions (`failed_twice`, `carried`, `restored`) and are what the loops tested; what each case proves is unchanged. Case 16 is new and pins the helper both ways: a condition that comes late (a file removed by a background `sleep 0.3`, the fixture's own figure, a CONVENTION) is waited for and nothing is said, and with `WAIT=0` a condition that never comes returns 1 with the FAIL line and its words (read in a subshell, so the suite's own count is not moved). The pass count goes from 41 to 43.
  - **A fourth assumption, in the first wait's own probe: fixed here.** The loop for (a) probed the lock FIRST (`flock -n <lock> true`) and read the log second. The probe holds the lock for an instant, and the detached push takes it with `flock -n`: a push that met the probe was skipped by its own rule and logged nothing, so the second failure never came. On the old suite that was a silent stall of the loop's length and then green (the next push still carried the answer); with the longer deadline it would have been the whole deadline. `failed_twice` now reads the log first and probes the lock only once the run has logged, as `restored` reads its file first. Made certain, measured 2026-11-26 (`t314-probe/` in the session scratchpad: two copies of the fixed suite whose probe holds the lock for `sleep 0.5`, one with the old order, `STATE_SYNC_WAIT=3`, 3 runs each): the old order 3 of 3 red on `waited 3 s for the failed detached push to log its failure and free the lock, which never came`, the new order 3 of 3 green.
  - **The bound is a GUESS knob, and it departs from the brief.** The brief asked for a wait "bounded, a few seconds". The bounds that failed were already about 11 s (measured 2026-11-26, the slowed runs above), so a few seconds cannot be the fix and could not go green on the slowed copy. 120 s, a GUESS knob, is how long a run that never ends is given, not a wait: about 11 times the bound that ran out and 300 times the slowest background run alone (0.2 s the failed push, 0.4 s the push, 0.2 s the restore, read 2026-11-26 from the fixture clones' `tooling-state.log` of one run with the fixture kept). A green run pays none of it. Chosen by this builder; the alternative priced was a wait with no bound, which would hang a gate on a background run that died.
  - **Red with its words**, measured 2026-11-26 (the slowed copy of the fixed suite with `STATE_SYNC_WAIT=3`, one run for each launch): launch 1 red on `waited 3 s for the failed detached push to log its failure and free the lock, which never came`, on `waited 3 s for the next detached push to put record-format%3A0007 on the branch alpha, which never came` and on the case's own line; launch 2 on the second of those and the case's line; launch 3 on `waited 3 s for the background restore to bring source-reader%3A0004 and free the lock, which never came` and on `a clone with no mirror restores`.
  - **The real suite after**, measured 2026-11-26 (`t314-thirty.sh`: 30 runs in a row, one at a time): 30 of 30 green, `43 passed, 0 failed`, 4 to 10 s a run. No cap on a suite's seconds was found in `tests/hooks/hookrun.sh` or the Makefile's `hooks-test` (searched 2026-11-26, method: a search of both for `timeout`), so a wait that runs out reaches its FAIL line.
  - **Not reproduced under load, on purpose**: the brief overruled the task line's "under load by T99's method" (two builders' load loops froze the host on 2026-11-26); the delay in a scratch copy makes each race certain instead.
  - **The tool was read for a race of its own and has none here**: a run writes its log line while it holds the lock, so "the lock is free and the line is there" is a sound end; a detached push that meets a held lock is skipped by design ("the next landing's push carries this state").

### T367, T411 (bundle) (found by 451 T347 and T355: the small lane's key of a test build and of each lint pass is written only by a passing wide build of the checks, and the pre-warm built `cargo test --no-run` only, keeping no key and running no clippy, so a builder's first test build and first lint of each crate after a handout took a wide build slot; measured 2026-11-27 from the clone's event log, 00:20Z to 03:30Z: 28 of 29 first test builds after a handout told wide (`dev/measurements/2026-11-27/prewarm-keys/tellings.py`))

- **Approach**: the pre-warm (`rust/gate/crates/rustc/src/rustc/prewarm.rs`) keeps the small lane's key of each build it runs that passes, and after the test builds it runs each lint pass of each moved crate, so the builder's first `make builder-checks` of a crate after a handout is told alone at its test build and at every lint pass. Reused, not copied: `Told` (`kept/alone.rs`) gained `keeping`, the key-keeping half of `cargo_with` (written beside itself, the build run, moved into place where it passed, nothing where told alone or told nothing), which `cargo_with` now calls; `lint.rs` exposes `passes`, `DENY` and `told` (a pass's key name and keyed words), which its own `pass` calls; `kept.rs`'s `binary_args` is `pub(super)`. The record: `dev/measurements/2026-11-27/prewarm-keys/` (`results.md`, `tellings.py` and its output `tellings.txt`, the hand run `demo.txt`).
  - **D1, the telling is the checks' own.** Measured, not chosen: a key holds the build's words, and the builder's test build is told by the binary key's words (`binary_args("test")`, `--message-format=json` among them), so the pre-warm tells its `cargo test --no-run --quiet` by those words, under the name `test`, and its passes by `lint::told`. The content ids are read as a test run reads them (`Kept::read` with `test`, so a dependency's `include_str!` file is in the key, as `alone.rs`'s fixture's `data/table.tsv` is); `moved` asks `reads_any` with `prewarm` as before, so what is built does not change. A key built otherwise would never stand: the red test's fixture compiles a table in, and a `prewarm`-read key left it out.
  - **D2, its own name beside the key.** CONVENTION: the pre-warm joins no run lock, so a run's wide build of the same crate can start while the pre-warm's is in flight; each writes beside the key by its own suffix (`.new` the checks', `.prewarm` the pre-warm's), so neither renames the other's file into place.
  - **D3, the lint after every test build; a red pass its crate's last.** The order the brief names: every moved crate's test build first (fewest dependencies first), then each crate's passes in `lint::passes`' order (three for a crate that names itself, 451 T325), each pass a job of its own under the test builds' rules - a slot only while another is spare, never cut, one `prewarm` `Phase` line a cargo call, one log line a pass. A red pass drops its crate's later passes, as `lint::linted` stops, and keeps no key (T355-D3). `L7R_PREWARM_LINT=0` warms the test builds alone (GUESS, a knob, default on: its cost is seconds nobody waits on).
  - **D4, the log's words.** A line a lint pass (`prewarm: <crate> - its lint pass <words> is warm (<s> s)`, or `cargo clippy <words> exited <n>; its later passes left to the builder's own lint, which says why`); the ending lines keep their crate count of test builds and add `, and <n> lint pass(es) with them` / `not run` where passes are left; a slot is signed `cargo <its words>`. The `slot-tell` lines the pre-warm's tellings write carry make target `prewarm`, so a count of a builder's tellings leaves them out.
  - **Measured first** (job 1, read-only, `tellings.py` over every log of the clone and the pool's log, 00:20Z to 03:30:03Z on 2026-11-27, 14 handouts): test-build tellings in pool trees 29 first after a handout (28 wide, 1 alone) and 129 later (39 wide, 90 alone); so the first builds are 28 of the 67 wide test tellings (42%), measured 2026-11-27 (`tellings.py`). Lint tellings (since T355, about 01:53Z): of the passes of a crate's first lint after a handout 4 wide and 5 alone (a key the tree's previous task left), 6 wide and 10 alone later. THE WAITS ARE SMALL: of 13 `slot-wait` lines, 283.5 s, one (4.0 s) was in a first test build after a handout and none in a lint since T355, the other 279.5 s in later builds and lints, measured 2026-11-27 (`tellings.py`). The task lines gate the fix on the first builds being most of the wide waits left; by count of wide tellings they are 42%, by seconds waited 1.4% of that window, measured 2026-11-27 (`tellings.py`). Built because the brief orders it: the first build of a crate no longer takes a wide slot whatever the load, which is what decides whether it waits.

Then `make builder-checks CRATE=rust/gate/crates/rustc`: the test build `slot-tell 0`, `slot-small 0`, its build 0.13 s, and both lint passes `slot-tell 0`, `slot-small 0`, the lint 0.3 s, measured 2026-11-27 (`demo.txt`).

### T414 (a red hook suite inside a batch gate left no record of which case failed: the red state-sync run of 2026-11-26 18:27 UTC left one event line - its name, 94.7 s, exit 1, observed 2026-11-26, method: the task line's reading of that event line - and nothing else, its log in the run's mktemp work directory, printed once and removed, the land log overwritten by the next landing, so 451 T314 could not tell which case had failed)

- **Approach**: `tests/hooks/hookrun.sh` keeps each RED job's whole log (after the LEAK line is appended) in the clone's COMMON git directory, `l7r-hooks-failed/<utc>-<job>-p<pid>.log` (T414-D1), and leaves its name, relative to that directory, in the work directory's `<job>.kept`; a green job keeps none and removes a stale `.kept`. The `hooks-test` recipe names the kept log in the suite's FAIL line (`HOOK TESTS FAILED: <suite> (whole log kept: <path>)`, appended, the line's head unchanged) and hands it to the event line's writer as a sixth span field, `suite:<t0>:<t1>:<rc>:<job>:<log>`, which `l7r-gate measure event-log phase` writes as the Phase line's `log` (`rust/gate/crates/measure/src/measure/event_log/phase.rs`). The user-level self-test's FAIL line, which lost its log the same way, keeps it through `hookrun.sh --keep` (fixed here). The kept logs are bounded to the last `HOOKS_FAILED_KEEP` (T414-D2), once a run, by `hookrun.sh --sweep <gitdir>` before the fan-out (T414-D3); T372's one sweep and the jobs' `--swept` stay as they were.

| the bound, once a run | `test-parts.2.sh`: "a job of a swept run removes no kept log", "the run's one sweep keeps the newest HOOKS_FAILED_KEEP logs", "the bound touches nothing but kept logs", "a job run by hand bounds them itself", red on the old code | n/a: tooling | none | none |
| the FAIL line and the event line name it, in the common git directory | `test-parts.3.sh` (the real recipe in a fixture clone, the failure in its LINKED tree): "the FAIL line names the kept log, in the common git directory", "the kept log holds the suite's whole log", "only the red suite's log is kept", "the event line's span carries the kept log"; `phase::tests::a_span_carries_its_kept_log` - each red on the old code | n/a: tooling | none | none |

- **T414-D1, the name** (CONVENTION): the brief offered `<git common dir>/l7r-hooks-failed/<utc>-<suite>.log`, the task line `.git/hooks-test/failed/<suite>@<utc>.log`. Taken: the brief's directory, beside `l7r-events` and `l7r-handoffs`, not inside `hooks-test/`, which holds what runs REUSE (stamps, seconds, renderings) - a reader's log kept apart from them is what makes the bound safe (D3). The name is `<utc to the nanosecond>-<job>-p<pid>.log`: the time first, so the names' order is their age (the bound sorts by name); the job, so a shard's log (`<guard>.<k>`) is its own; the runner's pid, because the common git directory is every worktree's and two trees can fail one suite in one second. It holds no colon or space, so it rides as a span field (the door splits on colons, and the recipe passes its spans unquoted - one unreadable span drops every Phase line of the run).
- **T414-D2, the bound** (GUESS knob, `HOOKS_FAILED_KEEP`, 50): about one fully red run's worth of the 70 suite files; a value that is not a number reads as 50. Nothing a later run reuses is removed: no runner, stamp, key or check reads `l7r-hooks-failed/` (grep of `tests/`, `scripts/`, `rust/` and the Makefile, 2026-11-27), so a removed log is only a reader's - only files named as kept logs are removed.
- **T414-D3, when the bound runs**: once a run, in `--sweep <gitdir>` before any job keeps a log, as T372 moved the temp sweep - a job bounding after keeping could remove a log another job of the same run is about to name, a run's red jobs can outnumber the bound. So after a run the directory holds at most the bound plus that run's failures, brought back to the bound by the next run's sweep. A job run by hand (no `--swept`) bounds after keeping its own, the newest, as it sweeps.

### T417, T352 (bundle) (the GM 2026-11-27 on the cap's abrupt cutoff: on 2026-11-26/27 three of about 35 builders reached the 300k cap, T315's at 308k and T325's at 310k refused only the mechanical end of their stop points; and the cap's one exit refused the handoff names the briefs give, found by T334 2026-11-26)

- **Approach**: a wrap-up band from the cap to a ceiling, and the handoff's exit taking the file the brief names.
  - **T352, the exit.** `rust/guard/src/guards/context_cap_hooks.rs` (`own_cap`) let through past the cap only a Write, Edit or Read of a file under `<git common dir>/l7r-handoffs/` whose name ends `<agent_id>.md`; `make builder-brief`'s build-half block names `<task>-build.md` (a bundle's `<a>-<b>-build.md`, `rust/gate/crates/task/src/builder_brief.rs`), the closing-half block reads it, and the coordinating session's briefs name `done-pending-<task>.md`. Now the exit also takes any `.md` file of that directory the builder's own BRIEF names (`context_cap_hooks/named.rs`: each word of the brief holding `/l7r-handoffs/` and ending `.md`, taken as that file name in this clone's directory), and the refusal names the brief's first such file, so the brief, the refusal and the Write agree. The brief is read where the split already reads it (`split::brief`, the transcript's first row; `split::is_code` reads the same text, one read where there were two).
  - **T352, why the brief and not "a name holding the task id".** The task the cap reads is its call's line's (`filed_at`): for a bundle, the first `T<n>` its description names, while the build-half file names every member - and an id matched inside a name needs a token rule (`T41` against `T417-build.md`) and a guess at every name form. The brief is the one text that says which file this builder was told to write. Kept beside it: the `<agent_id>.md` rule, for a brief that names no file.
  - **T352, the resume.** A resume's refusal (`handoff_of`) names a briefed file that is written first, then one ending `<agent>.md`, then the brief's first, then the cap's own name; its "not written yet" line follows the file it names, so a build half that wrote `<task>-build.md` is no longer told its handoff is unwritten.
  - **T352, the landing.** `open_handoffs` (`rust/gate/crates/land/src/land/writers.rs`) never refuses a landing by itself: its one caller, `writer_refusal`, runs only where the clone holds changes not the landing's own, and names an open handoff BESIDE them as their likely writer. So the reconciliation is in what "open" means there: a finished handoff names no writer. `done-pending-<task>.md` opens with no `T<n>` and was none already; a build half's `<task>-build.md` (and a bundle's) is now none too (`handoff_task`), its builder having ended as briefed. Open stays the cap's own `T<n>-<agent id>.md`, the file of a builder stopped mid-task whose successor is owed.
  - **T417, the band** (`context_cap_hooks/band.rs`). From the cap (`CONTEXT_CAP_TOKENS`, 300,000) to `WRAP_UP_CEILING_TOKENS` (340,000, a GUESS knob, the task line's "say 340k"), after the handoff's exit, the permit and `CONTEXT_OK` are judged as before: a Read or Grep; an Agent (or Task) call of `spec-fidelity` whose prompt opens `MODE 4: PLAN REVIEW`; a Bash command every one of whose simple commands is allowed and every make target it invokes one of `decide`, `plan-delta`, `plan-verdict`, `claims-triage`, `claims-owed`, `task-add`, `task-withdraw`, `builder-checks`. Each pass is recorded (`fire`, rule `wrap-up`), each refusal (`wrap-up-refused`) says it is the band, what was refused, what is still allowed and the handoff. Past the ceiling the guard is as it was: the old refusal, byte for byte its old render (the suite's case 1 and the message store's existing rows unchanged).
  - **T417, matching invocations.** A new reader in the shared tree walk, `shared::tree::commands`, lists every simple command as the walk splits it - heredoc bodies carried out, quoted strings stood in for, a subshell's and a `$(...)`'s commands listed (a `$(...)` inside double quotes too: bash runs it) - so `echo "make decide"` is an `echo`, a heredoc's `make decide` line is none, and `make decide && rm -rf x` is refused at its `rm`; `shared::make::invoked` reads the targets, so `make` with no goal is `.DEFAULT_GOAL`, refused. `shared::tree::shown` puts a refused command's quoted text back for the message (the walk's stand-ins otherwise reached it, seen in the first message bundle).
  - **T417, the command shapes decided.** Every brief's commands open `cd <tree> && export SPECIFY_FEATURE=...`: `cd` and `export` are allowed, and a segment of `VAR=value` words alone; `git` with `-C <path>`, `-c <k=v>` or `--no-pager` read past, then `status` or `diff`, any `--output` refused (it writes a file); `head`, `tail` and `grep` are allowed anywhere - they read, as the Read and Grep tools the band allows do, and `| tail -20` keeps a long `builder-checks` output out of a context already past the cap; a redirect (`> /tmp/x 2>&1`) is not judged, a log the command writes being the command's.
  - **T417, decision: `make plan-delta` is allowed though the task line's list does not name it.** It is the plan review's own command in every code builder's STOP POINT ("the plan review (`make plan-delta F=451`)"), and T325's builder, one of the line's motivating cases, was refused exactly it; it prints the MODE 4 dispatch the band allows. Left out, the band would refuse the step its own GM-quoted case names.
  - **T417, the second review round.** T315's case was a plan review's second round. A builder dispatches every round the same way, `spec-fidelity` with the MODE 4 prompt `make plan-delta` prints; `review_round_hooks` rewrites a later round into MODE 3 and routes it to `spec-fidelity-verify` LATER in the guard chain, after this guard has judged the original call - so the band admits it.
  - **T417, what stays refused in the band.** An Edit or a Write of any file but the handoff, any other dispatch (a `claims-triage` or `impl-drift` dispatch is refused by the band before the split is asked), any other make target or program, and a `SendMessage`: a builder in its band resumes no one.   - **T417, the other readers of the cap.** `builder_stop_hooks` lets a builder past the cap stop (unchanged: a builder in the band that stops before its stop point is done is not held back to finish it); `set_down_hooks::stalls` marks a stalled builder at or past the cap `capped`, which a band builder is only if it stalls (unchanged); `make task-progress` shows a builder's context against the cap (unchanged). ### T424 (a pre-warm test failed once inside the batch gate's coverage run of 2026-11-27 about 04:03 UTC, landing T367 T411 T414: "assertion failed: builds(&world).is_empty() && spare(&world.slots)", `rust/gate/crates/rustc/src/rustc/tests/prewarm.rs` line 261, and passed 3 of 3 alone straight after)

- **Approach**: a flaky check, not a defect: `prewarm.rs` is unchanged. Which half failed, measured 2026-11-27 (a scratch test, since removed, whose slots' `flock` program was a wrapper that, after taking each lock, left the open file on fd 3 of a `sleep 0.3` child - the "child another thread is starting holds a copy of the open file until its exec" of `slot.rs` lines 12-13, held for 0.3 s instead of the microseconds of a fork-to-exec window): the old form went red 3 of 3 run alone, plus once in the crate's run, each time on the `spare` half - `builds()` empty, cargo's calls `["--version"]` only. The fix is in the test: the slot is read let go by `let_go`, a taker that waits (10 ms polls and a 60 s ceiling, GUESS: a bound no load reaches, as `until_calls`'s; the slot tests' own `quick`), where the bare `spare` read it once. On the same slowed form the fixed check went green 3 of 3, beside an `assert!(!spare(..))` showing the slot still read held; a hold never let go still fails it (`let_go` false after 60.96 s, measured 2026-11-27 (a scratch test holding the slot, since removed)). Then the real test, 30 times in a row, one run at a time (`t424-thirty.sh` in the scratchpad): 30 passed, 0 failed.
- The candidates, each tested: THE CEILING - ruled out by the assertion that passed: the "stopped at its ceiling" line just above 261 held, so the run ended at its ceiling as meant, and a slow coverage build only makes fewer loop turns before it. `builds()` COUNTING LINT CALLS - none is made: with one slot the pre-warm's own `free_now` hold is on the only slot when `spare` opens that file again, a separate open under `flock`, so `spare` reads it held and no build, test or lint, starts (the slowed run's calls: `--version` alone); a lint call would start `clippy` and be left out anyway. A SLOT HELD BETWEEN `free_now` AND THE `filter` - `Option::filter` drops the rejected `Hold` at once, closing the file in process; it read held afterwards only while a copy of the file lived in a child. A SHARED DIRECTORY - `scratch` names carry the pid and a sequence number (`checks.rs`), so no other test's slots or calls file is this one's.
- The task line's premise, read: the `free_now(...).filter(spare)` take and this assertion date from 451 T316 (`1783cf6eed`), not from T367/T411 (`git diff 7b104cda01^ 7b104cda01` touches neither); T367/T411 add test threads that start processes (the lint passes), which can only widen the chance of a copy at that instant. The 04:03 failure itself is inferred, not observed: the simulation shows the assertion fails on exactly that transient and the other candidates cannot fail it at 261.

### T427, T428 (bundle) (found by T417's plan review and by T417 itself, 2026-11-26: the wrap-up band let a redirect write any file, and the resume refusal's last line was false inside the band)

- **Approach**: the band judges where a Bash command's redirects land, and the resume refusal says what a resumed builder runs at each edge.
  - **T427, the gap.** `context_cap_hooks/band.rs` judged a band command's programs and make targets but not its redirects (T417's section: "a redirect (`> /tmp/x 2>&1`) is not judged, a log the command writes being the command's"), so `tail -n 0 x > rust/guard/src/a.rs` or `grep '' a > b.rs` wrote a source file the band refuses as an Edit or Write. This reverses that one decision of T417: a redirect is judged now.
  - **T427, the rule.** In the band every redirect must land under `/tmp/` (the session's scratchpad is `/tmp/claude-<uid>/...`) or in the handoff the cap's exit allows (`is_handoff` or the brief's named file, `in_dir_named`, handed to the band by `own_cap` as a predicate, so the band re-derives neither). A redirect the walk cannot place (`> $(head -1 p)/b.rs`) is refused; a name no command assigns is empty, as bash reads it (`> $NOWHERE/b.rs` is `/b.rs`, refused). `2>&1` and `>/dev/null` are no write the walk reports (`sanitize` strips them before `redirects`), and a quoted `>` is no redirect. Two shapes the walk does not read are refused whole, as the band's other refused commands are, naming the command: a `cd` or `pushd` carrying a redirect (the walk moves the shell there and reads no write of it; filed for the walk as T436), and any `>&` left after `sanitize` strips `2>&1` and `>&2`, a `>& FILE` or `>&FILE` (filed for the walk as T433). The redirect refusal names the place: `Refused: a redirect writing <path> (in the band a redirect lands only under /tmp or in the handoff).`
  - **T427, reuse, not a re-parse.** The shared walk (`shared::tree::walk`) already places every redirect target, resolved against the call's cwd (`/tmp/../diagram/x.rs` normalized to `/diagram/x.rs`); but its `Target` could not tell a redirect from `make`'s own write where it stands (`(eff, "shell")`, the same `how` as a relative redirect), so filtering targets by path would have refused `make decide` itself. `Target` gains `redirect: bool`, set in `walk_text` from `writes_in`'s order (its redirects last). No other reader of the walk changes. `walk_text`'s `unread` block was folded into one filter to keep the function within clippy's 100 lines (observed 2026-11-27, method: `make builder-checks`'s clippy named it at 102, then 101, lines).
  - **T428, the message.** `resume_refusal`'s last line said a resumed builder past the cap is "still refused every call but its handoff's until the session grants it an hour", false inside the band since T417. It now says: "Even resumed, a builder past the cap may run only its stop point's steps and its handoff up to 340000 tokens, and only its handoff past that, unless the session grants it an hour", the figure `band::CEILING_TOKENS`. Its "not written yet" line said the handoff's Write "is the one call its cap lets through", false in the band too: now "its cap lets that Write through at any size". The message-check of the first wording failed both renderings (PastCap and Landed) for brevity and fidelity: the feature tag, the slowdown figures (the module's doc keeps them) and the one-step numbering cut, and the escape's "(two words or more)" added; its second round cut the one-task rationale line, the escape's ", recorded in the guard log" and the Landed reason's "since its dispatch" (its fidelity PASS); the third wording passed.
  - **Red first, measured 2026-11-27 in this tree.** T427, with the band's redirect check off (`.filter(|_| false)`) and `redirect` set false: the guard's unit tests 1 failed of 562 (`a_redirect_lands_only_under_tmp_or_in_the_handoff`), the shared crate's 1 of 522 (`a_redirect_is_marked_apart_from_its_programs_own_write`), the suite 2 failed of 102 (case 12's two source-file redirects); restored, 562, 522 and 102 green. The two whole-command refusals, probed after the plan review's first CLEAR (observed 2026-11-27, method: each shape added to `band/tests.rs`'s refused table before its rule): `cd /t > /t/rust/guard/src/a.rs` and `tail -n 0 x >& /t/rust/a.rs` each came back Allowed, the test 1 failed of 562 each time; with the rules, 562 green. T428: `a_resumes_refusal_names_the_fresh_dispatch_and_the_handoff`'s new assertions failed on the old wording (1 of 562), green on the new.
  - **The tests.** `band/tests.rs` `a_redirect_lands_only_under_tmp_or_in_the_handoff` (passed: `/tmp` logs, the scratchpad, `2>&1`, `>/dev/null`, an append to the handoff outside `/tmp`, a quoted `>`; refused: a source file absolute and relative, after a `cd`, `/tmp/..`, another handoff-directory file, an unassigned name, an unplaceable substitution; a quoted target passed; a `cd`, a `pushd` and two `>&` shapes refused whole); `tests.rs` `a_builder_in_its_wrap_up_band_finishes_its_stop_point` (through `own_cap`'s real handoff predicate: an append to the handoff let through, a redirect to `/t/a.rs` refused); `shared/src/tree/tests/commands.rs` `a_redirect_is_marked_apart_from_its_programs_own_write`; the suite's case 12 (two source-file redirects refused naming the place, at absolute paths outside `/tmp` since the fixture lives under it; four `/tmp`, `/dev/null` and `2>&1` forms passed); `tests/resume.rs` (the band's edges named, the old line gone, the escape's two-word rule).
  - **The messages.** Rendered by the suite into the tree's store by T338's hand route (`L7R_MESSAGE_CORPUS=<dir> bash tests/hooks/test-context-cap-hooks.sh`, its `messages.jsonl` over the store's file); the band's redirect refusal `a204de59391d5874` FIDELITY PASS, BREVITY PASS (922 characters); the resume refusals `8610b31a460c8a13` (PastCap, 811 characters) and `48fca3e12a239881` (Landed, 828) FIDELITY PASS, BREVITY PASS in the third round, after two rounds of brevity cuts; `make guard-messages` reads 34 wordings, each reviewed and within its budget.

### T369 (found by 451 T359's closing half, 2026-11-26, by reading: a task started in a second tree overwrote the first tree's mark, so the second tree's `make task-unstart` left the first tree's start row live in the log with no mark behind it)

- **Approach**: marks became per tree. `marks::write` (`rust/guard/shared/src/speckit/marks.rs`) writes `task-marks/<feature>/<task>/<tree key>.json`, one file a tree, and replaces only the starting tree's earlier mark of the task; every reader of the marks reads the new layout and the layout of before beside it, and `make task-unstart` removes this tree's file alone. Measured red first, 2026-11-26 (below).
  - **T369-D1, built: one mark a task A TREE, not a refusal at the second start.** Label: CONVENTION (a form of the tooling; no research claim). The task's line names the refusal; the brief left the choice to the reading. Reason: the clone's start of a task a builder started in a pool tree is the landing's ordinary path - 14 of the 103 tasks started since 2026-11-25 were started in two trees, each a builder's tree first and the clone after, observed 2026-11-26, method: the real clone's `task-starts.jsonl` read (read only) and its start rows grouped by feature, task and tree. Under the refusal, that path goes through the "a released pool tree's mark is stale" exception, and the takeover meets the defect again: the clone's start overwrites the builder's mark, the clone's unstart removes it, and the builder's row stays live with no mark. Closing it takes an unstart row written for the builder's tree, which erases the builder's own starts from the time breakdown. `event_log_hooks/filed.rs` `pool_task` records the same cost for a release. Per tree, the second start moves nothing, and each tree's unstart cancels that tree's own rows (`live_starts` is already per tree, T359-D9) and its own mark. The mark and the log then say the same thing in every case, the pool's state aside. The alternative priced: the refusal (`task_start.rs` and `bundle.rs`, the pool registry read to tell a stale mark), with the takeover's unstart row and its cost above. Chosen by this builder from the reading below.
  - **T369-D2, built: the tree key is the tree's resolved path, every character but `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` written `_`.** Label: CONVENTION. Reason: one name a tree, readable, and no hash a later build could spell otherwise. No reader derives it: a tree's mark is found by the `tree` its file names (`marks::own_file`), so a tree spelled two ways (a symlink) still has one mark, which its next start replaces.
  - **T369-D3, built: the layout of before T369 is read as written and replaced by its own tree's next start.** `marks::all` (through `files`) lists a task directory's files and a feature's own `<task>.json` files alike. `own_file` answers the old file where it names the tree, so `write`, `make task-unstart` and `clear` treat it as that tree's mark. Label: CONVENTION. Reason: the real clone holds six marks in the old layout (451 T352, T403, T404, T417, T419, T424), observed 2026-11-26, method: `ls` of `task-marks/451-time-retro-and-efficiency/`. They hold as before and go at their landing.
  - **T369-D4, built: the landing's sweep removes every tree's mark of a landed task** (`marks::remove`: `<task>.json` and the `<task>/` directory), and an empty task id removes nothing (it would name the feature's directory). A set-down's `clear` removes its own tree's FILES, found by what each names, where before it rebuilt the path from the task's name. Label: CONVENTION.
  - **The readers, every one** (found 2026-11-26 by `grep` of `marks::` and `task-marks` over `rust/`, `scripts/`, `tests/hooks/` and the Makefile):

    | reader | what it reads | after T369 |
    |---|---|---|
    | `marks::all`, `of_tree` (decide, the review-round guard, `plan/task.rs`) | every mark, a tree's newest | both layouts; a tree's newest own mark unchanged |
    | `speckit::holding_with` | every mark, own or another tree's | a task marked in two trees: own if this tree's is one, else another's (deduped as before) |
    | `set_down_hooks/stalls.rs` `in_progress` | any mark naming the task | unchanged: any tree's |
    | `task_withdraw.rs` | any mark naming the task refuses | unchanged |
    | `task_unstart.rs` | THIS tree's mark first, else another tree's (its refusal), else a bundle's | changed: found by tree; its file by `own_file`; no message changes |
    | `marks::clear` (`make set-down`), `marks::remove` (`make land`'s sweep, `scratch_sweep_hooks/disk.rs`) | the files | changed: D4 |
    | `scripts/gates/closing-checks.sh` | this tree's marks of the task, a glob | changed: both layouts' globs |
    | `land/ready.rs` `started_tasks`, `others_in_delta`; `filed.rs`; `core/logs.rs`; `plan/approach.rs`; `measure` (`task_time`, `where_time`, `feature_report/sources`); `task/wording.rs`, `set_down.rs`; `builder_stop_hooks`, `context_cap_hooks`, `sweep/tmp.rs` | the start log through `live_starts` | unchanged: already per tree (T359-D9) |
    | `static_runs_hooks` | the raw start log (T359-D9b) | unchanged |

### T365 (the guard crate's test binary ran 5.3 to 6.0 s under the default `TMPDIR` against 2.0 s under a fresh one, found by T340, measured 2026-11-26 (the task line's three runs of each by hand in `diagram-backlog-t270`, load 10 to 13))

- **Approach**: a measurement; no source changed. What was asked (the task line): which of `TempDir::new`'s sweep of dead processes' directories (`rust/guard/shared/src/tempdir.rs`, `sweep_dead`) and the fixtures' own scans makes the binary slow under `/tmp`, and whether the hook suites of `tests/hooks` and the live hooks pay it at every call. The record is `dev/measurements/2026-11-26/tmp-clutter/t365-results.md`, its scripts and raw outputs beside it; every figure below is the record's, measured 2026-11-26 in the pool tree `diagram-backlog-t270` from 22:54 to 23:25Z at load 3 to 23 with other builders running (the record's head).
  - **The method.** `strace` and `perf` are refused in the container, so the listings were counted in process by an `LD_PRELOAD` shim (`t365-shim.c`: each `opendir` of the temp directory, its `readdir64` calls and the time to its `closedir`); wall times by `/usr/bin/time`, five runs of each arm alternating; one `TempDir::new` timed alone in a loop of 300 calls in a release build (`t365-loop-main.rs`); the live hooks by 20 alternating runs a call after a warm-up (`t365-time.py`); the day's counts from the clone's event log (`t365-events.py`), all measured 2026-11-26 (the record's section 1 and 2).
  - **The cause is `sweep_dead`, at every `TempDir::new`.** It lists the WHOLE temp directory on each call, with no stamp and no once-a-process rule, and the guard test binary makes 509 such calls a run under either temp directory, measured 2026-11-26 (the shim, `t365-shim-testbin-*.txt`). On one thread the binary took 24.85 s under `/tmp` against 15.04 s under a new empty `TMPDIR`, a difference of 9.81 s, and the shim's 509 listings took 9.97 s, measured 2026-11-26 (`t365-bin-times.txt`, `/usr/bin/time`, and the shim). At 22 threads the medians were 5.34 s against 2.08 s over five runs each, the listings 82.2 thread-seconds at 161 ms a listing where one alone costs 19.6 ms, measured 2026-11-26 (`t365-bin-times.txt` and the shim); which lock the listings contend on is not measured (no tracing tool runs here). The fixtures' own scans are ruled out: `rust/guard` holds no `read_dir` of the temp directory but `sweep_dead`'s, measured 2026-11-26 (`grep -rn "read_dir(" rust/guard`, and the shim's count the same 509 under both directories).
  - **The cost of a listing.** In a directory that never grew, 0.06 ms + 0.41 ms for each 1,000 entries, linear to 80,000, measured 2026-11-26 (`t365-loop-new.txt`, the loop of 300). `/tmp` costs 13.4 to 16.0 ms for its 5,443 entries because its directory file is 21.9 MB from the 329,000 entries it once held, and a synthetic copy of that history costs 2.4 to 2.7 ms emptied, so an emptied `/tmp` would still list at about 2.5 ms, measured 2026-11-26 (`t365-loop-bloat.txt`, the same loop).
  - **Who else pays.** The live hooks list the temp directory 0 times, and a Bash PreToolUse took 31.6 ms median under `/tmp` against 30.5 under an empty `TMPDIR`, inside the spread, measured 2026-11-26 (`t365-hook-times.txt`, 20 alternating runs, load 2.8 to 2.9). The test runner's leak pin lists `/tmp` once a crate run (21.6 ms through `make rust-test`), the hook suites' runner globs it once a suite (16.5 ms), and `file-scale --selftest` lists it twice (76.4 ms median against 36.6), measured 2026-11-26 (`t365-shim-rust-test.txt`, `t365-glob.txt`, `t365-gate-times.txt`).

### T370, T372 (bundle) (T365's measurement, dev/measurements/2026-11-26/tmp-clutter/t365-results.md, levers A and C: the whole temp directory was listed at every `TempDir::new` and globbed before every hook suite, 14 to 16.5 ms each under a `/tmp` of 5,443 entries, measured 2026-11-26 (T365's timing loops))

- **Approach**: each of the two listings runs once where it ran once a call, and removes exactly what it removed.
  - **T370, the rule.** `TempDir::new` (`rust/guard/shared/src/tempdir.rs`) runs `sweep_dead` inside a `std::sync::Once`: the process's first `TempDir` lists the temp directory, no later one does. `sweep_dead` no longer takes a tag: it reads a name from its end - `l7r-`, anything, `-p<pid>`, `-<seq>` - so the one listing takes every tag's leftovers, a tag with hyphens of its own included (`l7r-gate-ci-stop-handler-p<pid>-<seq>`, the 29 leftovers T365 found). The dead-pid test, the three-hour age and the directory test are unchanged.
  - **T370, what it removes.** The same set of names as before, taken over all tags: a name the old rule matched for some tag `T` is `l7r-T-p<pid>-<seq>` with a pid and a sequence that hold no hyphen, which is what the new rule reads from the end. Pinned in `a_gone_process_s_directories_go_with_the_next_process_of_any_tag`: kept are the form before 449 T101 (`l7r-t-<pid>-<seq>`, with a name after it, and under a tag ending `-p5`), a hook suite's `l7r-hooks-suite-<guard>-p<pid>.<x>`, `l7r-test-scratch`, a file, a live pid's, one changed within three hours, a name with no tag and one not opening `l7r-`. Nothing a later run reuses goes: a dead process's `-p<pid>-` directory is read by nothing, and the one path that outlives its process on purpose (`TempDir::keep`) has no caller outside the helper's own tests, read 2026-11-26 (`grep -rn "\.keep()" rust`).
  - **T370, what changes for a leftover.** It went at the next `TempDir` of its own tag; it now goes at the first `TempDir` of the next process of any tag, so sooner. A process that changes its own `TMPDIR` after its first `TempDir` does not sweep the second directory; no caller does that (the runners set `TMPDIR` for a child).
  - **T370, the figures.** The guard crate's test binary run by hand from `rust/guard` with `TMPDIR` unset, the old build's binary kept as a copy and the two alternated: before 6.22, 5.74, 6.06 s and after 2.02, 2.06, 2.04 s, at load 8.7 to 12.4 on 22 cores with other builders running, 549 tests each run, measured 2026-11-26 (each run's `finished in`). `l7r-gate check file-scale --selftest`, the tool binary run by hand with `TMPDIR` unset, old build and new alternated: before 64.9, 57.3, 51.4, 46.0, 72.3 ms (median 57.3) and after 33.2, 33.8, 31.2, 31.8, 61.8 ms (median 33.2), at load 11.8, measured 2026-11-26 (wall by `EPOCHREALTIME` around each call). The self-test makes two `TempDir`s in one process and now lists once.
  - **T372, the route.** Of the task line's two, the clean-up once a run: `make hooks-test` starts every job from one `xargs` line of its recipe, so the sweep goes on that line, before the fan-out, and no path moves. The other route (the suites' directories under one subdirectory) would move every suite's `TMPDIR` one level down, and three places know its shape, observed 2026-11-26, method: `grep -rn l7r-hooks-suite` over the tree outside `specs/` and `dev/`: `make_only_hooks/tests.rs` (a command writing under such a path), `scratch_sweep_hooks/sweep/cargo.rs` (a comment naming a fixture clone's build log under it) and `tests/hooks/test-parts.2.sh`.

The Makefile's fan-out line is `hookrun.sh --sweep; xargs ... hookrun.sh --swept ...`. Each process's FIRST listing stands: the test runner's leak pin (`rustc.rs`'s `leak_checked`, one `TempDir` under `/tmp` a crate run), the one listing left in `file-scale --selftest`, and the ledger and gate-write guards' one `TempDir` an event. ### T364, T341 (bundle) (found by T340 and T315, 2026-11-26: a test run of the checks' tool waited for the end of its output pipe, not for the test binary's exit, which cost 3.1 s while a process a test left behind held the pipe, measured 2026-11-26 (T340, the binary by hand into a pipe), and after a one-line edit of a guard crate the tool spent about 2.0 s on one thread before its first cargo build, measured 2026-11-26 (T315, the process list sampled every 50 ms))

- **Approach**: two changes in the checks' tool, `l7r-rust` (`rust/gate/crates/rustc`).
  - **(a) A run ends at its program's exit** (T364, `rustc/drain.rs`, and `run_in` in `rustc.rs`): `Command::output` is replaced by a spawn. Each pipe is read on a thread of its own and the run waits on the child. Once the child has exited, the readers get `DRAIN` = 250 ms (a GUESS knob) to reach the pipe's end. A pipe still open after that is cut only where another process holds it: the run takes what was read so far and goes on. Where no other process holds it, the only writer has exited and the reader is merely late on a loaded machine, so the run waits for the pipe's end and loses no output (a cut there would drop the output's tail, a test build's last `executable` lines among it, and the crate would run fewer binaries). At the exit each pipe holds at most its buffer, so the bound is slack for scheduling, and it is what a leak now costs, a tenth of the 3.1 s that T340's leak cost, measured 2026-11-26 (T340, the binary by hand into a pipe). A pipe still held is named. `holders` reads `/proc/*/fd` for every process but this one with a descriptor on the pipe's inode, and writes one line, `rust-checks: HELD: <program> exited, but its output is still held by pid N (<its command line>) ...; fix: kill and wait what the test starts (451 T363)`, at the end of the run's stderr. `answer` also prints that line for a green crate (`drain::held_on`), whose stderr it does not otherwise show. This is the naming half of T363, a few lines, built here. T363's other half stays open as its own task: failing the crate, ending the leftover processes, and checking the run's process group.
  - **(b) A touch keeps the code views** (T341, `rustc/kept.rs`, `this_binary`, `code_ids_kept_by`). Measured first, with temporary step lines removed before the fix (`dev/measurements/2026-11-27/checks-start/results.md`, three runs before and three after). The time between `git ls-files` and the first build was the code views: all 1,504 Rust files read and hashed again, 5.8 to 6.5 s at load 45, measured 2026-11-27 (step lines, `dev/measurements/2026-11-27/checks-start/`). That happened because the views cache was stamped with the binary's size and modification time. `scripts/gates/l7r-gate.sh` runs a cargo build whenever any file under `rust/guard` is newer than `l7r-rust`, then `touch`es the binary, even though the tool builds from `rust/guard/shared` alone and from none of `rust/guard`'s other sources. The new stamp adds the binary's content id. A matching size and time is this binary's without reading anything. A moved time is still this binary's where the content id matches, and the new time is written back. A rebuilt binary is another binary, as before.

### T383, T385 (bundle) (found by T373, `dev/measurements/2026-11-26/edit-hook/t373-results.md` levers A and C: a hook on an Edit cost the session about 820 ms in its clone and a builder about 400 ms in a pool worktree, measured 2026-11-26 (T373's record, 20 runs a row in its sandbox), and two reads were most of it - the reversal tripwire parsing every line of the feature's event log, and the session's name read from the transcript's start)

- **Approach**: two reads made cheap, each deciding what it decided before; no guard message changes. Before and after, and the proof of the screen, are `dev/measurements/2026-11-26/edit-hook/t383-results.md`.
  - **T383, the reversal read** (`rust/guard/shared/src/guards/event_log_hooks/reversal.rs`, new: `event_log_hooks.rs` stood at 1,000 lines, the file-scale bar, observed 2026-11-26, method: `wc -l`, so `reversal` moved out whole and `append` calls `reversal::reversal`). The read took the feature's whole log and JSON-parsed every line to keep the earlier `PreToolUse` Edits of this path. Now each line is tested as text first (`candidate`) and only a line that passes is parsed; the test a parsed line must pass (`ev`, `tool`, `path` equal as JSON values) is word for word the old one, so the screen can only lose a line by dropping it and can never add one.
  - **DECISION, the screen is a superset by construction.** The task line's sketch is a search for the path's own JSON text, as `launch_line` searches for an id. That trusts every line to be spelled as serde spells it: JSON spells one string several ways (a quote as `\"` or `"`, `é` raw or as `é`), the parse reads them as equal and a text search does not. So `needle` gives the path's text (`"<path>"`) ONLY for a string path of printable ASCII with no quote and no backslash, the paths with one spelling in any writer that escapes no more than JSON requires or a non-ASCII character; any other path (a quote, a backslash, a control character, DEL, non-ASCII, or a path that is no string) is screened by the Edit tool's name alone (`"Edit"`) and its lines parsed as before. Both needles are the value's text without its key, so a writer that puts spaces at the colon is read too. What it trusts, said plainly: that no writer escapes a printable ASCII character it need not (`\/` for a solidus, `E` for a letter); serde, the hook's one writer, and `make events-refile` (serde again) do not, and every line of the clone's 34 logs opens `{"t":` in serde's compact form, observed 2026-11-26, method: `grep -c '^{"t": '` over each log, 0 in each. The cost of the wider screen where it applies: the Edit-marked lines parsed, 9,338 of the 451 log's 158,456, measured 2026-11-26 (the differential's counts).
  - **The proof on the real logs**, measured 2026-11-26 (a temporary test inside the crate, calling its own `candidate`, `needle` and `replaced`, over a copy of every log of the real clone's `.git/l7r-events/`, its source kept as `t383-differential.rs`): 34 logs, 468,589 lines; of the 8,661 lines the old read used, the screen for each line's own path dropped 0; for each of the 1,806 distinct paths, screen-then-parse gave the old read's list, 0 differing. No real path holds a quote, a backslash or non-ASCII (0 of 1,806, measured 2026-11-26 (the same differential)), so that case is the constructed fixtures' (`odd_paths`: a quote, a backslash, `é` and `山`, a tab, DEL, the empty path, null, a number; and three lines as another writer would spell them, `é`, `"` and spaced colons).
  - **T385, the session's name** (`rust/guard/shared/src/session.rs`, `titled`, now `last_title` and `title_line`). The transcript is read backward in 64 KiB blocks (`BLOCK`, a GUESS knob: the record recurred every 56 KB of the transcript T373 measured, and any size reads the same name) and the read stops at the first line, from the end, that answers. What one line says is the old loop's body moved to `title_line`, unchanged: only a line holding `custom-title` is parsed, a title that is no string is named by its `str()`, a blank title or another type is passed over. Lines end at `\n` and `\r` alike, as before; only whole lines are decoded - a block's unfinished head is held (`later`, a list joined once, so a line of many megabytes is not copied a block at a time) until the block before it supplies its start, so a record or a UTF-8 character cut by a block's edge is read whole; the last line counts without a newline, and one still being written fails its parse and is passed over, as the forward read's did. The LAST record wins as before.
  - **What changes, exactly** (T385's line asks it said): (1) a line that holds `custom-title`, parses as JSON and is no object ended the forward lookup with no name wherever it stood; read from the end, such a line BEFORE the last good record is never reached, so the good record names the session; one AFTER the last good record, or in a transcript with no good record, ends the lookup as before. (2) DECISION: a transcript that opens and then fails a read (truncated under the read, an I/O error) now ends the lookup with no name, as one that cannot be opened always did; the forward read kept what it had found before the failure. A name from part of a file is the worse answer, and the Python this was ported from raised in both cases.
  - **DECISION, the side file is not built here.** The option T383's line names second (the Edit lines kept beside the log, about 330 ms saved against the screen's 265 to 290, measured 2026-11-26 (T373's record, 20 runs a row in its sandbox)) needs `make events-refile` and its retask to keep two files in step, and a line missing from it is a missed reversal; the screen has no second file to drift. What is left of the read is filed (Found and left).
  - **Before and after**, measured 2026-11-26 (T373's sandbox reused; the binary built from `1ceb830054` and the binary of this tree as interleaved arms of one run, 20 counted runs after a warm-up round, `t383-time.py`; median / 90th centile in ms; load1 16.6 to 24.8 for the clone's run and 13.3 to 16.0 for the worktree's, both LOADED): the PreToolUse hook on an Edit of a doc, the session in its clone (dirty) 887.8 / 1113.1 to 204.2 / 686.1; a builder in a pool worktree 384.5 / 531.6 to 89.8 / 109.0. By guard: `event-log-hooks` alone 343.6 / 541.9 to 81.0 / 184.2 in the clone and 352.1 / 427.2 to 78.3 / 107.8 in the worktree; `clone-sync-hooks` alone 563.7 / 1230.9 to 96.7 / 366.0 in the clone (what is left is its `git status`), 2.7 / 3.0 and 2.7 / 3.4 in the worktree, where it has no opinion. Every call exited 0 with no output, and each binary wrote its log line (252 lines for 252 log-writing calls), observed 2026-11-26, method: the sandbox log's `t373-*` lines counted after the run, 3,638 against T373's 3,386. No real state was touched (`t383-leak-check.txt`).

### T164 (observed 2026-11-22: with three builders in one clone, the 449 T312 bundle's verify gate went red or "tree moved" four times on other builders' half-done edits, and seven of its ten finished review verdicts were rewritten NOT-REVIEWABLE because a page session and a test-file edit wrote into the clone while they ran; the T289 bundle's reviews earlier waited hours on a stale engine another bundle's edit caused, which also dropped its new-element units without a word)

- **Approach**: `make verify T=<task(s)> [F=] [FILES=] [REVIEW_TREE_OK=]` runs `scripts/gates/review-tree.sh`. It takes the bundle's own files using land-alone's attribution (`split`, read from `scripts/land-alone.sh` so the rule has one copy), makes a temporary commit on HEAD through a scratch index (the clone's HEAD and index untouched), and puts the clone's one review tree `<clone>-review` at it, adding it or resetting it. It draws every map `reviews owed --undrawn` names there, snapshots the owed units into the clone with `tree.json`, and starts `make done` detached there, with the record `.git/review-trees/<commit>.json`. `reviews prereq` and the pair guard judge a snapshotted unit by that record's gate at its key, and judge every other unit by the clone's stamp, as before. `reviews owed` names a map that is not current with its stale engine and the units it hides (`owed/hidden.rs`). The bare `make verify` is refused and names `T=`. The cost, measured on 2026-11-22 (method: each step's own timer in the log, `du -sh` of the target, `df`):

| step | figure | what it says |
|---|---|---|
| first run, tree added (verify1, 21:44) | setup 130 s, worktree 2.0 s, seeding 19.2 s, 7 maps drawn 128.5 s (the engines' first build into the new target), measured 2026-11-22 (its step's own timer in the run's log) | the first tree's cost is the engines' build; the gate went red at preflight in seconds (owed.rs past the 1,000-line bar, docs/make-targets.html stale), both fixed here |
| first full gate (verify3, 21:55) | setup 5.0 s and `make done` about 3 min to red (static, format, hooks-test), measured 2026-11-22 (its step's own timer in the run's log) | the kept check results seeded from the clone (`rust-checks`, `hooks-test`, keyed by content) serve every unchanged crate, so a "cold" review tree compiles only what the bundle changed |
| warm runs (verify4-verify6, 22:00-22:16) | setup 3-6 s, gate 75 s to red on format (verify4), 256 s to red on cover (verify5), 60 s to GREEN (verify6, only owed.rs changed since verify5), measured 2026-11-22 (its step's own timer in the run's log) | the warm gate costs about a minute over the crates a fix touches, measured 2026-11-22 (its step's own timer in the run's log) |
| the target's disk | 1.6 GB after verify1, 4.0 GB after verify3, 9.3 GB after verify5 and verify6 (the changed crates' coverage builds), 64-67 GB free throughout, measured 2026-11-22 (`du -sh` of the target, `df`) | not a third ~35 GB cache, measured 2026-11-22 (`du -sh` of the target, `df`): the kept results mean the review target holds only the tool builds and the changed crates' test and coverage builds |
| sharing the landing target, measured on a scratch copy of its `tool/` | cargo names artifacts the same across worktree paths and judges freshness by mtime: after the review tree built l7r_guard, the landing tree's build read `Fresh l7r_guard` although `pair_hooks/review.rs` and `state.rs` differ between the two trees | REJECTED: a shared target serves one tree the other's binaries, which is a wrong outcome (the gate would judge other code). One review tree per clone, with its own target, reset each run, never piled up |
| seeding the clone's 6.2 GB `.gencache` | 31 entries in the review tree were its own and 31,067 were seeded, and no seeded entry served a map, observed 2026-11-22, method: `find .gencache -type f -newermt` the tree's first run, counted each side. An entry is keyed by its engine binary's build id, and each tree's binary embeds its own source path (`strings tool/hamlet` names `diagram-backlog-review/rust/phases/...`), so the clone's build ids never match, observed 2026-11-22, method: `readelf -n` of each target's `tool/hamlet` and `tool/l7r-mode-a`, ids differing in every target | DROPPED (19.2 s and 6.2 GB a tree): the review tree's own `.gencache` is kept across resets (`clean -e .gencache`); the seeded entries were deleted (6.2 GB to 12 MB), measured 2026-11-22 (`du -sh` of the target, `df`) |
