### T230 (449 T224's builder, 2026-11-24, and 449 T433's, 2026-11-25: `make closing-checks T=<task>` printed "BLOCKED: every error static printed is in another task's files - ()" on errors in the task's own files; T239 is the same fault filed again and ticks with this task)

- **Approach**: The cause is the attribution's awk in `scripts/gates/closing-checks.sh` (`theirs`), not the parsing of the error lines.
  - **What the lines say.** Every error line naming a file in the clone's red static logs is in one of two forms, both parsed already. One is clippy's `-->` at two or three spaces, its path from `rust/` (`  --> phases/src/driver/check.rs:84:18`, T433's run 0859Z). The other is rustfmt's `Diff in <absolute path>:<line>:` (T431's run 0836Z, T433's 0900Z). Eight of the 25 logs held such lines, observed 2026-11-25, method: `grep -E -- '-->|Diff in'` over `.git/closing-checks/*/static.log`. Those logs are pruned after `CLOSING_CHECKS_KEEP_MIN` (a GUESS knob, 360 minutes, T72), so the durable evidence is the suite's cases, which carry those lines verbatim.
  - **Each form static prints, from the source.** `make static`'s recipe stops at its first red step, so one run's lines come from one step. Every red step was enumerated, observed 2026-11-25, method: the `static` recipe in `Makefile` and the `writeln!`s and `Ran`s of `rust/gate/crates/rustc/src/rustc.rs`. `lint` names its files by `-->`, and `format` by `Diff in`. `cover` prints `<path> - lines no test reaches` (parsed since T95), and a failing test's `thread '<name>' panicked at <path>:<line>:<col>:` (Rust 1.73's form; not parsed before). `dead` prints `  pub fn <name>: nothing in Rust calls it`, which names no file. The tree-wide text checks run before them and name no crate's file.
  - **Why the list came out empty.** `theirs` read another task's files with `NR == FNR`. In T433's two runs the clone held no other task's file: `others` was empty in 24 of the clone's 25 runs, observed 2026-11-25, method: `wc -c` of each run's `others`. T224's run, 2026-11-24, is pruned. Its cause is inferred from the same printed line. With an empty first file, `NR == FNR` holds on stdin too, so each error path was stored as one of another task's files and none was printed. No line began with `-` (the caller's mark), so "every error is another task's" held vacuously, and the one empty line printed as ` ()`. Reproduced in mawk, the clone's awk.
  - **The fix.** `theirs` tells the list apart by its file name (`FILENAME == o`) and skips an empty line. `blocked` returns on an empty attribution, never BLOCKED. A red whose lines name no file now says so: "no error line static printed names a file - none could be attributed, so all are counted as yours", followed by its first 8 failure lines, an APART crate's left out. This is said for static alone: hooks-test and quick stay counted whole (T86), so their reds carry no note. The BLOCKED line already names each file and its task once the attribution is read.
  - **The arrow.** A path is read only from a line that OPENS with the arrow (`^ *-->`) or with `Diff in`. Before, an arrow anywhere in a line counted, so a source line quoted under an error (`5 | let s = "a --> mine/src/lib.rs";`) was read as a path.
  - **The failing test.** The panic line's path is read as an error's. Without it, a cover red was BLOCKED whenever another task's file was named and the caller's own test failed: "nothing of yours was judged there", the same vacuous answer one level up.

| step | alone off: fixed and pinned | fresh block vs HEAD | pool manifests moved | the last resort |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `theirs` by file name, `blocked` on an empty attribution | the suite's two empty-`others` cases red on HEAD's script | n/a: tooling | none | n/a |
| the arrow opening its line | the quoted-source case red on HEAD's script | n/a: tooling | none | n/a |
| the panic line read | the mixed cover case and the panic-alone case red on HEAD's script | n/a: tooling | none | n/a |
| the unattributed note, static's counted lines | the no-file case and the APART-lines case red on HEAD's script | n/a: tooling | none | n/a |

### T436 (found by T427, 2026-11-27: `cd /t > /diagram/x.rs` truncated a file no walk reader saw)

- **Approach**: a `cd`'s, `pushd`'s or `popd`'s redirects are placed as any segment's, where the shell stood before it moved.
  - **The gap.** `walk_text` moved the shell at a `cd` or `pushd` and went on to the next segment before `writes_in`, and at a `popd` the same, so their redirects were no target (main-tree, house style, gm-tree; the band refuses such a `cd` whole since T427).
  - **Bash, measured 2026-11-27** (bash 5.3.9, scratch directories `a` and `b`): standing in `a`, `cd b > out1` and `cd b > $PWD/out2` each made `a/out1` and `a/out2`, nothing in `b` - a builtin's redirects are opened before it runs, and `$PWD` expanded there too.
  - **T436-D1, placed before the move** (`shared/src/tree.rs` `walk_text`): at a `cd`, `pushd` or `popd`, each of `redirects(&seg)` is a write resolved by `path_write` against the directory and the `$PWD` before `cd_to` or `popd` moves them, classed from the hint where the shell was last known before the move, marked `redirect`. The loop that turns a segment's writes into targets became `place`, which the `cd` branch and every other segment share (`walk_text` within clippy's 100 lines, observed 2026-11-27, method: `make builder-checks`'s clippy clean).
  - **Use**, measured 2026-11-27 (the same 73,482 Bash calls, the same script): a `cd` or `pushd` with a redirect to a file 0 invocations; 28 with `2>/dev/null`, which `sanitize` takes out and is no write.

### T457 (a landing's first pass grew from about 40 s to 34 min over 2026-11-27 - its cheap Phase lines 43-119 s until 04:17Z, then 226, 379, 719, 1,399, 757 and 2,031 s, growing with the batch: 6, 6, 13, 22, 23, 23 and 35 tasks, observed 2026-11-27, method: the clone's event log, `step: cheap` and `step: end` lines - with the landing process at 86-91% CPU feeding `git cat-file --batch` over plan.md, 1,017,606 bytes with 477 versions)

- **Approach**: the cause measured first, then one change in `rust/gate/crates/plan/src/plan/history.rs`.
  - **(1) The cause, measured 2026-11-27** (a scratch clone of diagram-backlog at 98b632638d with its `plan-seen` store, the 06:43Z batch's 35 tasks through `l7r-gate tick --land-check` - the first pass's own `tick::checks` - and `l7r-gate plan push 2988fee630...HEAD`, plan-gate.sh's call, each with a trace of every History made, its caller, each question and its answer; load average 9 to 20). The tick checks made 70 Histories, two a task: `inside.rs:76` (`built_inside`) and `status.rs:338` (`held_for`, through `tick_gate`). They asked 2,418 questions, and the record keeps no block or section text (675 blocks, 283 task verdicts, none with `text`), so each question walked the versions, 9 of the 69 distinct ones to the end (477 versions) and the rest 7 to 332 back, measured 2026-11-27 (the traced runs). Each version a question walked was parsed again (`blocks()` or `task_sections()` over up to 1 MB), 588,486 parses, and every History fetched its versions anew, 18,100 fetched in 760 `cat-file` chunks, measured 2026-11-27 (the traced runs). The run took 1,252 s and 232 MB at most, measured 2026-11-27 (the traced runs), `plan push` took 35.6 s (69 questions, 16,773 parses), measured 2026-11-27 (the traced runs), and one task alone 63 s, measured 2026-11-27 (the traced runs). So the cost was the re-parse per question, not git: it grows with the questions (the tasks of the batch) times the versions walked (the commits of plan.md).
  - **(2) Each version fetched and parsed once a process.** A version (a commit's plan.md) never changes. The first History to reach it fetches it and indexes it once: each block's key to (its block digest, its text), each task to (its section's digest, the section), every string interned. The index lives in a thread-local store keyed by (commit, path in the repository) and is shared by every History and question after; the raw text is dropped once indexed. A question keeps the newest-first walk and its chunks of 25 (D63), each step a hash lookup where it was a parse, so each answer is the one the walk gave: keys are unique within a version (`blocks` numbers a repeated heading `#2`), and a version that cannot be read is indexed as the empty text, as the walk read it. A History's list of versions is kept by (its path, the commit its reference names when asked): `git log` over the path took 0.3 s at 19,603 commits (measured 2026-11-27, `time git log` in the scratch clone) and the first pass made 70 of them, and a commit made between two Histories, as the landing makes, gives the second its own list.
  - **(3) After, the same runs** (measured 2026-11-27, the scratch clone, load 9 to 16): the 35-task tick checks 92 s and 80 MB at most (from 1,252 s and 232 MB), 477 versions fetched once; `plan push` 6.7 s and 79 MB (from 35.6 s and 194 MB), measured 2026-11-27 (the traced runs); every one of the 69 distinct answers and both commands' outputs the same as before (the traces diffed). Of the 92 s, 9.4 s is in History (the one indexing pass about 5 s of it), measured 2026-11-27 (the traced runs), and the other 83 s, about 2.4 s a task, is the tick checks' own judgment of the plan, outside History (found and left, below), measured 2026-11-27 (the traced runs).

### T446 (451 T304's remainder, part 2: the guards' work-tree `git diff` calls took the index lock whatever `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS` says, 142 of 200 commits refused beside three such loops, measured 2026-11-26 (T304's loop))

- **Approach**: the guards' work-tree reads - the four the task line names, and a fifth the search below found in the gate's preflight, which the gate-write guard asks - run on a private copy of the tree's index, or, for the one that only counts lines, write no refresh back. One new asker, `shared::tool::ask_git_private`, does it; the gate's and the scripts' `git status` calls were read and none changed.
  - **What each git read does with the lock**, measured 2026-11-27 (a scratch repository, git 2.53, `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` on every call; before each probe the index was refreshed and one tracked file's mtime moved with its content kept, so exactly one entry was stale; `.git/index`'s md5 read before and after, then the call run again with an empty `.git/index.lock` standing). `git diff --name-only`, `git diff --name-only <base>` and `git diff --numstat <base>` each REWROTE the index, and with the lock standing each still answered, exit 0: the diff takes the lock for its refresh and skips the refresh where it cannot. So the diff is what makes the session's add or commit die, and the old call never fails, which is why a held lock cannot show it red. `git add --dry-run --ignore-missing .` and `-u` left the index's bytes alone but died, exit 128 ("Unable to create ... index.lock"), with the lock standing: the add takes the lock on every call, stale entry or none. So beside another writer the conflict-marker guard read nothing to stage and passed a conflicted file unseen. `git diff --cached --name-only` and `git status --porcelain` neither wrote nor failed. The three diff forms that write nothing - `-c diff.autoRefreshIndex=false diff --name-only`, `diff-index --name-only <base>` and `diff-files --name-only` - each listed the stale, unchanged file as changed, so none is a drop-in for a list of names. `-c diff.autoRefreshIndex=false diff --numstat <base>` gave the plain call's lines and did not write.
  - **The private index**, measured 2026-11-27 (a linked worktree of that repository, with a stale file, a modified one, a staged new one, a deleted one and an untracked one; the index copied with `cp -p` and the read run with `GIT_INDEX_FILE` set to the copy while the worktree's own `index.lock` stood). `diff --name-only`, `diff --name-only <base>`, `diff --numstat <base>` and `add --dry-run` with `.` and `-u` each answered as the plain call did, and the worktree's index stayed byte for byte as it was. The worktree's index is not `.git/index` (it is `<common dir>/worktrees/<name>/index`), so the asker finds it with `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path index`. The copy keeps the index's mtime, because git's racy-entry test compares each entry's mtime with the index file's: a copy stamped now would call an entry clean that the real index calls racy, and could miss a same-size edit. A copy of the session clone's 3.7 MB index cost 8.5 ms, measured 2026-11-27 (20 copies under `time`). Where there is no index to copy (a repository with none yet, or no repository), the plain call answers: there is then no lock of the tree's for it to meet.
  - **Which tree each site reads at a real call**, read 2026-11-27. `static_runs_hooks.rs` `delta_crates`: the tree the call's `make static` or `make closing-checks` runs in (`run_tree`, 451 T295), asked only on the path that refuses a third run; a builder's closing check reads its pool tree, and the session's reads the clone. `freeze.rs` `changed_lines`: `clone_root` of the dispatching call's cwd (`handle.rs` `cascade_check`), on every check dispatch that passes. For the coordinating session that is the clone, which its own backgrounded `make land` or `make carry` commits in at the same time. `ledger_hooks.rs` `stages_ledger` and `conflict_marker_hooks.rs` `added`/`committed`: the tree of the add or commit being judged, before it runs. They meet a commit in that tree from another call (a background landing or carry in the clone, or a parallel call), never their own. Each is a read that can meet another writer's commit in the tree it asks, so each was changed.
  - **Every guard's git reads, searched for the two forms**, observed 2026-11-27, method: `grep` of `rust/guard/src` and `rust/guard/shared/src` (tests left out) for the verbs `diff`, `add`, `diff-files`, `diff-index`, `stash`, `update-index`, `checkout`, `reset`, `apply`, `merge` and `commit` passed to git, each hit read. The same grep found every script and gate subcommand a guard asks (`l7r-gate.sh` and `sync-with-main.sh` in an `ask`), and those were searched for the same two forms. A work-tree `diff` or an `add` was found only at the four named sites and at one more: the gate's `preflight.rs` `tree` (`git diff --name-only HEAD`, :92), which the gate-write guard asks (`unseen`, `preflight --tree-check`) of the clone on every add or commit while a gate runs there - beside the gate's own commits. It was changed the same way. The other hits take no index lock. Tree-to-tree diffs: `clone_sync_hooks.rs` :308 (`HEAD..<ref>`), `checks/rounds/cap.rs` :74 (a commit against a commit), `speckit/touch.rs` :76 (`origin/main...HEAD`), `feature_approval_hooks.rs` :297 (`<base> HEAD`), `sync-with-main.sh` :285 and :436 (ranges), and the gate's `plan/task.rs` :303 (a range). Index-only reads: `feature_approval_hooks.rs` :128 and :137 (`--cached`). `suite_tools/trace.rs` :155 reads the suite's own tree (`HOOKS_ROOT`). Matches of a command's words, not git calls: `shell_check_hooks`, `builder_pool_hooks`, `gate_write_hooks` :307, `discard_hooks`, `make_only_hooks`, `context_cap_hooks/band.rs`, `phase_source_hooks/search.rs` and `tree/git.rs`.
  - **The fix.** `ask_git_private(dir, repo, args)` copies the index (mtime kept) into a scratch directory removed on return and runs `git -C <repo> <args>` with `GIT_INDEX_FILE` set to it; the copy's own lock is the only lock taken. It is used by `delta_crates`' `diff --name-only <base>`, by `stages_ledger`'s two `diff --name-only` (through `Ctx::git_private`; its `diff --cached` and `rev-parse` stay on `Ctx::git`), by the gate's `preflight.rs` `tree` (its `diff --name-only HEAD`; the measure crate already builds on `l7r_shared`), and by `conflict_marker_hooks`' `git_lines`, all of whose calls (`add --dry-run`, `diff --cached`, `diff`, `status -- <paths>`) now take it. That costs at most three copies a judged add or commit, about 25 ms on the clone, measured 2026-11-27 (three times the copy's 8.5 ms), and keeps one reader. `changed_lines` takes `-c diff.autoRefreshIndex=false` instead: a sum of added and deleted lines is the same either way, since a file whose content is unchanged adds 0, and no copy is needed. `tool.rs`'s `command` comment names what the variable does not cover and where it goes. No guard message changes.
  - **The gate's and scripts' `git status` calls**, read 2026-11-27, for which tree each asks. `land.rs` `dirty` (:259), `writers.rs` `foreign` (:43) and `cheap.rs`'s claims files (:405) each ask the landing's own root through `Land::run`. `preflight.rs` `status_lines` (:339) asks the root the gate runs in. `builder_tree.rs` `held` (:231) asks the pool tree being handed out. `sync-with-main.sh` (:266, `git status` in the clone `done` runs from, with ROOT taken from that cwd; :271, ROOT; :494, the mirror's pool paths) and `land-tooling.sh` (:77, ROOT) ask their own trees. `l7r-gate.sh` (:174) asks TREE, the tree the binary is built from, which is what its build id describes. None asks the wrong tree, so none changed. Each takes the lock as the session's own work, or, where a guard asks the script, under T304's `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`.
  - **Red first**, measured 2026-11-27 (each site's own function on a fixture with one stale entry, `.git/index` compared byte for byte; `make rust-test` on each crate with the old site code and the new asker in place): `rust/guard` 568 passed, 2 failed (`what_a_commit_stages_is_read_without_rewriting_the_index`, "the commit's reading rewrote the index"; `the_crates_are_the_packages_above_the_deltas_rust_files`, "the delta's read rewrote the index"); `rust/guard/shared` 546 passed, 2 failed (`the_cascade_counts_dispatches_and_changed_lines`, "the count rewrote the index"; `what_is_staged_is_read_with_the_index_locked_and_leaves_it_as_it_was`, whose `git add .` with another's lock standing read an empty set where the conflicted `a.md` was wanted). `rust/gate/crates/measure` 281 passed, 1 failed (`the_tree_is_read_without_rewriting_the_index`, "the tree's read rewrote the index"). After: 570 of 570, 548 of 548 and 282 of 282. `a_git_read_on_a_private_index_leaves_the_index_and_meets_no_lock` pins the asker: the plain call answers where no index exists yet, the dry run is read with the lock standing (the plain one exits 128), a private diff leaves the index while a plain one rewrites it (the fixture proves itself), and no repository answers a failure.
  - **Beside a committer**, measured 2026-11-27 (`t446-lock-measure.sh`, T304's loop: a scratch clone of `/diagram`, 30,610 tracked files; three loops of the read beside 200 rounds of `touch Makefile`, `git add` and `git commit`; `private` is the asker's form in shell, `cp -p` of the index and `GIT_INDEX_FILE`; load average 22 to 32 from the machine's other work). The plain `diff --name-only` refused 125 of 200 commits and the private one 0 of 200, measured 2026-11-27 (that loop). The plain `add --dry-run --ignore-missing .` refused 200 of 200 and the private one 0 of 200, measured 2026-11-27 (that loop). The plain `diff --numstat HEAD~3` refused 151 of 200 and the form with `-c diff.autoRefreshIndex=false` 0 of 200, measured 2026-11-27 (the same loop, load average 19 to 39). Every refusal named `index.lock`. Scratch: `t446-lock.log` and `t446-lock-numstat.log` in the session scratchpad.

The changed guards' suites, run directly, measured 2026-11-27 (each suite's own count): conflict-marker-hooks 28 of 28, ledger-hooks 25 of 25, static-runs-hooks 42 of 42, checks-hooks 22 of 22, check-bundle-hooks 38 of 38, gate-write-hooks 32 of 32.

Every writer of a log is one of those, observed 2026-11-27, method: each writer's code read - `event_log_hooks.rs`' `write_line` serializes a row with serde_json's compact `Value::to_string` (the gate's `append_row*` reach it); `make events-refile` (`rust/gate/crates/measure/src/measure/event_log/refile.rs`) re-serializes a moved line with the same `Value::Object(e).to_string()` and keeps every other line's raw text; `scripts/state-sync.sh`'s `merge_in` copies lines byte for byte (`awk` printing `$0`, or `cp`). serde_json escapes only a quote, a backslash and a control character, never a letter.

### T437 (found by 451 T369 by reading, 2026-11-27, no case observed: a start mark whose tree no longer exists - a pool tree dropped, a worktree removed - stays until its task lands, and before this every reader took it as a live start)

- **Approach**: one predicate, `marks::gone(common, mark)` (`rust/guard/shared/src/speckit/marks.rs`), asked by the three readers that treat a mark as a start; `marks::all` stays whole.
  - **DECISION, a tree is GONE only on a positive finding** (label: tooling convention): its path is no directory, or `git rev-parse --git-common-dir --show-toplevel` run there fails or names another top or another common directory (a plain directory where the worktree stood resolves to the enclosing clone, so the top is compared, not the common directory alone). FAILS CLOSED: a mark naming no tree (read as this tree's by the hold, 405 D4) and a mark of the main worktree are never gone. Cost: one `git rev-parse` for each mark of another tree whose directory still stands (20 marks in the clone's common directory, observed 2026-11-27, method: `find task-marks -name '*.json' | wc -l`).
  - **DECISION, the hold** (`speckit::holding_with`, `rust/guard/shared/src/speckit.rs`): a gone tree's mark joins neither `started` nor `own`, so it holds no push, this tree's or another's. `all` still feeds `touch::prefixes`: a removed worktree's paths must still resolve its edit lines (the comment there says so).
  - **DECISION, the withdrawal** (`rust/gate/crates/task/src/task_withdraw.rs`): `Read.marks` is `all` less the gone, so a gone tree's mark is no "started" refusal; its other refusals (carried code, a review, the pool registry) stand.
  - **DECISION, the unstart** (`rust/gate/crates/task/src/task_unstart.rs`): the mark taken is this tree's, else a gone tree's, else a live other tree's (refused, its message unchanged). A gone tree's mark is removed from any tree - its file found by `own_file` under the tree the mark names, so the layout of before T369 too - and its `unstart` row names that tree, so `live_starts` drops that tree's start rows as well (pinned by the test's `holders` reading empty after it).
  - **Not changed, on purpose**: `land/ready.rs`'s `started_tasks` reads the start log for the landing's OWN tasks' readiness, not for a hold, and `others_in_delta` asks open tasks, not started ones; `set_down_hooks/stalls.rs` reads marks for a stall's report, not a hold or a withdrawal.
  - **Red first**, on the old code (2026-11-27, `make rust-test ... ONLY=`): `rust/gate/crates/task` `task_unstart task_withdraw` 7 passed, 2 failed (`a_mark_of_a_tree_gone_is_unstarted_from_any_tree`: refused, code 2, with `make -C <the removed tree>`; `a_task_worked_started_or_carried_is_refused_and_nothing_is_written`: the dead mark's "is started" refusal in place of the carried code's); `rust/guard/shared` `speckit::tests` 14 passed, 1 failed (`this_trees_started_task_holds_and_another_trees_only_by_the_edits_the_push_carries`: a removed worktree's task still held the push). ### T440 (observed 2026-11-27 by 451 T312's empty-HOME proof: `rust-checks-run.lock` and `rust-checks-run.json` found under the scratch HOME's `.cache/l7r-cargo-target/<tree>/` though `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` named a scratch target)

- **Approach**: `world_here` (`rust/gate/crates/rustc/src/rustc.rs`) takes the run's `target` from `target_of(home, tree, CARGO_TARGET_DIR)`: the directory given where it is set and not empty, else `$HOME/.cache/l7r-cargo-target/<tree>` as before.
  - **The claim restated** (constitution XIV): the task line says the run "shares the build cache but not the live run's lock". The code read otherwise: `runlock::dirs_of` already took the override's directory beside the home one, so the override was locked; the defect is the extra directory - the HOME-derived `world.target` - that every such run also locked and wrote its record into, a directory its cargo never built in. The task line's "measure whether the lock should follow CARGO_TARGET_DIR": it should, since every write a run makes under `world.target` follows with it.
  - **DECISION, the target itself follows, not only the lock's list** (label: tooling convention): dropping `world.target` from `dirs_of` alone would leave `cover_dir`'s `<target>/cover-<family>` (where `L7R_RUST_COVER_WORK` is unset) and the pre-warm's `prewarm.lock` written under the home cache, unlocked - the collision T23 fixed. With `target` resolved once, the coverage families, the pre-warm's lock, the run record and every `target_override.unwrap_or(target)` reader (`side.rs`, `times.rs`, `stale.rs`, `kept/alone.rs`) name one directory, and `dirs_of`'s dedup leaves one entry.
  - **What it stops serializing**: runs in ONE tree with DIFFERENT targets no longer wait on each other through the home directory. They share only the clone's `.git/rust-checks/` kept results, each a read-modify-write of one crate's file (`kept.rs`'s `keep_line`); a lost or torn line there is a key that matches nothing, so the next run re-runs that check - a cost, not a wrong green. Every real caller of the checks leaves `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` unset or sets it to the home path itself (`tests/hooks/guard-cases.sh`, the Makefile's `HAMLET_RUN`, which runs cargo, not the checks), so the normal runs are unchanged.
  - **Red first**, on the old code (2026-11-27, `make rust-test CRATE=rust/gate/crates/rustc ONLY="rustc::tests::runlock"`, `target_of` added with the old body first): 10 passed, 1 failed (`a_target_directory_given_is_the_run_s_target`: `"/h/.cache/l7r-cargo-target/b1"` where `"/s/t"` was given). Green after the change.

### T459 (found by 451 T443's review, 2026-11-27, by reading: a hook killed between the reversal index's temporary write and its rename leaves a `.<feature>.idx.<pid>.<n>.tmp` in `<events dir>/reversal/` that nothing removes; none seen in T443's runs)

- **Approach**: `store` (`rust/guard/shared/src/guards/event_log_hooks/reversal/index.rs`) sweeps the directory before it writes its own temporary file (`sweep`): every file named `.<stem>.idx.<pid>.<n>.tmp`, the pid and the sequence all digits, whose modification time is older than `SWEEP_AGE`, is removed. No guard message changes.
  - **T459-D1, built: the sweep runs when an index is written, never on a read.** Label: CONVENTION. Reason: the task's line names the rebuild; a write (a rebuild, or a log grown `STALE` past its index) is rare, so a hook that only reads pays nothing, and the leftover is a few hundred kilobytes at most until the next write. The alternative priced: the day's scratch sweep (`scratch_sweep_hooks`), which would put a reader of the events directory's inner layout into a second guard.
  - **T459-D2, built: every feature's temporary file in the directory, by its exact form.** Label: CONVENTION. Reason: the directory holds the indexes alone (the module's "WHERE IT LIVES"), and a feature whose index is never written again would otherwise keep its leftover for good; a file of any other name, or one whose age cannot be read, is left.
  - **T459-D3, built: `SWEEP_AGE` is one hour.** Label: GUESS (a knob, `make tunables`). Reason: a running writer's temporary file lives from its write to its rename, a rebuild's scan of the whole log between them, about 12 ms for the 451 log's 44.4 MB read a chunk at a time, measured 2026-11-27 (`dev/measurements/2026-11-27/edit-hook/t392-results.md`), so an hour is far past any writer still alive, and the task's line names it.

### T463 (found by 451 T455, dev/measurements/2026-11-27/land-test-time/results.md sections 1 and 4: six green land test runs of 61 to 102 s, 58 to 93 s over same-time controls, not reproduced in 70 runs, measured 2026-11-27 - the next one is to be caught alive)

- **Approach**: a test program run past a bound has its live state recorded once, beside its `test` Phase line, for any crate. `rust/gate/crates/rustc/src/rustc/alive.rs` (new): `Bound::of(world, manifest)` reads the bound - `AFTER`, 30 s, a GUESS knob (why beside it: the land crate's green runs took 1.9 to 12.3 s and its slow ones 61 to 102 s, measured 2026-11-27 (T455's record, sections 1 and 4)), moved by `L7R_RUST_ALIVE_MS` through the tree's own reader - and places the record in the event-log directory's `alive/` (as the sampler's `samples/`), named `<epoch>-<crate>-<pid>.txt`. `Bound::watch(pid, program)` starts a thread on `recv_timeout(bound)` beside the run's blocking `child.wait()`; the run ends the watch by dropping the sender, so a run inside its bound joins a thread that has already returned: nothing is signalled, polled or waited on for the record. Past the bound the thread writes, once, `record(/proc, pid)`: a head line (program, bound, load), then the program and every process under it (root first, by depth) with pid, parent, age, state, wait channel, cwd, command line (300 characters), `SigIgn`/`SigCgt` (T455's one lead is a TERM that may not land), and each thread's name, state and wait channel. libtest names each test's thread after its test, and the kernel cuts that name to 15 characters (`land::stop::tes` at best). The stat line is read after its name's last `)`, and the record is cut at `CAP`, 64 KiB, a GUESS knob, at a character's edge with a line saying so. The paths watched: a built binary run directly (`side.rs`'s `run_built`, the first record of a crate's binaries) and a crate's `cargo test` (`tested`, from `stepped` and `check`), which records cargo's whole tree with the test binary under it; doctests and builds are not watched. The Phase line takes `"alive": "<path>"` only where a record was written (`phase::wrote_alive`; `wrote` passes none). The program runs moved with this change from `rustc.rs` to `rustc/run.rs` (`Ran`, `run_in`, the new `run_seen`, the cargo calls, the new `cargo_seen` and `tested`, `leak_checked`), because the change took `rustc.rs` to 1,033 lines, past the 1,000-line bar, measured 2026-11-27 (`make quick`'s file-scale check); it is now 838 lines, with 210 in `run.rs`. Red first, measured 2026-11-27 (`make rust-test CRATE=rust/gate/crates/rustc ONLY=rustc::tests::alive` on the old code, the World unchanged): 2 failed, 1 passed of 3 - the built binary and the `cargo test` past a 100 ms bound named no record; the third, a run inside its bound recording nothing, held already. Green, measured 2026-11-27 (`make builder-checks CRATE=rust/gate/crates/rustc`): 152 passed, lint and format clean. The tests (`rustc/tests/alive.rs`): a stand-in binary, and a fake cargo, each start `sleep 46.3` and stay until a record appears (at most about 10 s, a test's own GUESS cap, never a fixed sleep). The record must hold that child's args, the run's cwd, `SigIgn=` and a thread line, and must be named on the crate's `test` line, one file. A run inside the 30 s bound (`AFTER`, the GUESS knob) writes no field and no directory. A fake `/proc` covers a name holding `) `, a process gone mid-read, a stat line with no name, an unrelated process left out, a root already gone, and the cap's cut inside a two-byte character.
  - **The lead read** (`rust/gate/crates/land/src/land/stop/tests.rs`, `a_running_landing_is_sent_term`): no spawn-and-signal race can make the TERM miss. `Command::spawn` returns only once `sleep` has been exec'd, and std resets the child's signal mask, observed 2026-11-27, method: the code read at HEAD and std's spawn path. The one way it misses is a TERM the test process was started ignoring: `SIG_IGN` passes through fork and exec, and the guard's handler keeps an inherited ignore (`tempdir/signals.rs`'s `listen`). No land test sets TERM to ignored in process: only `stop::stopped(15)` does, and no test calls it with 15, observed 2026-11-27, method: grep of the land crate and the shared tempdir code. Under `bash -c "trap '' TERM; exec <the land test binary> --exact ..."` the test is green at 30.02 s against 0.03 s plain, but `term_stops_every_held_group_and_exits_143` goes red at 10.14 s against 0.10 s, measured 2026-11-27 (one run each, `diagram-backlog-b1`'s built binary `l7r_gate_land-35df8d33ecfe35d2`). So an ignored TERM makes the binary red, not one of the six green slow runs. The test can wait 30 s, measured 2026-11-27 (the timing above), but that is not shown as their cause. The record's `SigIgn` line settles it on the next catch.

2. **The constraints.** T463's line; the brief's scope (never kill or slow the run, any crate, bounded in size, the land crate unchanged); 451 FR-013 (performance work); constitution X clause 13 (the 1,000-line bar, met by the `run.rs` split); the two tiers (first-tier checks only).
3. **Where each comes from.** G: the GM's words of 2026-11-20 counting work that measures where time goes as performance work. O: T455's record, sections 1 to 4, measured 2026-11-27; this task's red-first run and the lead's two timings, measured 2026-11-27.
4. **Do they describe the world here?** Yes, measured 2026-11-27: the tests run the real `answer` path, both ways a test program runs (a built binary and a `cargo test`), and read the real `/proc` of a stand-in with a live child; the lead was timed on the land crate's own built test binary.
5. **The order.** After T455, which filed it; before T469, the land test's bounded wait, so the next slow run is caught before the lead's fix changes what it would show; before T470, the per-test times.
6. **The exits.** Green: the crate's tests, lint and format clean with the red-first tests passing; the next slow run's Phase line names its record. Red: what failed recorded and the task set down, a claim that it cannot be done ruled through `make arbiter-ask`.
7. **The search smell.** Seventy runs did not reproduce the slow ones, measured 2026-11-27 (T455's record, section 4), so this builds an instrument rather than running the tests more.
8. **The budget.** One landing.
9. **Done, measured.** The red-first tests fail 2 of 3 on the old code and pass on the new, and the crate passes 152 tests with lint and format clean, measured 2026-11-27 (`make rust-test ONLY=` then `make builder-checks`).
10. **Before moving a constant.** n/a: `AFTER` (30 s) and `CAP` (64 KiB) are new GUESS knobs, each with its why beside it.
11. **Before fitting things into room.** n/a.
12. **Before any fix.** Nothing: tooling, no map changes; no defect is fixed here (the lead's test is filed, not changed).

**Found and left?**

Not fixed here: not ordered by the brief, and it needs that measurement first. Filed as T470; lands before T435.

### T452 (found by T449's reading of the night's bad rlib: `scripts/hooks/l7r-guard.sh` cut its own build with `timeout` (SIGTERM at `L7R_GUARD_BUILD_SECS`, 45 s), the cut T336 measured breaking the next link 16 of 31 times on `rust/guard` (`dev/measurements/2026-11-26/prewarm-link/`), observed 2026-11-27, method: the evidence of T449 (1) and the wrapper's `build` read)

- **Approach**: past its limit the guard build is LEFT TO FINISH, not cut (`scripts/hooks/l7r-guard.sh`, `build` and the new `detached_build`).
  - **The call** takes `guard.lock` on fd 9 as before (`flock -n`, or `-w` under the cold seam of 451 T286), checks `stale` under it, truncates `build.log`, and starts the build as `setsid bash <the wrapper>` with `L7R_GUARD_DETACHED=<its limit>`. The build gets stdin from `/dev/null` and its stdout and stderr appended to `build.log`, and it inherits fd 9 and so the lock. The call then closes its own copy and waits on the lock (`flock -w`) for what is left of its limit. If the build ends inside the limit, the result is the same as today's. Past the limit the call writes `l7r-guard: the build passed this call's <n> s limit; it carries on detached (pid <p>), and the next call after it ends runs what it built (feature 451 T452)` to `build.log` and runs the last good binary, as it did, or fails open where none was ever built, as it did. A second call while the build runs finds the lock held and runs what is there, as before.
  - **The detached build** is the old body, unchanged in what it decides (the linker check, the build, the heal of T449, the self-check and copy, `guard.failed`). It runs in a session of its own (`setsid`), so neither a hook's process group being killed nor the session ending takes it down. It first closes every inherited descriptor but its stdio, fd 9 and bash's 255, so a harness pipe or a caller's lock is not held to its end. It runs cargo, the heal's `rm` and the self-check with `9>&-`, so a lingering grandchild cannot pin `guard.lock`. Each result (`l7r-guard.good`, `guard.failed`, `guard.healed`) is stamped with the build's START time (`guard.started`, `touch -r`): a source edited while the build ran is newer than what it built, and the next call builds again. Without that stamp, the session's edits made during a detached build would be read as built (the plan review of the approach, the advisor's point). A build that ran past its call's limit says so at its end: `l7r-guard: the build took <n> s, past the hook's <m> s limit; it finished detached (feature 451 T452)`. This is the record of an overrun that T449 (1) found missing.
  - **The one cut left is a ceiling for a hung build**, `L7R_GUARD_DETACHED_SECS`: 600 s, a GUESS knob, taken from case 7's figure for a real build given room on a loaded machine. It is never under the call's own limit, so `make builder-tree`'s 1800 s (a GUESS knob, `L7R_BUILDER_GUARD_SECS` in `rust/gate/crates/task/src/builder_tree.rs`) and hooks-test's 600 s (a GUESS knob, T449's) keep their bounds. The heal of T449 waits for cargo's `tool/.cargo-lock` and rebuilds within what is left of the ceiling, not the hook's 45 s (a GUESS knob, `L7R_GUARD_BUILD_SECS`). Detached, a gate build holding the profile is waited out instead of leaving the heal to the next call.
  - **Print-fresh** (`L7R_GUARD_PRINT_FRESH=1`): a call whose own build it left running past the limit says `its build did not finish inside the <n> s limit; run again and it carries on`, the line it said before, instead of waiting a second limit on its own build's lock.
  - DECISION (rendering; the brief's "the hook returns within the limit"): the call waits on the lock with `flock -w`, not `wait $!`, because bash's `wait` takes no timeout and a polling loop costs a fork a tick. The cost, measured 2026-11-27 (`dev/measurements/2026-11-27/guard-detached-build/wall-fast.tsv`, the stub cargo building at once, 10 runs each, load 12 to 14): a call whose build finishes inside its limit took 160.5 ms median against 152.5 ms on HEAD's wrapper, +8 ms for the second bash start and the `flock` process. That happens only on the first call after a guard source changes. That call's real build, even T95's incremental one (its figure in the wrapper's header), is far longer than the added fork. Accepted (the builder's choice); the brief's "a hook never waits longer than today" holds at the limit, which is the bound that matters.
  - **Measured, the stub cargo sleeping 3 s past a 1 s limit with a good binary standing, 10 runs each, 2026-11-27, load 9.5 to 10.4** (`dev/measurements/2026-11-27/guard-detached-build/wall.sh`, `wall-before.tsv`, `wall-after.tsv`). Before (HEAD's wrapper): the call's wall was 1.034 s median (1.031 to 1.124 s), and the next call ran the slow build's binary 0 of 10 times, measured 2026-11-27 (`wall-before.tsv`). Each next call built again, because the first build was cut. After: the wall was 1.027 s median (1.026 to 1.032 s), and the next call ran the slow build's binary 10 of 10 times, with no build of its own, measured 2026-11-27 (`wall-after.tsv`).

| step | alone off: fixed and pinned | fresh block vs HEAD | pool manifests moved | the last resort |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| the build left to finish detached, the call bounded at its limit | `tests/hooks/test-l7r-guard.sh` cases 0, 6f and 6g. ### T465 (after T457 plan.md's history was still read once a process: every version fetched and parsed by the first question that walked far, 477 versions, about 5 s of 9.4 s inside History in a 35-task `tick --land-check` and 4.5 s of `plan push`'s 6.7 s, measured 2026-11-27, method: T457's traced runs over a scratch clone of diagram-backlog at 98b632638d, load 9 to 16)

- **Approach**: the digests of every version kept on disk, in `rust/gate/crates/plan/src/plan/history/index.rs` (new) and `history.rs`.
  - **(1) The index.** One file a plan path, `<common git dir>/plan-index/<path with / as %2F>.idx`: a header (the format and the digest code's stamp, T474 below), one `c <commit>` line a covered commit (its id its line's place), then one `b|s <digest> <runs> <key>` line a distinct (key, digest) with the ids of the commits holding it as runs (`0-24,30`). Digests only, never a text. Anything but what the encoder writes decodes as an empty index.
  - **(2) The walk.** T457's shape is kept: newest first, chunks of 25 (D63), the first answer wins. Per commit: in this thread's store, its version; covered by the index and not holding (key, digest), skipped by a lookup; covered and holding, the kept text, else that one version fetched; neither, the file read again once a History (another process may have indexed it since), then the chunk fetched, parsed and added. A dirty index is saved at a question's end: the file read again, merged, written to a temporary file and renamed.
  - **(3) The kept texts.** `plan-index/texts/<sha256 of (plan file, commit, kind, key)>.txt`: only the texts questions returned, used only where its digest is the question's, rewritten where it is not. 60 files, 728 KB after the 35-task run, measured 2026-11-27 (`du` over the scratch clone's `.git/plan-index`).
  - **(4) Measured 2026-11-27**, the 35 tasks through `l7r-gate tick --land-check` and `l7r-gate plan push 2988fee630...HEAD` over the scratch clone (script `t465-run.sh` in the session's scratchpad), wall / user, with the 1-minute load: base (HEAD code) x3, tick 12.0-17.0 s / 11.4-16.1 s and push 6.7-8.0 s / 6.2-7.4 s, load 14-26, cold (no index) x2, tick 12.6-13.2 s / 11.5-11.9 s and push 6.5-7.0 s / 6.0-6.5 s, load 12-18, warm x3, tick 8.0-8.3 s / 7.5-7.8 s and push 2.6-4.3 s / 2.4-3.5 s, load 9-14, measured 2026-11-27 (the runs of the script). Inside History, base 6.1-6.7 s (tick) and 4.8-12.8 s (push), warm 0.42 s and 0.42-0.64 s, measured 2026-11-27 (traced builds of the same runs). The save cost 0.01-0.31 s a process, measured 2026-11-27 (the traced builds). Outputs: the land JSON and push stderr and exit byte-identical to base in all 8 untraced runs, and the per-question answers (129 tick, 123 push) identical across base, cold and warm, measured 2026-11-27 (the answer files diffed). The index is 426,353 bytes for 477 versions, measured 2026-11-27 (`wc -c`).

**T465-D1 - Inverted (key, digest) -> commit runs, not a row a version.** Tooling, no research question: 477 versions hold about 79,500 (key, digest) entries but a few thousand distinct ones, so the file is 426 KB where a row a version and key would be about 12 MB, observed 2026-11-27, method: `wc -c` of the index and, for the rows, an estimate from a heading split of every version in Python.

**T465-D2 - Texts are keyed by (commit, key), never by digest alone.** A block digest strips archive lines, so two texts share one digest, and the walk's answer is the newest version's text (`a_digest_two_versions_share_answers_with_the_newer_text`).

**T465-D3 - Never stale: an entry is per commit, and what could break that is closed.** A version not read whole (a failed or truncated `cat-file`, a commit where the path is gone) is never written (`Version.whole`). A parser that digests otherwise is caught by the header's stamp (T474) and sampled by the canary: each load re-parses one covered commit (the first of the History's commits the file covers, else the last added) and drops the file on any difference.

**T465-D4 - A lost race costs a re-index, never a wrong answer.** The save merges what is on disk first; two renames at once lose at most the loser's additions. Accepted by the builder as a limitation: its cost is one more fetch of those versions in a later process; a lock was priced and not taken (every reader would wait on it for a gain of seconds at most).

**T465-D5 - Outside a repository the index is the History's own, never written.** The old behavior there.

- **Approach**: the index's header stamped with the hash of the code that computes a digest, as 451 T434 keyed the views cache by its code, in `rust/gate/crates/plan/src/plan/sections/digests.rs` (new), `sections.rs`, `history.rs` and `history/index.rs`.
  - **(1) One closed set.** The digest code moved out of `sections.rs` (whose other functions reach the plan template) into `sections/digests.rs`: `digest`, `strip_archive`, `block_digest`, the archive line, and `of`, a plan's (key, digest, text) of every block and task section; `sections.rs` re-exports the first three, so no caller moved, and `Version::of` only interns what `of` gives. `SOURCES` compiles in that file, the shared `plan_text.rs`, `regex.rs`, `sha256.rs` and `rust/Cargo.lock` (which pins `fancy-regex` and its dependencies); the stamp is their sha256 with `char::UNICODE_VERSION`, 79,752 bytes hashed once a process, measured 2026-11-27 (`wc -c`). The header is `l7r plan-index 1 <stamp>`; the probe plan is gone.
  - **(2) Held closed by a test.** `digests/tests.rs` `the_digests_reach_nothing_outside_their_hashed_sources` reads each hashed `.rs` file, comments out and literals emptied, for a `use` or a path through `super`, `crate`, `l7r_shared` or another crate but std and `fancy_regex`, a path from the crate root, a module file, a cfg but `cfg(test)`, a macro neither std's nor the file's, a compiled-in file outside the set, and a test module not the file's last item; `each_reach_rule_fires_on_a_file_that_breaks_it` proves each rule on a breaking snippet. Proved on the real set too: with `regex.rs` taken out of `SOURCES` the test failed, `digests.rs` reaching `the path l7r_shared::`, measured 2026-11-27 (`make rust-test ... ONLY=plan::sections::digests`, then restored).

**T474-D1 - Keyed by the digest code, not the crate's or the binary's build id.** The index lives in the common git directory, shared by the clone and every pool tree, and each tree's `l7r-gate` binary differs: keyed by the binary, every rebuild and every switch between trees would drop and rewrite the others' index, a re-index of about 5 s each, measured 2026-11-27 (T465's traced cold runs), as the whole-binary key of the views cache read all 1,504 Rust files again after every rebuild, 1.9 s at load 12, measured 2026-11-27 (451 T434's step lines). Keyed by this code, only an edit of it does. Chosen by the builder on T434's precedent and the brief's words.

**T474-D2 - Accepted: an edit of any hashed file re-indexes, and two trees whose hashed files differ drop each other's index.** Its cost: about 5 s a switch, measured 2026-11-27 (T465's traced cold runs), while a task edits the digest code or `Cargo.lock`, and nothing otherwise. Priced and not taken: a file a stamp (old ones never cleared), and a narrower lockfile key (the `fancy-regex` packages alone, more code for a file that rarely moves). Chosen by the builder.

**T474-D3 - Accepted: `fancy-regex`'s features and the toolchain are not in the stamp.** The workspace `Cargo.toml` names `fancy-regex = "0.14"` with its defaults and the plan crate names it by `workspace = true`; a feature or compiler change that digested otherwise would be caught by the canary, kept as T465-D3's sample, and missed only where the canary commit's digests stood. Priced and not taken: hashing `rust/Cargo.toml` (every workspace edit would re-index). Chosen by the builder.

**T474-D4 - No rule on code handed in.** T434's test refuses a closure or `dyn Fn` reaching the views; here the one way into the digests, `of`, takes a text alone, pinned by the reach test's count of its signature.

### T231 (449 T418's and T422's plan-review rows were written by hand to land on 2026-11-24 while `make ledger-owed WRITE=` refused them as the landing's own; on 2026-11-25 nearly every push and commit of the coordinating session printed `ledger-owed: N check pass(es) have no row` naming MODE 4 plan reviews of tasks not yet landed, and spec-only pushes carried those rows forward)

- **Approach**: one reading of whose a ledger row is - `ledger_passes/left.rs`'s split, which the push's check (`--refuse`) and the landing's check (`--refuse --landing --tasks`) already asked - asked by every reader and writer of the rows.
  - **Where each side read ownership**, measured 2026-11-25 (the code, and replays of the real pass log and ledger). Four readers, three rules. (a) The push's check (`push.rs`'s `ledger-owed --refuse`) and the landing's check (`cheap.rs`) leave a MODE 4 pass of an open task to that task's landing (451 T147). (b) The push's write (`sync-with-main.sh`'s `--write-plan-reviews`, every push route) wrote the row of EVERY recorded plan review, open task or not. (c) `make ledger-owed WRITE=` (`--by-hand`) refuses every recorded plan review as "the landing's own" (451 T105). (d) The listing and a commit's notice (`--brief`, `ledger_hooks.rs`) asked no ownership at all and named every such pass as owed, with "write them: make ledger-owed WRITE=", which (c) refuses.
  - **What that did.** Today's six 451 T243 plan-review rows were written by four unrelated pushes (d2a61853be 09:49, 9a1c8cd121 10:22, fdce5cc36f 10:40, 546cd2b775 11:18, each "the plan reviews' ledger rows, written at landing (feature 385 T72)") before T243 was ticked at f1458390c3 (11:24), measured 2026-11-25 (`git log --grep "385 T72" -p -- dev/review-ledger.md`, each row's cost cells matched to its pass in `check-passes.jsonl`). The coordinator's transcript holds the line "ledger-owed: N check pass(es) have no row" 906 times since 2026-11-12, measured 2026-11-25 (a count of that line in the session's transcript, tool results and their echoes alike); the one push refusal of today read (2026-11-25 14:50Z) left T243's review correctly and refused on an escalation-check pass, which was owed.
  - **The task line's premise, corrected.** The 2026-11-24 hand write fixed nothing: the refused T423-T418-T422 landings wrote both rows in their worktree each time (3214651875 and 4e4e315222, "the review passes' ledger rows, written at landing (make land)", in `diagram-backlog-land`'s reflog) and were refused on page session P7's 15 passes; the clone's listing named the two rows as owed because a refused landing's commits stay in its worktree, and the session read the listing, not the refusal, observed 2026-11-25, method: the coordinator's transcript at 2026-11-24 17:25-17:27Z and the landing worktree's reflog (and replayed 2026-11-25: `--write-plan-reviews` then `--refuse --landing 449-rust-codebase --tasks "T423 T424 T418 T422"` on the ledger and `plan-review.json` of 7f5d85fef7^ write both rows and refuse nothing). The landing's check never disagreed with `WRITE=`; the listing did.
  - **The rule as built.** A MODE 4 plan review naming its feature and task whose task has an OPEN line (`- [ ] T<n>`) in that feature's `tasks.md`, and is not a task this landing lands, belongs to its task's landing: the push that carries its tick (`make land`'s own write, `cheap.rs`'s `write_ledger`, now `--write-plan-reviews --landing <feature> --tasks <its tasks>`). Every other reader leaves it and names it in the existing note line (`the passes of N open task(s) left to their own landings and sessions`): the push's write (`--write-plan-reviews` with no landing), the push's and landing's checks (unchanged), and the listing and commit notice, which no longer offer it to `WRITE=`. A recorded plan review whose task has no open line - ticked, withdrawn, absent, or a block review naming no task - belongs to the next push, whichever it is; the listing names it as such (`N recorded plan review row(s) the next push writes`), never as `WRITE=`'s. `WRITE=`'s refusal (T105) stays, its message naming both owners.
  - **Open is an open line, not "ticked in neither file".** `left.rs` read a plan review's task as open while no `- [x]` line named it, so a withdrawn or renumbered task was open for ever; harmless while only the checks left it, its row would never be written once the push's write left it too. The open test is now `- [ ] T<n>` in `tasks.md`. `whose.rs` (T157, other checks' passes of a STARTED task) keeps its own ticked test: a started task's session writes those rows itself, and nothing here changes who writes them.
  - **Red first**, measured 2026-11-25 (`make rust-test CRATE=rust/gate/crates/reviews`, the two new tests in `ledger_passes/left/tests.rs` against HEAD's `ledger_passes.rs` and `left.rs`): an unrelated push's `--write-plan-reviews` wrote 2 rows where the open task's must be left ("ledger-owed: 2 plan review row(s) written", want 1 and the left note), and the `--brief` notice named a recorded ticked task's review as "1 check pass(es) have no row ... WRITE=". After the fix the crate passes 206 of 206, and `make rust-test CRATE=rust/gate/crates/land` passes with the landing's write asserted to carry `--landing 449-x --tasks T1`.

### T431 (found 2026-11-27: `make builder-brief` refused T369's brief as a new mechanism, `make -`, passed only by SIZING_OK)

- **Approach**: the mechanism test reads a make word as a target only when it is a name, never a flag.
  - **The gap.** `rust/guard/shared/src/builder_brief.rs` `mechanism` took the characters after each `make ` that are lowercase letters, digits or `-`: in `make -C <tree> task-unstart` (T369's line) and `make -C <tree> that cannot run` (T437's) that is `-` (the uppercase `C` ends it), which has a hyphen and is no Makefile target, so the brief was refused as `make -`, no target of the Makefile yet. The same held for `make -j4` and `make --no-print-directory`.
  - **T431-D1, the target is the first word past the flags** (`builder_brief.rs` `first_target`): after each `make `, a word opening `-` is a flag and is skipped, and where it is one of the flags whose argument is the next word (GNU make's `-C`, `-f`, `-I`, `-o`, `-W` and their long forms, `FLAG_ARGS`) that argument is skipped too; the first word left is read as the target, so `make -C <tree> new-thing` is still refused as a new mechanism while `make -C <tree> task-unstart` is read as `task-unstart`. A flag with its argument attached (`-Crust`, `--directory=rust`) is one word. The gate's `builder_brief.rs` and the builders' queue (`shared/src/builder_queue.rs`, an unlisted task's KIND) call this one function, so both read the same. (Round 1 read no word past a flag, and the plan review blocked it: a new target behind `make -C <tree>`, the pool trees' own form, would have passed the sizing check.)
  - **Red first, measured 2026-11-27 in this tree.** `shared/src/builder_brief.rs` `a_make_flag_is_no_new_target` (T369's and T437's lines with `task-start`, `task-unstart` and `task-withdraw` known, `make -j4`, `make --no-print-directory`, a bare `make -`, and the positive cases `make -C <tree> new-thing`, `make --directory rust -f x.mk -j4 task-start, then make -s 2-up` and `make new-thing`) on the old code: 2 passed, 1 failed of `builder_brief::tests` (`left: Some("`make -`, no target of the Makefile yet")` for T369's line); on round 1's code (no word read past a flag): 2 passed, 1 failed (`left: None` for `make -C <tree> new-thing`).

### T240 (449 T432's builder, 2026-11-25: spec-fidelity MODE 4 was dispatched a third time on T432's section after two BLOCKED rounds and no guard refused it; the arbiter, asked after, ruled no fault, ask:449-T432-plan-round3)

- **Approach**: The guard already held a plan review's third round on one task (`review_round_hooks.rs`, `PLAN_ROUND_CAP`). What failed is its count. `plan_rounds` counts the task's rows of `plan-review.json`'s `block_reviews` back to the last CLEAR, and a section review never wrote a BLOCKED row.
  - **The cause, from the source.** `make decide`'s dispatch (`plan::bundle::task_prompt`) has the reviewer record by `make plan-verdict TASK=`, which is `record::record_task`. That function wrote the verdict to `tasks.<id>`, overwriting the last one, and reached `record_blocks` only on CLEAR. A BLOCKED section verdict therefore left no `block_reviews` row. Only `make plan-delta`'s block reviews (`BLOCKS=1`) wrote BLOCKED rows: 449's record holds 4 BLOCKED rows and 383 CLEAR, and 451's holds 7 and 258, all from block reviews. Observed 2026-11-25, method: `jq` over both `plan-review.json` files, and the T432 rows in the history of 449's record (`git log` of the file, `jq` of each commit), which hold two CLEAR rows and no BLOCKED one. T432's two BLOCKED rounds counted 0, so its third dispatch was "round 1" and was let through (`permitted/other-mode` in `make guard-log GUARD=review-round`). The arbiter bundle's `plan_rounds` (`arbiter/bundle/reviews.rs`) reads the same rows, so it showed the arbiter none of a section's BLOCKED rounds either.
  - **The fix: what counts.** `record_task` appends a `block_reviews` row for a BLOCKED section verdict. The row names the section's blocks (the same keys the CLEAR path computes), and its `tasks` lists the task and any bundle member that shares the section. The blocks' own verdicts stay unwritten, because only a CLEAR is their review. The count is taken from the recorded verdicts, not from the dispatch log. A round is a verdict: T432's NOT-REVIEWABLE return recorded nothing, and the session's own ask counted it out ("a NOT-REVIEWABLE dispatch that does not count", the `asked` text of ask:449-T432-plan-round3; the ruling did not dispute it), while a dispatch log would count it, along with any dispatch another guard refused. The same verdict recorded again on unchanged bytes (the same `tasks.<id>` entry) is the same round, not another.
  - **The fix: the subject.** The guard took its subject from `plan door active-task`, the `.git/active-task` mark under `.specify/feature.json`'s feature. It now takes it from the section the dispatch names ("feature <NNN-slug>, task <T>", `task_prompt`'s words) when that feature is in the clone. A block review's dispatch (`plan::bundle::delta_prompt`) names its feature ("of feature <NNN-slug>'s plan") and, in its bundle's directory `plan-<NNN-slug>-blocks-<T05-T07>-<8 hex>`, the tasks whose blocks it holds: each named task is counted and the first past its cap holds the dispatch (the MODE 4 review of this section, round 1: a third `make plan-delta` round under another active feature went unheld). Only a dispatch naming neither, a hand-written prompt or a block review of no task's blocks, falls back to the active task. A `continue` or `accept` on a plan round is read from the feature its trigger names, where `make arbiter-ruled` files it (`checks::arbiter::continues` and `closed` read `rulings(root, prefix)`, no longer the active feature's). Before this change, a hold under another active feature could never be lifted.
  - **The refusal** reads "BLOCKED: round 3 of <T>'s plan review. Nothing was dispatched.", followed by `checks::arbiter::refusal`'s `make arbiter-bundle TRIGGER="round:spec-fidelity|plan:<NNN-slug>#<T>@3"`. Its first line lost the tripwire's rule, which the next line states (message-check's BREVITY cut, 2026-11-25).

| step | alone off: fixed and pinned | fresh block vs HEAD | pool manifests moved | the last resort |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| a BLOCKED section verdict written as a `block_reviews` row | `a_blocked_task_section_is_a_round_of_its_blocks` red on HEAD, measured 2026-11-25 (`make rust-test CRATE=rust/gate/crates/plan`: 0 rows, 1 wanted); suite case 12 "the third dispatch is refused" red on HEAD | n/a: tooling | none | n/a |
| the subject read from the dispatch, a section's or a block review's | `a_section_dispatch_counts_the_section_it_names`; suite case 12 "held under another active feature" and "...and a block review of its blocks" red on HEAD | n/a: tooling | none | n/a |
| a plan round's rulings read from its trigger's feature | the shared crate's `rulings_and_owed_triggers_read_back`; suite case 12 "the arbiter's continue releases round 3" red before it | n/a: tooling | none | n/a |

### T240 Approach (checklist part A)

1. **The goal, in the world.** The third MODE 4 dispatch on one task's section, after two BLOCKED verdicts, is refused until the round arbiter rules. The refusal names `make arbiter-bundle` with the trigger.
2. **The constraints.** The root CLAUDE.md's tripwires: "a check's third round on one subject" owes the round arbiter's ruling before the next check. Feature 432: the ruling stays in the arbiter's log. 451 T141: one review of a bundle is one round of each of its tasks.
3. **Where each comes from.** G: CLAUDE.md's tripwire line. R: ask:449-T432-plan-round3 in `specs/449-rust-codebase/arbiter.jsonl`. O: the recorder's source and the two records' rows, 2026-11-25.
4. **Do they describe the world here?** Yes, measured 2026-11-25 (the suite run on HEAD's code and on the fix): the suite's case 12 plays T432's sequence through the real `l7r-gate plan record-task` and the real hook: a BLOCKED round, a dispatch whose return recorded nothing, a second BLOCKED round, then the third dispatch.
5. **The order.** No dependency. T227 (the record checks' counter, kept per active feature) is separate. This task's counter no longer has that flaw: a section review and a block review each name their subject. Only a dispatch naming neither falls back to the active task.
6. **The exits.** Green: `make closing-checks T=T240 F=451`. Red: what failed is recorded and the task set down, and a claim that it cannot be done is ruled through `make arbiter-ask`.
7. **The search smell.** none.
8. **The budget.** One landing.
9. **Done, measured.** RED FIRST, measured 2026-11-25. On HEAD's code, the plan crate's new test failed, measured 2026-11-25 (`make rust-test CRATE=rust/gate/crates/plan`): `block_reviews` held 0 rows where 1 was wanted. `tests/hooks/test-review-round-hooks.sh` gave 88 passed and 2 failed: "the third section round was not held (rc=0)" and "the held round followed the active task (rc=0)". After the fix it gave 90 passed and 0 failed. With the cap disabled (`plan_cap_held` returning ""), it gave 87 passed and 3 failed. The block-review case, added after the MODE 4 review's round 1, failed with the block subject disabled (90 passed, 1 failed: "the block review's round followed the active task (rc=0)"), and the final code gives 91 passed, 0 failed. Logs are in the session scratchpad.
10. **Before moving a constant.** n/a.
11. **Before fitting things into room.** n/a.
12. **Before any fix.** The finding: a tripwire the root CLAUDE.md requires did not fire, so a third review round ran without the arbiter's ruling. No map changes.

**Found and left?**
- A plan round's `continue` or `accept` was read from the active feature's `arbiter.jsonl`, not from its trigger's. Effect: a hold under another active feature could not be lifted by its ruling. Fixed here.
- The arbiter's bundle listed none of a section review's BLOCKED rounds. Effect: the arbiter ruled on a third round without seeing the first two. Fixed here by the same row.
- The shared arbiter refusal (`checks::arbiter::refusal`) offered `ARBITER_OK="<reason>"` without its two-word bar (`escape::enough`). Effect: a one-word reason was refused again with no hint why (message-check's FIDELITY finding, 2026-11-25). Fixed here: `<reason, two words or more>`, in the one function that writes it, observed 2026-11-25, method: `grep -rn 'ARBITER_OK=' rust/` (the other hits, in `checks/handle.rs`'s tests, are a different text). The guards' wordings that carry it are reviewed again by message-check.

**Performance work?** no: it holds a review round; no check runs faster or slower.

### T430 (found by 451 T406 by reading, no firing observed: an Edit, a Write or a shell write INTO a gated tree from a session standing in another tree was not held - `gate_refusal` judged a file tool, and `shell_write` was reached, only where `c.own`, the tree the hook's process stands in (read 2026-11-27 from `rust/guard/src/guards/gate_write_hooks.rs`); the coordinating session wrote the clone twice while its gate ran on the night of 2026-11-26/27, seen only because it stood IN the clone (observed 2026-11-27, method: the coordinating session's report in T430's brief))

- **Approach**: `rust/guard/src/guards/clone_sync_hooks.rs` `pretool` called `cx.session.canonical()` (the transcript's last
  `/rename`, else the sessions json) before `dirty(&clone)`, and a dirty clone returned without reading it: only `misrouted`, on a
  clean clone, judges by the name. The call moves into the `misrouted(...)` argument after the dirty return - no new branch or
  closure, every verdict and message as before. Red-first: `a_dirty_clones_edit_reads_no_transcript` (its tests.rs) counts
  `Session::reads` on a dirty clone's Edit - 1 on the old code (`left: 1, right: 0`; 29 passed, 1 failed), 0 now (30 of 30) - and
  pins the clean path still reading it (at least 1).
- **The figure moved since T373.** T385 landed first: `titled` reads the transcript from its end, one 64 KiB block where a
  `/rename` stands, so the 383 ms T373 priced (measured 2026-11-26 (T373's lever B, `t373-results.md`); the block a GUESS knob, `session.rs` `BLOCK`) is gone on a titled transcript. What lever B still saves is the transcript with no
  `custom-title` record, which `titled` reads back to its first byte and then asks the sessions json. Measured 2026-11-27 (load 10 to
  14 on 22 cores), `l7r-guard --only clone-sync-hooks PreToolUse` on an Edit in a scratch clone of `diagram-backlog` (its mirror a
  no-checkout clone at the same HEAD, the claim map's file rewritten by the call), the session's 294 MB transcript copied, 20 runs
  an arm, arms interleaved after one warm-up round (`dev/measurements/2026-11-27/clone-sync-name/t384-time.py`, two runs,
  `t384-timing-run1.tsv` and `-run2.tsv`), median / 90th centile ms:

| case | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| dirty clone, titled transcript | 100.2 / 123.3 | 102.9 / 143.7 (flat: T385's read is one block) |
| dirty clone, no `/rename` in the transcript | 630.6 / 657.6 | 94.9 / 161.1 |
| clean clone, titled | 97.3 / 107.1 | 96.4 / 117.8 (unchanged path) |
| clean clone, no `/rename` | 712.1 / 949.3 | 861.6 / 1017.7 (unchanged path; the spread is the load) |

  Run 1's dirty-titled "after" row (270.7 / 800.0) did not come back in run 2 and is the load's (load 30 at that run's start);
  the code there does strictly less.
- **Lever F, DECLINED** (`git diff-index --quiet HEAD` before `git status --porcelain`): it does not keep every verdict. Measured
  2026-11-27 (git probes in the scratch clone under `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`, as `shared/src/tool.rs` runs every git it asks): a tracked file
  touched with its content unchanged reads DIRTY to `diff-index` (exit 1, again on a second call, since no refresh is written) and
  CLEAN to `status` (0 lines) - a clean clone judged dirty would skip `misrouted`'s refusals and `behind`'s fast-forward; an
  untracked file alone reads clean to `diff-index` (exit 0) and dirty to `status` (1 line), and the guard's verdict depends on it
  (`an_edit_outside_a_clone_or_into_a_dirty_one_is_let_through` dirties the clone with an untracked `wip.txt`), so a clean answer
  owes the `status` call anyway - the clean path made slower; an unborn HEAD exits 128. Only `update-index --refresh` first would
  cure the stat case, and that writes the index under its lock, which 451 T304 removed. T373's saving was under 3 s a day (measured 2026-11-26 (T373's lever F, `t373-results.md`)).

### T478 (found by 451 T465's build half: plan.md's digest index keeps every answered text under the clone's `.git/plan-index/texts/` and nothing prunes it, 60 files, 728 KB after one 35-task `tick --land-check` and `plan push`, measured 2026-11-27, method: `du` over T457's scratch clone, and the clone diagram-backlog's own directory held 108 files, 1.3 MB, observed 2026-11-27, method: `ls | wc -l` and `du -sh`)

- **Approach**: the kept texts are pruned when one is written, least recently used first, to a byte cap, in `rust/gate/crates/plan/src/plan/history/index.rs` and `history.rs`.
  - **(1) The cap.** `TEXTS_CAP`, 4 MiB over the whole `texts/` directory (every plan path's texts share it), a GUESS knob, its why beside it: about five 35-task passes' answers at T465's 728 KB a pass, and about three times what the clone's directory held on 2026-11-27.
  - **(2) The prune.** `keep_text` writing a new or changed text then runs `prune(dir, kept, cap)`: every file in the directory but the one just written, newest mtime first, counted after that one's own size; each file past the cap is removed, its failure ignored (a pool tree may have removed it first). Every file counts, so a temporary file a killed process left is dropped in its turn too. The text just written is never dropped, even when it alone passes the cap.
  - **(3) What counts as read.** A text's mtime is touched (`index::touch`, `File::set_modified`, never atime, which `relatime` makes unreliable) on `kept_text`'s hit, a digest the question's, and on `keep_text` finding the same text already kept (an answer read from the thread's version that the file already holds). A miss touches nothing.
  - **(4) The cost.** A prune is one `read_dir` and a `stat` a file: 1.5 ms median, 2.1 ms longest of 20 over 432 files (5.0 MB, four copies of the clone's 108 texts), measured 2026-11-27 (a `scandir` and stat loop in the scratchpad, load 13). It runs only where a text is written, so a warm pass, whose answers are kept already, prunes little, and a cold pass writing about 60 texts spends about 0.09 s of its 12 s on it, measured 2026-11-27 (T465's 60 texts times that 1.5 ms, against T465's cold tick of 12.6-13.2 s).
  - **(5) Red first**, measured 2026-11-27 (`make rust-test CRATE=rust/gate/crates/plan ONLY=plan::history` on the old code, the tests only added): 14 passed, 2 failed of 16 - `index/tests.rs` `a_kept_text_written_prunes_the_texts_to_their_cap_least_recent_first` left all 7 files where 4 were owed, and `tests.rs` `a_kept_section_text_is_found_by_its_section_digest` found a hit's mtime untouched. Green after: 16 of 16.

**T478-D1 - A byte cap, least recently used first, not a time window.** A window (drop what was not read for N days) bounds the directory by how busy the clone was, not by size: a day of many landings grows it as far as that day's answers go. A cap bounds the disk whatever the rate, which is what the task line asks; ordering it by a touched mtime keeps a text asked again and again, where a cap ordered by write time alone (first in, first out) would drop the hottest text, fetch it and write it back. Chosen by the builder; the cost is one `set_modified` a read, and texts a quiet week never asked stay until the cap is reached.

**T478-D2 - A prune at each write, not once a process.** The brief says prune when a text is written. Measured at 1.5 ms a write, about 0.09 s of a cold pass, measured 2026-11-27 (the scan's timing in (4), times T465's 60 texts), and once a process would save that but let one process's writes pass the cap, and its once-flag is a static the tests' threads share. Accepted by the builder as the cost.

### T473 (found by 451 T463's build: nothing prunes the event-log directory's `alive/` records it writes, at most 64 KiB each (`CAP`, a GUESS knob), one for each test program run past 30 s, so the directory grows without bound, observed 2026-11-27, method: reading `rust/gate/crates/rustc/src/rustc/alive.rs`'s `write`)

- **Approach**: each record written prunes `alive/` to its newest `KEEP`, in `rust/gate/crates/rustc/src/rustc/alive.rs`.
  - **(1) The knob.** `KEEP`, 50 records, the one just written among them, a GUESS knob, its why beside it: at `CAP` each the directory stays under about 3.2 MiB, and slow runs are rare - T455 saw six in its window and 70 runs reproduced none, measured 2026-11-27 (`dev/measurements/2026-11-27/land-test-time/results.md`) - so 50 holds weeks of them.
  - **(2) The prune.** `write` writes the record, then `prune(dir, kept, KEEP)`: every other file of the directory ordered oldest first by mtime, then name (several crates' watch threads can write in one second, so the name's epoch alone does not order them), and the oldest removed until `KEEP` are left, a removal's failure ignored (another run's prune may have taken the file first). The record just written is never dropped. A record that could not be written prunes nothing.
  - **(3) The fixture.** The stand-in test (`tests/alive.rs`'s `lingering`) waited for any file in the directory, so a seeded record would have ended it before its bound; it now waits for crate `rust/a`'s own record (`-rust-a-` in its name).
  - **(4) Red first**, measured 2026-11-27 (`make rust-test CRATE=rust/gate/crates/rustc ONLY=rustc::tests::alive` on the old code, the test only added): 4 passed, 1 failed of 5 - `a_record_written_keeps_only_the_newest_records`, 60 seeded records with old mtimes and a run past a 100 ms bound, left 61 where 50 were owed. Green after: 5 of 5, the new test 1.55 s, measured 2026-11-27 (`/usr/bin/time` over its `make rust-test ONLY=`).

**T473-D1 - The newest N, not those under M days.** The task line offers both. A count bounds the disk at `KEEP` times `CAP` whatever the rate, and a slow run is the rare thing worth keeping, so an age limit would throw away the last catch after a quiet month. Chosen by the builder.

### T473 Approach (checklist part A)

### T479 (found by 451 T432, 2026-11-27, by reading: a landing's ticks exempted every feature's started task of the same id)

- **Approach**: a landing's ticks exempt the landed feature's started tasks alone, at the push and in the first pass.
  - **The gap.** `rust/guard/shared/src/speckit.rs` `holding_with` skipped every started task whose id `L7R_LAND_TICKS` named, in whichever feature's directory it was asked of, so feature 449's landing of T5 un-held feature 451's started T5 at the push (`scripts/sync-with-main.sh` asks `l7r-gate speckit-todo --holding` of each touched or pointed feature) and in the first pass (`rust/gate/crates/land/src/land/parity.rs` `others_in_progress` handed the landing's ticks to every other directory).
  - **T479-D1, the ticks handed in with their feature** (`holding_for(d, ticks, landed)`, new): the ticks apply only where `landed` names the asked directory. `holding` (the push's and the CI merge's reader) passes `SPECIFY_FEATURE`, which `make land` exports beside `L7R_LAND_TICKS` (`land.rs`), as T432 scoped `L7R_LAND_READY`; a push with ticks and no feature named exempts nothing, failing closed. NOT the environment alone: the in-process callers (`ready.rs`'s `hold` and `export_ready`) run inside `l7r-gate land`, whose own `SPECIFY_FEATURE` is the session's and may name another feature - `self.export` reaches the children only - so `holding_with(d, ticks)` keeps its meaning, the ticks taken as the directory's own (`holding_for(d, ticks, py_name(d))`).
  - **T479-D2, the CLI scoped** (`rust/gate/crates/cohort/src/speckit_todo.rs` `answer`): `--holding` reads `SPECIFY_FEATURE` beside `L7R_LAND_TICKS` and asks `holding_for`; `holding_reply` (in process, the landed directory) keeps `holding_with`.
