### T310 (451 T305, 2026-11-26: 73 of three days' 272 untied check dispatches were subagent-dispatched; re-read against what landed since, 2026-11-27: of its three halves one still holds, measured below)

- **Approach**: the builder reading (`builder_brief`, `rust/guard/shared/src/guards/set_down_hooks/builders.rs`) reads a pool builder's brief marker first, through the marker's one reader (`l7r_shared::builder_brief::parse`, 451 T334), and falls to its old description reading only where the prompt holds no marker naming a task.
  - **(a) The reader - HOLDS, fixed here.** The brief no longer opens `Build 451 T<n>`: since T334 it opens `BUILDER-BRIEF 451 T<n>[,T<m>] KIND= JOBS= TREE=`, and the session describes the dispatch `Fix: 451 T340 orphaned sleeps`, `Build half: ...`, `Measure: ...`. The old reading wants the description to open with the feature number (`BRIEF`, `^\s*(\d{3})\b`), so it refused every one: all 103 depth-1 agents of the session's `subagents/` whose prompt opens with the marker are described `<Kind>: 451 T<n> ...` (`Fix`, `Build half`, `Closing half`, `Measure`, `Close`), none with a leading number, observed 2026-11-27 (method: each meta's `description` against its transcript's first record, the session c6fd72d1). Every pool builder read as no builder, for every caller: the event log's booking (`event_log_hooks/filed.rs`), the Stop hook's stall check (`set_down_hooks/stalls.rs`), the builder's own Stop (`builder_stop_hooks.rs`), a check's own task (`check_bundle_hooks/own.rs`) and the ledger's left passes (`reviews/ledger_passes/left/whose.rs`, which had found the tree by T305's pool reading instead).
  - **(b) The booking of a builder's checks - HOLDS, fixed by (a).** The dispatch line itself is booked: 133 of the 134 Agent `PreToolUse` lines the pool's builders wrote in the 24 h to 2026-11-27T11:00Z carry a task (121 `spec review`, 13 `other subagent`, the one untied a `spec-fidelity` dispatch by T463's builder), because the dispatching builder's own lines read its `Fix: 451 T<n>` description for the task, observed 2026-11-27, method: the 451 log's Agent `PreToolUse` lines whose `by` is a marker-briefed builder, counted by their `task` field. What is untied is the CHECK's own lines: of the 133 agents those builders launched (one dispatch of the 134 left no agent meta, not traced further), 15 had lines with no task - 140 of their 1,408 lines - each a check whose own description names none (`Plan review of 451 changed blocks`, `451 plan-delta review`, `message-check two guard messages`), so the booking fell to the builder reading of its parent, which refused, observed 2026-11-27 (method: the 451 and 449 logs' lines of the last 24 h whose `by` agent's meta names a marker-briefed builder as `parentAgentId`, counted by their `task` field). The lines' `ms` is tool time, not the check's duration, so no minutes are claimed here. With (a), such a line is booked to the parent's marker task and its feature (`filed`'s `theirs`).
  - **(c) The start row and mark of a handed-out tree - NO LONGER HOLDS, not built.** 451 T332/T344 answered it by the pool's registry instead: a line written in a pool tree takes the task the registry says holds the tree (`pool_task`, `filed.rs`), and that doc comment records why a handout writes no start - the start log's other readers (the landing's "was it started", the stall check, the time breakdown's first start, the undo at release) would read a start nobody made as one. The marks are per tree since T254/T369, so a mark made in the clone no longer stands for a builder's tree, and since T437 a mark of a gone tree is inert. With (a) a builder's check is booked by its parent's marker, so it needs no start row either.
  - **The callers that change.** Each now reads a pool builder as one; each keeps its own further test: the stall check and the builder's own Stop act only on a task with a start in `task-starts.jsonl` (and an open box), so a two-tier pool builder that never runs `make task-start` stays quiet in both, and one that does is held as T84 and T268 meant; `own.rs` names the check's task, which it named nothing for before. No guard message changes.
  - **The cost.** The prompt's first record is now read for every depth-1 agent the reader is asked about, where before only for one whose description held no id: one line of one file. Its callers ask it per running agent (`stalls.rs`, the session's live agents), per Stop (`builder_stop_hooks`), per check dispatch (`own.rs`), per pass's parent (`whose.rs`), and per event-log line only where no earlier link named the task.
  - **Red first**, measured 2026-11-27 (`make rust-test CRATE=rust/guard/shared ONLY="guards::event_log_hooks::tests::booked"` on the old code, the test only added): 6 passed, 1 failed of 7 - `a_pool_builders_check_is_booked_by_its_brief_marker`, `agent_builder` of a builder described `Fix: 451 T340 orphaned sleeps` read None where `("451", [T340])` was owed. Green after: 7 of 7, and `make builder-checks CRATE="rust/guard/shared rust/gate/crates/task rust/guard rust/gate/crates/reviews"` clean (573, 146, 587, 214 passed), with the set-down, event-log, builder-stop and check-bundle hook suites (46, 25, 7, 38 passed).

**T310-D1 - The marker read first, its task word's ids; a marker naming none falls to the description.** The marker is what `make builder-brief` prints and the guard checks, so it is the brief's own statement of its task, where the description is the session's free text. Reading it first means a pool builder whose description happens to open with a number still reads by its marker. A marker whose task word holds no `T<n>` is malformed for this purpose, and falling through keeps the 449-era description and first-line readings as they were (pinned by the test's `anone`). Chosen by the builder.

**T310-D2 - The whole prompt to `parse`, not its first line.** The guard (`builder_brief_hooks.rs`) accepts a marker on any line of its own, indented or not, so the reader takes the same text the guard did; a marker only mentioned in a sentence is no marker (`parse`'s rule, pinned by the test's `asaid`). The old first-line reading of a bundle brief is kept on the prompt's first line.

### T386 (T373's lever D: clone-sync's clean path listed the sessions directory once per claim of the clone)

- **Approach**: `rust/guard/src/guards/clone_sync_hooks.rs`: `pid_of` listed and parsed `~/.claude/sessions` on every call, and
  `misrouted` (a clean clone's edit, the path T384 made the one that pays) called it through `forked_from`, listed it again in
  `parked_by`, then once more through `sid_is_live` for each claim file naming the clone. A new `Sessions` (each parsed record
  with its file's stem, in the listing's order) is read at most once a decision, lazily through a `OnceCell` in `misrouted`, and
  `pid_of`, `sid_is_live`, `forked_from` and `parked_by` take it; `pid_of` is the first record naming the session, its stem all
  digits, as before. The claim-map walk passes a file whose size is 0 by its `metadata` (it follows a link, as `is_file` did) before
  opening it: an empty file names no clone, so no verdict moves. Every message unchanged. Red-first, measured 2026-11-27:
  `a_clean_clones_edit_lists_the_sessions_directory_once` (its tests.rs; three dead claims of the clone, two empty claim files, one
  of another clone, then a live claimant) counts the listings through a thread-local `LISTINGS` - 5 on the old code (`left: 5,
  right: 1`; 30 passed, 1 failed), 1 now on both the let-through and the live-claim refusal (31 of 31).
- **The figures**, measured 2026-11-27 in a scratch of the live state (a no-checkout mirror of /diagram, a checked-out clean clone,
  the live claim map copied - 2,868 files, 1,580 empty, the 130 non-live claims of `diagram-backlog` rewritten to the scratch clone,
  its one live claimant dropped - and `~/.claude/sessions` copied, 72 json records), the old binary the clone's hook build at the
  same `clone_sync_hooks.rs` commit (07ca2aa5b4), the new this tree's: opens under T373's preload shim (`t386-opens.txt`) 12,728 to
  1,818 - session json 9,402 to 72, claim files 2,868 to 1,288; time (`dev/measurements/2026-11-27/clone-sync-sessions/t386-time.py`,
  20 runs an arm, arms interleaved after one warm-up, load 17 to 20 on 22 cores), median / 90th centile ms:

| run | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 1 (`t386-timing-run1.tsv`) | 267.5 / 528.8 | 144.9 / 196.7 |
| 2 (`t386-timing-run2.tsv`) | 219.7 / 300.8 | 122.3 / 382.1 |

- **Pruning dead claim files is NOT this task**: it deletes, and wants its own rule, priced: measured 2026-11-27 (`t386-timing-nomap.tsv`),
  the new binary with an empty claim map 202.1 / 504.2 ms against 124.6 / 136.4 with the full one, back to back at load 14 to 16 -
  no saving above the load's noise once empty files are passed by size, so it is not filed.

### T485 (451 T481's `make guard-messages` named two escalation-hooks refusals, keys a01405381091d548 and eee895a7b090e5af, as rendered at HEAD with no verdict)

- **Approach**: no guard change and no verdict recorded: neither key is a wording HEAD renders. Measured 2026-11-27.
  - **T485-D1, the keys are the wording before 451 T282, from a store older than it.** The suite at this tree's HEAD (30193ea012) renders its section 10's offer and question cases at 494 and 479 characters, measured 2026-11-27 (`L7R_MESSAGE_CORPUS=<dir> bash tests/hooks/test-escalation-hooks.sh` into a private corpus: 67 passed, 0 failed; the texts' lengths read from its `messages.jsonl`). Under T282's mask they key to `e8301989f2d8f60f` and `7dd4088ec3ff42c4`, both PASS in `dev/guard-messages.tsv`, measured 2026-11-27 (`l7r-guard messages check` over that corpus). The task's keys come out of the same texts with their last line cut ("If the line offers him nothing, go on and say nothing of this to him." and its QUESTION twin), at 424 and 408 characters, hashed under T282's mask: exactly `eee895a7b090e5af` and `a01405381091d548`, measured 2026-11-27 (the mask and the key recomputed by hand from `rust/guard/src/suite_tools/messages.rs`'s `Masks::wording` and `key`). That last line is what 148fa78bdf (T299 and T282) added, with the mask. The same cut texts keyed WITHOUT the mask are the record's BASELINE rows `4da09dff87312ac3` and `a908329f0c8990d8`, measured 2026-11-27 (the same hand recomputation). So T481's reading combined an older guard's renderings with a newer guard's key. Of the clone's stores, the review tree's (`diagram-backlog-review`, its file written 2026-11-24 21:43) and the t271 tree's (2026-11-26 11:14) hold those renderings, both before 148fa78bdf (2026-11-26 15:26 -0500), and the clone's own store and the land tree's hold only HEAD's wording, observed 2026-11-27, method: each worktree's `hooks-test/messages/escalation-hooks.sh.jsonl` read for the cut forms, with its mtime. A store file is rewritten only when its suite runs (`tests/hooks/hookrun.sh`), so it is a store older than the commit, not a stale guard binary.
  - **T485-D2, no message-check dispatch.** The brief asked for one on `make guard-messages BUNDLE=1`'s bundle. With the corpus above in this tree's store, the bundle holds no escalation unit (every escalation wording HEAD renders has a verdict). A verdict on the keys would record a wording no guard renders, and cutting the guard would answer a FAIL nobody reached. This differs from the brief's literal step, and the plan review rules on it.
  - **Why the batch gates did not catch them**: there was nothing for them to catch. The gate's `make hooks-test` re-renders every suite into the clone's store first, and the clone's store holds the 494 and 479 renderings, both PASS. Only a pool tree's store, which no first-tier builder re-renders, kept the old ones. The same thing showed in this tree: its store held 451 T483's nine gate-write renderings (its done commit 1902ea23c2, not carried here) over a HEAD with the old wording, and `make guard-messages` here named all nine as owed. All nine are in that commit's `dev/guard-messages.tsv`.

### T447 (Superseded by T397: `make land` carries its tasks' done commits before its first pass, so the refusal this task would add can never fire)

- **Approach**: no code. The task would have `make land`'s first pass (`cheap.rs`) refuse a landing task whose done commit (`refs/l7r/done/<feature>-<task>`) the landing tree's HEAD does not hold. Since 451 T397 part (c), no landing reaches that pass with such a commit uncarried. Read 2026-11-27 at 30193ea012:
  - **The one route into the first pass.** `Land::cheap_refusals` has one caller, `Land::land` (`rust/gate/crates/land/src/land.rs`, the `cheap` phase). `Land::land`'s one production caller is the phase wrapper (`land/phase.rs`), which every `make land` and `make land-batch` runs. In `Land::land` the order is: `unfinished::refusals`, then `self.carry_done(d, tasks)` (a non-zero code returned at once), then `alone_owed`, then the first pass.
  - **What the carry leaves.** `Land::carry_done` (`rust/gate/crates/land/src/land/carry_done.rs`) asks `l7r_gate_task::builder_done::to_carry` for exactly the set T447 would refuse: the landed tasks' done refs whose commit HEAD lacks, by `uncarried`'s author time and subject. It carries each through `carry::cli`, the same call `make carry COMMIT=` makes. A carry that does not end verified returns 2 ("refused before anything ran - nothing landed, nothing ticked"), and the first pass never runs. So the first pass sees either no such commit or no landing.
  - **The land-alone route.** `alone_owed` stands after the carry, so a dirty clone's landing worktree (`land/alone.rs`) is checked out at the carried HEAD. Its inner `make land` comes back through `Land::land`, where `to_carry` finds nothing.
  - **Pinned**: `land/carry_done/tests.rs` holds `a_landing_carries_its_tasks_done_commit_before_its_first_pass`, `a_carry_that_stops_lands_nothing_and_names_its_hand_command` and `a_dirty_clone_carries_before_it_lands_alone`. Measured 2026-11-27 (`make rust-test CRATE=rust/gate/crates/land ONLY="land::carry_done"`): 4 ran, 0 failed.

| step | alone off: fixed and pinned | fresh block vs HEAD | pool manifests moved | the last resort |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| closed, Superseded by T397 | n/a: no code; T397's `carry_done` tests pin it | n/a: tooling | none | none |

### T387 (found by 451 T373, lever E: while a plan review holds text every Bash call's PreToolUse loads, snapshots and SAVES the 3.0 MB `checks-open.json`, 97 to 118 ms of CPU, and checks-hooks spends 98 ms on every Agent PostToolUse on the same file, measured 2026-11-26, `dev/measurements/2026-11-26/edit-hook/t373-results.md`)

- **Approach**: the check state is saved only where a call changed it, and a rounded dispatch drops the two fields no reader needs, in `rust/guard/shared/src/checks/` (`planhold.rs`, `handle.rs`, `rounds.rs`). Measured 2026-11-27, before and after interleaved, 20 runs each, on a copy of the clone's state (2,994,673 bytes, 3,054 dispatches), load 14 to 16 (`dev/measurements/2026-11-27/t387-hold-writes/results.md`).
  - **(1) The held text is kept once a hold and tree.** `planhold::snapshot` keeps a live hold's places under `plan_snaps["tree:<root>"][<hold id>]` at the first call in that tree, and takes nothing at a later call's start; `restore` compares the tree's kept text (and a call-keyed snapshot an earlier build wrote, read first and removed) and, after a write-back, retakes it, so a place no write-back could find is named once. `prune_snaps` drops the kept text of a hold gone, at a return, a purge and a restore. `handle` saves at the PreToolUse and the PostToolUse only where `plan_holds` or `plan_snaps` moved (or the feature switched). `checks-hooks`' prefilter (`"plan_snaps"` in the file) is unchanged and still finds the kept text.
  - **(2) A launch or return no row names is not booked.** `handle::concerns`: an Agent launch whose call id is no dispatch's or hold's, or a return whose agent is none's and that no waiting wave row could pair, returns before `book_keep` and saves nothing; a `TaskStop` is always booked. A first cut compared a clone of the whole state around `book_keep` - 95.5 ms of CPU on the Agent case, 55 ms of it the clone and compare, measured 2026-11-27 (`t387-time.py`) - and was replaced.
  - **(3) The prune.** `rounds::returned` drops `counted` and `quote_notes` from every rounded row: both are read only by that row's own return, before it rounds (`rounds::returned`, `fixloop::returned`). Every other field has a reader, inventoried first (the results file's table): `owed` and `manifest` the arbiter's bundle, `reply` apply-edits' `settled.rs` (all time) and the earlier-rounds bundles, `marks` the launch (left while T488 is open). 281 KB, 9.7% of the state, measured 2026-11-27 (`json.dumps` of the clone's state with and without them).
  - **(4) Red first**, 2026-11-27 (`make rust-test CRATE=rust/guard/shared ONLY="checks::handle::hold_writes"`, the tests only added): 3 failed of 5 - `a_bash_true_during_a_hold_writes_nothing` (the state rewritten on every call), `an_agent_launch_no_check_or_hold_names_writes_nothing`, and `a_command_that_overwrote_held_text_is_still_written_back`, a DEFECT of HEAD: a call begun while another call's change stood snapshotted the changed text, so its end wrote that change back over the first call's restore. Green after: 579 of 579 in `rust/guard/shared`, 592 of 592 in `rust/guard`, with `a_rounded_dispatch_drops_what_only_its_return_read` and, through both guards, `a_hold_kept_by_record_edit_is_written_back_by_checks_hooks`; the hook suites checks-hooks 22, record-edit-gate 9, record-edit-hooks 14 passed.
  - **(5) The figures.** CPU medians, before against after: a Bash `true`'s PreToolUse under a hold 98.8 against 42.6 ms, its PostToolUse 92.6 against 38.2, a non-check Agent's PostToolUse 108.1 against 52.6, and writes 22 of 22 against 0 of 22 each, measured 2026-11-27 (`t387-time.py`). A Bash call under a hold paid 191 ms of CPU, now 81, measured 2026-11-27 (`t387-time.py`), and at T373's 1,176 such calls and 212 Agent ends a day about 130 s plus 12 s a day, an estimate from T373's counts, measured 2026-11-26 (`t373-holds.py`; an upper bound: T373's hold count is one). The prune: 36.0 / 33.4 / 48.4 ms on the pruned copy, about 4 to 6 ms a call at a lower load, measured 2026-11-27 (`t387-time.py`). What is left is the parse of the 3.0 MB state, measured 2026-11-27 (`t387-time.py`, the after build), filed as T490.

**T387-D1 - Kept once a hold, not retaken at each call's start.** The brief: "save only where the snapshot changed". Retaking the text at each start where it changed would keep the HEAD defect of (4): a concurrent call's start would take the other call's change as the held text. Kept once, a change a hooked call made is written back at that call's end and blamed on it; a change no hooked call made (an editor, a command past its one PostToolUse) is written back at the next call's end, where HEAD took it as held at the next start - the hold's purpose, the text the review reads standing still. The write-back's message is unchanged, its "since the call began" read as since the hold's first call. Chosen by the builder.

**T387-D2 - A call-keyed snapshot is still read.** A session running a build from before this one writes `plan_snaps[<call id>]` at its PreToolUse; its PostToolUse may run this build after a rebuild, so `restore` reads and removes that snapshot first. Retiring the read is one line once no older build runs. Chosen by the builder.

| step | alone off: fixed and pinned | fresh block vs HEAD | pool manifests moved | the last resort |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| the hold's text kept once a hold and tree, the state saved only where it moved, a launch or return no row names unbooked, a rounded row's `counted` and `quote_notes` pruned (`checks/planhold.rs`, `handle.rs`, `rounds.rs`; tests `handle/hold_writes.rs`, `planhold/tests.rs`, `rounds/tests.rs`, `checks_hooks/tests.rs`), red first 3 of 5, measured 2026-11-27 | n/a: tooling, no map drawn | n/a: tooling | none | n/a |

### T387 Approach (checklist part A)

1. **The goal, in the world.** A Bash call while a plan review holds text, and an Agent call's end, cost the hook its read of the check state and no write; the hold still puts back held text a command overwrote.
2. **The constraints.** T387's line and the brief (save only where the snapshot changed, red first on a Bash `true` writing nothing; every reader of the kept dispatches found before any field is dropped; the write-back pinned; no guard message changed); feature 385 T85 and 451 T78, T80, T123 (the hold, its write-back, its tree); 451 FR-013; the two tiers.
3. **Where each comes from.** O: T373's figures, measured 2026-11-26; this task's red-first run and its interleaved timing, measured 2026-11-27; the reader inventory by grep over `rust/`, 2026-11-27.
4. **Do they describe the world here?** Yes: the timing runs the real binaries' `--only record-edit-hooks` and `--only checks-hooks` on a copy of the clone's own state, and the two-guard test drives both guards' `decide` on one call.
5. **The order.** After T373, which measured it; before T302 (T373's section); T488, T489 and T490 after it.
6. **The exits.** Green: the red-first tests passing, both crates' first-tier checks and the two guards' suites clean. Red: what failed recorded and the task set down, a claim that it cannot be done ruled through `make arbiter-ask`.
7. **The search smell.** None.
8. **The budget.** One landing.
9. **Done, measured.** A Bash `true` under a hold writes the state 0 of 22 times (22 of 22 before), its two hooks 81 ms of CPU against 191, measured 2026-11-27; `make builder-checks CRATE="rust/guard rust/guard/shared"` clean.
10. **Before moving a constant.** n/a.
11. **Before fitting things into room.** n/a.
12. **Before any fix.** Nothing a map shows. The check it breaks at HEAD: the hold's write-back, which a concurrent call's end undid (4); fixed here.

**Found and left?**
- A check-wave dispatch never applies its reading marks (`rounds::pair_wave` sets a wave row running without `apply_marks`; 362 of the 3,054 rows carry unapplied marks, observed 2026-11-27, method: counting rows with `marks` by `wave` and `state` in the clone's state): a wave round's sentences are read as a first look at the next round, so its round count is wrong. Not fixed here: it changes how rounds are counted, outside this task's saving of the state. Filed as T488; lands before T490.
- A running hold past `HOLD_MAX_S` is never purged (`planhold::purge` drops only pending holds): a review whose return never came keeps every Bash call of the clone on the state's load, about 40 ms each now, measured 2026-11-27 (`t387-time.py`), and keeps refusing held text without `PLAN_EDIT_OK`. Not fixed here: purging it changes that refusal and needs its own ruling. Filed as T489; lands before T490.
- The state's parse floor, 36 to 43 ms of CPU on every hook that reads it, measured 2026-11-27 (`t387-time.py`): whole old rows are held by `settled.rs`, which reads every reply. Not fixed here: a new store, several readers. Filed as T490; lands before T302.

**Performance work?** yes (a `[perf]` task, 451 FR-013): it makes the guards' hooks faster - a Bash call under a plan hold 191 to 81 ms of CPU, an Agent call's end 108 to 53, measured 2026-11-27. Not an engine-speed task: no checklist answers owed.

### T388 (an Agent call's PreToolUse took 154 ms and its PostToolUse 135, its guards' causes not read, found by T373, measured 2026-11-26 (`t373-tools2.tsv`, 20 runs))

- **Approach**: a measurement; no source changed. What was asked (the task line): which read or process each Agent-hook guard spends its time on, before any change. The record is `dev/measurements/2026-11-27/agent-hook/results.md`, its scripts and tables beside it; every figure below is the record's, measured 2026-11-27 from 06:33 to 06:52 local at load 4.0 to 12.6 on 22 cores with other builders running, each the median / 90th centile ms of one hook call over 20 counted runs after a warm-up, the arms interleaved (`t388-time.py`).

### T487 (a removed stub's verdict and an archive split refused a 12-task landing's ticks twice while `make plan-delta` owed nothing)

- **Approach**: traced on the real record and plan (observed 2026-11-27, method: each commit's `plan-review.json` entry for `### T475 Approach (checklist part A)` read with `jq` from e2e18eee43 to 3b773899aa, and a throwaway test replaying the landing's ticks over 23ca09d5d7's spec files with `task::archive`). Three causes, each fixed or filed:
- the entry was set to the unfilled stub's digest (6b67b7e2) by T310's carry, cec429b447: T310's pool tree had reviewed T475's stub, and `merge.rs` gives a same-day tie to the incoming side. No removed verdict wrote it. Not fixed here: a merge tie-break that reads the merged plan is its own design. Filed as T495; lands before T484.
- the ARCHIVE then left the block behind (`rust/gate/crates/plan/src/plan/task.rs`, `archivable`): T475's heading names 451 T451, a ticked task with no section of its own, so T451's "section" was T475's heading block alone. It was taken first, and T475's whole section, starting at the same byte, was skipped as inside it. The orphan `### T475 Approach`, judged alone by the stale entry, refused the ticks of T479, T481 and T310 (the log `land-b9b.log`; the guard log's eleven refusals at 11:29Z and 11:36Z, observed 2026-11-27, method: `~/.claude/guard-log` read for `T475 Approach`). `make plan-delta`, run before the landing, saw T475's section current under its task verdict. Fixed here: a section is skipped only where it lies wholly inside a taken one.
- the brief's literal case (`record.rs`, `record_blocks`): a CLEAR on `(removed) <key>` deleted that key's entry even where plan.md still holds a block of that key. It did not fire tonight but would erase a live block's verdict. Fixed here: the entry is removed only where the plan holds no such block.
- the readers' remaining difference (`status.rs`): `make plan-delta` owed a `(removed)` block that a task's CLEAR verdict answers for, which no tick owes; bb51ce5d2c was a review round spent on `(removed) ### T475 (<why: ...>)`. Fixed here: `status::delta_keys` reads plan-delta's keys through the tick's own `in_scope` with every task in scope, and `plan.rs`'s `plan_delta` asks it.

| step | alone off: fixed and pinned | fresh block vs HEAD | pool manifests moved | the last resort |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| the archive takes a task's whole section | `task::tests::a_heading_that_names_a_ticked_task_leaves_none_of_its_own_section_behind` | n/a | none | `make plan-delta` and a review of the orphan |
| a removal keeps a live block's verdict | `record::tests::a_block_review_names_each_block_and_a_removal_leaves_the_record` | n/a | none | a review of the live block |
| plan-delta asks the tick's question | `status::tests::plan_delta_and_a_tick_owe_a_removed_stub_block_alike` | n/a | none | a review of the removed block |

### T486 (451 T485's keys were a pool tree's stale store of rendered guard messages, not a wording HEAD renders)

- **Approach**: a warm handout (`make builder-tree`'s take, `rust/gate/crates/task/src/builder_tree.rs`) empties the tree's `<git dir>/hooks-test/messages` once the tree is at the clone's HEAD, so `make guard-messages` there reads only what this HEAD's suites render. ### T491 (451 T388: pair-hooks spent 50 of its 92 ms on every Agent call reading the feature's whole 50 MB event log for its first line, measured 2026-11-27 (T388's sandbox arms), to answer "not due" for a step-back switched off since 2026-10-21)

- **Approach**: two changes in the gate's `reviews` crate. Measured 2026-11-27.
  - **T491-D1, `due` asks the switch first.** `checkpoint.rs` `due` reads `suspended(root)` before `state_in`. With the switch off it skips `state_in` and goes down the not-due branch: no event log read, no reopening walk, no `git log`. That branch still writes the `checkpoint-admitted` mark for an Agent call, as before. The check goes in `due` only, not in `state_in`. `status` prints `state_in`'s map, and `open_checkpoint`'s off-switch message reads it, so both stay as they were. `hold_in` also reads `state_in` while off and returns "". It runs once per `make tick`, not on every Agent call, so it is left as it is.
  - **T491-D2, `first_event` reads line by line up to its first event.** `glyph.rs` `first_event` uses a `BufReader` and `read_until(b'\n')` in place of `read_to_string` on the whole log. The find rule is unchanged: the answer is the first line that does not parse (a blank line counts) or that is not an `ASIDE` line. A line that does not parse gives None, as before. A file that cannot be opened or read gives None, as before. One answer changes: bytes that are not UTF-8 *after* the first event used to make the whole read fail (None). They now leave the start as read. That is a corrupt log's tail, and the start was always the first event's.
  - **Red first.** Two tests failed on the old code (0 passed, 2 failed), measured 2026-11-27 (`make rust-test ONLY=` on the two tests before the fix): `glyph::tests::the_start_reads_the_log_only_to_its_first_event` (a log whose third line is not UTF-8: `left: None, right: Some(60.0)`) and `checkpoint::tests::an_off_switch_answers_not_due_without_reading_the_start` (with the switch off and a commit to `specs/900-x`, the old `due` wrote the reopening into the clock: `assertion failed: !...CLOCK.exists()`). Both pass after the change. The crate's 216 tests pass, measured 2026-11-27 (`make builder-checks`).
  - **Before and after, on T388's sandbox.** Method: `t388-time.py` copied as `t491-time.py`, with `T491_BIN` and `T491_GATE` aiming it at copies of this tree's own guard and gate binaries built before and after the change. The arm is `gp.PreToolUse:only=pair`, 20 runs after a warm-up, measured 2026-11-27 (t491-time.py). Results, median / 90th centile, measured 2026-11-27 (t491-time.py on T388's sandbox, 20 runs): before 84.7 / 119.1 ms (load 8.8 to 10.0), after 33.5 / 37.0 (load 12.4 to 13.1). Run again, measured 2026-11-27 (t491-time.py on T388's sandbox, 20 runs): before 88.1 / 94.7 (load 11.9 to 12.4), after 31.5 / 36.2 (load 11.1 to 11.9). That is about 53 ms off every Agent call, a little more than T388's 50 (its `+shortlog` arm still read 2,000 lines), measured 2026-11-27 (the medians above). About 296 x 0.053 = 16 s a day, measured 2026-11-27 (T388's count of 2026-11-26's Agent calls times the saving above).

### T489 (found by 451 T387: a running plan hold past its knob `HOLD_MAX_S` (1800 s, a GUESS) is never purged - `planhold::purge` drops only pending holds - so a review whose return never came keeps `plan_holds` non-empty, every Bash call of the clone loading the 3.0 MB state, and its held text refused without `PLAN_EDIT_OK`)

- **Approach**: `planhold::purge` (`rust/guard/shared/src/checks/planhold.rs`) drops every dead hold - a pending one past `PENDING_S`, as before, and now a running one past `HOLD_MAX_S` (`dead`). It runs in `snapshot`, at a call's `PreToolUse` whenever `plan_holds` is non-empty, and `handle` saves the state where the hold part moved (451 T387), so the first call after the limit purges and saves once, and `record_edit_gate`'s prefilter (`plan_holds` empty) sends every later call past the load.
  - **It puts back nothing it does not own.** `prune_snaps` drops the purged hold's kept text with it, so a call begun under the hold and ending after the purge finds no kept text and writes nothing back; a call-keyed snapshot of an older build (T387-D2) is skipped for a hold gone (`restore` asks `plan_holds`). Said where it is purged: `purge`'s doc comment, and the escape column of `docs/guards.md`'s `record_edit_hooks.rs` row.
  - **A late return is harmless.** The review's `SubagentStop` names no hold or dispatch, so `handle::concerns` books nothing and nothing is saved; `planhold::returned` would drop nothing. Its verdict is still checked by `make plan-verdict`, which refuses a section changed while it was reviewed.
  - **The figures.** A Bash `true`'s `record-edit-hooks` `PreToolUse` with a running hold taken 4,000 s ago, CPU median of 20 interleaved, on a copy of the clone's state (2,994,673 bytes): 7.8 ms after against 95.4 ms on the clone's build from before 451 T387, its `checks-hooks` `PostToolUse` 5.4 against 6.8, state writes 0 of 20 against 20 of 20, measured 2026-11-27 (`dev/measurements/2026-11-27/t489-dead-hold/t489-time.py`, `results.txt`). A build with T387 and not T489 was not timed (no worktree for it); T387's own figure for a Bash call under a hold is 42.6 + 38.2 ms, measured 2026-11-27 (`t387-time.py`).
  - **Red first**, 2026-11-27 (`make rust-test CRATE=rust/guard/shared ONLY="checks::handle::hold_writes"`, the test only added): `a_running_hold_past_its_limit_is_purged` failed, 5 passed of 6 (`plan_holds` still holding the hold). Green after: 6 of 6; `planhold/tests.rs`'s `a_hold_is_live_or_dead_by_its_age` now pins the running hold's purge, and `a_snapshot_is_written_back_when_held_text_changes` checks its kept-once case at a call inside the limit, where it read one far past it.

**T489-D1 - Held text is editable without `PLAN_EDIT_OK` once its hold is past `HOLD_MAX_S`.** The task line: "a purge changes that refusal and needs its own ruling"; the brief: purge it. A review returns well inside the limit (`HOLD_MAX_S`'s own comment), and past it its hold already counted as dead and `PLAN_EDIT_OK` passed it, so the purge drops only the token's ceremony. What still guards a review that is merely late: `make plan-verdict` refuses a verdict on a section changed while it was reviewed. Chosen by the builder on the brief.

### T488 (found by 451 T387: a check-wave dispatch never applies its reading marks - `rounds::pair_wave` sets a wave row running without `apply_marks`, which only `rounds::launched` calls; 362 of the clone's 3,054 dispatches carried unapplied marks, observed 2026-11-27, method: counting rows with `marks` by `wave` and `state` in the clone's state)

- **Approach**: `rounds::pair_wave` (`rust/guard/shared/src/checks/rounds.rs`), on pairing a wave agent, applies the reading marks - the fresh round's edits reset, the seen sentences, the notes read - of every row of the agent's `check-wave` run still carrying them (`same_run`: `wave:<run>:<tag>`), once; where a dispatch outside the run has returned on a fresh subject, the reset keeps the blocks that dispatch's kept reply holds and drops the rest (`outside_edits`). `rounds::returned` now also drops `marks` from a rounded row (T387's prune, which left it while this task was open).
  - **Why the run, at its first return** (T488-D1). No `PostToolUse` launches a wave row - the Workflow replays each unit's `PreToolUse` and the agent is paired at its `SubagentStop` - so the pairing is the wave's launch. Applied per row at its own return, a fresh row returning after a sibling of its run had recorded its EDIT blocks on the same subject reset them, and the freeze (`freeze::edit_refusal`) then refuses the session's applying of that sibling's block: two units of one quote-check wave on one page, split by notes, are the shape.
  - **Why not across runs** (T488-D2). The same reset at a run's first return would empty `edits[s]` that a check outside the run (record-format on the same `q:` page, the shape the wave units' `q:` pages pair, observed 2026-11-27, method: a Python read of the clone's `checks-open.json`, `dev/measurements/2026-11-27/t488-wave-marks/wave-units.txt`) recorded since the wave's dispatch, and the freeze would then refuse the applying of that check's blocks; where one has returned unanswered on the subject, the reset keeps the blocks its kept reply holds (`reply::blocks` of `reply::reply_file`, the reply `rounds::returned` keeps for every reply it records edits from) and drops the earlier round's.
  - **What the 362 rows become** (observed 2026-11-27, method: as above). Their own counts do not move: a row's `counted` is fixed at its dispatch, observed 2026-11-27, method: reading `rounds::dispatch`. The unapplied marks only ever OVER-counted the next round: without `seen` or `notes_read`, `first_look` and `fresh_reading` are both false, so a later dispatch read as a repeat - early cap trips, never missed ones. The rows touch 27 units (13 modal-depiction pop-ups, 7 quote-check and 7 record-format questions), 37 runs from 2026-10-19 to 2026-11-22, observed 2026-11-27, method: a Python read of the clone's `checks-open.json`, `dev/measurements/2026-11-27/t488-wave-marks/wave-units.txt`; `rounds` holds none of the 27 today, so no live count moves. 341 of the 362 are rounded, and the next return drops their marks unapplied (applying a month-old reading now would be wrong); 21 never rounded keep theirs, inert. Observed 2026-11-27 on the clone's state (`dev/measurements/2026-11-27/t488-wave-marks/wave-units.txt`, a Python read of the clone's `checks-open.json`).
  - **Did a past ruling read a wrong count?** Of the 15 arbiter rulings in `specs/*/arbiter.jsonl` on round triggers of the 27 units, 14 (2026-10-10 to 10-12) precede every wave row the state holds (its earliest dispatch 2026-10-10 21:08, its first wave row 2026-10-19), so read no wave's miscount. The 15th, `round:quote-check|q:0004@3` (449, 2026-11-22, `accept`), is the footnote-flag trip of `fixloop::hold` (a footnote flagged in rounds in a row, counted from replies), not the round cap: only its `@3` comes from the count. `arbiter-owed.json` holds no `round:` trigger. The `first_look` side is not replayed here: it would need each round's page text rebuilt from git history, and the one ruling in range is the footnote trip.
  - **Red first**, 2026-11-27 (`make rust-test CRATE=rust/guard/shared ONLY="checks::rounds"`, the test only added): `a_wave_applies_its_reading_marks_once_for_its_run` failed, 19 passed of 20 (the fresh round's edits left at the pairing). Green after with the outside-run case added: 20 of 20; `make builder-checks CRATE="rust/guard/shared rust/guard"` 584 and 595 passed, lint and format clean; the hook suites checks-hooks 22, record-edit-gate 9, record-edit-hooks 14 passed.

**T488-D1 - A wave's marks are applied for its whole run at its first return.** The brief: "apply them as the single dispatch's return does". A single dispatch applies them at its launch, before any return of its round records edits; a wave's only hooked moment per row is its return, so the run's marks are applied at the run's first, before any of its returns records edits. Rows of the run never paired (an agent with no return) have their `seen` and `read` applied anyway: the Workflow launched them. Chosen by the builder.

**T488-D2 - A fresh reset keeps another check's returned edits.** At a run's first return, on a subject where a dispatch outside the run has returned unanswered, `edits` is cut to the EDIT blocks that dispatch's kept reply holds: reset whole, the freeze would refuse the applying of that check's blocks, a guard firing on correct work; left whole, an earlier round's edits would stay listed, which the fresh round is to drop. A block an earlier round proposed word for word again is kept, as the returned check proposed it too. Chosen by the builder.

### T495 (a carry's record merge gave a same-day tie to the pool tree's verdict on a stub over the clone's CLEAR on the filled block, 451 T487)

- **Approach**: the record's merge (`rust/gate/crates/plan/src/plan/merge.rs`) now takes the merged plan.md where it is known: where the two sides' entries for a key differ and the plan holds one's digest for that key and not the other's (`blocks` by the block's `sha256`, `tasks` by the section's `section_sha256`, both from `sections::digests::of`), that entry wins; else the old rule, the later `reviewed` day, a tie theirs. The merged plan is known only to `make carry`: git's driver (`merge-record %O %A %B`) is given none, and mid-merge the work tree holds ours' plan.md and no `CHERRY_PICK_HEAD` exists (probed 2026-11-27, method: a scratch repo whose driver dumped its env, `.git` and the work tree's plan.md during a `git cherry-pick`, git 2.53.0). So the carry (`rust/gate/crates/land/src/land/carry.rs`) runs its pick with `-c merge.plan-review.driver=false`: a record both sides changed stops unmerged, and `resolve_all` merges it after the other paths, given its feature's plan.md as this pass resolved it by section, or as the pick wrote it where it merged clean. The clone's driver is what merged T310's carry (the clone's git config defines it; no landing log names the record among a carry's resolved files).

| step | alone off: fixed and pinned | fresh block vs HEAD | pool manifests moved | the last resort |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| the merge prefers the entry on the text the plan holds | `merge::tests::the_entry_whose_digest_the_merged_plan_holds_wins_a_same_day_tie` (and the mirror), `where_the_plan_holds_neither_or_both_the_newer_wins_a_tie_theirs` | n/a | none | a review of the block again |
| the carry merges the record in process, beside the merged plan | `carry::tests::record::a_carry_keeps_the_verdict_on_the_text_the_merged_plan_holds`, `a_plan_both_sides_changed_is_merged_first_and_its_text_decides_the_record` | n/a | none | a review of the block again |

It then asks `plan_cap_held(root, dir, task, doc)` for each task, lazily, in the order the dispatch names them. ### T494 (451 T388: a guard's gate call paid the gate launcher's 17.5 ms source walk on every call, and review-round and check-bundle a 2.5 ms `/usr/bin/env` start, about 460 calls a day, measured 2026-11-27 (T388's sandbox arms))

- **Approach**: one helper, `tool::ask_gate` (`rust/guard/shared/src/tool.rs`), which pair-hooks (`pair_hooks.rs` `gate`, through `reviews` and `review.rs` `decided`), review-round-hooks (`active_task`, `later_round`'s stale-terms call) and check-bundle-hooks (`decide_first`) now call. Measured 2026-11-27.
  - **T494-D1, the launcher run by `bash`, not by its shebang.** `ask_gate` starts `bash <script> <args>`, as pair-hooks already did and as 451 T456 did for `l7r-hook`. A script that cannot start now answers bash's 127 where the exec answered -1. Every caller reads only exit 0 (`active_task`), exit 1 with output (`decide_first`) or the output (`stale-dirs`, the checkpoint), so 127 holds nothing, as -1 did.
  - **T494-D2, the freshness signal: an earlier call through the same launcher, in the same hook process, exited 0.** After such a call to a plain subcommand, the later calls pass `L7R_GATE_FRESH=<the binary>`, 449 T205's seam, and the launcher skips `stale()`. Exit 0 means the launcher ran its binary, so that binary was fresh then or had just been built. Every way its build can fail exits 1 before the `exec`. The two ways it runs a stale binary anyway (`L7R_GATE_STALE_OK`, or an `L7R_GATE_FRESH` already exported) hold for the later call too, because that call runs under the same environment. So the guard may know the binary is fresh only under three conditions: the same launcher path, the same process, and a plain subcommand. A variant (`rust`, `browser`, `embed`, `mode-a`, `hamlet`) runs another binary built from other sources, so it neither proves freshness nor uses the proof. A failed call proves nothing, and an `L7R_GATE_FRESH` the process already exports is left as it is. The proof lives in a thread-local and lasts one hook process, tens of ms. A source edited inside that window is missed by the later call, as it would be by a call started that much earlier. The launcher still checks that the variable names its own binary and that the binary is executable. A wrong name here only walks as before, so no stale gate can run where it would not have run already. The binary is named as the launcher names it: `${L7R_GATE_TARGET:-<the account's home in /etc/passwd>/.cache/l7r-cargo-target/<the tree's name>}/tool/l7r-gate`, with no name for a launcher given by a relative path. `the_gate_binary_named_is_the_one_the_launcher_runs` pins that name: against the real launcher's `L7R_GATE_PRINT_FRESH=1` answer under a target, and against its own text for the default.
  - **T494-D3, priced and declined: the guard launcher's walk, and an in-process walk.** `l7r-guard.sh`'s walk covers `rust/guard`, `rust/Cargo.toml`, `rust/Cargo.lock` and `.cargo/config.toml` against `l7r-guard.good`. It does not cover `rust/gate`, and it is not compared against the gate's binary, so it cannot stand for any part of the gate's walk. The gate's walk covers 1,859 paths over `rust/gate`, `rust/guard` and those files, measured 2026-11-27 (`t494-walk.py`'s count on T388's sandbox). An in-process walk would be the same check without the fork, but the stats are its cost: a Python `lstat` walk of the 1,859 paths took 111.6 ms median against `find`'s 51.4, 20 runs at load 22, measured 2026-11-27 (`t494-walk.py`). A kept stamp stays declined, for `l7r-guard.sh`'s 451 T439 reason. What would reopen it: a walk that costs less than the fork, measured. So pair-hooks' own first call on every Agent call still walks, 296 x 17.5 ms = 5 s a day, measured 2026-11-27 (T388's count of 2026-11-26's Agent calls times its walk).
  - **Red first.** The helper is new, so its tests are new; there was no old code to fail. `a_gate_call_after_one_that_exited_0_skips_the_launcher_s_walk` uses a stub launcher that prints the `L7R_GATE_FRESH` it was given. A first call is given none. The call after a call that exited 0 is given the binary. A call after a failed call, a variant, another launcher and an exported variable are given none. A script that cannot start answers 127. The guard's 598 tests pass, and `make builder-checks CRATE="rust/guard rust/guard/shared"` is green, measured 2026-11-27 (`make builder-checks`). The suites passed, measured 2026-11-27 (each run by `bash tests/hooks/test-<guard>.sh`): review-round 91 passed, pair 104 passed, check-bundle 38 passed, none failed.
  - **Before and after, on T388's sandbox.** The method is T491's `t491-time.py`, copied as `t494-time.py`. Two arms were added to it, `binafter` and `onlyafter`, so the before binary and the after binary run interleaved in the same rounds. Both binaries are this tree's own, with T497 in, copied before and after this change. The gate is T491's after copy, checked fresh against the sandbox's sources with `L7R_GATE_PRINT_FRESH=1`. Each arm ran 20 times after a warm-up, every run exiting 0, measured 2026-11-27 (`t494-pair1.tsv`, `t494-pair2.tsv`). Medians, before -> after, run 1 at load 11.1 to 19.2, run 2 at load 15.0 to 18.2:
    - a plan review's whole PreToolUse (`sf`, every guard): 210.9 -> 181.6 ms, and 246.3 -> 214.0, measured 2026-11-27 (`t494-time.py`, 20 runs);
    - a record check's (`rf`): 308.4 -> 295.6 ms, and 369.5 -> 306.6, measured 2026-11-27 (`t494-time.py`, 20 runs);
    - review-round alone (`--only`, the bash start alone, with no earlier call to ride): 62.5 -> 56.2 ms, and 59.8 -> 56.3, measured 2026-11-27 (`t494-time.py`, 20 runs).
  - **The walks counted.** A logging `find` was put first on `PATH`, because ptrace is refused in the container. One hook call, measured 2026-11-27 (`t494-find.log`): a plan review's launcher walks went 2 -> 1, a record check's 2 -> 1, and a builder's brief's stayed 1 -> 1.
  - **The day.** About 98 x 0.030 + 65 x 0.0175 = 4 s, measured 2026-11-27 (T388's count of 2026-11-26's plan reviews and record checks, times the medians' saving above, with the walk's 17.5 ms standing for the noisier record-check pair). That is half of T388's 8 s, measured 2026-11-27 (T388's record): pair-hooks' own walk stays (D3).

### T490 (451 T387: every hook that read `checks-open.json` parsed the whole 3.0 MB state, 36 to 43 ms of CPU, while the hot calls read none of its 2.29 MB of `dispatches` or 0.51 MB of `versions`, measured 2026-11-27 (`t387-time.py`, 20 runs))

- **Approach**: route (b), the hot hooks read the state in part. `checks::handle` reads the state through `handle/part.rs`'s `Part`, not `load`. Measured 2026-11-27 (`dev/measurements/2026-11-27/t490-part-read/`).
  - **T490-D1, the routes priced; (b) built.** Each route's ceiling was measured on the before binary, with one copy of the clone's state stripped. Bash `true` PreToolUse under a hold, CPU median, measured 2026-11-27 (`t490-time.py`, 20 runs, load 10 to 12, `t490-pricing2.txt`):
    - (a) moves settled rows to a second file. Its ceiling is the `dispatches`-dropped arm: 34.2 to 10.9 ms, measured 2026-11-27 (`t490-time.py`, 20 runs, `t490-pricing2.txt`).
    - (c) prunes old versions. Its ceiling is the `versions`-dropped arm: 37.4 to 32.9 ms, measured 2026-11-27 (`t490-time.py`, 20 runs, `t490-pricing2.txt`). It also changes an answer, because `versions()` already keeps 12 a subject and `oscillation` reads that history, so pruning moves the reversal tripwire.
    - (b) the partial read: 37.1 to 18.4 ms, measured 2026-11-27 (`t490-time.py`, 20 runs, `t490-time-run1.txt`; below).

    (a) saves about 7 ms a hook more than (b), measured 2026-11-27 (the two arms above, at different loads). Its price is the file's contract. The state lives in the clone's common git dir, which every pool tree shares (`planhold.rs`'s header, `state_path`), and each tree runs a guard and a gate built from its own sources (`l7r-guard.sh`'s `$TARGET`). So a tree not yet at the new HEAD would read a state with its settled rows gone and answer differently, in `settled.rs`, the earlier-rounds bundle and cascade's count. It would also need eight cold readers taught to read two files (observed 2026-11-27, method: T387's reader table). (b) changes no file and no cold reader.
  - **T490-D2, what is read in part, and when the rest is parsed.** `Part::read` parses every top-level key but `dispatches`, `versions` and `seen` as values. Those three are scanned, never made values. For a launch or a return it also keeps each dispatch's `aid`, `state` and the truth of its `wave` and `reply` (`Row`), which `concerns` reads. `Part::whole` parses the three from the same text the moment a call reads a row or saves:
    - every `save` and `keep_trips` in `handle` takes `st.whole()`;
    - a counted check's dispatch, and spec-fidelity's hold;
    - the freeze, on an `apply-edits` command (`APPLY` names that word) or on an Edit, Write or MultiEdit of a path with a subject (`subject_of_path`);
    - a booked launch or return.

    The calls before `whole` change only other keys (the hold's snapshot and restore, the feature switch, `switch_feature` split out), so the merged state is the whole parse plus the call's changes, and `save`'s bytes are the old ones by construction. `load` is unchanged, and every cold caller keeps it (`close`, `drop_run`, `record_answer`, the gate).
  - **T490-D3, every text reads as the whole parse.** The scan is a visitor (`Skip`) that parses every token through `deserialize_any`, as `Value` does, not `IgnoredAny`'s scan, which takes a number past f64 (451 T493's `1e400`). So a text it takes is one the whole parse takes. A text the partial read cannot take falls back to the whole parse at once: not JSON, an empty file, a non-object at the top, `dispatches` or a row that is not an object, or trailing bytes. A duplicate key keeps the last, as `Value` does. The cheaper scan is priced and left: Filed as T506 (below).
  - **Red first.** `handle/hold_writes.rs` `a_call_that_reads_no_row_parses_no_row` failed on the old code: 1 failed of 8, `left: 5, right: 0`. Its five calls were a Bash call under a hold, its end, an Explore's dispatch, its launch and its return, measured 2026-11-27 (`make rust-test CRATE=rust/guard/shared ONLY="checks::handle::hold_writes"`, counting `checks::parsed`'s whole parses on the thread). Green after. `handle/part/tests.rs` holds three more tests:
    - each row truth is `!falsy`, over 19 JSON values;
    - 14 shapes read as the whole parse, both with and without rows: not JSON, empty, `[]`, `1`, trailing bytes, a non-object `dispatches` and row, `1e400` in a skipped row and in `versions`, a lone surrogate in `seen`, and duplicate keys at three levels;
    - every hook mode answers and saves byte for byte as a forced whole read (`WHOLE`), over 13 calls on a state with a running check, a pending row, a waiting wave row and a hold, and again on a state that is not JSON.

    `make builder-checks CRATE="rust/guard/shared rust/guard"` is clean: 593 and 598 tests passed, measured 2026-11-27 (`make builder-checks`).
  - **Every answer unchanged, on a copy of the clone's state.** `t490-diff.py` ran 15 calls on each binary's own copy and compared the exit code, stdout, stderr and the state's bytes after every call: 15 of 15 the same, and 15 of 15 on a state that is not JSON, measured 2026-11-27 (`t490-diff.txt`). The calls were a hold's first call (its save) and end, a steady one, a frozen page's Edit, the held plan's Edit, an `apply-edits`, an Explore's dispatch, launch and return, a pending dispatch launched, a running check's return, the hold's review's return, a TaskStop and a quote-check's dispatch. The state's bytes are the same after every call, so every cold reader of T387's table reads what it read. Its code is unchanged too.
  - **Before and after**, CPU median ms, run 1 then run 2, measured 2026-11-27 (`t490-time.py`, 20 interleaved runs, load 3.2 to 4.8 and 4.5 to 4.7):
    - a Bash `true` under a hold, PreToolUse (record-edit-hooks): 37.1 -> 18.4, and 38.3 -> 19.5;
    - its PostToolUse (checks-hooks): 32.7 -> 15.0, and 31.9 -> 15.7;
    - a non-check Agent's PostToolUse (checks-hooks): 45.9 -> 29.6, and 46.2 -> 29.1;
    - that Agent's PreToolUse (check-bundle-hooks): 28.7 -> 10.2, and 29.4 -> 10.1.

    A Bash call under a hold pays both hooks: about 70 to 34 ms, measured 2026-11-27 (the two rows above summed). Each Agent call pays about 35 ms less over its two hooks, so about 296 x 0.035 = 10 s a day, measured 2026-11-27 (T388's count of 2026-11-26's Agent calls times the saving above). The SubagentStop arm did not move (93.7 -> 92.0), because every return there is booked and saved: Filed as T505 (below).

The cause is 14 check-wave rows that are `returned` with no reply, 861 to 863 hours old, which `concerns` takes as a wave still waiting to be paired (observed 2026-11-27, method: counting with Python's `json` the rows of a copy of the clone's state that `concerns`' wave test holds). Not fixed here: it is an age limit on a waiting wave row, or a save only where a booking changed a row, which is a change to the rounds' rules beyond this brief. Filed as T505; lands before T302.

  - **T504-D1, the three callers moved, each answer unchanged (observed 2026-11-27, method: the grep below).** `engine_freeze_hooks.rs` asks `plan engine-edit` through `ask_gate`, from `/` with the question on stdin as before. `pair_hooks/state.rs` `stamp_fresh` asks `stamp --fresh diagram` through `ask_gate`, from the clone as before. `builder_stop_hooks.rs` asks `plan decided` through `ask_gate_within` with its `ASK_LIMIT` (40 s, a GUESS knob), from the builder's tree as before. Each already ran by `bash` and reads only `.ok()`, or the code and `.out`, so a launcher that cannot start answers nothing new (T494-D1's reasoning). Each subcommand is plain (`plan`, `stamp`), so an exit 0 proves the binary ran (T494-D2) and is now proof for the calls after it. A subcommand that exits 1 to say "no", as `stamp --fresh` does for a stale stamp, proves nothing and walks as before. The proof is keyed on the launcher's path. In a session clone the guard tree is the clone, so engine-freeze's launcher is the one gate-write's `preflight` asks. For the builder-stop and pair guards it is the launcher of the tree or clone they ask.
  - **The search that found the set.** `grep -rn "l7r-gate.sh"` over the non-test files of `rust/guard/src` and `rust/guard/shared/src`, run 2026-11-27, with `"bash"` searched over the same files as a cross-check. After this task, every hit that starts the launcher goes through the shared asker: `pair_hooks.rs` `gate`, `review_round_hooks.rs` (twice), `check_bundle_hooks.rs`, `record_edit_hooks.rs`, `measure_hooks.rs`, `gate_write_hooks.rs`, `clone_sync_hooks.rs` (twice), `ledger_hooks.rs` (its `Ctx::gate` path, given to `ask_gate`), and the three moved here. The other hits start nothing. They are the stale-suite list in `suite_tools/deps.rs`, the `own-make` command written into a no-poll message, and comments in `make_only_hooks.rs`, `scratch_sweep_hooks/sweep/cargo.rs`, `shared/src/make.rs`, `builder_pool.rs` and `event_log_hooks.rs`. `tool.rs` is the asker itself. The other `"bash"` starts are not the gate: `finished_run_hooks/runs.rs` runs `writer-alive.sh` and `shell_check_hooks.rs` runs bash's own parse. Nothing is left.
  - **Red first.** There are three new tests. Each is handed `L7R_GATE_FRESH` after an earlier call through the same launcher exited 0, and on the old code each fails at its last assertion: 0 passed, 3 failed, measured 2026-11-27 (`make rust-test CRATE=rust/guard ONLY=...`). They are `the_engine_edit_question_rides_an_earlier_fresh_gate_call`, `the_stamp_rides_an_earlier_fresh_gate_call` and `the_decided_question_rides_an_earlier_fresh_gate_call`. Each stub answers yes only when it is given the proof. Each test first asserts the answer with no proof, so it also pins the call as it was before. The brief's other red test, a launcher with no shebang and no exec bit, cannot be red here. All three already ran by `bash`, and their existing stubs are written with no shebang and no exec bit (`engine_freeze_hooks/tests.rs` `world`, `builder_stop_hooks/tests.rs` `the_hook_blocks_the_stop_through_the_gate_script`, `pair_hooks/state/tests.rs` `a_green_gate_is_the_stamp_else_the_recorded_key`), so that start stays pinned by the tests already there. `make builder-checks CRATE="rust/guard rust/guard/shared"` is green: guard 606 passed, measured 2026-11-27. The three suites passed, measured 2026-11-27 (`bash tests/hooks/test-<guard>.sh`): engine-freeze 41, pair 104, builder-stop 7, none failed. No guard message changed.
  - **One Edit hook, before and after, on T388's sandbox.** The method is `t504-time.py`, which uses T500's environment with the guard tree set to the sandbox clone, as a session clone's hooks run. The hook is the whole `l7r-guard PreToolUse` on an Edit of `rust/guard/src/lib.rs` while a glyph-check review is live, so engine-freeze asks `plan engine-edit` (exit 0: refused). The binaries are this tree's own, copied before and after the change. Arms are interleaved round-robin after one uncounted warm-up. Each arm ran 20 times, and every run exited 2 (the refusal), measured 2026-11-27 (`t504-run1.tsv` to `t504-run3.tsv`). The load was high, 1-minute 19.8 to 24.6 across the three runs, from the other builders, measured 2026-11-27 (`/proc/loadavg`, the runs' own lines).
    - With a `make done` standing in the clone (`exec -a "make done" sleep`), gate-write asks `preflight` after engine-freeze. The `find` shim on `PATH` (`t504-trace.sh`) counts 2 launcher walks before and 1 after, measured 2026-11-27 (one run each). The second call's walk is ridden. Medians went 281.9 -> 276.9, 269.2 -> 246.7 and 225.8 -> 212.2 ms, measured 2026-11-27 (`t504-time.py`, 20 runs). Minima went 233.3 -> 201.9, 203.7 -> 174.3 and 206.2 -> 187.2 ms, measured 2026-11-27 (`t504-time.py`, 20 runs).
    - The control, with no `make done`, makes one gate call and has nothing to ride. The shim counts 1 walk in each binary. Medians went 217.0 -> 233.3, 194.2 -> 224.4 and 166.6 -> 175.7 ms, measured 2026-11-27 (`t504-time.py`, 20 runs). Minima went 161.4 -> 155.2, 153.8 -> 161.5 and 153.2 -> 144.2 ms, measured 2026-11-27 (`t504-time.py`, 20 runs).
    - At this load the medians cannot resolve a 17.5 ms walk: the control's medians moved 9 to 30 ms with no change in its work, measured 2026-11-27 (`t504-time.py`, 20 runs). The saving rests on the walk count (2 -> 1) and on T494's measure of one walk, 17.5 ms, measured 2026-11-27 (`t504-trace.sh`; T494's record). The minima agree with it: the gate arm's fell 19 to 31 ms, and the control's moved -9 to +8 ms, measured 2026-11-27 (`t504-time.py`, 20 runs).
  - **Where it saves.** In an Edit hook the save needs engine-freeze's call to exit 0 before a later call through the same launcher. Engine-freeze runs before gate-write (`lib.rs`'s order), and exits 0 only on an engine edit under a live review or roll. That is the edit it refuses, and `preflight` follows it while a gate runs. `record edit-route` asks only for a record or plan file, which `plan engine-edit` does not call engine code, so it never follows an exit-0 engine-edit call. A SubagentStop's `plan decided` rides only an earlier exit-0 call through the same tree's launcher in that hook process, and its own exit 0 now serves a later one; neither was measured here. The pair guard's `stamp_fresh` shares its walk with the pair guard's own `gate` calls when the guard tree is the clone. That is why this task claims a walk saved only on the Edit path measured.

### T504 Approach (checklist part A)

1. **The goal, in the world.** No guard starts the gate launcher outside the shared asker. Each guard's call shares the hook process's freshness proof, and its own exit 0 proves the binary fresh for the calls after it.
2. **The constraints.** No guard message or verdict changes (the brief). A stale gate binary is never run where the launcher would not run it already (T494-D2). A caller's reading of a failed start does not change (T494-D1).
3. **Where each comes from.** O: 451 T500's found-and-left item and T494's walk, 17.5 ms a call, measured 2026-11-27 (T494's record). R: `rust/guard/shared/src/tool.rs` (`ask_gate`, `ask_gate_within`). O: the timings and walk counts above.
4. **Do they describe the world here?** Yes. In the sandbox the measured Edit reached engine-freeze's gate call, every run exiting 2 with its refusal, and gate-write's `preflight` in the gate arm, as the shim's second walk before the change shows, measured 2026-11-27 (`t504-time.py`, `t504-trace.sh`).
5. **The order.** After T494 (the asker) and T500 (`ask_gate_within`). Before T501.
6. **The exits.** Green: the three red tests pass, the suites pass, and the walk count drops. Red: what failed recorded and the task set down, a claim that it cannot be done ruled through `make arbiter-ask`.
7. **The search smell.** None.
8. **The budget.** One landing.
9. **Done, measured.** The Edit hook with a gate running walks the launcher once where it walked twice, measured 2026-11-27 (`t504-trace.sh`). Its minimum fell 19 to 31 ms over three runs of 20 at load 20 to 25, measured 2026-11-27 (`t504-time.py`). The grep finds no launcher start left outside the asker.
10. **Before moving a constant.** n/a.
11. **Before fitting things into room.** n/a.
12. **Before any fix.** Nothing a reader sees: every verdict and message is unchanged.

**Found and left?** none.

**Performance work?** yes: it takes a launcher walk, 17.5 ms measured 2026-11-27 (T494's record), off a gate call that follows an exit-0 engine-edit, builder-stop or stamp call in the same hook process. That includes an engine Edit refused under a live review while a gate runs, which walks once where it walked twice, measured 2026-11-27 (`t504-trace.sh`).

### T470 (found by 451 T463: its line asked for libtest's per-test times on a slow test run beside the live record, not built there because whether the words move cargo's fingerprint was unmeasured)

- **Approach**: a crate's built test binary, run directly (`side.rs`'s `run_built`), is given libtest's per-test times as its words: `-Z unstable-options --report-time` in place of `-q`, under `RUSTC_BOOTSTRAP=1` in the binary's environment (`alive::TIMES`). libtest then prints the pretty format, a `test <name> ... ok <time>` line a test, observed 2026-11-27, method: this crate's built binary run with those words. `alive::split` takes those lines out of the binary's stdout, so the checks read what `-q` left them: the `running` and `test result:` lines and a failure's output. Where that binary ran past its bound and its record was written, `alive::times` puts the lines on the end of the record, slowest first (an untimed line, an ignored test, last), cut at `CAP`, T463's GUESS knob. A run inside its bound writes nothing new, and no file is added to `alive/`, so `KEEP` still counts records. The crate's `cargo test` (`tested`) is not given them. With `RUSTC_BOOTSTRAP=1` in cargo's environment, a scratch crate over thiserror 2.0.21 rebuilt proc-macro2, thiserror, quote, syn and thiserror-impl ("the env variable RUSTC_BOOTSTRAP changed"), and its next plain run rebuilt thiserror and the crate again, measured 2026-11-27 (`cargo test --no-run -v`, three runs). The rustc crate itself stayed Fresh, 22 units, 0.56 s, with that variable, measured 2026-11-27 (`cargo test --no-run -v` in this tree's target). The difference is that crate's graph: no proc-macro2. Only rust/mode_a builds proc-macro2 among the crates read (`cargo tree`, 2026-11-27, of the rustc, core, tree, pool, guard, shared and mode_a manifests). The test binaries' inherited variable reaches only what a test spawns, and no test under `rust/` runs cargo or make on a real target, observed 2026-11-27, method: grep of `rust/` for `Command::new("cargo")`, `Command::new("make")`, `l7r-gate.sh` and `var("CARGO")`. The one real cargo, `the_real_cargo_tests_a_real_crate`, builds in a scratch target. DEPARTURE from the line's literal `--format json`: `test_line`'s summary, `only::judge` and a red crate's shown output all read libtest's human stdout, which JSON would replace. Nor `--logfile` beside `-q`: libtest writes "`--logfile` is deprecated" to stderr on every run, observed 2026-11-27 (this crate's built binary, `od -c` of its stderr); without the variable libtest refuses `-Z`. Red first, measured 2026-11-27 (`make rust-test CRATE=rust/gate/crates/rustc ONLY=rustc::tests::alive`, `side.rs` at HEAD): 1 failed, 5 passed of 6, the new `a_caught_binary_s_per_test_times_end_its_record_slowest_first`. Green, measured 2026-11-27 (`make rust-test CRATE=rust/gate/crates/rustc`, run by the rebuilt `l7r-rust`, so its own binaries took the new words): 157 passed with T363's tests. The pins on a binary's words in `side.rs` and `only.rs` now name `-Z unstable-options --report-time` where they named `-q`.

### T363 (found by T340, 2026-11-26: rust/guard's stand-in sessions left nine `sleep 5` processes a run, which held the test phase's output pipe 3.1 s past the binary's exit, measured 2026-11-26 (T340, the binary by hand into a pipe), and nothing failed for it; T364 cut the wait and names a pipe's holder, failing nothing)

- **Approach**: the leak pin (`run.rs`'s `leak_checked`) also fails a crate whose tests left a process running, by name, and ends it, as it fails one that left a file. `rustc/left.rs` (new): every process the tests start inherits the run's own `TMPDIR`, a fresh directory of this run, wherever it is reparented once its parent exits. So after the run (`go`), `left::ended` reads `/proc` for each process but this one, alive and no zombie, whose `environ` holds exactly `TMPDIR=<the run's>` (`marked`). Where one is found it waits `GRACE`, 1 s, a GUESS knob (why beside it: slack for a child a test signalled and has not seen end; 1 s, not 100 ms, because a falsely red batch gate costs about ten minutes and an arbiter round and the load reached 37 on 2026-11-27, observed 2026-11-27, method: `uptime` in this tree; waited only where something was found, so a clean run pays nothing), and reads again. Each process found both times is named `pid N (its command line)`, sent SIGKILL, and the crate fails with the fix: kill and wait what a test starts, and a stand-in shell waits on its background process. It covers both paths, a built binary run directly and a crate's `cargo test`, and a doctest run, since all run inside `leak_checked`. WHY the environment, not a process group (the line's suggestion): `land`'s stop sends TERM to the process groups it holds (`land/stop.rs`'s `kill_group`), and a test run moved into a group of its own would escape it; a process started with a cleared environment escapes this check; the two under `rust/` (`pages/src/runner/work.rs`, `diffrun/src/run.rs`) are each waited on by the code that starts them, observed 2026-11-27, method: grep of `rust/` for `env_clear`, each site read. What T364 already names is kept: a holder of the output pipe is still cut at `DRAIN` and named on its `HELD` line, and is now red too, being a process the tests left. The pin adds the descendant that holds no pipe, which nothing named. Red first, measured 2026-11-27 (`make rust-test CRATE=rust/gate/crates/rustc ONLY="rustc::tests::left rustc::tests::drain"`, `run.rs` at HEAD): 2 failed, 6 passed of 8. They are the new `a_test_run_that_leaves_a_process_behind_fails_by_name_and_the_process_is_ended` (a stand-in `cargo test` leaves `sleep 46.7` with its output closed) and T364's holder test, now `a_crate_whose_run_left_a_holder_names_it_and_is_red`. The fake `/proc` test (a zombie, a process gone mid-read, a `TMPDIR` that only starts with the run's, this process, an entry that is no pid) and a run that waits on its child held already. Green, measured 2026-11-27 (`make rust-test CRATE=rust/gate/crates/rustc`): 157 passed. The motivating crate, rust/guard, run fresh through the new pin: 603 passed, nothing left, measured 2026-11-27 (`make rust-test CRATE=rust/guard FRESH=1`), so T340's fixes hold and the batch gate does not turn red there.

### T505 (451 T490: every SubagentStop booked and rewrote the whole 2.6 MB check state, 92 to 95 ms of CPU a stop and 22 of 22 writing, because 14 check-wave rows `returned` with no reply, 861 to 863 hours old, still counted as waiting for an agent, measured 2026-11-27 (`t490-time.py`'s agent-stop arm, 20 runs))

- **Approach**: a wave row waits for an agent only for `WAVE_WAIT_S` after its dispatch (`rust/guard/shared/src/checks/rounds.rs`, `wave_waits`). Both readers of the wait ask it: `handle::concerns`, which decides whether a return is booked, and `rounds::pair_wave`, which pairs a return with a row. `Row` (`handle/part.rs`) now keeps the row's `t` for `concerns`, read as `t_of` reads it. Measured 2026-11-27 (`dev/measurements/2026-11-27/t505-wave-wait/results.md`).
  - **T505-D1, the knob.** `WAVE_WAIT_S` is 6 hours, a GUESS knob labeled in its doc comment, as `HOLD_MAX_S` is (`make tunables` walks no tooling crate, by its own rule). It covers the 30-minute queue (`WAVE_PENDING_S`) plus the longest wave agent's run many times over: 585 s, the longest of 362 wave agents' wall cells, measured 2026-11-27 (`check-passes.jsonl` joined to the state's wave rows by agent id). It is timed from the dispatch (`t`), because a row keeps no return time. A pending wave row past it stops waiting too. A pending row's own liveness, `WAVE_PENDING_S` in `live`, is unchanged. Chosen by the builder, on the brief's "an age limit (as planhold's `HOLD_MAX_S`)".
  - **What a late reply loses.** An agent paired after the wait would have booked its row's reply, counted its round, and written its EDIT blocks into `edits` and `own_edits`. Past the wait it is treated as any agent no row names: none of that is booked, and nothing is saved. The row stays `returned` with no reply, as it stood before the late agent: `running` and `open_round` read it as they did. The wait is a wave's whole run, so only a unit retried hours later meets this. Said in `WAVE_WAIT_S`'s doc comment.
  - **Why the age and not a save only where a booking changed a row.** A save-only-on-change needs the whole parse to compare, the 55 ms clone and compare T387 replaced, measured 2026-11-27 (T387's `t387-time.py`). The age keeps a stop that concerns nothing from parsing any row (T490's `Part`).
  - **Red first.** `handle/hold_writes.rs` `a_wave_row_past_its_wait_is_not_booked` failed on the old code: 1 failed of 9, the state's inode moved (`left: 16393625, right: 16393621`), measured 2026-11-27 (`make rust-test CRATE=rust/guard/shared ONLY="checks::handle::hold_writes"`). Green after. Two tests were extended, observed 2026-11-27, method: this tree's diff. `a_return_concerns_a_wave_row_that_waits_for_its_reply` now pins a pending row and a reply-less row past the wait. `rounds/tests.rs`'s pairing test now pins a reply-less row past the wait left unpaired. `part/tests.rs` reads `t` over its 19 values. `make builder-checks CRATE="rust/guard/shared rust/guard"`: 595 and 606 passed, measured 2026-11-27.
  - **Before and after**, CPU median ms, the clone's guard at 495a852db9 against this tree, on a copy of the clone's state (2,618,222 bytes), measured 2026-11-27 (`t490-time.py`, 20 interleaved runs, load 4.4 to 4.6 and 2.5 to 2.6):

    - the other four cases (a Bash call's two hooks under a hold, an Agent's two): unchanged, within 2 ms, writes unchanged, measured 2026-11-27 (`t490-time.py`, 20 runs).

### T508 (451 T507, `dev/measurements/2026-11-27/t507-part-cost/results.md`: the Bash hooks' prefilters read the whole 2.6 MB check state to find one key on every Bash call, 4.83 ms of a no-hold `PreToolUse`'s 7.11 and 2.75 of a `PostToolUse`'s 4.72, measured 2026-11-27 (`t507-time.py`, 20 runs))

- **Approach**: both prefilters stream the state (`rust/guard/shared/src/checks/scan.rs`, new: `after_first`, `held_after`, `holds`, `snaps`). `record_edit_gate::holding` calls `checks::scan::holds`, and `checks_hooks::state_holds_snaps` calls `checks::scan::snaps`. The old `holds_text` is gone; its test oracle is kept in `checks/scan/tests.rs`. No guard message changed. The record is `dev/measurements/2026-11-27/t508-prefilter-stream/results.md`.
  - **T508-D1, the stream.** The file is read `CHUNK` (64 KiB, a GUESS knob: item 10) at a time into one reused buffer, and `memchr`'s `memmem` (a dependency of `rust/guard/shared` since 451 T392) searches the bytes. The last `needle.len() - 1` bytes are carried over, so a key cut by a chunk's edge is found whole on the next read. After `"plan_holds":`, the bytes are decoded to their UTF-8 prefix and asked the old test (`trim_start`, `{`, `trim_start`, not `}`), reading on only while that text cannot yet answer.
  - **T508-D2, UTF-8 checked as `read_to_string` checked it.** Every byte is checked as it is read, the bytes of a character cut by a chunk's edge held for the next. So a file with one bad byte anywhere is a no to both prefilters, as before. The read stops early only on a no; a yes reads on to the end to check the rest. Leaving the check out was measured to change an outcome: on a copy of the state under a hold with one bad byte, checks-hooks' `PostToolUse` ran `handle`, which wrote its empty reading over the file, where HEAD left it unchanged, measured 2026-11-27 (`t508-nonutf8.py`, one call a build). With the check, both builds leave the file unchanged, measured 2026-11-27 (the same script).
  - **T508-D3, the route.** B, the stream, was chosen over A (`memmem` over the whole string) and C (A, with the string handed on to `handle` under a hold). All three were priced on the same arms, measured 2026-11-27 (`t508-time.py`, 20 interleaved runs, a copy of the clone's state, B as built, runs 3 and 4, load 9.6 to 10.9). Savings in ms of CPU against HEAD, run 3 and run 4, measured 2026-11-27 (`t508-time.py`, 20 runs):

    | case | A | B | C |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | bash-pre, no hold | 1.95, 1.14 | **3.97, 3.52** | 1.92, 1.38 |
    | bash-pre, under a hold | 1.02, 1.65 | 2.71, 3.34 | **3.54, 3.79** |
    | bash-post, no hold | 0.39, 0.44 | **2.30, 2.47** | 0.55, 0.35 |
    | bash-post, under a hold | 0.15, 0.74 | **1.22, 2.11** | -0.84, -0.10 |

    C beats B only on bash-pre under a hold, and only if more than 71 to 83% of Bash calls ran under a hold would it win there, while with bash-post counted B wins every case, measured 2026-11-27 (`t508-time.py`, runs 3 and 4). Runs 1 and 2, of the first B without the UTF-8 check, ranked the routes the same, measured 2026-11-27 (`t508-time.py`, 20 runs, load 4.9 to 6.8). Under a hold B as built already reads the whole file, so C's saving can be had beside it: filed as T509.
  - **T508-D4, no prefix read.** The key is searched in the WHOLE file. The writer sorts the top-level keys (`checks::save`), so `plan_holds` and `plan_snaps` sit after `dispatches`, the bulk of the file: byte 1,999,829 of 2,618,222, observed 2026-11-27, method: `grep -bo` on the copy. It ran over five copies of the clone's state: the state as it is, a hold after its snapshot, no hold, a hold ended with its snapshot left, and no `plan_holds` key. Each copy was read at 71 to 95 chunk sizes, including every size that cuts either key at each of its bytes, and through `holds` and `snaps` themselves. The crate's test holds the stream to the old whole-string read on 27 fixtures, 6 of them not UTF-8, at every chunk size, measured 2026-11-27 (`make rust-test`). In the timing runs every call's exit code and stdout agreed across the four builds: 1 distinct output in each case, measured 2026-11-27 (`t508-time.py`).
  - **Other readers of the state**, observed 2026-11-27, method: a grep of the guards for `checks-open.json`, `state_path` and calls into `checks::`, each caller's matcher read. None reads the whole state to find one key on a hot path:
